remainder). A density that underflows in double is formed from its logarithm. Nothing is
floored or clipped: a term $2^k$ times smaller than its neighbours still rounds away, as
any negligible term does. Factoring applies where $|P|\ge2^{-200}$, so that $\hat u$ cannot
overflow; below, the computation is the unscaled one. Power-of-2 scaling is exact, so on
every cell where nothing underflowed the results are **bit for bit** those of the unscaled
code: checked on all 90,405 such cell-representations of the grid (C0 and C1).

**Domain of validity (added 2026-10-29).** $\tau_U$ and $\tau_{U2}$ bound the rounding error of
the double computation under the standard model $\mathrm{fl}(x\circ y)=(x\circ y)(1+\varepsilon)$,
which assumes every intermediate and result is a normal double. That assumption is
**not** met when a ratio term the production code forms in double ($u$, $v$, $w_k$, or a
density product inside them) is subnormal or underflows to 0: the error is then absolute,
up to $2^{-1074}$, not relative, and no $2^k$ factoring of the *bound* restores it. The
bounds therefore certify only cells on which no such term leaves the normal range. The
frozen Φ₂ tail run found 51 Arm B cells outside this domain (|ρ| 0.99–0.9975, $k$ from
$-1094$ to $-1089$; in each a reference $u$ or $v$ near $10^{-323}$ that double returns as 0),
each a $\tau_{U2}$ "violation" of up to $1.1\times10^{11}$ (E-063). How
such cells are to be handled — excluded from the certified domain by a stated rule, bounded
by an absolute underflow term, or computed otherwise in production — is **open** and is
decided through a derivation here and a preregistration, not by this note.

```{r cxh-tauu-2nd-def}
# The exact remainder bound of @sec-condx-hess-2nd, from a cell's primitive
# aggregates. S scales every primitive budget (S = 1 is production), as the
# perturbation in cxh_cell_err does. NULL when eta-bar >= 1. Evaluated in the
# cell's units of 2^k (z$hat): the one term with two density powers,
# (dP_rho/P)^2, carries sk = 2^k. The result is in those units too.
cxh_second <- function(z, S = 1) {
  h <- z$hat; g <- h$agg; P <- abs(z$P); eb <- S * g$eP / P; sk <- h$sk
  if (!is.finite(eb) || eb >= 1) return(NULL)
  lin <- list(u = S * h$prim$u, v = S * h$prim$v, w = S * h$prim$w)
  v2 <- (lin$v + S^2 * g$xrr / P + eb * (S * g$ePrr + S^2 * g$xrr) / P +
         sk * (S * g$ePr / P)^2 + eb^2 * abs(h$v)) / (1 - eb)^2
  w2 <- (lin$w + S^2 * g$xdr / P + eb * (S * g$edPr + S^2 * g$xdr) / P +
         (S * g$ePr / P) * (S * g$edP / P) + eb^2 * abs(h$w)) / (1 - eb)^2
  list(eb = eb, lin = lin, u = lin$u / (1 - eb), v = v2, w = w2)
}
# tau_U2, the bound Arm B of the Phi2 tail study tests against: first-order
# tau_U plus the exact remainder (production, S = 1), in units of 2^k (k = z$hat$k).
cxh_tau2 <- function(z) {
  b <- cxh_second(z); if (is.null(b)) return(NULL)
  t <- z$hat$tau
  list(u = t$u + b$u - b$lin$u, v = t$v + b$v - b$lin$v, w = t$w + b$w - b$lin$w)
}
# the rounding part of tau_U, and the values, in units of 2^k
cxh_rnd <- function(z) {
  h <- z$hat; c(h$tau$u - h$prim$u, h$tau$v - h$prim$v, h$tau$w - h$prim$w)
}
cxh_hval <- function(z) c(z$hat$u, z$hat$v, z$hat$w)

```

```{r cxh-tauu-2nd}
# (1) The bound holds far outside the first-order regime: primitives perturbed
#     at S times their budgets, S set per cell so that eta-bar = 0.01, 0.1, 0.5;
#     the raw move must not exceed the bound.
# (2) Control: the first-order bound S * delta alone is exceeded at eta-bar = 0.5.
# (3) At S = 1, the excess of the bound over first order on the stress cells
#     inside Arm B's domain (P >= 1e3 delta_P), and the cancellation driving it.
#     Both sides use the same perturbed primitives (zp) and the same reference
#     (z0, unperturbed). The only allowance is the two computations' own
#     rounding, tau_U's rounding part (tau - prim) of each: no fixed tolerance.
# Prediction before running: (1) holds; (2) fires; (3) is ~2e-3 or less except
# where 2u^2 - r or E - 2uD nearly cancels.
set.seed(20261028)
cxh_dP_cut <- 1e3 * (4 * cxh_dPhi + 3 * 2^-52)       # prereg Arm B: P >= 1e3 delta_P
sec <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(cxh_stress)), function(q) {
  st <- cxh_sets[[cxh_stress$set[q]]]; rho <- cxh_stress$rho[q]
  thi <- st$thi; thj <- st$thj
  ti <- c(-Inf, thi[-3], Inf); tj <- c(-Inf, thj[-3], Inf)
  out <- NULL
  for (x in 0:1) for (ci in 0:2) for (cj in 0:2) {
    a <- ti[ci + 1:2] - thi[3] * x; b <- tj[cj + 1:2] - thj[3] * x
    A <- list(cxh_grad(ci, 3, x), cxh_grad(ci + 1, 3, x))
    B <- list(cxh_grad(cj, 3, x), cxh_grad(cj + 1, 3, x))
    z0 <- cxh_cell_err(a, b, rho, A, B)
    if (!(z0$P > 0 && z0$agg$eP > 0)) next
    mv <- c(r2 = 0, r1 = 0, r0 = 0)
    for (tg in c(0.01, 0.1, 0.5)) {
      S <- tg * z0$P / z0$agg$eP; bd <- cxh_second(z0, S)
      for (it in 1:100) {
        e <- setNames(lapply(cxh_prims, function(nm) sample(c(-1, 1), 4, TRUE)), cxh_prims)
        zp <- cxh_cell_err(a, b, rho, A, B, e, scale = S)
        d <- abs(cxh_hval(zp) - cxh_hval(z0))            # same k: units of 2^k
        b2 <- c(bd$u, bd$v, bd$w); b1 <- c(bd$lin$u, bd$lin$v, bd$lin$w)
        # the recomputations' own rounding: tau_U's rounding part, per computation
        rd <- cxh_rnd(z0) + cxh_rnd(zp)
        ok <- !is.na(b1) & b1 > 0
        mv["r2"] <- max(mv["r2"], d[ok] / (b2[ok] + rd[ok]))
        mv["r0"] <- max(mv["r0"], d[ok] / b2[ok])
        if (tg == 0.5) mv["r1"] <- max(mv["r1"], d[ok] / b1[ok])
      }
    }
    b <- cxh_second(z0); if (is.null(b)) next      # eta-bar >= 1: no bound
    inD <- z0$P >= cxh_dP_cut
    l1 <- c(b$lin$u, b$lin$v, b$lin$w); ok <- !is.na(l1) & l1 > 0
    kap <- if (any(ok)) max((c(b$u, b$v, b$w) / l1)[ok]) - 1 else NA   # NA: exact cell
    out <- rbind(out, c(mv, P = z0$P, inD = inD, eb = b$eb, kappa = kap))
  }
  out
}))
sec2_ratio <- max(sec[, "r2"]); sec2_raw <- max(sec[, "r0"]); sec2_ctl <- max(sec[, "r1"])
sec2_dom <- sec[sec[, "inD"] == 1, , drop = FALSE]
sec2_kappa <- max(sec2_dom[, "kappa"], na.rm = TRUE); sec2_ndom <- nrow(sec2_dom)
sec2_kappa_over_eb <- max(sec2_dom[, "kappa"] / sec2_dom[, "eb"], na.rm = TRUE)

```

```{r cxh-tauu-2nd-assert}
stopifnot(sec2_ratio <= 1, sec2_raw > 1, sec2_ctl > 1, sec2_kappa_over_eb > 2)
```

Results (R 4.5.2; the chunks above extracted and run, 2026-10-28).

* **The bound holds** where first order does not: with every primitive perturbed at
  $\bar\eta$ = 0.01, 0.1 and 0.5, on 315 cells, no move exceeds the bound plus the two
  computations' own rounding (τ_U's rounding part of each), with no further tolerance. The
  rounding allowance is not vacuous: without it the move exceeds the bound by up to 7%, at
  cells with $P\approx10^{-14}$ where the perturbation is no larger than the summation
  rounding.
* **Control:** at $\bar\eta=0.5$ the first-order bound alone is exceeded by up to 40,796×
  (806× before exponent factoring, which masked underflowing cells as NaN), far more than
  $(1-\bar\eta)^{-2}=4$: the $\bar\eta^2|v|$ (or $|w|$) term at a cancelling $2u^2-r$ (or
  $E-2uD$), as predicted.
* **At $S=1$, on the 311 stress cells in Arm B's domain:** the excess of the bound over first
  order is at most $5.5\times10^{-5}$. The ratio excess$/\bar\eta$ is large (2.0e4), but it
  is not an allowance at the cut: the excess has terms that do not scale with $\bar\eta$
  ($X_{\rho\rho}/P$, $(\delta P_\rho/P)^2$), so the ratio grows as $\bar\eta$ shrinks. An earlier
  version of this paragraph extrapolated it to "an allowance near 0.8 at the cut"; that
  extrapolation was unsound and is withdrawn. What the derivation does establish: no
  constant multiple of $\bar\eta$ bounds the excess in general. What a grid shows is in
  `verify_tau2_grid.log` (c), for those cells only.

Tolerances. Set before running: the bound holds; the control fires. The comparison has no
numerical tolerance: its only allowance is the derived rounding of the two computations,
which is itself τ_U's first-order rounding model. **History, chosen after measuring and
since retired:** a first version allowed a guard $S\ge10^8$ and a tolerance $10^{-6}$ (the
bare excess measured 7% at $S\approx1$, $1.6\times10^{-6}$ at $S\ge10^4$, $3.5\times10^{-10}$
at $S\ge10^8$, the $1/S$ scaling of rounding); the derived allowance replaced both, on the
user's safeguard that a tolerance cover demonstrable recomputation error only. **Chosen after
measuring:** the floor 2 on excess$/\bar\eta$, which only asserts that the non-uniformity
was seen.

### $\varepsilon_1$: the block-error budget of the production-validation gate

**Added 2026-10-25**, step 2 of the conditional-mode production-validation gate
(E-062, 2026-10-25, G1; E-064 on
a development branch). G1 defines $\varepsilon_1$ as the block error whose propagation
through $U_\rho^{-1}$, ψ, Γ̂ and the sandwich moves any SE by at most $10^{-6}$ relative, and
T3 by at most $10^{-7}$ relative. It is anchored to what production must deliver, not to
$\tau_U$. This subsection turns that into a rule and freezes it, before $\tau_U$ is revised
(step 3).

**The rule.** A block entry $j$ is a pair's $U_\rho$, or one entry of its $U_\theta$: here
$J=19$ (three pairs, $1+6$, $1+5$ and $1+5$). An additive error $e_j$ moves ψ, Γ̂,
$W_D=\mathrm{diag}(\hat\Gamma)^{-1}$, θ̂ (refitted), every sandwich SE and T3. The pipeline
is the frozen simulation's (E-065), with the analytic
blocks. With $c_{jt}$ the relative sensitivity of target $t$ to $e_j$ (central differences):
$$\varepsilon_{1,j}=\min_t\frac{\mathrm{tol}_t}{J\,|c_{jt}|},\qquad
\mathrm{tol}=10^{-6}\ \text{(each SE)},\ 10^{-7}\ \text{(T3, at each study }N\text{)}.$$
**Equal shares across the $J$ entries.** Errors within $\varepsilon_1$ in every entry *at
once* move each target by at most its tolerance, to first order. G1's wording ("the block
error") does not say whether the budget is per entry or joint. Per entry would allow up to
$J=19$ times the tolerance jointly. The joint, equal-share reading is the conservative one,
and it is the one frozen here; see the flags below.

**Evaluation points.** These are G2's (a) and (b): `condx_A` at its fitted values
($N=1500$), and populations C and D at θ\* (`@sec-condx`'s `pop` and `popD`; θ\*_D matches
E-065 §2 to 4.6e-7). T3 is evaluated at $N=500$ and 1500, the
study's sizes. G2's (c), the link 3 replicates, are not selected yet. Their $\varepsilon_1$
is computed by this same rule when they are.

```{r cxh-eps1}
#| cache: true
# eps_1: the block-error budget of the production-validation gate
# (E-062 2026-10-25, G1). A block entry j is U_rho for a pair, or
# one entry of a pair's U_theta (19 entries here). An additive error e_j in it
# moves psi, Gamma-hat, W_D = diag(Gamma-hat)^-1, theta-hat, every sandwich SE
# and T3, as in the frozen simulation's pipeline (E-065).
# Sensitivities are central differences of that pipeline in e_j. The rule:
#   eps_1j = min over targets t of tol_t / (J |c_jt|),
# with tol = 1e-6 (relative SE, each parameter) and 1e-7 (relative T3), J the
# number of entries. Equal shares: any errors within eps_1 move each target
# by at most tol jointly, to first order.
cxh_psi_e <- function(d, fit, e) {          # cxh_psi with additive block errors
  psi1 <- lapply(seq_len(cx_p), function(j) {
    th <- fit$th[[j]]
    cx_uni_score(d$Y[, j], d$x, th) %*% t(solve(cxh_H(d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w, th)))
  })
  psir <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(cx_pairs)), function(m) {
    i <- cx_pairs[m, 1]; j <- cx_pairs[m, 2]
    cells <- cx_pair_cells(d$Y[, i], d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w)
    pd <- cxh_pair_d(cells, fit$th[[i]], fit$th[[j]], fit$rho[m])
    Ur <- sum(cells$w * pd$Ur) + e$r[m]; U1 <- colSums(cells$w * pd$Ut) + e$t[[m]]
    u <- pd$u[match(cells$key, cells$ukey)]
    -(u + cbind(psi1[[i]], psi1[[j]]) %*% U1) / Ur
  })
  cbind(do.call(cbind, lapply(psi1, function(P) P[, -ncol(P), drop = FALSE])),
        sapply(psi1, function(P) P[, ncol(P)]), psir)
}
cxh_gn <- function(s, W, th) {               # Gauss-Newton, as condx_sim_run.R
  for (it in 1:200) {
    D <- cx_delta(th)
    step <- drop(solve(t(D) %*% W %*% D, t(D) %*% W %*% (s - cx_sig_th(th))))
    th <- th + step
    if (max(abs(step)) < 1e-14) return(th)
  }
  stop("cxh_gn: no convergence")
}
# SEs (up to the common 1/sqrt(N-1), which cancels in relative terms), and T3
# at each N in Ns: T = (N-1) r'Wr, a and b from U Gamma.
cxh_targets <- function(d, fit, th0, e, Ns) {
  G <- cx_gamma(d, cxh_psi_e(d, fit, e)); W <- diag(1 / diag(G))
  th <- cxh_gn(fit$s, W, th0); D <- cx_delta(th); B <- solve(t(D) %*% W %*% D)
  se <- sqrt(diag(B %*% t(D) %*% W %*% G %*% W %*% D %*% B))
  r <- fit$s - cx_sig_th(th); U <- W - W %*% D %*% B %*% t(D) %*% W
  UG <- U %*% G; df <- length(r) - length(th)
  a <- sqrt(df / sum(diag(UG %*% UG))); b <- df - a * sum(diag(UG))
  T3 <- vapply(Ns, function(N) a * (N - 1) * drop(t(r) %*% W %*% r) + b, 0)
  c(se, T3)
}
cxh_eps1 <- function(d, fit, th0, Ns, rel_h = 1e-4) {
  npair <- nrow(cx_pairs)
  sizes <- vapply(seq_len(npair), function(m)
    length(fit$th[[cx_pairs[m, 1]]]) + length(fit$th[[cx_pairs[m, 2]]]), 0)
  zero <- list(r = numeric(npair), t = lapply(sizes, numeric))
  base <- cxh_targets(d, fit, th0, zero, Ns)
  # block values, to scale the difference step
  Ub <- lapply(seq_len(npair), function(m) {
    i <- cx_pairs[m, 1]; j <- cx_pairs[m, 2]
    cells <- cx_pair_cells(d$Y[, i], d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w)
    pd <- cxh_pair_d(cells, fit$th[[i]], fit$th[[j]], fit$rho[m])
    list(r = sum(cells$w * pd$Ur), t = colSums(cells$w * pd$Ut))
  })
  ent <- do.call(rbind, c(lapply(seq_len(npair), function(m) c(m, 0)),
                          lapply(seq_len(npair), function(m) cbind(m, seq_len(sizes[m])))))
  sens <- function(h) t(apply(ent, 1, function(q) {
    m <- q[1]; k <- q[2]
    scale <- if (k == 0) abs(Ub[[m]]$r) else max(abs(Ub[[m]]$t))
    hh <- h * scale; ep <- zero; em <- zero
    if (k == 0) { ep$r[m] <- hh; em$r[m] <- -hh } else { ep$t[[m]][k] <- hh; em$t[[m]][k] <- -hh }
    (cxh_targets(d, fit, th0, ep, Ns) - cxh_targets(d, fit, th0, em, Ns)) / (2 * hh) / abs(base)
  }))
  C1 <- sens(rel_h); C2 <- sens(rel_h / 10)          # linearity check
  J <- nrow(ent); nse <- length(th0)
  tol <- c(rep(1e-6, nse), rep(1e-7, length(Ns)))
  eps <- apply(abs(C1), 1, function(cj) min(tol / (J * cj)))
  list(ent = ent, C = C1, lin = max(abs(C1 - C2)) / max(abs(C1)), eps = eps,
       base = base, tol = tol, J = J, Ub = Ub, zero = zero)
}
eps1_A <- cxh_eps1(dA, fitA, cxh_gn(fitA$s, diag(1 / diag(GA_h)), th0), 1500)
thC <- cxh_gn(fit0$s, diag(1 / diag(cx_gamma(pop, cxh_psi(pop, fit0)))), th0)
thD <- cxh_gn(fitD$s, diag(1 / diag(cx_gamma(popD, cxh_psi(popD, fitD)))), th0)
eps1_C <- cxh_eps1(pop, fit0, thC, c(500, 1500))
eps1_D <- cxh_eps1(popD, fitD, thD, c(500, 1500))
# thD against the prereg's theta* (E-065 §2, 5 digits)
gap_thD <- max(abs(thD - c(-0.57365, 0.679073, -0.2, 0.9, 0.3,
                           0.781272, 0.721837, 0.589381, 0.284399)))
# Verification: perturb every entry at once by eps_1j, signs aligned with each
# target's sensitivity in turn; the pipeline's actual relative move must not
# exceed tol (first order, so a small allowance), and the binding target
# reaches it (tight).
cxh_eps1_check <- function(E, d, fit, th0, Ns) {
  t(sapply(seq_along(E$tol), function(tg) {
    e <- E$zero; sg <- sign(E$C[, tg]) * E$eps
    for (q in seq_len(nrow(E$ent))) {
      m <- E$ent[q, 1]; k <- E$ent[q, 2]
      if (k == 0) e$r[m] <- sg[q] else e$t[[m]][k] <- sg[q]
    }
    mv <- abs(cxh_targets(d, fit, th0, e, Ns)[tg] / E$base[tg] - 1)
    c(move = mv, tol = E$tol[tg])
  }))
}
chk_A <- cxh_eps1_check(eps1_A, dA, fitA, cxh_gn(fitA$s, diag(1 / diag(GA_h)), th0), 1500)
chk_C <- cxh_eps1_check(eps1_C, pop, fit0, thC, c(500, 1500))
chk_D <- cxh_eps1_check(eps1_D, popD, fitD, thD, c(500, 1500))
eps1_table <- rbind(
  data.frame(point = "condx_A", eps1_A$ent, eps = eps1_A$eps),
  data.frame(point = "pop_C", eps1_C$ent, eps = eps1_C$eps),
  data.frame(point = "pop_D", eps1_D$ent, eps = eps1_D$eps))
names(eps1_table)[2:3] <- c("pair", "entry")         # entry 0 = U_rho, k = U_theta[k]

```

```{r cxh-eps1-assert}
chk_all <- rbind(chk_A, chk_C, chk_D)
stopifnot(max(eps1_A$lin, eps1_C$lin, eps1_D$lin) < 1e-3,
          all(chk_all[, "move"] <= chk_all[, "tol"] * (1 + 1e-2)),
          # tight at the binding target of each point (eps_1 is a minimum over targets)
          all(sapply(list(chk_A, chk_C, chk_D), function(z) max(z[, "move"] / z[, "tol"])) >= 0.5),
          # threshold SEs: tau-hat = s_tau, untouched by the pair blocks
          all(chk_all[c(1:5, 11:15, 22:26), "move"] == 0),
          gap_thD < 1e-5, all(is.finite(eps1_table$eps)), all(eps1_table$eps > 0))
```

```{r cxh-ru}
# Gate step 3: the tau_U adequacy rule (E-062 2026-10-25), at G2's
# points (a) condx_A and (b) populations C and D, every cell of every pair.
# R_U = max_j B_j / eps_1j, B_j = tau_U of block entry j with the certified
# corner budget. Pass iff R_U <= 0.1 and every cell is inside the certified
# domain: finite bounds in [-2.5, 2.5] (the corner budget's and the corrected
# phi2 model's validated range), |rho| <= B = 0.999, and tau_U's validity
# P >= 1e3 delta_P (first order). Shares: the corner budget's part of B_j,
# tau_U(delta_Phi) - tau_U(0), against the rest.
cxh_ru_point <- function(d, fit, E) {
  dP <- 4 * cxh_dPhi + 3 * 2^-52
  out <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(cx_pairs)), function(m) {
    i <- cx_pairs[m, 1]; j <- cx_pairs[m, 2]; thi <- fit$th[[i]]; thj <- fit$th[[j]]
    cells <- cx_pair_cells(d$Y[, i], d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w)
    full <- cxh_pair_tau(cells, thi, thj, fit$rho[m])
    zero <- cxh_pair_tau(cells, thi, thj, fit$rho[m], dPhi = 0)
    Ki <- length(thi); Kj <- length(thj)
    ti <- c(-Inf, thi[-Ki], Inf); tj <- c(-Inf, thj[-Kj], Inf)
    bnd <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(cells$ci), function(r)
      c(ti[cells$ci[r] + 1:2] - thi[Ki] * cells$x[r], tj[cells$cj[r] + 1:2] - thj[Kj] * cells$x[r])))
    P <- vapply(full$cells, `[[`, 0, "P")
    list(B = c(full$tUr, full$tUt), B0 = c(zero$tUr, zero$tUt),
         maxb = max(abs(bnd[is.finite(bnd)])), rho = abs(fit$rho[m]),
         minP = min(P), ok_P = all(P >= 1e3 * dP),
         finite = all(is.finite(c(full$tUr, full$tUt))))
  })
  B <- unlist(lapply(out, `[[`, "B")); B0 <- unlist(lapply(out, `[[`, "B0"))
  # the order of E$ent: U_rho of pairs 1..3, then U_theta of pair 1, 2, 3
  np <- nrow(cx_pairs); sizes <- vapply(out, function(o) length(o$B) - 1, 0)
  idx <- c(cumsum(c(1, sizes[-np] + 1)),
           unlist(lapply(seq_len(np), function(m) sum(sizes[seq_len(m - 1)] + 1) + 1 + seq_len(sizes[m]))))
  B <- B[idx]; B0 <- B0[idx]
  ratio <- B / E$eps
  list(R_U = max(ratio), at = E$ent[which.max(ratio), ],
       share_corner = (B - B0)[which.max(ratio)] / B[which.max(ratio)],
       maxb = max(vapply(out, `[[`, 0, "maxb")), maxrho = max(vapply(out, `[[`, 0, "rho")),
       minP = min(vapply(out, `[[`, 0, "minP")),
       in_domain = all(vapply(out, function(o) o$ok_P && o$finite && o$maxb <= 2.5 && o$rho <= 0.999, TRUE)))
}
ru <- list(condx_A = cxh_ru_point(dA, fitA, eps1_A),
           pop_C = cxh_ru_point(pop, fit0, eps1_C),
           pop_D = cxh_ru_point(popD, fitD, eps1_D))
ru_table <- t(sapply(ru, function(z) c(R_U = z$R_U, pair = z$at[[1]], entry = z$at[[2]],
  share_corner = z$share_corner, max_bound = z$maxb, max_rho = z$maxrho, min_P = z$minP,
  in_domain = z$in_domain)))
R_U <- max(ru_table[, "R_U"])
gate_pass <- R_U <= 0.1 && all(ru_table[, "in_domain"] == 1)
# tau_U verified on the domain's own cells: the perturbation check of
# cxh-tauu-check (every primitive at +-K x its bound, 100 draws per cell),
# on every cell of every pair at the three points.
set.seed(20261026)
cxh_ru_verify <- function(d, fit) {
  K <- 1e4
  unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cx_pairs)), function(m) {
    i <- cx_pairs[m, 1]; j <- cx_pairs[m, 2]; thi <- fit$th[[i]]; thj <- fit$th[[j]]
    Ki <- length(thi); Kj <- length(thj)
    ti <- c(-Inf, thi[-Ki], Inf); tj <- c(-Inf, thj[-Kj], Inf)
    cells <- cx_pair_cells(d$Y[, i], d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w)
    vapply(seq_along(cells$ci), function(r) {
      ci <- cells$ci[r]; cj <- cells$cj[r]; x <- cells$x[r]
      a <- ti[ci + 1:2] - thi[Ki] * x; b <- tj[cj + 1:2] - thj[Kj] * x
      A <- list(cxh_grad(ci, Ki, x), cxh_grad(ci + 1, Ki, x))
      B <- list(cxh_grad(cj, Kj, x), cxh_grad(cj + 1, Kj, x))
      z0 <- cxh_cell_err(a, b, fit$rho[m], A, B)
      max(vapply(1:100, function(it) {
        e <- setNames(lapply(cxh_prims, function(nm) sample(c(-1, 1), 4, TRUE)), cxh_prims)
        zp <- cxh_cell_err(a, b, fit$rho[m], A, B, e, scale = K)
        ok <- z0$prim$w > 0
        max(abs(zp$u - z0$u) / K / z0$prim$u, abs(zp$v - z0$v) / K / z0$prim$v,
            abs(zp$w - z0$w)[ok] / K / z0$prim$w[ok])
      }, 0))
    }, 0)
  }))
}
ru_verify <- c(condx_A = max(cxh_ru_verify(dA, fitA)), pop_C = max(cxh_ru_verify(pop, fit0)),
               pop_D = max(cxh_ru_verify(popD, fitD)))

```

```{r cxh-ru-assert}
stopifnot(all(ru_verify <= 1 + 1e-3), min(ru_verify) > 0.5,
          all(ru_table[, "in_domain"] == 1), gate_pass)
```

### Gate step 3: τ_U revised and judged by the adequacy rule

**Executed 2026-10-25.** Step 3 of the gate (E-064) revises τ_U to
the corrected δ_D model above. It then judges τ_U by the user's rule, over G2's points (a)
and (b): R_U = max_j B_j/ε_{1,j}, where B_j is τ_U of block entry $j$ under the certified
corner budget. The rule passes iff R_U ≤ 0.1 and every cell is inside the certified domain.
The certified domain: finite bounds in $[-2.5,2.5]$ (where both the corner budget and the
corrected model are validated); $|\rho|\le B=0.999$; and τ_U's first-order condition, read
as $P\ge10^3\delta_P$, the same cut as the Φ₂ preregistration's Arm B.

| Point | R_U | Binding entry | Corner-budget share | Max bound | Max \|ρ\| | Min P |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `condx_A` | 2.0e-6 | pair 3, U_ρ | 0.70 | 0.93 | 0.52 | 0.012 |
| population C | 2.8e-5 | pair 3, U_θ[3] | 0.71 | 0.90 | 0.56 | 0.011 |
| population D | 8.5e-7 | pair 1, U_ρ | 0.79 | 0.90 | 0.56 | 0.010 |

* **R_U = 2.8e-5 ≤ 0.1: the rule passes at (a) and (b).** Every cell is inside the certified
  domain, with a wide margin on every condition. The bound is not under strain. The
  dominant term is the corner budget δ_Φ (70–79% of the binding B_j), not the density.
* **τ_U verified on the domain's own cells**, not just the stress grid: the perturbation
  check on every cell of every pair at the three points gives a largest move/bound of
  1.000005, the second-order excess already seen.
* **G2 (c), executed 2026-10-28: the rule passes at the 100 link 3 replicates.** These are
  replicates 1–25 of each cell, accepted under L1. The same functions were run at each
  replicate's Stage 1 fit (E-066; per replicate in
  `link3_ru.csv`). R_U = 7.0e-6, at C500 replicate 12, pair 3, U_ρ. Every replicate is in
  domain: max bound 1.13, max |ρ| 0.65, min P 4.8e-3. ε₁ is finite and positive, and its
  linearity is ≤ 2.7e-8. The domain-cell check is ≤ 1.000005. The corner budget's share of
  the binding B_j is 0.68–0.82, so δ_Φ dominates, as at (a)–(b).

Tolerances, set before running: R_U ≤ 0.1 (the user's rule); the domain conditions above; the
domain-cell check's 1 + 10⁻³, the stress grid's allowance. The cut $P\ge10^3\delta_P$ is this
section's reading of "δP ≪ P", **adopted by the user 2026-10-25**. G2 gave no number.


Results (frozen values: `eps1_table`; 19 entries per point).

* **Linearity:** the sensitivities at steps $10^{-4}$ and $10^{-5}$ (relative to the block)
  agree to ≤ 1.4e-8 relative.
* **Joint check:** every entry is perturbed at once by $\pm\varepsilon_{1,j}$, with signs
  aligned with each target in turn. Every target moves by at most its tolerance, and the
  binding one moves by 0.92–0.95 of it: the budget is tight where it binds. The binding
  target is T3 at every point.
* **Threshold SEs move by exactly 0** (τ̂ = $s_\tau$; the pair blocks do not reach them).
* **The smallest $\varepsilon_{1,j}$:** 1.2e-8 (`condx_A`), 5.2e-10 (C) and 1.6e-8 (D).
  The ranges are 1.2e-8–1.6e-7 (`condx_A`), 5.2e-10–2.3e-7 (C) and 1.6e-8–2.9e-7 (D).

Tolerances. Linearity $10^{-3}$, the joint check's allowance $1+10^{-2}$ and θ\*_D $10^{-5}$
were set before running. **Chosen after measuring:** the tightness check was first written
for every target. It failed because a non-binding target cannot reach its tolerance when
$\varepsilon_1$ is a minimum over targets. It is now asserted for the binding target only
(≥ 0.5 of tolerance), and the exact-zero threshold-SE check was added after seeing it.

**Flags, decided by the user 2026-10-25:** (1) joint, 19-entry budget, as frozen; (2) the
relative SE and T3 criteria are unchanged, and population C's stringent budget is retained;
(3) the link 3 points are added by the same rule when they are selected. As first raised:

1. **Joint versus per entry** (above). Frozen: joint, equal shares.
2. **T3 at population C is nearly zero.** There $F\approx0$, so T3 equals the shift $b$,
   0.0189. A $10^{-7}$ relative tolerance on that is $1.9\times10^{-9}$ absolute, and it
   drives C's $\varepsilon_1$ to 5.2e-10, 20–30 times below `condx_A`'s and D's. That is
   G1 as written. Whether a near-zero T3 at a correctly specified population should anchor
   the budget is a question about G1, not settled here.
3. **G2 (c):** the link 3 replicates' $\varepsilon_1$ awaits their selection.

### Gate step 6, link 1: ψ against an extrapolated Gateaux derivative {#sec-condx-link1}

**Discharged 2026-11-10.** This link is discharged by its re-execution under the
preregistration frozen 2026-11-10 (E-098; R 4.6.0, base R):
gap 2.64e-11 on population C and 2.09e-11 on D against the 1e-9 criterion, every floor
holding (E-098). The code below was first executed in a side
session on 2026-10-28 (R 4.5.2: 2.6e-11 and 2.1e-11) with its tolerances set beforehand, so
the frozen run was a re-execution of a result already seen, not a blind test. It does not
certify the accuracy of $\Phi_2$ (both sides share `Phi2`), anything about Mata, or anything
outside one binary covariate, one group and three items.

**What it checks.** The influence function of an estimator functional $T$ at $F$ is the
Gateaux derivative $\psi(z)=\frac{d}{de}T\big((1-e)F+e\,\delta_z\big)\big|_{e=0}$. Here
$T$ is `cx_stage1`: the univariate probits, then the pair likelihoods, solved to
convergence. It contains no Hessian block. The finite differences inside it are Newton
steps, and they change how fast it converges but not where. `cxh_psi` builds ψ from the
closed-form blocks. So the comparison involves neither `cx_psi_n`'s finite-difference
Hessian nor the closed forms' own derivation. The two sides share only the score functions
and the $\Phi_2$ integrator.

`@sec-condx-hess` already compared ψ with a central difference at $e=\pm10^{-5}$ and found
2.7e-8. That figure is the difference's own truncation error, so a check at $10^{-6}$
cannot see a formula error below that level. Here the derivative is taken by Richardson
extrapolation instead:

* steps $h_m=h_{k}2^{-m}$, $m=0,\dots,4$, with $h_k=w_k/4$ for pattern $k$. The
  contaminated weight $(1-e)w_k+e$ vanishes at $e\approx-w_k$, so the expansion in $e$
  has radius about $w_k$, and a fixed step would sit close to it for the sparsest
  pattern ($w_{\min}=1.7\times10^{-3}$ at C);
* $D_m$ is the central difference at $h_m$, then $R^{(1)}_m=(4D_{m+1}-D_m)/3$ and
  $R^{(2)}_m=(16R^{(1)}_{m+1}-R^{(1)}_m)/15$, which leaves an $O(h^6)$ error;
* the oracle is $R^{(2)}_2$ (the finest step). Its error estimate is
  $E=|R^{(2)}_2-R^{(2)}_1|$, taken entrywise.

Both populations are covered: C (`pop`, correctly specified) and D (`popD`, Stage 1
misspecified, where the information identity fails and the Hessian form is what makes ψ
the true influence function). That is G2 (b).

**Resolution controls.** A check is only as useful as the smallest error it can see. Each
block, $H_j$, $U_\rho$ and $U_\theta$, is scaled in turn by $1+10^{-6}$ (`cxg_psi`'s
`scale`), and the resulting ψ must miss the oracle by more than ten times the tolerance.
This shows that the link resolves a $10^{-6}$ relative error in any one block. It does
not resolve ε₁ (5.2e-10 at its smallest), and is not meant to. Bounding the evaluation
error at that level is τ_U's job (`R_U` above), not this link's.

Tolerances, **set before running**:

* oracle adequacy: $\max E\le10^{-10}$ on each population. If this fails, the link is
  *inconclusive* (the oracle is too coarse), not failed;
* the link: $\max_{k,\cdot}|\psi_{\text{an}}-R^{(2)}_2|\le10^{-9}$, absolute, on each
  population. ψ's entries are $O(1)$–$O(10)$ (reported below), so this is about
  $10^{-10}$ relative. It sits a decade above the adequacy bound;
* resolution controls: each must miss by more than $10^{-8}$.

```{r cxg-link1}
#| cache: true
# Gate step 6, link 1 (discharged 2026-11-10). psi from the closed-form blocks against a
# Richardson-extrapolated Gateaux derivative of cx_stage1. Every name defined
# here starts with cxg_. Depends on cx-setup, cx-stage1, cxh-forms, and on
# pop/fit0 (cx-gateaux) and popD/fitD (cx-misspec).

# cxh_psi with each block optionally scaled: scale = c(H, Ur, Ut). Used only
# for the resolution controls; at scale = 1 it is cxh_psi.
cxg_psi <- function(d, fit, scale = c(1, 1, 1)) {
  psi1 <- lapply(seq_len(cx_p), function(j) {
    th <- fit$th[[j]]
    cx_uni_score(d$Y[, j], d$x, th) %*%
      t(solve(scale[1] * cxh_H(d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w, th)))
  })
  psir <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(cx_pairs)), function(m) {
    i <- cx_pairs[m, 1]; j <- cx_pairs[m, 2]
    cells <- cx_pair_cells(d$Y[, i], d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w)
    pd <- cxh_pair_d(cells, fit$th[[i]], fit$th[[j]], fit$rho[m])
    Ur <- scale[2] * sum(cells$w * pd$Ur); U1 <- scale[3] * colSums(cells$w * pd$Ut)
    u <- pd$u[match(cells$key, cells$ukey)]
    -(u + cbind(psi1[[i]], psi1[[j]]) %*% U1) / Ur
  })
  cbind(do.call(cbind, lapply(psi1, function(P) P[, -ncol(P), drop = FALSE])),
        sapply(psi1, function(P) P[, ncol(P)]), psir)
}

# Richardson table for the Gateaux derivative at pattern k. Returns the
# oracle R2_2 and its error estimate |R2_2 - R2_1|.
cxg_gateaux_k <- function(d0, k) {
  T_e <- function(e) {
    d <- d0; d$w <- (1 - e) * d0$w; d$w[k] <- d$w[k] + e
    cx_stage1(d)$s
  }
  h <- d0$w[k] / 4 * 2^-(0:4)
  D  <- sapply(h, function(hh) (T_e(hh) - T_e(-hh)) / (2 * hh))
  R1 <- (4 * D[, -1] - D[, -5]) / 3
  R2 <- (16 * R1[, -1] - R1[, -4]) / 15
  list(val = R2[, 3], err = abs(R2[, 3] - R2[, 2]), D_fine = D[, 5])
}
cxg_link <- function(d0, fit) {
  g <- lapply(seq_along(d0$w), function(k) cxg_gateaux_k(d0, k))
  orc <- t(sapply(g, `[[`, "val")); err <- t(sapply(g, `[[`, "err"))
  psi <- cxg_psi(d0, fit)
  ctl <- sapply(list(H = c(1 + 1e-6, 1, 1), Ur = c(1, 1 + 1e-6, 1),
                     Ut = c(1, 1, 1 + 1e-6)),
                function(sc) max(abs(cxg_psi(d0, fit, sc) - orc)))
  list(gap = max(abs(psi - orc)), err = max(err),
       gap_cols = apply(abs(psi - orc), 2, max),
       same_as_cxh = max(abs(psi - cxh_psi(d0, fit))),
       psi_max = max(abs(psi)), w_min = min(d0$w),
       gap_plain_fine = max(abs(psi - t(sapply(g, `[[`, "D_fine")))),
       ctl = ctl)
}
cxg_C <- cxg_link(pop, fit0)
cxg_D <- cxg_link(popD, fitD)

```

```{r cxg-assert}
stopifnot(
  cxg_C$same_as_cxh == 0, cxg_D$same_as_cxh == 0,
  cxg_C$err <= 1e-10, cxg_D$err <= 1e-10,
  cxg_C$gap <= 1e-9,  cxg_D$gap <= 1e-9,
  all(cxg_C$ctl > 1e-8), all(cxg_D$ctl > 1e-8))
```

The check that `cxg_psi` at unit scale reproduces `cxh_psi` exactly (`same_as_cxh == 0`)
guards the copy. It was set before running.

Results (side session, 2026-10-28, E-064; **re-executed
by the user 2026-10-28, figures identical**):

| | C (`pop`) | D (`popD`) |
|---|---|---|
| $\max\lvert\psi_{\text{an}}-R^{(2)}_2\rvert$ | 2.6e-11 | 2.1e-11 |
| oracle error estimate $\max E$ | 3.0e-11 | 4.1e-11 |
| $\max\lvert\psi\rvert$ | 4.85 | 4.25 |
| $w_{\min}$ | 1.7e-3 | 1.1e-3 |
| plain central difference at the finest step, for comparison | 2.0e-5 | 2.4e-5 |
| control $H\times(1+10^{-6})$ | 4.9e-6 | 4.3e-6 |
| control $U_\rho\times(1+10^{-6})$ | 3.8e-6 | 3.9e-6 |
| control $U_\theta\times(1+10^{-6})$ | 4.7e-7 | 4.4e-7 |

* **The analytic ψ agrees with the Gateaux derivative to the oracle's own resolution**
  on both populations. The gap is no larger than $E$, so no formula error is visible above
  about $3\times10^{-11}$ absolute, or $10^{-11}$ relative to $\max|\psi|$. That is about
  a thousand times tighter than `@sec-condx-hess`'s 2.7e-8. At D, the population where
  the Hessian form matters, the result is the same.
* **Extrapolation is what makes this possible.** At these step sizes ($h\le w_k/4$) a
  plain central difference misses by 2e-5, because the steps are close to the expansion's
  radius. Two Richardson levels remove that error.
* **Every block is resolved.** A $10^{-6}$ relative error in any one block moves ψ by
  4e-7 to 5e-6. That is four to five decades above the observed gap. $U_\theta$'s control
  is the weakest, because it enters only through the propagation term.

Nothing was chosen after measuring. The diagnostic field `gap_plain_fine` was renamed
after the first run (it had been mislabelled `D_coarse` but held the finest step) and
re-run with identical figures. The assertions were not changed.

## Conditional mode: the pooled score for Module 2's root-finder {#sec-condx-rootfind}

**Rendered in the full document 2026-11-11** (quarto 1.10.18, R 4.6.0, Rmpfr 1.1.3, this
machine; every chunk of the file ran, exit 0; the prose banners were edited after that render, no
chunk was). *Drafted by a
read-only agent; run by the main session, standalone and then in the render.* The chunks below are the bodies of
a verification script of E-096 (with `setup`'s `Phi2` and `cx-setup`'s
`cx_phi2` copied in as a preamble; R 4.6.0, Rmpfr 1.1.3; log beside it). The figures quoted
are that run's.

`dwlsmv_cx_pair_fit()` hands `dwlsmv_rootfind()` (@sec-rootfind) an evaluator that is not
the one that section derived: `dwlsmv_cx_rf_eval()` calls the single-table evaluator once
per covariate group and pools the results,
$$\tilde{\bar S}=\tilde w_0\tilde s_0+\tilde w_1\tilde s_1,\qquad
\tilde c=\tilde w_0\tilde c_0+\tilde w_1\tilde c_1,\qquad
\tilde\tau_S=\tilde w_0\tilde\tau_0+\tilde w_1\tilde\tau_1
+3\varepsilon\,(\tilde w_0|\tilde s_0|+\tilde w_1|\tilde s_1|),$$
usable iff both groups are, with $\tilde w_x=\mathrm{fl}(N_x/\mathrm{fl}(N_0+N_1))$ and
$\varepsilon=2^{-52}$ (Mata's `epsilon(1)`). This section derives what that $\tau_S$ bounds
(Result C1), what "usable" must mean for the pooled score (Result C2), and which of the
root-finder's premises carry over from one table to two (Result C3). It changes no
estimator: $\hat\rho$ is still the root of the pooled score of @sec-condx's item 2, with
the item fits held fixed.

**Notation.** Group $x\in\{0,1\}$ has the $K_i\times K_j$ table $n_x$, $N_x=\sum n_x$,
observed cells $\mathcal O_x$, and bounds $a_x=\tau_i-b_ix$, $b_x=\tau_j-b_jx$.
$\bar S_x(\rho)=S_x(\rho)/N_x$ is @sec-rootfind's $\bar S$ for that table, $\tilde s_x$ its
computed value and $\tilde\tau_x$ the computed single-table bound. $N=N_0+N_1$,
$w_x=N_x/N$ exactly, and $u=2^{-53}$. In real arithmetic
$$\bar S=\frac1N\sum_x\sum_{\mathcal O_x}n_{rs,x}u_{rs,x}=\sum_x w_x\bar S_x
\quad\text{and}\quad \ell(\rho)=\ell_0(\rho)+\ell_1(\rho),$$
so the pooled score is $N^{-1}\,\mathrm d\ell/\mathrm d\rho$ of a sum of two
single-table log-likelihoods. This identity is exact, and nothing below needs
$w_0+w_1=1$.

### Result C1: the evaluation error of the pooled score

**Assumptions.**

- **(A1)** The counts are integers and $N<2^{53}$, so $N_x$ (Mata's `sum()` of integer
  counts) and $\mathrm{fl}(N_0+N_1)$ are exact.
- **(A2)** Group $x$ is usable at $\rho$. Then, to first order, $|\tilde s_x-\bar S_x|\le\tilde\tau_x$
  (@sec-rootfind, the stopping rule). C1 inherits every caveat of that bound unchanged.
  Its $\delta_D$ term is a measured margin, not a derived bound (@sec-deltad). Its
  $\delta_\Phi$ was measured for bounds in $[-2.5,2.5]$ and $|\rho|\le B$. The shifted
  bounds $a-bx$ can leave that range; on `condx_A` and `condx_D` they lie in $[-0.93, 0.87]$.
- **(A3)** IEEE double, round to nearest, and no underflow or overflow in the products
  $\tilde w_x\tilde s_x$ and $\tilde w_x\tilde\tau_x$. A fused multiply-add can only remove
  roundings, so the bound holds for it too.
- **(A4)** $N_0,N_1\ge1$. Result P1's refusal of a constant $x$ guarantees it.

**The operations**, in the code's order: $M=\mathrm{fl}(N_0+N_1)=N$ (exact by A1);
$\tilde w_x=w_x(1+\alpha_x)$; $p_x=\tilde w_x\tilde s_x(1+\beta_x)$;
$\tilde{\bar S}=(p_0+p_1)(1+\gamma)$, every $|\alpha|,|\beta|,|\gamma|\le u$. Hence
$$\tilde{\bar S}-\bar S=\sum_x w_x(\tilde s_x-\bar S_x)
+\sum_x w_x\tilde s_x\big[(1+\alpha_x)(1+\beta_x)(1+\gamma)-1\big].$$

**Lemma.** Write $d=|\tilde{\bar S}-\sum_x w_x\tilde s_x|$ and $A=\sum_x w_x|\tilde s_x|$.
Then $d\le\big((1+u)^3-1\big)A$, which is $3uA$ to first order. The inexact weights enter
only as the relative errors $\alpha_x$, each charged once. Their failure to sum to 1 is
irrelevant, because the target is $\sum_xw_x\bar S_x$ and no weight is formed as
$1-\tilde w_{1-x}$.

**Result C1.** Let $E=\sum_xw_x\tilde\tau_x+d$, the largest error of $\tilde{\bar S}$
compatible with (A2): the error is linear in the exact $\bar S_x$, so it is extreme at a
vertex of the box $|\bar S_x-\tilde s_x|\le\tilde\tau_x$. Then:

1. **First order:** $|\tilde{\bar S}-\bar S|\le\sum_xw_x\tau_x+3u\sum_xw_x|\tilde s_x|$.
   This is the bound the pooling needs.
2. **The code's $\tilde\tau_S$, all orders, given the $\tilde\tau_x$:**
   $E\le\tilde\tau_S/(1-u)^4$.

*Proof of 2.* Rounding is monotone, and $\tilde w_x\ge w_x(1-u)$. So
$\mathrm{fl}(\tilde w_0\tilde\tau_0+\tilde w_1\tilde\tau_1)\ge(1-u)^3T$ with
$T=\sum w_x\tilde\tau_x$. The charge $\mathrm{fl}(3\varepsilon\cdot\mathrm{fl}(\sum\tilde w_x|\tilde s_x|))$
is at least $6u(1-u)^4A$, because $3\varepsilon=6u$ exactly. The last addition costs one
more factor $1-u$, so $\tilde\tau_S\ge(1-u)^4(T+6u(1-u)A)$. Finally
$E\le T+((1+u)^3-1)A\le T+6u(1-u)A$, since $3u+3u^2+u^3\le6u-6u^2$ for $u\le1/10$. ∎

**Verdict: (b), sufficient but loose.** The code charges $\varepsilon=2u$ per rounding,
the convention of @sec-rootfind's $(|\mathcal O|+2)\varepsilon$ and of $\delta_P$'s
$3\varepsilon$. The derived need is $u$ per rounding. The factor of 2 does real work: it
absorbs the second-order terms of the combining step, so $\tilde\tau_S$ falls short of $E$
only through the rounding of $\sum\tilde w_x\tilde\tau_x$ itself, a relative
$\le(1-u)^{-4}-1\approx4u$. That shortfall needs $A\lesssim T$, both groups' scores within
their own $\tau$ of 0 at once. It is the same order as the rounding of the single-table
$\tilde\tau_x$'s own evaluation, which @sec-rootfind's first-order model also drops. The
looseness costs little. Since $\tilde\tau_x\ge(|\mathcal O_x|+2)\varepsilon\sum w|\tilde u|$
and $\sum w|\tilde u|\ge|\tilde s_x|$ up to rounding, the charge is at most
$3/(|\mathcal O_x|+2)$ of the propagated term, and is measured at no more than 0.027 of
$\tilde\tau_S$ on every realistic evaluation below. **The recommended expression is the
code's, unchanged:**
$\tau_S=\tilde w_0\tilde\tau_0+\tilde w_1\tilde\tau_1+3\varepsilon(\tilde w_0|\tilde s_0|+\tilde w_1|\tilde s_1|)$.
Tightening $3\varepsilon$ to $1.5\varepsilon$ would move $\tau_S$ by under 1.4% and would
lose the second-order cover.

At the pooled root the two group scores are **not** small. On `condx_A` and `condx_D`,
$|\tilde s_x|$ is 0.002 to 0.054 there, while $|\tilde{\bar S}|\le0.009\,\tilde\tau_S$:
the pooled zero is a cancellation between the groups. This is the regime C1's $A$ term
exists for, and the reason the stress set below includes cancellation cases.

### Result C2: what "usable" means for the pooled score

The pooled score sums over the stacked observed cells $\mathcal O=\mathcal O_0\cup\mathcal O_1$,
each cell a triple $(r,s,x)$ with its own probability $\pi_{rs}(a_x,b_x;\rho)$. Apply
@sec-rootfind's definition (adopted 2026-09-29) to that table:
$$\mathcal R_P=\{\rho:\min_{(r,s,x)\in\mathcal O}\tilde\pi_{rs,x}(\rho)>\delta_P\}
=\mathcal R_{P,0}\cap\mathcal R_{P,1}.$$
**"Both groups usable" is exactly this rule**, neither stricter nor looser than v1's
applied to the stacked table.

- **Necessary.** An observed cell with $\tilde\pi\le\delta_P$ in either group has
  $\tilde u$ with relative error above 1. It enters $\bar S$ with weight $n_{rs,x}/N>0$, and
  (A2) fails for its group, so C1 has no premise. A small $w_x$ rescues nothing: a
  one-observation cell carries weight $1/N$ whichever group holds it, the same weight as
  in v1.
- **Not sufficient** for the first-order model, exactly as in v1 and as @sec-condx-hess
  notes for $\tau_U$: the model needs $\delta_P\ll\pi$, and usability gives only
  $\delta_P<\pi$.
- **A cell empty in one group only** is not in that group's $\mathcal O_x$. The same
  $(r,s)$ in the other group is a different cell, with different bounds, and is tested
  under them. Nothing special follows. (Result P2 shows the boundary consequences of such
  a cell differ from v1's; see C3, item 8.)
- **$N_x$ small** changes the rule not at all. **$N_x=0$** is excluded by (A4). If it
  were reached, `dwlsmv_rf_eval()` would return $(x,1,0,c_x,0)$, because Mata's `sum()`
  skips the missing $w=0/0$, and the pooled value would be group 0's. That is accidental,
  not derived.
- **$\rho=0$ is usable: v1's argument does not transfer.** It used $\pi_{rs}(0)=p_rq_s$
  with each marginal an empirical proportion $\ge1/N$. In group $x$ the marginals are
  model-implied by the parallel-shift probit. For a binary item that fit is saturated per
  group (@sec-condx, *Separation*), so $\pi(0)\ge N_x^{-2}$ follows from P1. For $K\ge3$ no lower
  bound is derived, and the abort at $\rho=0$ (rc 3498) remains the only guard. On the six
  pairs here the smallest group cell probability at 0 is 0.048 (R's $\Phi_2$).

### Result C3: what `dwlsmv_rootfind()` assumes, and what carries over

| Use in `dwlsmv_rootfind()` / @sec-rootfind | Carries to the pooled score? |
|---|---|
| Sign decisions (walk $d\bar S<0$; bracket update by computed sign) | Yes. They read computed signs only, and certainty comes from C1 at the stopping rule and the endpoint check. |
| Bracket orientation $(+,-)$ is a maximum's | Yes, exactly: $\bar S=N^{-1}(\ell_0+\ell_1)'$, so an accepted root is a local maximum of the pooled log-likelihood. |
| $c$ as expected information; Property 3 ($c>0$); the Fisher step points uphill | Yes. $\sum_xw_xc_x$ is the per-observation expected information of the product multinomial with $N_0,N_1$ fixed, and $c>0$ iff some $c_x>0$. |
| $H/c\ge\tfrac12$, the premise of $\tau_\rho$'s factor 16 and of the probes' certainty | **Not carried; measured only here.** $H/c=\sum_xw_xc_x(H_x/c_x)/\sum_xw_xc_x$ is a $c$-weighted mean of the group ratios, each at the *common* $\rho$, which is not its own root. v1's range (0.98–1.06) was measured at single-table roots. R, six pairs: pooled 0.9959–1.0026, groups 0.830–1.125. Needs (M2). |
| Stopping rule $|\bar S|\le\tau_S$, $h-\ell\le\tau_\rho$ | Yes, given C1 and the $H/c$ premise. |
| Uniqueness: at most one sign change (Levels R3/R4; the 1,086,996-pair development test) | **No.** That evidence is per single table. Quasi-concavity is not preserved by sums: $\ell_0+\ell_1$ can be bimodal when the groups' maxima are far apart and sharp. The endpoint check still catches an odd number of extra changes (status 5). On R's grid each of the six pairs has one change; a pooled development test is owed. |
| Usable set "one run" (Level R3) | Not measured pooled. $\mathcal R_P$ is an intersection, and either group can set the frontier. |
| Boundary statuses 2/3/4 as *outputs* | Yes: generic. |
| Their *interpretation* by v1's per-table cases (@sec-emptycells, @sec-kindE: the empty-cell $2\times2$ ends at status 2 with $\hat\rho=-\sigma_eB$; R5's exact zero from $1-2^{-16}$) | **No** (Result P2). A table empty in one group need not be a boundary when pooled, and @sec-kindE's single-table derivation does not apply. |
| The endpoint cap 54, the exit bounds $k\le56$ / $k\ge57$ | Yes, given their premise "every unusable point lies outside $[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12]$", now for the intersection. R: $\pm\tfrac12$ usable on all six pairs; the frontiers at 0.977–0.997; $\pm B$ unusable on all six (off-diagonal cells vanish as $|\rho|\to1$), so the frontier bisection runs on every check. Needs (M3) on `binormal()`. |
| The root-search cap 40 (chosen after measuring v1 pairs) | **Not carried.** The loop's rate is $|1-H/c|$ of the pooled ratio. Needs (M1). |
| `dwlsmv_rf_end()`'s cheap path | Not taken: `fe == &dwlsmv_rf_eval()` is false for the pooled evaluator, so every bisection step is a full pooled evaluation. The points, decisions and $k$ are the same (the cheap path is a speed change only); the cost per step is two full tables. |
| The zero-probe at $\bar S(0)=0$; the entry rule (status 1, or 6 with $k\ne3$) | Yes, given C1 and the $H/c$ premise. |

**Measured in Mata, 2026-11-11** (E-096, StataMP 18,
`binormal()`; `condx_A` and `condx_D` only, six pairs; the 100 link 3 datasets were not run). A
measurement, not a test.

- (M1) Every pair ends at status 1. The root search takes 8 or 9 evaluations, against the cap 40.
  The endpoint check takes 104 or 105 over its two sides, so at most 53 on a side, against the cap
  54 per side. Total  112 to 114. The drafted reopening triggers compared the total 
  40 and the two-sided check count with 54, so they fired on every pair as written; neither cap was
  reached (a cap reached is status 7, and there is none).
- (M2) /c hat\rho 0.9959 to 1.0026, never below 	frac120
- (M3) Both groups are usable at pm\tfrac12 all six pairs, and some group is unusable at
  pm B all six. So the frontier bisection runs on every check, which is why the check count
  sits just under its cap and each pair costs about 113 pooled evaluations.
- (M4) 0\bar S|/\tau_S hat\rho at most 0.66, and the combining charge is at most 0.0006
  of 	au_S0

Six pairs from two datasets of one design do not establish these premises in general.

### Verification

Chunks `setup` (`Phi2`) and `cx-setup` (`cx_phi2`) must have run. Every name defined here
starts with `cxr_`. **What is verified is the pooling step alone, exactly.** R's $\Phi_2$
(`integrate`) is not Mata's `binormal()`, so the $\tilde s_x,\tilde\tau_x$ produced here are
realistic doubles, not Mata's bits, and the single-table $\tau_x$ is **not** re-verified. It is
taken as given, as (A2) states. For each case the double pooling is replayed operation for
operation, and $E$ is computed from the same doubles at 256 bits. All $N_x$ are below
$2^{53}$, so the only roundings in the reference are the final divisions at $2^{-256}$.

**Deciding criterion** (one, fixed before running): Result C1.2, $E\le\tilde\tau_S/(1-u)^4$,
on every case. **Diagnostics**, not criteria: the lemma ($d\le((1+u)^3-1)A$);
$E/\tilde\tau_S$, which is close to 1 by construction because $E$ contains the given worst
case $\sum w\tilde\tau$, so it tests only the rounding of that sum and $d$; $d$ over the
code's charge, the informative ratio; the charge's share of $\tilde\tau_S$; and two negative
controls, $\tau_S$ without the charge and with $uA$ in place of $6uA$, each of which must be
exceeded somewhere.

**The domain, enumerated before running.** *Fixtures:* every pair of `condx_A` and
`condx_D` (K = (3, 3, 2), $x$ the last column, N = 1500) at the items of
`condx_ref_{A,D}_s.csv`. The grid is 101 points uniform in Fisher $z$ over $[-0.999,0.999]$,
the walk's trial points $\pm(1-2^{-k})$, $k=1..9$, together with $\pm0.999$ and $0$, the
R root $r^*$, and $r^*\pm10^{-k}$, $k=1..12$. That gives 622 points usable in both groups.
*Stress:*

- (a) every fixture evaluation recombined with fourteen $(N_0,N_1)$: 1499:1, 1:1499,
  1000:500, 500:1000, 1:2, 2:1, 1:3, 3:1, 1:1, 7:11, $2^{40}$:3, $(2^{52}-1)$:1,
  $(10^9+7)$:$(10^9+9)$ and 3:$2^{50}$;
- (b) cancellation, $s_1\leftarrow-(N_0s_0/N_1)(1+k2^{-52})$ for $k=-2..2$, at the true
  $N$ and at 1499:1 and 1000:500;
- (c) four constructed tables at every grid point usable in both groups:
  - T1, tail bounds after the shift, a sparse group 0 and a group 1 of one observation;
  - T2, perfect association in group 0 only;
  - T3, 1499:1 with the one $x=1$ observation in a tail cell;
  - T4, weights $\tfrac13:\tfrac23$, with one cell empty in group 1 only;
- (d) 20,000 random draws, seed 20261111;
- (e) 5,000 draws with both group scores near 0 or exactly 0, the regime where the
  $(1-u)^{-4}$ matters.

```{r cxr-core}
# Depends on cx-setup (Phi2, cx_phi2). Every name defined here starts with cxr_.
stopifnot(requireNamespace("Rmpfr", quietly = TRUE))   # not attached: it masks pnorm, dnorm, outer
mpfr <- Rmpfr::mpfr; asNumeric <- Rmpfr::asNumeric
cxr_u   <- 2^-53                      # unit roundoff
cxr_eps  <- .Machine$double.eps        # 2^-52 = Mata's epsilon(1)
cxr_dPhi <- 9.3908313968469e-16        # @sec-rootfind's delta_Phi (chosen after measuring there)
cxr_dP   <- 4 * cxr_dPhi + 3 * cxr_eps
cxr_prec <- 256
cxr_corner <- function(A, B) A[-1, -1] - A[-nrow(A), -1] - A[-1, -ncol(A)] + A[-nrow(A), -ncol(A)]

# One table, in the arithmetic of dwlsmv_rf_evalp(): (x, ok, S/N, c, tau_S).
# Phi2 is R's (integrate), not Mata's binormal(): the values are realistic
# doubles, not Mata's bits. Only the pooling step is verified exactly.
cxr_rf_eval <- function(x, n, a, b) {
  A <- c(-Inf, a, Inf); B <- c(-Inf, b, Inf)
  C <- outer(seq_along(A), seq_along(B), Vectorize(function(r, s) Phi2(A[r], B[s], x)))
  P <- cxr_corner(C)
  O <- n > 0; Po <- ifelse(O, P, 1)
  if (anyNA(Po) || min(Po) <= cxr_dP) return(c(x = x, ok = 0, S = NA, c = NA, tau = NA))
  D <- cxr_corner(outer(A, B, Vectorize(function(p, q) cx_phi2(p, q, x))))
  w <- n / sum(n); u <- (D / Po) * O
  pos <- P > 0; Pp <- ifelse(pos, P, 1)
  W <- cxr_corner(outer(A, B, Vectorize(function(p, q) {
    if (!is.finite(p) || !is.finite(q)) return(0)
    z <- (p * p - 2 * x * p * q + q * q) / (2 * (1 - x * x))
    exp(-z) / (2 * pi * sqrt(1 - x * x)) * (z + 7) })))
  tau <- sum(w * (cxr_eps * W + abs(u) * cxr_dP) / Po) + (sum(O) + 2) * cxr_eps * sum(w * abs(u))
  c(x = x, ok = 1, S = sum(w * u), c = sum(((D * D) / Pp) * pos), tau = tau)
}

# The pooling of dwlsmv_cx_rf_eval(), operation for operation (vectorised over
# cases): N0 + N1, two divisions, two products, one sum; tau_S as the code writes it.
cxr_pool <- function(N0, N1, s0, s1, c0, c1, t0, t1) {
  M <- N0 + N1; w0 <- N0 / M; w1 <- N1 / M
  list(S = w0 * s0 + w1 * s1, c = w0 * c0 + w1 * c1,
       tau = w0 * t0 + w1 * t1 + 3 * cxr_eps * (w0 * abs(s0) + w1 * abs(s1)),
       comb = 3 * cxr_eps * (w0 * abs(s0) + w1 * abs(s1)))
}

# Exact side, 256 bits, from the same doubles. The exact s_x is anywhere in
# [s~_x - tau_x, s~_x + tau_x] (the single-table result, taken as given), so the
# worst error of the pooled value is E = |S~ - sum w s~| + sum w tau (linear in s,
# extreme at a vertex). Result C1: E <= tau~_S / (1 - u)^4. Lemma: d <= ((1+u)^3 - 1) A.
cxr_exact <- function(N0, N1, s0, s1, t0, t1, S, tau, comb) {
  p <- cxr_prec; n0 <- mpfr(N0, p); n1 <- mpfr(N1, p); M <- n0 + n1
  ms0 <- mpfr(s0, p); ms1 <- mpfr(s1, p)
  d  <- abs(mpfr(S, p) - (n0 * ms0 + n1 * ms1) / M)
  Tt <- (n0 * mpfr(t0, p) + n1 * mpfr(t1, p)) / M
  A  <- (n0 * abs(ms0) + n1 * abs(ms1)) / M
  E  <- d + Tt; mt <- mpfr(tau, p); u <- mpfr(2, p)^-53
  lemma <- ((1 + u)^3 - 1) * A
  data.frame(
    ok_C1    = as.logical(E <= mt / (1 - u)^4),            # deciding criterion
    ok_lemma = as.logical(d <= lemma),                    # diagnostic
    ratio    = asNumeric(E / mt),                          # observed / bound
    excess_u = asNumeric((E - mt) / (u * mt)),             # in units of u tau~_S (C1 allows <= ~4)
    r_lemma  = ifelse(asNumeric(A) == 0, 0, asNumeric(d / lemma)),
    r_d_code = ifelse(comb == 0, 0, asNumeric(d / mpfr(comb, p))),
    f_comb   = comb / tau,                                 # share of tau~_S that is the combining charge
    # negative controls: tau_S without the combining charge; with u A instead of 6u A
    ctl_none = as.logical(E > mpfr(tau - comb, p)),
    ctl_1u   = as.logical(E > mpfr(tau - comb, p) + u * A))
}
cxr_run <- function(N0, N1, e0, e1) {          # e0, e1: data frames of cxr_rf_eval rows
  q <- cxr_pool(N0, N1, e0$S, e1$S, e0$c, e1$c, e0$tau, e1$tau)
  cbind(N0 = N0, N1 = N1, s0 = e0$S, s1 = e1$S, t0 = e0$tau, t1 = e1$tau, S = q$S, tauS = q$tau,
        cxr_exact(N0, N1, e0$S, e1$S, e0$tau, e1$tau, q$S, q$tau, q$comb))
}
cxr_summ <- function(r, nm) {
  cat(sprintf("%-28s n = %6d | C1 fails %d | lemma fails %d | max ratio %.17g | max excess %.3f u*tauS | ratio > 1: %d | max d/lemma %.3f | max d/code-charge %.3f | comb share median %.3g max %.3g | ctl_none caught %d, ctl_1u caught %d\n",
      nm, nrow(r), sum(!r$ok_C1), sum(!r$ok_lemma), max(r$ratio), max(r$excess_u), sum(r$ratio > 1),
      max(r$r_lemma), max(r$r_d_code), median(r$f_comb), max(r$f_comb), sum(r$ctl_none), sum(r$ctl_1u)))
}
```

```{r cxr-data}
#| cache: true
# condx_A, condx_D (K = (3, 3, 2), x the last column, N = 1500), at the
# fitted items of condx_ref_{A,D}_s.csv (read as text, converted exactly).
cxr_K <- c(3L, 3L, 2L); cxr_prs <- t(combn(3, 2))
cxr_load <- function(t) {
  d  <- read.csv(file.path(root, "fixtures", "data", sprintf("condx_%s.csv", t)))
  sv <- read.csv(file.path(root, "fixtures", "expected", sprintf("condx_ref_%s_s.csv", t)),
                 colClasses = "character")
  v <- setNames(as.numeric(sv$value), sv$label)
  th <- lapply(1:3, function(j) c(v[sprintf("y%d|t%d", j, seq_len(cxr_K[j] - 1))], v[sprintf("y%d~x", j)]))
  list(d = d, th = lapply(th, unname), rho = unname(v[c("y1~~y2", "y1~~y3", "y2~~y3")]))
}
cxr_tab <- function(yi, yj, Ki, Kj) table(factor(yi, 0:(Ki - 1)), factor(yj, 0:(Kj - 1)))
# A pair's two tables and shifted bounds, as dwlsmv_cx_pair_fit() builds them.
cxr_pair <- function(L, i, j) {
  Ki <- cxr_K[i]; Kj <- cxr_K[j]; thi <- L$th[[i]]; thj <- L$th[[j]]
  ti <- thi[-Ki]; tj <- thj[-Kj]; x <- L$d$x
  list(n0 = unclass(cxr_tab(L$d[x == 0, i], L$d[x == 0, j], Ki, Kj)),
       n1 = unclass(cxr_tab(L$d[x == 1, i], L$d[x == 1, j], Ki, Kj)),
       a0 = ti, a1 = ti - thi[Ki], b0 = tj, b1 = tj - thj[Kj])
}
cxr_evalpair <- function(q, x) {
  e0 <- cxr_rf_eval(x, q$n0, q$a0, q$b0); e1 <- cxr_rf_eval(x, q$n1, q$a1, q$b1)
  list(e0 = e0, e1 = e1)
}
cxr_S <- function(q, x) {                       # pooled S/N in double, NA if unusable
  e <- cxr_evalpair(q, x)
  if (!e$e0[["ok"]] || !e$e1[["ok"]]) return(NA_real_)
  cxr_pool(sum(q$n0), sum(q$n1), e$e0[["S"]], e$e1[["S"]], 0, 0, 0, 0)$S
}
# The rho grid, fixed before running: 101 points uniform in Fisher z over
# [-0.999, 0.999], the walk's trial points 1 - 2^-k (k = 1..9) and +-0.999 on
# both sides, 0, and the R root r* with r* +- 10^-k, k = 1..12.
cxr_walk <- c(0, 1 - 2^-(1:9), 0.999); cxr_walk <- sort(unique(c(-cxr_walk, cxr_walk)))
cxr_grid0 <- sort(unique(c(tanh(seq(atanh(-0.999), atanh(0.999), length.out = 101)), cxr_walk)))
cxr_root <- function(q) {                       # the walk's trial points, then uniroot
  d <- sign(cxr_S(q, 0)); inner <- 0
  for (x in d * c(1 - 2^-(1:9), 0.999)) {
    s <- cxr_S(q, x)
    if (is.na(s)) stop("unusable trial point before a sign change")
    if (d * s < 0) return(uniroot(function(z) cxr_S(q, z), sort(c(inner, x)), tol = 1e-15)$root)
    inner <- x
  }
  stop("no sign change up to the bound")
}
cxr_front <- function(q, d) {                    # usable end on side d, bisected to 1e-7 (diagnostic)
  if (!is.na(cxr_S(q, d * 0.999))) return(d * 0.999)
  lo <- 0; hi <- 0.999
  while (hi - lo > 1e-7) { m <- (lo + hi) / 2; if (is.na(cxr_S(q, d * m))) hi <- m else lo <- m }
  d * lo
}
cxr_L <- list(A = cxr_load("A"), D = cxr_load("D"))
cxr_fix <- list(); cxr_diag <- list(); cxr_evals <- list()
for (t in names(cxr_L)) for (m in 1:3) {
  i <- cxr_prs[m, 1]; j <- cxr_prs[m, 2]; q <- cxr_pair(cxr_L[[t]], i, j)
  r <- cxr_root(q)
  g <- sort(unique(c(cxr_grid0, r, r + 10^-(1:12), r - 10^-(1:12))))
  g <- g[abs(g) <= 0.999]
  E <- lapply(g, function(x) cxr_evalpair(q, x))
  e0 <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, lapply(E, `[[`, "e0")))
  e1 <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, lapply(E, `[[`, "e1")))
  ok <- e0$ok == 1 & e1$ok == 1
  N0 <- sum(q$n0); N1 <- sum(q$n1)
  cxr_evals[[sprintf("%s %d-%d", t, i, j)]] <- list(e0 = e0[ok, ], e1 = e1[ok, ], N0 = N0, N1 = N1)
  res <- cxr_run(N0, N1, e0[ok, ], e1[ok, ])
  cxr_fix[[length(cxr_fix) + 1]] <- cbind(set = t, pair = sprintf("%d-%d", i, j), x = g[ok], res)
  # Diagnostics (R's Phi2): sign changes of the pooled S where |S| > tau_S, H/c
  # at r* by a central difference, each group's min pi at 0 and usability at +-1/2.
  P <- cxr_pool(N0, N1, e0$S, e1$S, e0$c, e1$c, e0$tau, e1$tau)
  sg <- sign(P$S)[ok & abs(P$S) > P$tau]
  h <- 1e-5; Hc <- -(cxr_S(q, r + h) - cxr_S(q, r - h)) / (2 * h) /
    cxr_pool(N0, N1, 0, 0, cxr_evalpair(q, r)$e0[["c"]], cxr_evalpair(q, r)$e1[["c"]], 0, 0)$c
  Hx <- sapply(c("0", "1"), function(xg) {          # each group's own H_x/c_x at the pooled root
    nn <- q[[paste0("n", xg)]]; aa <- q[[paste0("a", xg)]]; bb <- q[[paste0("b", xg)]]
    -(cxr_rf_eval(r + h, nn, aa, bb)[["S"]] - cxr_rf_eval(r - h, nn, aa, bb)[["S"]]) / (2 * h) /
      cxr_rf_eval(r, nn, aa, bb)[["c"]] })
  minpi <- sapply(c("0", "1"), function(xg) {
    aa <- q[[paste0("a", xg)]]; bb <- q[[paste0("b", xg)]]
    A <- c(-Inf, aa, Inf); B <- c(-Inf, bb, Inf)
    min(cxr_corner(outer(seq_along(A), seq_along(B), Vectorize(function(r, s) Phi2(A[r], B[s], 0))))) })
  cxr_diag[[length(cxr_diag) + 1]] <- data.frame(set = t, pair = sprintf("%d-%d", i, j), N0 = N0, N1 = N1,
    rho_R = r, rho_ref = cxr_L[[t]]$rho[m], gap = r - cxr_L[[t]]$rho[m],
    unusable_pts = sum(!ok), sign_changes = sum(diff(sg) != 0), Hc = Hc, H0c0 = Hx[1], H1c1 = Hx[2],
    s0_at_root = cxr_evalpair(q, r)$e0[["S"]], s1_at_root = cxr_evalpair(q, r)$e1[["S"]],
    minpi0 = minpi[1], minpi1 = minpi[2],
    usable_half = all(sapply(c(-0.5, 0.5), function(x) !is.na(cxr_S(q, x)))),
    usable_mB = !is.na(cxr_S(q, -0.999)), usable_pB = !is.na(cxr_S(q, 0.999)),
    frontier_m = cxr_front(q, -1), frontier_p = cxr_front(q, 1))
}
cxr_fix <- do.call(rbind, cxr_fix); cxr_diag <- do.call(rbind, cxr_diag)
```

```{r cxr-stress}
#| cache: true
# The stress set, enumerated before running.
# (a) splits: every usable fixture evaluation above, recombined with synthetic
#     (N0, N1); the composition takes (s~_x, tau_x, N_x) as independent inputs.
cxr_splits <- rbind(c(1499, 1), c(1, 1499), c(1000, 500), c(500, 1000), c(1, 2), c(2, 1),
                    c(1, 3), c(3, 1), c(1, 1), c(7, 11), c(2^40, 3), c(2^52 - 1, 1),
                    c(1e9 + 7, 1e9 + 9), c(3, 2^50))
cxr_all0 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cxr_evals, `[[`, "e0"))
cxr_all1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cxr_evals, `[[`, "e1"))
cxr_sa <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(cxr_splits)), function(k)
  cxr_run(cxr_splits[k, 1], cxr_splits[k, 2], cxr_all0, cxr_all1)))
# (b) cancellation: s1 replaced by -(N0 s0 / N1)(1 + k 2^-52), k = -2..2, so that
#     the pooled sum cancels to a few ulps; at the true N and at 1499:1 and 1000:500.
cxr_sb <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list(c(NA, NA), c(1499, 1), c(1000, 500)), function(sp) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(cxr_evals), function(nm) {
    ev <- cxr_evals[[nm]]; N0 <- if (is.na(sp[1])) ev$N0 else sp[1]; N1 <- if (is.na(sp[2])) ev$N1 else sp[2]
    do.call(rbind, lapply(-2:2, function(k) {
      e1 <- ev$e1; e1$S <- -(N0 * ev$e0$S / N1) * (1 + k * 2^-52)
      cxr_run(N0, N1, ev$e0, e1) }))
  }))
}))
# (c) constructed tail and sparse tables, every grid point where both groups are usable:
#     T1 3x3, bounds far in the tails after the shift (b_i = 2, b_j = -1.8), group 0
#        sparse with empty cells, group 1 a single observation (N0:N1 = 1251:1);
#     T2 2x2, perfect association in group 0 only (empty off-diagonal), group 1 full;
#     T3 3x2, N0:N1 = 1499:1, the one x = 1 observation in a tail cell;
#     T4 3x3, weights 1/3 : 2/3 (N0 = 500, N1 = 1000), one empty cell in group 1 only.
cxr_T <- list(
  T1 = list(n0 = matrix(c(3, 0, 0, 10, 1200, 9, 0, 28, 1), 3, byrow = TRUE),
            n1 = matrix(c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0), 3, byrow = TRUE),
            thi = c(-2.4, 2.3, 2.0), thj = c(-2.2, 2.45, -1.8)),
  T2 = list(n0 = matrix(c(300, 0, 0, 400), 2, byrow = TRUE),
            n1 = matrix(c(200, 20, 30, 250), 2, byrow = TRUE),
            thi = c(0.1, 0.5), thj = c(-0.2, 0.3)),
  T3 = list(n0 = matrix(c(400, 100, 300, 300, 50, 349), 3, byrow = TRUE),
            n1 = matrix(c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1), 3, byrow = TRUE),
            thi = c(-0.3, 1.1, 1.2), thj = c(0.2, -0.9)),
  T4 = list(n0 = matrix(c(60, 40, 20, 50, 120, 60, 10, 40, 100), 3, byrow = TRUE),
            n1 = matrix(c(150, 80, 0, 90, 260, 120, 20, 90, 190), 3, byrow = TRUE),
            thi = c(-0.6, 0.5, 0.4), thj = c(-0.3, 0.8, -0.2)))
cxr_sc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(cxr_T), function(nm) {
  T <- cxr_T[[nm]]; Ki <- length(T$thi); Kj <- length(T$thj)
  q <- list(n0 = T$n0, n1 = T$n1, a0 = T$thi[-Ki], a1 = T$thi[-Ki] - T$thi[Ki],
            b0 = T$thj[-Kj], b1 = T$thj[-Kj] - T$thj[Kj])
  E <- lapply(cxr_grid0, function(x) cxr_evalpair(q, x))
  e0 <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, lapply(E, `[[`, "e0")))
  e1 <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, lapply(E, `[[`, "e1")))
  ok <- e0$ok == 1 & e1$ok == 1
  cat(sprintf("stress %s: %d of %d grid points usable in both groups (group 0 only %d, group 1 only %d)\n",
              nm, sum(ok), length(ok), sum(e0$ok == 1 & e1$ok == 0), sum(e0$ok == 0 & e1$ok == 1)))
  cbind(tab = nm, cxr_run(sum(T$n0), sum(T$n1), e0[ok, ], e1[ok, ]))
}))
# (d) random, seed fixed in advance: 20000 draws; N_x log-uniform integers in
#     [1, 2^40]; s_x = +-10^U(-12, 3); tau_x = |s_x| 10^U(-17, -10) + 10^U(-18, -12).
set.seed(20261111)
cxr_nr <- 20000
cxr_rN <- function() pmax(1, floor(2^runif(cxr_nr, 0, 40)))
cxr_rs <- function() sample(c(-1, 1), cxr_nr, TRUE) * 10^runif(cxr_nr, -12, 3)
cxr_N0 <- cxr_rN(); cxr_N1 <- cxr_rN(); cxr_s0 <- cxr_rs(); cxr_s1 <- cxr_rs()
cxr_t0 <- abs(cxr_s0) * 10^runif(cxr_nr, -17, -10) + 10^runif(cxr_nr, -18, -12)
cxr_t1 <- abs(cxr_s1) * 10^runif(cxr_nr, -17, -10) + 10^runif(cxr_nr, -18, -12)
cxr_sd <- cxr_run(cxr_N0, cxr_N1, data.frame(S = cxr_s0, c = 1, tau = cxr_t0),
                  data.frame(S = cxr_s1, c = 1, tau = cxr_t1))
# (e) both groups at a root at once (A << sum w tau, where the combining charge
#     cannot absorb the rounding of sum w tau): 5000 draws, same seed stream;
#     s_x = +-10^U(-30, -14), or exactly 0 in every tenth draw; tau_x = 10^U(-16, -12).
cxr_ne <- 5000
cxr_eN0 <- pmax(1, floor(2^runif(cxr_ne, 0, 40))); cxr_eN1 <- pmax(1, floor(2^runif(cxr_ne, 0, 40)))
cxr_es0 <- sample(c(-1, 1), cxr_ne, TRUE) * 10^runif(cxr_ne, -30, -14)
cxr_es1 <- sample(c(-1, 1), cxr_ne, TRUE) * 10^runif(cxr_ne, -30, -14)
cxr_es0[seq(1, cxr_ne, 10)] <- 0; cxr_es1[seq(1, cxr_ne, 10)] <- 0
cxr_se <- cxr_run(cxr_eN0, cxr_eN1, data.frame(S = cxr_es0, c = 1, tau = 10^runif(cxr_ne, -16, -12)),
                  data.frame(S = cxr_es1, c = 1, tau = 10^runif(cxr_ne, -16, -12)))
```

cxr_summ(cxr_fix[abs(cxr_fix$S) <= cxr_fix$tauS, ], "fixtures, |S| <= tau_S")
cxr_summ(cxr_sa, "(a) synthetic splits")
for (k in seq_len(nrow(cxr_splits))) {

}

for (nm in names(cxr_T)) cxr_summ(cxr_sc[cxr_sc$tab == nm, ], sprintf("(c) %s", nm))

cxr_summ(cxr_se, "(e) both groups near 0")
cxr_allr <- rbind(cxr_fix[, names(cxr_sd)], cxr_sa, cxr_sb, cxr_sc[, names(cxr_sd)], cxr_sd, cxr_se)
cxr_summ(cxr_allr, "ALL")
cat(sprintf("\nlargest ratio overall %.17g at (N0, N1, s0, s1, t0, t1) = (%s)\n", max(cxr_allr$ratio),
            paste(format(unlist(cxr_allr[which.max(cxr_allr$ratio), c("N0", "N1", "s0", "s1", "t0", "t1")]),

cxr_atr <- merge(cxr_fix, cxr_diag[, c("set", "pair", "rho_R")], by = c("set", "pair"))
cxr_atr <- cxr_atr[cxr_atr$x == cxr_atr$rho_R, ]
cat(sprintf("fixture evaluations: tau_S range [%.3g, %.3g]\n", min(cxr_fix$tauS), max(cxr_fix$tauS)))
cat("at the R root: set pair tau_S |S|/tau_S comb share ratio\n")
print(data.frame(cxr_atr[, c("set", "pair", "tauS")], absS_over_tau = abs(cxr_atr$S) / cxr_atr$tauS,
                 comb = cxr_atr$f_comb, ratio = cxr_atr$ratio), digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
