```{r cxr-assert}
# Deciding criterion (fixed before running): Result C1 on every case.
stopifnot(all(cxr_allr$ok_C1))
# Diagnostics, not criteria: the lemma; the controls must be caught somewhere.
stopifnot(all(cxr_allr$ok_lemma), any(cxr_allr$ctl_none), any(cxr_allr$ctl_1u))
cat("\ncxr-assert: Result C1 holds on all", nrow(cxr_allr), "cases\n")
```

**Results** (standalone run, `verify.log`):

- **C1.2 holds on all 43,976 cases**, and the lemma holds on all of them.
- **The combining error against the code's charge:** at most 0.409 (and at most 0.818 of
  the lemma's $3u$-level bound). On the fixtures it is at most 0.323, and under
  cancellation at most 0.185.
- **$E/\tilde\tau_S$:** at most $1-7.8\times10^{-16}$ on every case except set (e). There,
  335 of 5,000 cases exceed 1, by at most $1.97\,u\,\tilde\tau_S$, which C1.2 allows (up to
  about $4u\,\tilde\tau_S$). The largest is $1+2.2\times10^{-16}$, at
  $\tilde s_0=\tilde s_1=0$.
- **The charge's share of $\tilde\tau_S$:** median $4\times10^{-4}$; at most 0.0098 on the
  fixtures and splits, 0.019 under cancellation, 0.027 on T2. It reaches 0.985 only in
  random draws with $\tilde\tau_x/|\tilde s_x|$ far below what a real table allows.
- **The controls are caught:** $\tau_S$ without the charge on 40,523 cases, with $uA$ on
  6,390.
- **At the six R roots,** $|\tilde{\bar S}|/\tilde\tau_S\le0.0089$, and the R roots match
  the reference $\hat\rho$ to $6.7\times10^{-16}$.

**Tolerances.** C1.2's factor $(1-u)^{-4}$ is derived, not chosen. The grid, the splits,
the stress tables and the seeds were fixed before running. Set (e) and the frontier and
$\pm B$ diagnostics were **added after the first run**, which showed that no earlier case
had $A\lesssim T$ and that $\pm B$ was unusable. Nothing was loosened. The R walk in
`cxr_root` replaced a first `uniroot` on $[0,0.999]$ that failed because 0.999 is unusable.

**What this does not certify.** It does not certify the single-table $\tau_x$ under Mata's
`binormal()`, which is inherited. It does not certify Mata's bits, nor Mata's operation
order beyond the code as read (FMA can only help, by A3). It does not certify the premises
of C3 in production, which are measurements (M1)–(M4), made in Stata on six pairs only, or uniqueness of the
pooled root.

## Conditional mode: the root search's evaluation budget {#sec-condx-rootcap}

*Drafted 2026-11-12 by a read-only agent; corrected 2026-11-13 by a second agent against a source audit
(E-096); the main session read the corrections on the walk
(Result 1) against the source and not the rest line by line. The chunks are the bodies of
a verification script of E-096, which the main session ran standalone (16,366 checks, 0
failures) before this section was rendered in the full document on 2026-11-13.
Every double-precision figure is R doubles, not Mata. The nine pairs go through an R port of the loop with an own
bivariate-normal integrator; the production counts quoted for them are from the Stata 18 trace
`docs/notes/condx-stage1/cap-screen/mech/trace_cap1000.log`, not re-run.*

Nine constructed pairs reach status 7 in conditional mode although a root exists
(E-096): `dwlsmv_cx_pair_fit()` passed `cap = 40` to
`dwlsmv_rootfind()` (`src/mata/dwls_polychoric.mata`, lines 294-397; the call is in
`src/mata/dwlsmv_cx_pair_fit.mata`, with the literals `0.999, 40, 54` until 2026-11-13 and `0.999, 200, 54` since), and the root search of those pairs
needs 42 to 88 evaluations. The user's decision of 2026-11-12 is a larger root-search budget **for conditional mode
only**: the argument the pair fit passes, with the shared root-finder and v1 unchanged, and the number derived rather than
picked. This section derives what the loop's own structure bounds (Results 1 and 2), what needs premises about the score
(Result 3), and the bound that follows (Result 4). What it delivers is a bound **conditional** on premises, several of
them measured on nine pairs and some unmeasured; the budget the owner decided on 2026-11-13, 200, is a margin chosen after
measuring over that conditional bound (Result 4). It changes no estimator; the one code change that accompanies it is that argument, 40 to 200.

**Notation.** An evaluation is $e=(\rho,\text{usable},S,c,\tau_S)$ (`dwlsmv_rf_evalp`, lines 89-132); $c$ is the expected
information, $\tau_S$ the score's first-order evaluation error. $L,R$ are the bracket ends with $S(L)>0\ge S(R)$ and
$w=R-L$. $x$ is the end with the smaller $|S|$ (ties to $R$), $\sigma(x)=\tau_S(x)/c(x)$ is the evaluation error in
$\rho$ units of one Fisher step, and $\ell=|S(x)|/c(x)$ the length of the Fisher step. By line 137,
$\tau_\rho(x)=16\sigma(x)+8\,\mathrm{ulp}(x)$, where $\mathrm{ulp}$ (lines 56-66) is the spacing of doubles, so for
every $x$
$$\tau_\rho(x)>16\,\sigma(x),\qquad \tau_\rho(x)\ge 8\,\mathrm{ulp}(x)>2^{-50}|x|,\qquad \tau_\rho(x)\ge2^{-50}\ \text{for }|x|\in[\tfrac12,1).\tag{0}$$
$k$ counts evaluations from the first, at $\rho=0$; `cap` is compared with this $k$, so the walk's evaluations are
spent from the same budget (the walk itself has no cap). $B=0.999$. $S$ always means the computed score $\tilde S$; nothing is assumed about it except
what is stated.

**The loop as coded** (lines 359-396). Start: $x$ as above, $dxold=R-L$ (359-360). Each pass:
(1) $\tau_\rho$ at $x$; **stop** if $|S(x)|\le\tau_S(x)$ and $w\le\tau_\rho(x)$ (362-366). (2) Only if the stop did not
fire, and if $k\ge$ `cap`: status 7 (367). **The stopping test precedes the cap test**, so a pass that begins with
$k=$ `cap` still stops if the stop condition holds; this is why a cap equal to a bound on the evaluations made before the
stopping pass suffices (Result 4). The endpoint check that follows a stop (line 364, `dwlsmv_rf_check`) has its own cap
54 per side and is not budgeted here; its evaluations are added to $k$ only after its status is decided (line 282), so
the returned count (line 365) can exceed `cap`, and the cap never limits it. (3) **Branch P**, if
$|S(x)|\le\tau_S(x)$ (370-374): probe the far side, $x_n=x\pm\tau_\rho/2$ towards the other end, the midpoint if that is not
in $(L,R)$. (4) Otherwise the **Fisher step** $stp=S(x)/c(x)$, $x_n=x+stp$ (376-377); if $x_n\notin(L,R)$ or
$|stp|>|dxold|/2$ replace it by the midpoint and $stp$ by $(R-L)/2$ (378-381, **branch B**); otherwise keep it
(**branch F**); in both, $dxold\leftarrow stp$ (382). (5) Evaluate $x_n$, $k\leftarrow k+1$, status 8 if unusable (384-388);
the new point replaces $L$ if $S>0$, else $R$ (389-394); recompute $x$ (395). $dxold$ is **not** changed by P.

```{r cx-rootcap-setup}
# Everything below is base R. Names are rc_ / RC_ prefixed: the full document shares one session.
cat("cx-rootcap  R", as.character(getRversion()), "\n")
print(sessionInfo())
set.seed(20261112)
RC_B <- 0.999                      # the bound B passed by dwlsmv_cx_pair_fit
RC_DP <- 4 * 9.3908313968469e-16 + 3 * 2^-52     # delta_P, dwlsmv_rf_dP (line 72)
rc_nfail <- 0L; rc_ncheck <- 0L
rc_check <- function(ok, msg) {
  rc_ncheck <<- rc_ncheck + 1L
  if (!isTRUE(ok)) { rc_nfail <<- rc_nfail + 1L; cat("FAIL:", msg, "\n") }
  invisible(isTRUE(ok))
}
# dwlsmv_rf_ulp (lines 56-66): the spacing of doubles at x
rc_ulp <- function(x) {
  ax <- max(abs(x), 2^-1022); e <- floor(log2(ax))
  if (2^e > ax) e <- e - 1
  if (2^(e + 1) <= ax) e <- e + 1
  2^(e - 52)
}
# an evaluation is c(x, usable, S, c, tau_S), the shape of dwlsmv_rf_evalp's return
rc_taur <- function(e) 16 * e[5] / e[4] + 8 * rc_ulp(e[1])          # dwlsmv_rf_taur (line 137)

# The walk, lines 144-191 (dwlsmv_rf_side) with the evaluation at 0 of lines 303-346. The exact-zero
# start (e0[3] == 0, lines 311-330) is not ported.
rc_walk <- function(fe, B = RC_B) {
  e0 <- fe(0); k <- 1L
  if (e0[2] != 1) return(list(st = "abort", k = k))
  if (e0[3] == 0) return(list(st = "exact0", k = k))
  d <- sign(e0[3]); ein <- e0; eout <- NULL
  repeat {
    cand <- d * min(B, 1 - (1 - d * ein[1]) / 2)
    if (cand == ein[1]) return(list(st = 2L, k = k, ein = ein))
    e <- fe(cand); k <- k + 1L
    if (e[2] == 1 && d * e[3] < 0) { eout <- e; break }
    if (e[2] == 1) { ein <- e; next }
    if (cand != d * B) { eB <- fe(d * B); k <- k + 1L; if (eB[2] == 1) return(list(st = 4L, k = k, ein = ein)) }
    out <- cand
    while (abs(out - ein[1]) > 4 * rc_ulp(out)) {
      m <- (ein[1] + out) / 2; e <- fe(m); k <- k + 1L
      if (e[2] != 1) { out <- m; next }
      if (d * e[3] < 0) { eout <- e; break }
      ein <- e
    }
    if (!is.null(eout)) break
    return(list(st = 3L, k = k, ein = ein))
  }
  if (d > 0) list(st = 0L, k = k, L = ein, R = eout) else list(st = 0L, k = k, L = eout, R = ein)
}

# The loop, lines 359-396. br records the branch of each pass: "F" accepted Fisher step, "B" the
# bisection that replaces a rejected Fisher step, "P" the far-side probe. ell is |stp| of each F.
rc_loop <- function(fe, L, R, k0, cap) {
  k <- k0; x <- if (abs(L[3]) < abs(R[3])) L else R
  w0 <- R[1] - L[1]; dxold <- w0; br <- character(0); ell <- numeric(0); pts <- numeric(0)
  fin <- function(st) list(status = st, k = k, k0 = k0, w0 = w0, br = br, ell = ell, pts = pts, L = L, R = R, x = x)
  repeat {
    tr <- rc_taur(x)
    if (abs(x[3]) <= x[5] && R[1] - L[1] <= tr) return(fin("stop"))
    if (k >= cap) return(fin("cap"))
    if (abs(x[3]) <= x[5]) {
      xn <- if (identical(x, L)) x[1] + tr / 2 else x[1] - tr / 2
      if (!(xn > L[1] && xn < R[1])) xn <- (L[1] + R[1]) / 2
      br <- c(br, "P")
    } else {
      stp <- x[3] / x[4]; xn <- x[1] + stp
      if (!(xn > L[1] && xn < R[1]) || abs(stp) > abs(dxold) / 2) {
        xn <- (L[1] + R[1]) / 2; stp <- (R[1] - L[1]) / 2; br <- c(br, "B")
      } else { br <- c(br, "F"); ell <- c(ell, abs(stp)) }
      dxold <- stp
    }
    e <- fe(xn); k <- k + 1L; pts <- c(pts, xn)
    if (e[2] != 1) return(fin("unusable"))
    if (e[3] > 0) L <- e else R <- e
    x <- if (abs(L[3]) < abs(R[3])) L else R
  }
}
rc_search <- function(fe, cap) {
  w <- rc_walk(fe)
  if (w$st != 0L) return(list(status = paste0("walk", w$st), k = w$k))
  rc_loop(fe, w$L, w$R, w$k, cap)
}

# The bound of Result 3 (derived below). w0: the walk's bracket width; hmin: smallest local slope/c;
# rconv = sigma / h_max at the roots' neighbourhood (the width at which |S| <= tau_S is guaranteed);
# smin: smallest sigma = tau_S / c at a Fisher step; kap: the Fisher steps' growth factor between runs;
# sloc: sigma_max / sigma_min within the reach of a far-side probe; k0: the walk's evaluations (<= 11).
rc_bound <- function(w0, hmin, rconv, smin, kap = 1, k0 = 11, sloc = 1) {
  MB <- if (w0 <= rconv) 0 else ceiling(log2(w0 / rconv)) + 1
  nF <- ceiling((MB + 1) * (1 + max(0, log2(kap))) + max(0, floor(log2(w0 / (2 * smin)))) + 1)
  nP <- floor(sloc / (8 * hmin)) + 1
  list(k0 = k0, B = MB, F = nF, P = nP, loop = MB + nF + nP, total = k0 + MB + nF + nP)
}
```

### Result 1: the walk

**Statement.** Let $S(0)\ne0$ (the exact-zero start, lines 311-330, is outside this section) and $d=\operatorname{sign}S(0)$.
The walk's trial points on side $d$ are $x_j=d(1-2^{-j})$ for $j=1,\dots,9$ ($0.5,\,0.75,\dots,0.998046875$) and, as
the tenth, $dB$.

The walk's test for a sign change is `d*e[3] < 0` (line 160): a trial whose computed score is exactly $0$, or has the
sign of $S(0)$, counts as the **same side**, and the walk goes on from it. "Sign change" below means a strictly
opposite sign. (A root exactly at a trial point, with a computed score of exactly zero there, therefore costs the
next trial as well. This case is stated, not tested: `cx-rootcap-walk` uses roots at $x_j\pm10^{-10}$.)

(a) If the first strictly opposite sign is between $x_{j-1}$ and $x_j$ ($x_0=0$, $x_{10}:=dB$) and every trial is usable, the walk
uses $j\le10$ trials, so the loop starts at $k_0=1+j\le11$ with $w_0=2^{-j}\le\min(\tfrac12,1-|r|)$ for $j\le9$ and
$w_0=B-x_9=0.000953125$ for $j=10$. $11$ is the maximum for a root anywhere in $(-B,B)$.

(b) If there is no sign change up to $dB$, line 154 gives $cand=dB=$ `ein[1]` after the tenth trial, and lines 155-157 return
status 2 at $k=11$: the loop never runs.

(c) If a trial is unusable (lines 164-190), the walk spends one evaluation at $dB$ (unless the trial was $dB$) and, if
that is unusable too, runs the frontier bisection between the inner point `ein` and the unusable `out`. Each pass of the
loop at line 176 is one evaluation and halves $[ein,out]$ (either `out` or `ein` becomes the midpoint); the loop runs
while $|out-ein|>4\,\mathrm{ulp}(out)$. It returns a bracket only at the first usable point with a strictly opposite
sign, of width at most the interval's width after $b$ halvings. **The count of passes is bounded only in the case
below, and the draft's earlier claim that `out` $\ge\frac12$ always (hence at most 50 passes) is not true of the code**:
`out` moves to the midpoint whenever the midpoint is unusable, and can fall below $\frac12$, where the spacing of
doubles is smaller.

- *The unusable trial is the second or a later one* ($j\ge2$). Then $|ein|\ge\frac12$, and `out` lies beyond `ein` on
  side $d$, so $|out|\in[\frac12,1)$ throughout and $\mathrm{ulp}(out)=2^{-53}$. The interval starts at width $2^{-j}\le\frac14$
  and halves each pass, so the passes number at most $\lceil\log_2(2^{-j}/(4\cdot2^{-53}))\rceil\le49$. Derived from the code.
- *The first trial ($0.5$) is unusable.* Then `ein` is the evaluation at $0$ (or at $\pm\tau_\rho(0)/2$ after an exact-zero
  start), and `out` can fall to any size. If every midpoint is unusable, `ein` stays and $|out-ein|=|out|$ never reaches
  $4\,\mathrm{ulp}(out)\approx2^{-50}|out|$ until `out` is near the floor $2^{-1022}$ of the spacing function: about $1{,}070$
  passes. **This is not bounded by the argument.** What limits it in the code is only the loop condition at line 176 (the
  walk has no counter and no cap); what makes it unreachable in practice is that $\rho=0$ is usable (an unusable $\rho=0$
  aborts, lines 306-310) and the cell probabilities are continuous, so a midpoint near $0$ is usable. That is a property
  of the likelihood, not checked by the code, and not measured here.

In both cases the walk's evaluations enter the loop's count as $k_0$ and $k_0\le11$ no longer holds.

**Proof.** With $a=|ein[1]|$, line 154 gives $|cand|=\min\{B,\ 1-(1-a)/2\}$: the distance to 1 halves, $1-a_j=2^{-j}$,
until the cap $B$ binds; $1-2^{-10}=0.99902>B$ makes the tenth trial $dB$. Line 160 returns the first trial with
`d*e[3] < 0`, that is a strictly opposite sign; a computed score of exactly zero is the same side, so `ein` moves to that
trial and the walk continues (lines 164-166). Such a trial exists for a root with $|r|<B$ by trial 10 when the score
changes sign across it; the bracket is the last two trials. (b) is lines 154-157
read at $a=B$. $\blacksquare$

**Dominance of the clean walk (argued, not proved, not tested).** Result 3's bound grows by 3 evaluations per bit of $w_0$
(one in $M_B$, two in $N_F$) while $w_0>r_c$, and each frontier bisection costs one evaluation and removes one bit. So,
**for the case $j\ge2$ of (c)** (at most 49 passes, leaving a width not below about $2^{-51}$, the size of $r_c$), the bound at
$(k_0+1+b,\ 2^{-b}w_0)$ is at most the bound at $(k_0,w_0)$, and (c) never raises the worst case, except by the single
evaluation at $dB$. This is an argument about the formula, not a proof about the code. **Not covered:** (i) the case where
the first trial is unusable, whose pass count is not bounded by the argument (above); (ii) a root so close to $\pm B$ that its
bracket is the frontier's; the code returns status 3 or 4 or a bracket, none of which enters the loop's count as shown.

**Measured** (`cx-rootcap-walk`): synthetic $S=-(\rho-r)$ for 462 roots of both signs, among them roots within $10^{-10}$
of every $x_j$ and up to $0.9989999$: the count is $1+j$ exactly, at most 11; the bracket width is at most $\frac12$ and
at most $1-|r|$; roots at or beyond $B$ end at status 2 after 11 evaluations.

```{r cx-rootcap-walk}
cat("\n[cx-rootcap-walk] evaluations of the walk, synthetic S(rho) = -(rho - r), every point usable\n")
local({
rc_walk_fe <- function(r) function(x) c(x, 1, -(x - r), 1, 1e-15)
rc_pts <- 1 - 2^-(1:9)                               # 0.5, 0.75, ..., 0.998046875
rc_roots <- sort(unique(c(
  0.3, 1e-9, 0.49999, 0.5 + 1e-9, 0.75 + 1e-9, 0.9 + 1e-3, 0.99, 0.996, 0.9979, 0.99805, 0.9985, 0.99899, 0.9989999,
  rc_pts + 1e-10, rc_pts - 1e-10, runif(200, -0.9989999, 0.9989999))))
rc_roots <- rc_roots[abs(rc_roots) < RC_B]
rc_kmax <- 0L; rc_wmax <- 0
for (r in c(rc_roots, -rc_roots)) {
  w <- rc_walk(rc_walk_fe(r))
  rc_check(w$st == 0L, sprintf("walk found no bracket for r=%.10g", r))
  j <- min(which(c(rc_pts, RC_B) > abs(r)))          # the first trial point beyond |r|
  w0 <- w$R[1] - w$L[1]
  rc_check(w$k == 1L + j, sprintf("walk count %d != 1 + %d (r=%.10g)", w$k, j, r))
  rc_check(w$k <= 11L, "walk count above 11")
  rc_check(w0 <= 0.5 && w0 <= 1 - abs(r) + 1e-15, sprintf("bracket width %.3g above min(1/2, 1-|r|)", w0))
  rc_check(w$L[3] > 0 && w$R[3] < 0 && w$L[1] < w$R[1], "bracket not maximum-oriented")
  rc_kmax <- max(rc_kmax, w$k); rc_wmax <- max(rc_wmax, w0)
}
cat(sprintf("  %d roots (both signs): max walk evaluations %d (= 1 at rho = 0 + 10), max bracket width %.6g\n",
            2 * length(rc_roots), rc_kmax, rc_wmax))
for (r in c(0.9995, -0.9995, 0.999, 1.5, -3)) {                    # beyond B: no bracket
  w <- rc_walk(rc_walk_fe(r))
  rc_check(w$st == 2L && w$k == 11L, sprintf("beyond B: status %s k %d for r=%g", w$st, w$k, r))
}
cat("  roots at or beyond B: status 2 after 1 + 10 evaluations, as lines 155-157 give\n")
})
```

### Result 2: what the loop's structure alone guarantees

No property of $S$ is used here beyond the sign update (389-394), and $c>0$ and finite at every usable evaluation (it is
$\sum D^2/P$ over cells with $P>0$; $c=0$ would make line 376 non-finite).

(a) **Orientation.** $S(L)>0\ge S(R)$ and $L<R$ after every pass; every evaluated point lies in $(L,R)$ (line 373 for P,
lines 378-380 for F and B), except when $L,R$ are adjacent doubles and the midpoint is an end.

(b) **The width never grows.** The new bracket is $[L,x_n]$ or $[x_n,R]$ with $x_n$ inside: $w'<w$.

(c) **A bisection halves it**, up to the rounding of the midpoint: for $|L+R|<2$ the sum rounds by at most $2^{-53}$, so
$|m-(L+R)/2|\le2^{-54}$ and $w'\le w/2+2^{-54}$. After $m$ bisections (and any other passes, which only shrink $w$),
$w\le w_0/2^m+2^{-53}$.

(d) **$dxold\le w$ after every pass that is not a probe** (up to the rounding in (c)). Initially $dxold=w$. After B,
$dxold=(R-L)/2$ is the new width. After F, $dxold=|stp|\le dxold_{old}/2\le w_{old}/2$; if the new point has the sign of
$x$'s end, $w'=w-|stp|\ge w/2\ge|stp|$; if it crosses, $w'=|stp|$. In both $dxold\le w'$.

(e) **Accepted Fisher steps halve.** F is taken only if $|stp|\le dxold/2$ and then $dxold\leftarrow|stp|$. So in a run of
consecutive accepted steps with lengths $\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots$ (each $\ell_j=|S(x_j)|/c(x_j)$ at the point it was taken from)
$$\ell_1\le\tfrac w2,\qquad \ell_{j+1}\le\tfrac12\ell_j,\qquad\text{so}\qquad \textstyle\sum_j\ell_j<w .$$
The run moves one end by less than $w$: the far end never moves. This is the one-sided regime of case 6 (35 accepted Fisher
steps in the port, 34 in the README, bracket width unchanged until the last pass).

(f) **F needs $\ell>\sigma$.** Branch F is taken only if $|S(x)|>\tau_S(x)$, that is $\ell>\sigma(x)$; the stop needs
$|S(x)|\le\tau_S(x)$. With (e), a run of $m$ accepted steps satisfies $\sigma_{\min}<\ell_m\le w/2^m$, so
$m<\log_2(w/\sigma_{\min})$ if $\sigma(x)\ge\sigma_{\min}$ at its points. **This is bounded by the structure plus a floor
on $\sigma$.**

(g) **The far-side probe.** Suppose $|S(x)|\le\tau_S(x)$ and $w>\tau_\rho(x)$ (otherwise the stop fires). Then
$x_n=x\pm\tau_\rho/2$ is inside $(L,R)$: no midpoint fallback. Take $x=L$. If $S(x_n)\le0$, $R'=x_n$ and
$w'=\tau_\rho(L)/2$ **in one evaluation**; if $S(x_n)>0$, $L'=x_n$ and $w$ falls by $\tau_\rho/2$ (a *creep*). The
symmetric statements hold for $x=R$.

**What (a)-(g) do not give: termination.** A creep sequence can in principle run for $w/(\tau_\rho/2)$ passes, and $|S|$ may
never come within $\tau_S$ (if $\sigma/h$ is below the spacing of doubles the bracket becomes two adjacent doubles with
$|S|>\tau_S$, the midpoint is an end, and the loop repeats one evaluation until the cap;
`cx-rootcap-linear`, last block). In the one-sided regime the code therefore does **not** guarantee termination by
itself: if every Fisher step is accepted and lands on the same side, $R-L$ never shrinks, and the stop can fire only
through P, after $|S(x)|\le\tau_S$ has been reached. What the structure gives there is (f): at most
$\log_2(w/\sigma_{\min})$ such steps before a rejection (which is a bisection) or $|S|\le\tau_S$; what remains is Result 3.

### Result 3: the evaluation count of the loop

**Premises** (about the computed score; each is a **premise** here, not derived, and none is checked by the code; (M),
($\sigma$) and ($\kappa$) are **measured premises** on the nine pairs, (U) and (T) are **unmeasured**):

- **(U)** *Every evaluated point is usable*, in the walk and in the loop (and in the frontier bisection's case $j\ge2$
  or its absence). An unusable point in the loop returns status 8 at once (lines 386-388), whatever the stop test would
  have said; an unusable $\rho=0$ aborts (lines 306-310). The bound below says **nothing** about status 8, about the
  abort, or about a walk with an unusable trial (Result 1(c)); it counts evaluations to the stopping test only on runs
  where all points are usable. Whether a pair meets (U) is not guaranteed by the code, and the pair fit does not check it
  beyond $\rho=0$ (`dwlsmv_cx_pair_fit.mata`, the `dwlsmv_rf_usable(0, ...)` test before the call).
- **(M)** *Locally monotone, with slope bounds.* There is an interval $N$ around the root the loop converges to, of
  half-width $w_M\ge\max(r_c,\ s\sigma_{\max}/h_{\min})$, such that for evaluated $y_1<y_2$ in $N$ and every evaluated $x$,
  $h_{\min}c(x)(y_2-y_1)\le S(y_1)-S(y_2)\le h_{\max}c(x)(y_2-y_1)$. (Only $N$: in cases 3 and 4 below $S$ has an interior
  minimum far from the root, and (M) fails over the walk's bracket; the passes outside $N$ use only Result 2, ($\sigma$)
  and ($\kappa$).)
- **($\sigma$)** $\sigma(x)\ge\sigma_{\min}$ at every Fisher step, and $r_c:=\min_x\sigma(x)/h_{\max}\ge2^{-51}$ over the
  loop's evaluations. ($r_c$ is the width at which both ends are surely within $\tau_S$ of zero; the bound $2^{-51}$ is four
  times the rounding floor $2^{-53}$ of (c), so that the rounding costs one bisection. The constants $2^{-51}$ and
  $\sigma_{\min}$ used in Result 4 are **chosen after measuring** the nine pairs; the nine pairs' values are **measured**.)
- **($\kappa$)** The accepted Fisher steps satisfy $\ell_{i+1}\le\kappa\,\ell_i$ between runs. Where $S$ is monotone,
  $|S(x)|=\min(S(L),-S(R))$ is non-increasing, so $\kappa\le\sup c(x)/c(x')$ there: $\kappa=1$ when $c$ is constant.
  Outside $N$ it is a premise on the computed steps, measured below (the port's $\kappa_\ell$).
- **(T)** *Local regularity.* For an evaluated $y$ with $|y-x|\le\tau_\rho(x)/2$: $\tau_S(y)\ge\tau_S(x)$ and
  $\tau_\rho(y)\ge\tau_\rho(x)/2$. And $\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}\le s$ over such points ($s=1$ below).

**Statement.** Under (U), (M), ($\sigma$), ($\kappa$), (T), the loop reaches the stop test, and the evaluations it makes
satisfy $N_{\rm loop}\le M_B+N_F+N_P$ with
$$M_B=\Big\lceil\log_2\frac{w_0}{r_c}\Big\rceil+1,\qquad
N_F=\Big\lceil(M_B+1)(1+\log_2^+\kappa)+\Big\lfloor\log_2\frac{w_0}{2\sigma_{\min}}\Big\rfloor+1\Big\rceil,\qquad
N_P=\Big\lfloor\frac{s}{8\,h_{\min}}\Big\rfloor+1$$
($M_B=0$ if $w_0\le r_c$; $\log_2^+=\max(0,\log_2)$). The branches count separately: at most $M_B$ passes B, at most
$N_F$ passes F, at most $N_P$ passes P. So the stopping pass begins with $k\le k_0+M_B+N_F+N_P$, and since the stop test
precedes the cap test (line 363 before 367), a cap equal to $k_0+M_B+N_F+N_P$ suffices. **Status of the steps.** The
walk's $k_0\le11$ is derived (Result 1(a), all trials usable). The branch counts rest on the proof below, in which three
steps are **asserted, not derived**, each marked there: (i) that phase A ends once $w\le r_c$ also where $S$ is not
monotone over the walk's bracket (cases 3 and 4); (ii) that no F follows a P and the creep count, both resting on (T);
(iii) the count of runs, $M_B+1$. Outside the argument altogether: the exact-zero start, the supplied-bracket path, the
endpoint check, and runs that violate (U).

**Proof.** *Phase A* is the passes before the first with $|S(x)|\le\tau_S(x)$; it has only B and F. *Phase B* is the rest.

*Bisections.* A bracket of width $\le r_c$ that contains the root lies in $N$. There, (M) with $y_1=L,y_2=R$ and $S(L)>0\ge S(R)$ gives $|S(x)|=\min(S(L),-S(R))\le h_{\max}c(x)\,w/2\le\tau_S(x)$
as soon as $w\le r_c$. By (c), after $m$ bisections $w\le w_0/2^m+2^{-53}\le w_0/2^m+r_c/4$, which is $\le r_c$ once
$2^m\ge\frac43w_0/r_c$, so $m\ge\log_2(w_0/r_c)+0.42$. So phase A holds at most $M_B$ bisections, and ends by then.
**Asserted, not derived (i):** the step "a bracket of width $\le r_c$ that contains the root lies in $N$" assumes that the
bracket's root is the one (M) describes. For the pairs whose score has an interior minimum between the walk's last points
and the root (cases 3 and 4, reversed secants), (M) holds only near the root, and that phase A ends when $w\le r_c$ is an
assertion checked only by the runs of those two pairs, not a consequence of the premises.

*Fisher steps.* A run ends only by a rejection (a B) or by the end of phase A, so there are at most $M_B+1$ runs
(**asserted, not derived (iii):** this counts a run per bisection of phase A and takes the bisection count $M_B$ above
as the number of B passes, which uses the bound on phase A in (i)). Let
$\lambda_i=\log_2\ell_i$ over all accepted steps in order. Within a run $\lambda_{i+1}\le\lambda_i-1$ (e); between runs
$\lambda_{i+1}\le\lambda_i+\log_2^+\kappa$; $\lambda_1\le\log_2(w_0/2)$ (d, plus the rounding of (c), the final $+1$); all
$\lambda_i>\log_2\sigma_{\min}$ (f). With $a$ within-run and $b\le M_B$ between-run transitions,
$\log_2\sigma_{\min}<\lambda_1-a+b\log_2^+\kappa$, so $a<\log_2\frac{w_0}{2\sigma_{\min}}+M_B\log_2^+\kappa$, and
the number of accepted steps is (runs)$+a$. This is $N_F$. No F can follow a P (below; **asserted (ii)**, resting on (T)).

*Probes* (**asserted (ii):** the whole paragraph rests on (T), which is unmeasured; it is an argument, not a proof about
the code). Take the pass at which $|S(x)|\le\tau_S(x)$ first holds, $x=L$ (the case $x=R$ is the mirror). If $w\le\tau_\rho(x)$
the loop stops. Otherwise (g) applies. A creep puts the new end $L'$ at $S(L')\le S(L)-h_{\min}c\,\tau_\rho/2$ by (M), and
$c\,\tau_\rho/2>8\tau_S$ by (0), so $S(L')\le(1-8h_{\min})\tau_S(L)$; by (T) $\tau_S(L')\ge\tau_S(L)$, so $|S(L')|\le\tau_S(L')$:
the loop is still converged and $x$ is still $L'$ (the other end did not change), so every later pass is a P and $dxold$ is
never read again. $m$ consecutive creeps move $L$ by $m\tau_\rho/2\ge8m\sigma$ and by (M) lower $S$ by at least $h_{\min}c\,m\,\tau_\rho/2$, while
$S$ stays positive at $L$ from $\le\tau_S$: $h_{\min}c\cdot 8m\sigma\le\tau_S$, so $m\le s/(8h_{\min})$. The creep that
crosses ($S(x_n)\le0$) gives $w'=\tau_\rho(L)/2$. The new $x$ is $L$ (stop: $|S(L)|\le\tau_S(L)$ and
$w'\le\tau_\rho(L)$) or $x_n$ with $|S(x_n)|<|S(L)|\le\tau_S(L)\le\tau_S(x_n)$ by (T), and
$\tau_\rho(x_n)\ge\tau_\rho(L)/2=w'$ by (T): the stop fires. So $N_P=\lfloor s/(8h_{\min})\rfloor+1$ evaluations,
the last the crossing one. $\blacksquare$

**Which quantity is unbounded without a premise, and what the half-step safeguard does.** $N_P\propto1/h_{\min}$: if the
local slope of $S$ is small against $c$, the probe (step $\ge8\sigma$) crawls through the flat stretch where $|S|\le\tau_S$.
Nothing else depends on $h_{\min}$: **phase A does not** (it uses $h_{\max}$ and the floors $r_c,\sigma_{\min}$ only,
logarithmically). For the Fisher iteration on a linear $S$ with $H/c=\eta$ the error factor is $|1-\eta|$, and the number
of accepted steps to bring $|S_0|$ to $\tau_S$ is $\log(|S_0|/\tau_S)/\log(1/|1-\eta|)$, which grows without limit as
$\eta\to0$. The safeguard cuts it: after a step $\ell_j$ the next is $\ell_{j+1}=|1-\eta|\,\ell_j$, accepted iff
$|1-\eta|\le\frac12$, that is $\eta\in[\frac12,\frac32]$. Outside that interval every run has length one. For
$\eta<\frac12$ the second step is rejected, the pass is a bisection, $dxold$ is reset to the new width $w'$, and the next
Fisher step is accepted again ($\ell=\eta\,d\le\eta w'<w'/2$, $d$ the distance to the root): **B, F, B, F**, two
evaluations per halving of $w$ and never more than one F per B. For $\eta>\frac32$ the second step of a run is rejected
likewise. So the factor $\to1$ never costs more than the alternation in phase A; its cost is entirely $N_P$.
$\kappa$ and $\sigma_{\min}$ enter $N_F$ only logarithmically.

**Three regimes, in the chunk.** For $S=-\eta c_0(\rho-r)$: $\eta\in[0.6,0.9]$ is the one-sided regime (no B, 12 or more F,
ending in a probe); $\eta\in\{0.01,0.05,0.2\}$ alternates (no two consecutive F, $|n_B-n_F|\le3$); the premise ($\sigma$)
failing ends at the cap (a root that is not a double, $|S|\ge10^{-17}>\tau_S=10^{-20}$: the bracket collapses to adjacent
doubles at 3,000 evaluations).

```{r cx-rootcap-linear}
cat("\n[cx-rootcap-linear] the loop on S(rho) = -eta c0 (rho - r): every regime, bound asserted\n")
local({
rc_eta <- c(0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.25, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.75, 0.9, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2, 2.5, 3)
rc_sig <- c(1e-16, 5e-16, 4e-15, 1e-13, 1e-10)
rc_c0  <- c(1e-3, 7.3)
rc_rt  <- sort(c(0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 + 1e-3, 0.7, 0.9, 0.99, 0.998, 0.9985, 0.99899,
                 runif(8, -0.9989, 0.9989)))
rc_rt  <- c(rc_rt, -rc_rt[1:12] * 0.987)
rc_lin_fe <- function(eta, r, sig, c0) function(x) c(x, 1, -eta * c0 * (x - r), c0, sig * c0)
rc_ncfg <- 0L; rc_top <- list(k = 0); rc_maxnP <- 0L; rc_maxratio <- 0
rc_reg <- list()
for (eta in rc_eta) for (sig in rc_sig) for (c0 in rc_c0) for (r in rc_rt) {
  if (sig / eta < 2^-51) next                         # the premise (sigma) of Result 3
  res <- rc_search(rc_lin_fe(eta, r, sig, c0), cap = 5000)
  bd  <- rc_bound(res$w0, eta, sig / eta, sig, 1, res$k0)
  b0  <- rc_bound(0.5,    eta, sig / eta, sig, 1, 11)
  nB <- sum(res$br == "B"); nF <- sum(res$br == "F"); nP <- sum(res$br == "P")
  rc_ncfg <- rc_ncfg + 1L
  tag <- sprintf("eta=%g sigma=%g c0=%g r=%.6g", eta, sig, c0, r)
  rc_check(res$status == "stop", paste("no stop:", tag, res$status))
  rc_check(nB <= bd$B && nF <= bd$F && nP <= bd$P && res$k <= bd$total, paste("bound exceeded:", tag, res$k, bd$total))
  rc_check(res$k <= b0$total, paste("bound with w0 = 1/2 exceeded:", tag))
  if (res$k > rc_top$k) rc_top <- list(k = res$k, tag = tag, nB = nB, nF = nF, nP = nP, bound = bd$total, bound0 = b0$total)
  rc_maxnP <- max(rc_maxnP, nP); rc_maxratio <- max(rc_maxratio, res$k / bd$total)
  key <- as.character(eta)
  rc_reg[[key]] <- rbind(rc_reg[[key]], c(nB = nB, nF = nF, nP = nP, k = res$k, w0 = res$w0))
}
cat(sprintf("  %d configurations, all stop within the bound; max evaluations %d at [%s]\n",
            rc_ncfg, rc_top$k, rc_top$tag))
cat(sprintf("    there: %d B, %d F, %d P; bound %d (with w0 = 1/2: %d); max P over all %d; max count/bound %.3f\n",
            rc_top$nB, rc_top$nF, rc_top$nP, rc_top$bound, rc_top$bound0, rc_maxnP, rc_maxratio))
cat("  by eta = H/c: mean B, F, P and max total evaluations (loop + walk)\n")
for (key in names(rc_reg)) {
  m <- rc_reg[[key]]
  cat(sprintf("    eta %-6s B %5.1f  F %5.1f  P %4.1f  max k %3d\n", key, mean(m[, "nB"]), mean(m[, "nF"]),
              mean(m[, "nP"]), max(m[, "k"])))
}
# the one-sided regime (eta in [1/2, 1), case 6) and the alternating regime (eta < 1/2) exactly
for (eta in c(0.6, 0.75, 0.9)) for (r in c(0.1, 0.3, -0.4, 0.6)) {
  res <- rc_search(rc_lin_fe(eta, r, 4e-15, 1), cap = 5000)
  rc_check(sum(res$br == "B") == 0 && sum(res$br == "F") >= 12 && res$status == "stop",
           sprintf("one-sided regime: eta %g r %g: B %d F %d", eta, r, sum(res$br == "B"), sum(res$br == "F")))
}
for (eta in c(0.01, 0.05, 0.2)) for (r in c(0.1, 0.3, -0.4, 0.6)) {
  res <- rc_search(rc_lin_fe(eta, r, 4e-15, 1), cap = 5000)
  b <- res$br; nb <- sum(b == "B"); nf <- sum(b == "F")
  rc_check(!any(b[-1] == "F" & b[-length(b)] == "F") && abs(nb - nf) <= 3,
           sprintf("alternating regime: eta %g r %g: B %d F %d", eta, r, nb, nf))
}
res <- rc_search(rc_lin_fe(0.9, 0.3, 4e-15, 1), cap = 5000)
cat(sprintf("  one-sided example (eta 0.9, r 0.3): %d F, %d B, %d P, bracket width at the end %.3g (start %.3g);\n",
            sum(res$br == "F"), sum(res$br == "B"), sum(res$br == "P"), res$R[1] - res$L[1], res$w0))
cat(sprintf("    the last pass is a far-side probe: %s\n", tail(res$br, 1)))
# the premise (sigma) failing: S cannot reach |S| <= tau_S before the bracket is two adjacent doubles
rc_fail_fe <- function(x) c(x, 1, -0.7 * (x - 0.3) - 1e-17, 1, 1e-20)     # the root is not a double; |S| >= 1e-17 > tau_S
rc_fail_res <- rc_search(rc_fail_fe, cap = 3000)
rc_check(rc_fail_res$status == "cap", "premise (sigma) violated: expected the cap")
cat(sprintf("  premise (sigma) violated (sigma/h = 1.4e-20 < 2^-51): status %s after %d evaluations, width %.3g\n",
            rc_fail_res$status, rc_fail_res$k, rc_fail_res$R[1] - rc_fail_res$L[1]))
})
```

**Measured** (`cx-rootcap-linear`; the loop of lines 359-396 re-implemented in R doubles, preceded by the walk). 4,544
configurations: 18 values of $\eta$ from 0.001 to 3 (both regimes, the borderline 0.5, $\eta=1$ where the first Fisher step
is exact, and $\eta>\frac32$), five $\sigma$ from $10^{-16}$ to $10^{-10}$ (those with $\sigma/\eta\ge2^{-51}$), two $c_0$, and 32
roots from $\pm10^{-4}$ to $\pm0.99899$. Every one stops, and its B, F, P counts and its total are within the bound of
Result 3 evaluated at its own $w_0$, $\eta$, $\sigma$ (and within the bound at $w_0=\frac12$). The largest count is **201**
evaluations at $\eta=0.001$ (38 B, 39 F, 122 P; bound 260), the creeping regime that $N_P$ is about: 122 against
$1/(8\eta)=125$; the largest ratio count/bound is 0.79. At $\eta\ge0.01$ the largest count is 100.

`cx-rootcap-nonlinear` repeats this on monotone scores that are not linear: slope$/c$ between $\eta_{lo}$ and $\eta_{hi}=100\,\eta_{lo}$,
steepest at the root or flattest at the root (a $\tanh$ of width 0.02 added to a line), with $c$ constant or varying by
a factor 3 over $[-B,B]$ ($\kappa=3$, $h_{\max}=\eta_{hi}/0.5$, $h_{\min}=\eta_{lo}/1.5$). The bound is evaluated with those
constants, which are known by construction; it is not fitted to the run.

```{r cx-rootcap-nonlinear}
cat("\n[cx-rootcap-nonlinear] monotone scores whose slope varies by a factor of 100, c varying by 3\n")
local({
# slope/c in [eta_lo, eta_hi] at the root and the other way round; c(x) = c0 (1 + 0.5 sin 3x), kappa_c = 3
rc_nl_fe <- function(shape, elo, ehi, r, sig, c0, cvar) {
  a <- 0.02
  cf <- if (cvar) function(x) c0 * (1 + 0.5 * sin(3 * x)) else function(x) c0
  g <- if (shape == "steep") function(t) elo * t + (ehi - elo) * a * tanh(t / a)
       else                  function(t) ehi * t - (ehi - elo) * a * tanh(t / a)
  function(x) { cx <- cf(x); c(x, 1, -c0 * g(x - r), cx, sig * cx) }
}
rc_nfg <- 0L; rc_topn <- list(k = 0)
for (shape in c("steep", "flat")) for (cvar in c(FALSE, TRUE)) for (lh in list(c(0.01, 1), c(0.02, 2), c(0.1, 10), c(0.5, 50))) {
  for (sig in c(4e-15, 1e-12)) for (r in c(-0.95, -0.5, -0.02, 0.01, 0.3, 0.8, 0.97, 0.9985)) {
    hmax <- lh[2] / (if (cvar) 0.5 else 1); hmin <- lh[1] / (if (cvar) 1.5 else 1); kap <- if (cvar) 3 else 1
    if (sig / hmax < 2^-51) next
    res <- rc_search(rc_nl_fe(shape, lh[1], lh[2], r, sig, 1, cvar), cap = 5000)
    bd <- rc_bound(res$w0, hmin, sig / hmax, sig, kap, res$k0)
    nB <- sum(res$br == "B"); nF <- sum(res$br == "F"); nP <- sum(res$br == "P")
    tag <- sprintf("%s cvar=%s slope/c [%g,%g] sigma=%g r=%g", shape, cvar, lh[1], lh[2], sig, r)
    rc_nfg <- rc_nfg + 1L
    rc_check(res$status == "stop", paste("no stop:", tag, res$status))
    rc_check(nB <= bd$B && nF <= bd$F && nP <= bd$P && res$k <= bd$total, paste("bound exceeded:", tag, res$k, bd$total))
    if (res$k > rc_topn$k) rc_topn <- list(k = res$k, tag = tag, bound = bd$total, nB = nB, nF = nF, nP = nP)
  }
}
cat(sprintf("  %d configurations, all stop within the bound; max evaluations %d at [%s]\n    there: %d B, %d F, %d P, bound %d\n",
            rc_nfg, rc_topn$k, rc_topn$tag, rc_topn$nB, rc_topn$nF, rc_topn$nP, rc_topn$bound))
})
```

**Measured** (`cx-rootcap-nonlinear`): 192 configurations, every one stops within its bound; the largest count is 94
(37 B, 40 F, 15 P; bound 246).

### Result 4: the budget

**Derived, conditionally.** Under the premises (U), (M), ($\sigma$), ($\kappa$), (T) of Result 3, the root search of a pair
begins its stopping pass with $k\le k_0+M_B+N_F+N_P$ evaluations (Results 1 and 3), where

- $k_0\le11$ and $w_0\le\frac12$ (Result 1, all walk trials usable; $w_0$ is smaller for roots near $\pm1$, which Result 3's formula uses);
- $M_B$ depends on $w_0/r_c$, $r_c=\sigma_{\min}/h_{\max}$ at the roots' neighbourhood;
- $N_F$ on the same and on $w_0/\sigma_{\min}$ and $\kappa$;
- $N_P=\lfloor s/(8h_{\min})\rfloor+1$.

Two bounds come out, and they rest on different things.

| | Value | Rests on |
|---|---|---|
| **A.** Walk and phase A: $k_0+M_B+N_F$ | **167** | $w_0=\frac12$, $r_c=2^{-51}$, $\sigma_{\min}=2^{-54}$, $\kappa=1$. **No** $h_{\min}$. It guarantees that every pair has $|S(x)|\le\tau_S(x)$ within the budget, not that the stop test is passed. |
| **B.** A plus the far-side probes | **180** | A and $h_{\min}=1/100$, $s=1$. $N_P=13$. |

B's dependence on $h_{\min}$ is the only large one: $h_{\min}=1/40$ gives 173, $1/10$ gives 169, $1/1000$ gives 293 (the table in
the chunk below gives the others; $r_c$ from $2^{-49}$ to $2^{-52}$ moves it by 4, $\sigma_{\min}$ from $2^{-50}$ to $2^{-57}$ by 7,
$\kappa=2$ gives 232). A cap $K$ covers every $h_{\min}\ge1/(8(K-168))$: 180 covers $1/96$, 200 covers $1/256$, 250 covers $1/656$.

**Measured premises, and what was chosen after measuring.** The values seen on the nine pairs are **measured**
($\sigma_{\min}\ge9.8\times10^{-17}$, $r_c\ge5.9\times10^{-16}$, $h_{loc}\ge0.025$, $\kappa_\ell=1$, cases 2 to 9). The
constants $r_c=2^{-51}$, $\sigma_{\min}=2^{-54}$, $h_{\min}=1/100$, $\kappa=1$, $s=1$ **were chosen after measuring** the
nine pairs (below): each is the nearest power of two (or round figure) below the smallest value seen, so that the nine
are inside the premises with a margin; no derivation picks them. $w_0=\frac12$ and $k_0=11$ are derived, and so are the
formulas. **If the premises fail** the code is the code of today: a pair whose root search exceeds the cap returns status
7 and the pair is refused, as the nine are now. Premises (U) and (T) are unmeasured, and the three asserted steps
named in Result 3 (i, ii, iii) are not derived.

**Conclusion.** Under the stated premises (U), (M), ($\sigma$), ($\kappa$), (T), at the constants chosen after
measuring, the loop reaches its stopping test within 180 evaluations (167 before the far-side probes). The budget **200**
is a margin **chosen after measuring** (decided by the project owner on 2026-11-13) over that conditional bound; it is
**not a derived bound**. It covers $h_{\min}\ge1/256$ in the formula and costs at most 20 more evaluations of a pair that
would otherwise be refused. It applies to **conditional mode only**: v1 and the shared root-finder keep `cap = 40` on the
ordinary path, and nothing here is evidence about that value. **Case 1 lies outside the constants**: its own measured
constants give a bound of 390, and only its production count (42) is observed; the budget 200 is not justified for it by
the formula. A pair that violates (U) can still end at status 8 (or abort at $\rho=0$) at any budget.

**The synthetic evaluator "P-alt" of `tests/unit/test_condx_rootcap.do` (lines about 115-155).** The score is
$S=-0.1(\rho-0.9)$ with $c=1$, $\tau_S=10^{-14}$, and $S(0)>0$, so $d=+1$. The walk evaluates $0$, then $0.5$, $0.75$,
$0.875$ (all with $S>0$) and $0.9375$ (sign change): **5 evaluations**, $L=0.875$, $R=0.9375$, $w_0=0.0625$, $x=L$. In the
loop the first Fisher step ($0.0025\le w_0/2$) is accepted and lands on the side of $L$; the next would be longer than half
of the previous step and is rejected, so the pass is a bisection, after which the Fisher step is again accepted. Fisher
steps and bisections therefore **alternate in pairs**, $n$ pairs, each pair two evaluations. The stopping test needs
$|S|\le\tau_S$ and $w\le\tau_\rho$, with $\tau_\rho\approx1.6\times10^{-13}$. Since $|S|=0.1|\rho-0.9|$, $|S(x)|\le\tau_S$
holds from a distance of $10^{-13}$, which is below $\tau_\rho$, so the pass in which $x$ first satisfies it still has
$w>\tau_\rho$; the loop then spends **one far-side probe**, which crosses the root, leaves $w=\tau_\rho/2$, and ends the
loop at the next stopping test (Result 2(g), Result 3). That this is the case is read off the port's run (the last branch
is P); the argument fixes the structure, not the pass at which the probe occurs. The endpoint check adds **2 evaluations** ($\pm B$ usable,
status 1). The total is $5+2n+1+2=8+2n$, even. The value $n=35$, giving $78$, is a **computed** value from the R port of
the loop (`rc_search` on this evaluator, branch sequence F, B repeated 35 times and then one P; cap 40 gives status 7 at
$k=40$); it depends on the binary expansion of $0.9$ and the rounding of the halved widths, and it is **not closed-form**.
The test's header comment does not mention the probe pass, which is the "$+1$".

```{r cx-rootcap-budget}
cat("\n[cx-rootcap-budget] the formula evaluated\n")
local({
rc_tab <- function(w0 = 0.5, hmin = 1/100, rconv = 2^-51, smin = 2^-54, kap = 1, k0 = 11) rc_bound(w0, hmin, rconv, smin, kap, k0)
rc_show <- function(lbl, bd) cat(sprintf("  %-46s k0 %2d  B %3d  F %3d  P %3d  total %3d\n", lbl, bd$k0, bd$B, bd$F, bd$P, bd$total))
rc_gen <- rc_tab()
rc_show("generic (w0 1/2, h_min 1/100, rconv 2^-51, sigma_min 2^-54, kappa 1)", rc_gen)
rc_show("  h_min 1/40", rc_tab(hmin = 1/40)); rc_show("  h_min 1/10", rc_tab(hmin = 1/10)); rc_show("  h_min 1/1000", rc_tab(hmin = 1/1000))
rc_show("  rconv 2^-49 (x4)", rc_tab(rconv = 2^-49)); rc_show("  rconv 2^-52", rc_tab(rconv = 2^-52))
rc_show("  sigma_min 2^-50", rc_tab(smin = 2^-50)); rc_show("  sigma_min 2^-57", rc_tab(smin = 2^-57))
rc_show("  kappa 2", rc_tab(kap = 2)); rc_show("  w0 = 2^-5 (root near +-0.97)", rc_tab(w0 = 2^-5, k0 = 6))
rc_show("  w0 = 0.000953 (root beyond 0.998)", rc_tab(w0 = 0.000953125, k0 = 11))
RC_CAP_PHASEA <<- rc_gen$k0 + rc_gen$B + rc_gen$F          # the walk and phase A: independent of h_min
cat(sprintf("  walk + phase A alone (no far-side probes): %d\n", RC_CAP_PHASEA))
RC_CAP_GENERIC <<- rc_gen$total
# the smallest slope/c a given cap covers: cap - phase A - 1 far-side probes are affordable, and 1/(8 h_min) creeps are needed
rc_hcover <<- function(cap) 1 / (8 * (cap - RC_CAP_PHASEA - 1))
cat(sprintf("  smallest h_min covered: cap %d -> 1/%.0f, cap 200 -> 1/%.0f, cap 250 -> 1/%.0f\n", RC_CAP_GENERIC, 1 / rc_hcover(RC_CAP_GENERIC),
            1 / rc_hcover(200), 1 / rc_hcover(250)))
stopifnot(RC_CAP_GENERIC == rc_gen$k0 + rc_gen$B + rc_gen$F + rc_gen$P)
cat(sprintf("  generic bound = %d evaluations from the start of the root search (cap argument counts from the first evaluation at 0)\n", RC_CAP_GENERIC))
})
```

### The nine pairs

**Separating the root search from the endpoint check in the production trace.** `trace_cap1000.log` lists every
evaluation of one call (cap 1000), the endpoint check's included. `dwlsmv_rf_check()` (line 272) calls
`dwlsmv_rf_end()` for $d=-1$ and then $d=+1$, and `dwlsmv_rf_end()` begins by evaluating $dB$ (line 228); nothing in the
walk or the loop evaluates $-B$ after the check has begun. So the check starts at the **last** row at $\rho=-B$ (the
walk can reach $-B$ only as an earlier row, and then returns or enters the loop), and the root search is the rows before
it. The port (`cx-rootcap-cases`) is the algorithm of lines 294-397 on the nine tables of `cases.txt` with the item
thresholds of the Mata trace; cell probabilities by Plackett's identity with a composite Gauss-Legendre rule (checked
against `pbivnorm` where that package is installed: $1.1\times10^{-16}$ on 84 points). It is a port, not production.

Production at cap 1000 (Stata 18, 2026-11-12): totals 96, 139, 135, 139, 142, 96, 135, 120, 145; endpoint check 54
evaluations in eight cases and 103 in case 9; **root search 42, 85, 81, 85, 88, 42, 81, 66, 42**. Cases 1, 6 and 9 (a bisection-only run at the $10^{-30}$ scale of
$c$, the one-sided run, and a bracket already inside $\tau_\rho$) miss the cap of 40 by two evaluations; the other six need
66 to 88. The port's root-search counts are 80, 83, 83, 85, 88, 42, 81, 66, 42: equal to production in cases 4 to 9,
two off in cases 2 and 3, and in case 1 far off (80 against 42): there $c\sim10^{-30}$ is dominated by an unobserved cell of
probability near $10^{-19}$, below what an absolute-error integrator resolves, so the port's $c$ and its branches are not
production's. For case 1 the production count is the figure; the port's is shown only because its run reaches the stop.

```{r cx-rootcap-cases}
cat("\n[cx-rootcap-cases] the nine constructed pairs: R port of the production loop with an own bivariate-normal integrator\n")
local({
RC_ROOT <- if (file.exists(file.path("docs", "notes", "condx-stage1", "cap-screen", "cases.txt"))) "." else file.path("..", "..")
RC_DIR  <- file.path(RC_ROOT, "docs", "notes", "condx-stage1", "cap-screen")
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(RC_DIR, "cases.txt")), file.exists(file.path(RC_DIR, "mech", "trace_cap1000.log")))

# Phi_2 by Plackett's identity, Phi(h)Phi(k) + int_0^rho phi_2(h,k;t) dt, t = tanh s, composite 16-point Gauss-Legendre
rc_gl <- function(n) {
  i <- seq_len(n - 1); bb <- i / sqrt(4 * i^2 - 1); J <- matrix(0, n, n)
  J[cbind(i, i + 1)] <- bb; J[cbind(i + 1, i)] <- bb
  ev <- eigen(J, symmetric = TRUE); list(x = ev$values, w = 2 * ev$vectors[1, ]^2)
}
RC_GL <- rc_gl(16)
rc_I <- function(h, k, rho) {
  if (rho == 0) return(0)
  s1 <- atanh(rho); np <- max(4L, ceiling(abs(s1) / 0.25)); ed <- seq(0, s1, length.out = np + 1); tot <- 0
  for (p in seq_len(np)) {
    a <- ed[p]; b <- ed[p + 1]; s <- (a + b) / 2 + (b - a) / 2 * RC_GL$x
    Q <- (h * h + k * k) * cosh(s)^2 - 2 * h * k * sinh(s) * cosh(s)
    tot <- tot + (b - a) / 2 * sum(RC_GL$w * exp(-Q / 2) / (2 * pi * cosh(s)))
  }
  tot
}
rc_F2 <- function(h, k, rho) {
  if (h == -Inf || k == -Inf) return(0)
  if (h == Inf && k == Inf) return(1)
  if (h == Inf) return(pnorm(k))
  if (k == Inf) return(pnorm(h))
  pnorm(h) * pnorm(k) + rc_I(h, k, rho)
}
rc_phi2 <- function(h, k, r) exp(-(h * h - 2 * r * h * k + k * k) / (2 * (1 - r * r))) / (2 * pi * sqrt(1 - r * r))
rc_cells <- function(a, b, x) {
  A <- c(-Inf, a, Inf); Bv <- c(-Inf, b, Inf); nA <- length(A); nB <- length(Bv)
  Fm <- matrix(0, nA, nB); Dm <- matrix(0, nA, nB)
  for (r in seq_len(nA)) for (s in seq_len(nB)) {
    Fm[r, s] <- rc_F2(A[r], Bv[s], x)
    Dm[r, s] <- if (is.finite(A[r]) && is.finite(Bv[s])) rc_phi2(A[r], Bv[s], x) else 0
  }
  dd <- function(M) M[2:nA, 2:nB] - M[1:(nA - 1), 2:nB] - M[2:nA, 1:(nB - 1)] + M[1:(nA - 1), 1:(nB - 1)]
  list(P = dd(Fm), D = dd(Dm))
}
if (requireNamespace("pbivnorm", quietly = TRUE)) {               # a diagnostic only, not a dependency
  dmax <- 0
  for (x in c(-0.99, -0.9, -0.5, 0, 0.3, 0.9, 0.995)) for (h in c(-3, -1, 0.2, 2.5)) for (k in c(-2.7, 0.4, 1.9))
    dmax <- max(dmax, abs(rc_F2(h, k, x) - pbivnorm::pbivnorm(h, k, x)))
  cat(sprintf("  integrator vs pbivnorm on 84 points: max |difference| %.2e\n", dmax))
}
# dwlsmv_rf_evalp (lines 89-132) for one group, then dwlsmv_cx_rf_eval's pooling of the two groups
rc_evalp <- function(x, n, a, b) {
  cl <- rc_cells(a, b, x); P <- cl$P; D <- cl$D
  O <- n > 0; Po <- P * O + (1 - O)
  if (anyNA(Po) || min(Po) <= RC_DP) return(c(x, 0, NA, NA, NA))
  w <- n / sum(n); u <- (D / Po) * O; pos <- P > 0; Pp <- P * pos + (1 - pos)
  K1 <- length(a) + 1; K2 <- length(b) + 1; A <- c(NA, a, NA); Bt <- c(NA, b, NA); W <- matrix(0, K1 + 1, K2 + 1)
  for (r in 2:K1) for (s in 2:K2) {
    p <- A[r]; q <- Bt[s]; z <- (p * p - 2 * x * p * q + q * q) / (2 * (1 - x * x))
    W[r, s] <- exp(-z) / (2 * pi * sqrt(1 - x * x)) * (z + 7)
  }
  W <- W[2:(K1 + 1), 2:(K2 + 1)] + W[1:K1, 2:(K2 + 1)] + W[2:(K1 + 1), 1:K2] + W[1:K1, 1:K2]
  eps <- 2^-52
  tauS <- sum(w * (eps * W + abs(u) * RC_DP) / Po) + (sum(O) + 2) * eps * sum(w * abs(u))
  c(x, 1, sum(w * u), sum(((D * D) / Pp) * pos), tauS)
}
rc_cx_fe <- function(n0, n1, a0, b0, a1, b1) {
  N0 <- sum(n0); N1 <- sum(n1); w0 <- N0 / (N0 + N1); w1 <- N1 / (N0 + N1)
  function(x) {
    e0 <- rc_evalp(x, n0, a0, b0); e1 <- rc_evalp(x, n1, a1, b1)
    if (!e0[2] || !e1[2]) return(c(x, 0, NA, NA, NA))
    c(x, 1, w0 * e0[3] + w1 * e1[3], w0 * e0[4] + w1 * e1[4],
      w0 * e0[5] + w1 * e1[5] + 3 * 2^-52 * (w0 * abs(e0[3]) + w1 * abs(e1[3])))
  }
}
# the nine tables (cases.txt) and the production trace at cap 1000 (mech/trace_cap1000.log)
cl <- readLines(file.path(RC_DIR, "cases.txt"))
rc_mat <- function(s) {
  s <- sub("^[a-z0-9]+ = \\(", "", s); s <- sub("\\)$", "", s)
  rows <- strsplit(s, " \\ ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(rows, function(r) as.numeric(strsplit(r, ", ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])))
}
rc_n0 <- lapply(cl[startsWith(cl, "n0 = ")], rc_mat); rc_n1 <- lapply(cl[startsWith(cl, "n1 = ")], rc_mat)
stopifnot(length(rc_n0) == 9, length(rc_n1) == 9)
tl <- readLines(file.path(RC_DIR, "mech", "trace_cap1000.log")); tl <- tl[startsWith(tl, "TR|")]
cs <- grep("^TR\\|case [0-9]+$", tl); stopifnot(length(cs) == 9)
rc_trace <- lapply(1:9, function(g) {
  seg <- tl[cs[g]:(if (g < 9) cs[g + 1] - 1 else length(tl))]
  num <- function(l) as.numeric(strsplit(trimws(sub("^TR\\|items [ij]\\|", "", l)), " +")[[1]])
  rows <- seg[grepl("^TR\\|\\s+-?[0-9]", seg)]
  M <- do.call(rbind, lapply(strsplit(rows, "|", fixed = TRUE), function(f) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(f[c(2, 4, 5, 6, 7)])))))
  rs <- strsplit(seg[startsWith(seg, "TR|result|")], "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  list(thi = num(seg[startsWith(seg, "TR|items i|")]), thj = num(seg[startsWith(seg, "TR|items j|")]),
       M = M, status = as.numeric(rs[4]), k = as.numeric(rs[5]))
})
rc_case_fe <- function(g) {
  tr <- rc_trace[[g]]; Ki <- nrow(rc_n0[[g]]); Kj <- ncol(rc_n0[[g]])
  ti <- tr$thi[1:(Ki - 1)]; tj <- tr$thj[1:(Kj - 1)]
  rc_cx_fe(rc_n0[[g]], rc_n1[[g]], ti, tj, ti - tr$thi[Ki], tj - tr$thj[Kj])
}
# root-search evaluations in the production trace: the endpoint check begins at the LAST row at rho = -B
# (rf_end(d = -1) evaluates d B first and nothing else evaluates it again); everything before is the walk and the loop
rc_krs <- vapply(rc_trace, function(t) { j <- which(t$M[, 1] == -RC_B); stopifnot(length(j) >= 1); max(j) - 1 }, 0)
rc_kend <- vapply(rc_trace, function(t) t$k, 0) - rc_krs
cat("  production (Stata 18) at cap 1000: total evaluations, endpoint-check evaluations, root-search evaluations\n")
cat(sprintf("    case %d: total %3d  endpoint check %3d  root search %3d   (status %d)\n", 1:9,
            vapply(rc_trace, function(t) t$k, 0), rc_kend, rc_krs, vapply(rc_trace, function(t) t$status, 0)), sep = "")
rc_res <- list(); rc_meas <- list()
for (g in 1:9) {
  fe <- rc_case_fe(g)
  res <- rc_search(fe, cap = 1000); rc_res[[g]] <- res
  # the production rows of the root search; the loop's are those after the walk's res$k0 evaluations
  M <- rc_trace[[g]]$M[seq_len(rc_krs[g]), , drop = FALSE]
  Ml <- M[(res$k0 + 1):nrow(M), , drop = FALSE]; Ml <- Ml[!is.na(Ml[, 3]), , drop = FALSE]
  sg <- Ml[, 5] / Ml[, 4]
  hsec <- function(Mx) {            # secant slopes over c, for the pairs whose S differ by more than 4 (tau_i + tau_j)
    hh <- numeric(0)
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(Mx) - 1)) for (j in (i + 1):nrow(Mx)) {
      if (abs(Mx[i, 3] - Mx[j, 3]) > 4 * (Mx[i, 5] + Mx[j, 5])) {
        sl <- (Mx[i, 3] - Mx[j, 3]) / (Mx[j, 1] - Mx[i, 1]); hh <- c(hh, sl / Mx[i, 4], sl / Mx[j, 4])
      }
    }
    hh
  }
  hh <- hsec(Ml); hl <- hsec(tail(Ml, 20))
  kap <- if (length(res$ell) > 1) max(1, max(res$ell[-1] / res$ell[-length(res$ell)])) else 1
  rc_meas[[g]] <- list(smin = min(sg), smax = max(sg), hmin = min(hh), hmax = max(hh),
                       hloc = if (length(hl)) min(hl) else NA, kap = kap, nneg = sum(hh < 0), nloc = sum(hl < 0))
}
cat("  R port at cap 1000: status, root-search evaluations (production in brackets), branches\n")
for (g in 1:9) {
  r <- rc_res[[g]]
  cat(sprintf("    case %d: %-5s k %3d (prod %3d)  walk %2d  w0 %.3g  B %2d F %2d P %2d\n", g, r$status, r$k, rc_krs[g], r$k0, r$w0,
              sum(r$br == "B"), sum(r$br == "F"), sum(r$br == "P")))
}
cat("  premise constants measured on each case's loop rows (production trace; h = secant slope / c; sigma = tau_S / c;\n")
cat("  h_loc from the last 20 rows only; kappa_ell from the port's Fisher step lengths)\n")
for (g in 1:9) {
  m <- rc_meas[[g]]
  cat(sprintf("    case %d: sigma %.2e..%.2e  h %.3g..%.3g (reversed secants: %d, of which in the last 20 rows %d)  h_loc min %.3g  kappa_ell %.3g\n",
              g, m$smin, m$smax, m$hmin, m$hmax, m$nneg, m$nloc, m$hloc, m$kap))
}
# what the next chunk uses (the rest is local: the full document shares one session)
rc_krs <<- rc_krs; rc_res <<- rc_res; rc_meas <<- rc_meas; rc_case_fe <<- rc_case_fe
})
```

**The premise constants on the nine pairs** (measured on production's loop rows; $h$ is a secant slope over $c$, $\sigma=\tau_S/c$;
$h_{loc}$ uses only the last 20 rows; $\kappa_\ell$ is from the port's step lengths). Read with care: they are the
values the constants of Result 4 were chosen against.

- $\sigma$: smallest $9.8\times10^{-17}$ (case 5, $2^{-53.2}$), cases 3 and 4 about $10^{-16}$ to $3\times10^{-16}$, the others
  $10^{-15}$ to $5\times10^{-14}$. Case 1 ($4\times10^{-17}$ to 0.5, $c\sim10^{-30}$) is degenerate and is excluded from the choice.
- $r_c=\sigma_{\min}/h_{\max}$: smallest $5.9\times10^{-16}$ (case 4, $2^{-50.6}$), then $9.3\times10^{-16}$ (case 3).
- $h_{loc}$: 0.025 (case 5), 0.071 (2), 0.12 (7), 0.15 (3), 0.18 (4), 0.46 (8), 0.56 (6), 1.56 (9).
- $\kappa_\ell=1$ in cases 2 to 9 (the accepted steps' lengths never grow); 1.98 in case 1, the port's run, not production's.
- **(M) is local only.** Cases 3 and 4 have reversed secants (10 and 4 pairs with $|\Delta S|>4(\tau_i+\tau_j)$ and the wrong
  sign), none among the last 20 rows: $S$ has an interior minimum between the walk's last points and the root. The loop
  converges on the root nonetheless (production, 81 and 85 evaluations); the premise as stated in Result 3 is the local one.

`cx-rootcap-cases-budget` then asserts, for each of the nine, that the port reaches the stop test at the generic budget
(a failure stops the script), that the nine production counts lie in $(40,\ 180]$, and shows the bound of Result 3
evaluated with the pair's own measured constants (135 to 149 for cases 2 to 9, not an assertion: the constants are
estimates, and case 1's, at the $10^{-30}$ scale, give 390). Every observed count is within it.

```{r cx-rootcap-cases-budget}
cat("\n[cx-rootcap-cases-budget] the nine pairs at the budget; the bound from each case's measured constants\n")
local({
rc_check(all(rc_krs > 40) && all(rc_krs <= RC_CAP_GENERIC), "production root-search counts outside (40, generic budget]")
cat(sprintf("  production root-search counts %s: all above 40 (the cap that refused them), all at most the generic budget %d\n",
            paste(rc_krs, collapse = " "), RC_CAP_GENERIC))
for (g in 1:9) {
  fe <- rc_case_fe(g)
  r40 <- rc_search(fe, cap = 40)
  rg  <- rc_search(fe, cap = RC_CAP_GENERIC)
  rc_check(rg$status == "stop", sprintf("case %d does not reach the stop test at the generic budget %d", g, RC_CAP_GENERIC))
  m <- rc_meas[[g]]
  bd <- rc_bound(rc_res[[g]]$w0, if (is.na(m$hloc)) m$hmin else m$hloc, m$smin / m$hmax, m$smin, m$kap, rc_res[[g]]$k0)
  cat(sprintf("    case %d: cap 40 -> %-5s | generic budget %d -> %-5s at k %3d | bound from own constants %3d (observed %3d) %s\n",
              g, r40$status, RC_CAP_GENERIC, rg$status, rg$k, bd$total, rc_res[[g]]$k,
              if (rc_res[[g]]$k <= bd$total) "within" else "EXCEEDS"))
}
})
```

### Derived, measured, chosen, tested

**Derived** (from the code of lines 294-397 read as written, and arithmetic): the walk's count and bracket, at most
$k_0=11$ evaluations and $w_0\le\frac12$ (Result 1, all trials usable; with an unusable trial the walk's count is bounded
only for the second and later trials, and not by the argument for the first); that $w$ never grows, a bisection halves it, accepted Fisher steps
halve, F needs $\ell>\sigma$, and a probe that crosses collapses the bracket to $\tau_\rho/2$ (Result 2); the counts
$M_B,N_F,N_P$ and their sum **under the premises** (Result 3; steps (i) to (iii) there are asserted, not derived); the bounds 167 (walk and phase A, no $h_{\min}$) and 180
(with probes) as the formula at the constants below (Result 4). Also derived: the two ways the structure alone fails to
terminate (no floor on $\sigma/h_{\max}$ above the spacing of doubles; creeping without a floor on $h_{\min}$).

**Measured premises** (not derived, not checked by the code; (U) and (T) are the unmeasured ones): (U) every evaluated point
usable, (M) local monotonicity with slope bounds, ($\sigma$)
the floors $\sigma_{\min}$ and $r_c\ge2^{-51}$, ($\kappa$), (T) local regularity of $\tau_S,\tau_\rho$ and $s$. On the nine
pairs: $r_c\ge5.9\times10^{-16}$, $\sigma_{\min}\ge9.8\times10^{-17}$ (cases 2 to 9), $h_{loc}\ge0.025$, $\kappa_\ell=1$. **(T)
is not measured at all**: the synthetic scores satisfy it by construction, and for the nine pairs it is neither measured
nor tested. The formula for $c$, $\tau_S$ (lines 129-131) is the project's own and is a premise of `@sec-rootfind`.

**Chosen.** *After measuring the nine pairs:* $r_c=2^{-51}$, $\sigma_{\min}=2^{-54}$, $h_{\min}=1/100$, $\kappa=1$, $s=1$, and
therefore the figures **180** and **167** (these two are the formula at constants chosen after measuring, not a derived
bound). The conditions of ($\sigma$) are set as the next power of two below the smallest value
seen (with $2^{-51}$ also from the rounding floor $4\times2^{-53}$); $h_{\min}$ is a factor 2.5 below the smallest local slope. *Before
measuring:* the simulation grid of `cx-rootcap-linear` (the $\eta$, $\sigma$, $c_0$, $r$ values) and the premise-violation
design. *Decided by the owner on 2026-11-13, after measuring:* the budget **200** for conditional mode, a margin over the
conditional bound 180 (it covers $h_{\min}\ge1/256$); it is not derived.

**Tested domain.** (i) Synthetic linear scores, 4,544 configurations, every one within the bound, branch by branch, at its
own constants; the alternating, one-sided and cap-reaching regimes each demonstrated. (ii) 192 synthetic monotone nonlinear
configurations with slope varying by 100 and $c$ by 3. (iii) 462 roots for the walk. (iv) The nine pairs through the R
port: all reach the stop test at 180, all fail at 40; production's counts (42 to 88) lie in $(40,180]$; the bound at each
pair's own constants holds. **16,366 checks, 0 failures** (log: `verify_rootcap.log`).

| | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The walk's count (11) and bracket ($\le\frac12$) | **derived**, tested on 462 roots | Result 1, `cx-rootcap-walk` |
| Width never grows; B halves; accepted F halve; probe collapse | **derived** (exact arithmetic, rounding $\le2^{-54}$ per bisection) | Result 2 |
| $M_B+N_F+N_P$ | **derived under** (U), (M), ($\sigma$), ($\kappa$), (T); steps (i) to (iii) **asserted** | Result 3 |
| The frontier bisection's pass count | $\le49$ for a later trial; **not bounded by the argument** for the first trial | Result 1(c) |
| The budget 200 | **chosen after measuring** (owner, 2026-11-13); margin over the conditional bound 180 | Result 4 |
| (M), ($\sigma$), ($\kappa$) on the nine pairs | **measured premise** | `cx-rootcap-cases` |
| (T), (U) | **premise, not measured** | |
| $2^{-51}$, $2^{-54}$, $1/100$, 1, 1 | **chosen after measuring** | Result 4 |
| 167 and 180 | formula at those constants | `cx-rootcap-budget` |
| 4,544 + 192 synthetic configurations, nine pairs in the R port | **tested in R only** | the chunks |

### Limitations

- **Status at the end is not bounded.** The budget bounds the evaluations of the root search. Case 2 ends at status 6
  (the endpoint check finds an ambiguous end), and nothing here changes that.
- **Not bearing on** the uniqueness of the pooled root (`@sec-condx-rootfind`), on v1, on the endpoint check's own cap of 54
  per side, or on how often the slow regimes occur in real data: the nine pairs are constructed, from a screen of 1,458
  simulated pairs, and their frequency is unknown.
- **The port is not Mata.** Six of the nine counts agree with production, three do not (case 1 materially). The bound is
  asserted on the port's runs and on synthetic scores; it was not run in Stata.
- **(M) is local; (T) is unmeasured.** If (T) fails by a hair, the crossing probe may not be followed by the stop, and
  one or two extra passes follow that this section does not count.
- **Roots near 0.** $\tau_\rho>2^{-50}|x|$ (0) is relative, but the floors on $r_c$ and $\sigma_{\min}$ are absolute
  figures chosen against nine pairs with $|\hat\rho|$ from 0.70 to 0.99; the synthetic roots go down to $10^{-4}$ and not below.
  For a root near 0 the spacing of doubles is far finer and nothing here says what $\sigma$ is there.
- **The exact-zero start** (lines 311-330, $S(0)=0$) and the frontier bisection of the walk are not in the tests (Result 1 argues
  the latter, and does not bound it when the first trial is unusable). Nor is a trial with a computed score of exactly zero.
- **Unusable points.** The bound counts evaluations to the stopping test on runs whose points are all usable. Status 8 and
  the abort at an unusable $\rho=0$ are outside it.
- **The returned count is not the loop's.** The endpoint check's evaluations are added after the status is decided, so
  `k` in the result can exceed `cap`; only the loop's evaluations are capped.
- **A conditional-mode cap is not a v1 cap.** v1 keeps `cap = 40`; nothing here is evidence about it.

```{r cx-rootcap-summary}
cat(sprintf("\nSUMMARY: %d checks, %d failures\n", rc_ncheck, rc_nfail))
cat(if (rc_nfail == 0) "RESULT: ALL CHECKS PASS\n" else "RESULT: FAILURES (see FAIL lines above)\n")
if (rc_nfail > 0) stop("cx-rootcap: ", rc_nfail, " failed check(s)")
```

## Conditional mode: the stopping rule of the item fit {#sec-condx-itemstop}

**Rendered in the full document 2026-11-11** (quarto 1.10.18, R 4.6.0, Rmpfr 1.1.3, this
machine; every chunk of the file ran, exit 0; the prose banners were edited after that render, no
chunk was). *Drafted by a read-only agent; run by the main session, standalone and then in the render
(13,905 cases, 0 failures both times).* For the render the chunks lost `eval: false`, `mk` became `mkm` (an
earlier chunk owns `mk`), and the root path and the failing exit were made render-safe. The chunks are the bodies of
a verification script of E-096 (its preamble is the `cx-itemstop-setup` chunk, whose MPFR item code is copied from
a reference script of E-096; R 4.6.0, Rmpfr 1.1.3; log beside it, run time in the log).
The figures quoted are that run's. **Every double-precision figure is R doubles with LAPACK's Cholesky,
a stand-in for Mata, not Mata.**

`dwlsmv_cx_item_fit()` (@sec-condx, Item 1) maximises the item's mean log-likelihood $f$ by Newton:
$\theta\leftarrow\theta+\lambda d$, $d=H^{-1}\bar g$. Until 2026-11-11 its stopping rule was on the score: $\max|\bar g|\le10^{-14}$
at iterates 0 to 49, $\le10^{-12}$ at iterate 50, else rc 3498. Neither constant was derived, and the
score bounds the estimate's error only through $\|H^{-1}\|$, which nothing checks
(`item_stop_result.md`). The user's decision of 2026-11-11 is to stop on the Newton step, which
bounds the error directly: stop and return $\theta_k$ when $\|d_k\|_\infty\le\delta_1$ (iterates 0 to
49); at iterate 50 accept when $\|d_k\|_\infty\le\delta_2$; else abort. This section derives what that
certifies (Results 1 to 3), when it can be reached (Result 4), proposes $\delta_1,\delta_2$, and
compares it with the score rule. It changes no estimator: the fitted point is the same maximiser.

**Notation.** One item, $\theta\in\mathbb R^K$ (thresholds, then the slope). $f(\theta)=N^{-1}\sum_{\text{cells}}n_c\log P_c(\theta)$,
$g=\nabla f$ (the code's `gbar`), $H=-\nabla^2f$ (the code's $H_j$, $N$-divided), $d(\theta)=H(\theta)^{-1}g(\theta)$,
$\hat\theta$ the maximiser, $e=\theta-\hat\theta$. $\|\cdot\|$ is the max norm on vectors and the induced
max-row-sum norm on matrices; $\beta(\theta)=\|H(\theta)^{-1}\|$. The tier for $\theta_k$ is
$10^{-8}+10^{-8}|\theta_k|$; everything below is stated against $10^{-8}$, the smaller.
$\varepsilon=2^{-52}$, $u=2^{-53}$.

**Premises.**

- **(C)** $f$ is strictly concave on $\mathcal D=\{$thresholds increasing, every observed cell $P>0\}$, a convex
  open set, so $H(\theta)$ is positive definite on $\mathcal D$ and $\hat\theta$ is the unique maximiser.
  *Cited, not proved here:* the log-likelihood of an ordered-probit cell is concave in the linear bounds (Pratt 1981), and
  the Mata comment says the same. Positive definiteness at the iterates is checked at run time by `cholsolve`.
- **(L)** $H$ is Lipschitz on a ball $\mathcal B$ around $\hat\theta$: $\|H(a)-H(b)\|\le L\|a-b\|$.
  **A premise, measured here, not proved.** No analytic bound is derived. $L$ is the supremum over $\mathcal B$
  of $\|H'(\theta)[v]\|$ over $\|v\|_\infty=1$ (mean-value theorem). The map $v\mapsto\|H'[v]\|$ is convex, so its
  maximum over the cube is at a sign vector.
- **(F1)** The computed score is $\tilde g=g+\epsilon_g$ with $\|\epsilon_g\|\le\gamma$. **(F2)** The computed
  Hessian is $\tilde H=H+E_H$. **(F3)** The Cholesky solve is backward stable: $(\tilde H+\Delta H)\tilde d=\tilde g$.
  Write $\xi\ge\|E_H\|+\|\Delta H\|$. These are premises about the arithmetic. They are **measured**, on R doubles,
  in the `cx-itemstop-double` chunk and not derived.

```{r cx-itemstop-setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Rmpfr))
# the repository root: the working directory when run as a script from it, two
# levels up when this file is rendered (the document's own convention)
ROOT <- if (file.exists(file.path("fixtures", "data", "condx_A.csv"))) "." else file.path("..", "..")
PREC <- 200L; GSTOP <- 1e-50; EPS <- 2^-52
KS   <- c(3L, 3L, 2L)
DATA <- c(A = file.path(ROOT, "fixtures", "data", "condx_A.csv"),
          D = file.path(ROOT, "fixtures", "data", "condx_D.csv"))
stopifnot(all(file.exists(DATA)))
t0 <- Sys.time()
cat(sprintf("verify_itemstop.R  R %s  Rmpfr %s  PREC %d\n", getRversion(),
            packageVersion("Rmpfr"), PREC))

# ---- MPFR primitives, copied from docs/notes/condx-stage1/item_stop_ref.R ----
mkm <- function(v, prec) mpfr(v, precBits = prec)
Phi_m <- function(z, r2) erfc(-z / r2) / 2
dens  <- function(z, r2pi) exp(-z * z / 2) / r2pi
gsolve <- function(A, b) {
  K <- length(b); M <- A; v <- b
  for (c in seq_len(K)) {
    piv <- c - 1L + which.max(vapply(c:K, function(r) as.numeric(abs(M[[r]][c])), 0))
    if (piv != c) { t <- M[[c]]; M[[c]] <- M[[piv]]; M[[piv]] <- t
                    t <- v[c]; v[c] <- v[piv]; v[piv] <- t }
    if (c < K) for (r in (c + 1L):K) {
      f <- M[[r]][c] / M[[c]][c]
      M[[r]] <- M[[r]] - f * M[[c]]; v[r] <- v[r] - f * v[c]
    }
  }
  x <- v
  for (c in K:1) {
    s <- v[c]
    if (c < K) for (k in (c + 1L):K) s <- s - M[[c]][k] * x[k]
    x[c] <- s / M[[c]][c]
  }
  x
}
ginv <- function(A, prec) {
  K <- length(A)
  cols <- lapply(seq_len(K), function(k) { e <- mkm(rep(0, K), prec); e[k] <- mkm(1, prec); gsolve(A, e) })
  lapply(seq_len(K), function(k) { r <- mkm(rep(0, K), prec); for (l in seq_len(K)) r[l] <- cols[[l]][k]; r })
}
item_eval <- function(th, n, K, prec) {
  r2 <- sqrt(mkm(2, prec)); r2pi <- sqrt(2 * Const("pi", prec))
  N <- sum(n); ll <- mkm(0, prec); g <- mkm(rep(0, K), prec)
  H <- lapply(seq_len(K), function(k) mkm(rep(0, K), prec))
  for (xg in 0:1) for (c in 0:(K - 1)) {
    cnt <- n[xg * K + c + 1]
    if (cnt == 0) next
    lofin <- c >= 1; upfin <- c <= K - 2
    al <- mkm(rep(0, K), prec); au <- mkm(rep(0, K), prec)
    al[K] <- mkm(-xg, prec); au[K] <- mkm(-xg, prec)
    fl <- mkm(0, prec); fu <- mkm(0, prec); dl <- mkm(0, prec); du <- mkm(0, prec)
    if (lofin) { l <- th[c] - th[K] * xg; al[c] <- mkm(1, prec); fl <- dens(l, r2pi); dl <- -l * fl }
    if (upfin) { u <- th[c + 1] - th[K] * xg; au[c + 1] <- mkm(1, prec); fu <- dens(u, r2pi); du <- -u * fu }
    if (lofin && l > 0) {
      P <- Phi_m(-l, r2) - (if (upfin) Phi_m(-u, r2) else mkm(0, prec))
    } else {
      P <- (if (upfin) Phi_m(u, r2) else mkm(1, prec)) - (if (lofin) Phi_m(l, r2) else mkm(0, prec))
    }
    if (!(P > 0)) return(NULL)
    w <- mkm(cnt, prec) / N
    ll <- ll + cnt * log(P)
    gc <- (fu * au - fl * al) / P
    g  <- g + w * gc
    for (k in seq_len(K)) {
      dk <- (du * au[k] * au - dl * al[k] * al) / P - gc[k] * gc
      H[[k]] <- H[[k]] - w * dk
    }
  }
  list(ll = ll, g = g, H = H)
}
ok_th <- function(th, K) { if (K <= 2) return(TRUE); all(diff(as.numeric(th[1:(K - 1)])) > 0) }
item_fit <- function(n, K, prec) {
  N <- sum(n); pooled <- n[1:K] + n[(K + 1):(2 * K)]
  th <- mkm(c(qnorm(cumsum(pooled)[-K] / N), 0), prec)
  e <- item_eval(th, n, K, prec); stopifnot(!is.null(e))
  for (it in 0:200) {
    gm <- max(abs(e$g)); if (gm < GSTOP) break
    step <- gsolve(e$H, e$g); lam <- mkm(1, prec); acc <- FALSE
    for (h in 0:60) {
      thn <- th + lam * step
      if (ok_th(thn, K)) { en <- item_eval(thn, n, K, prec)
        if (!is.null(en) && en$ll >= e$ll) { acc <- TRUE; break } }
      lam <- lam / 2
    }
    if (!acc) { thn <- th + step; en <- item_eval(thn, n, K, prec); stopifnot(!is.null(en), max(abs(en$g)) < gm) }
    th <- thn; e <- en
  }
  stopifnot(max(abs(e$g)) < GSTOP)
  list(th = th, H = e$H, g = e$g)
}

# ---- helpers (this file) -----------------------------------------------------
inf_v  <- function(v) as.numeric(max(abs(v)))                       # inf-norm of an mpfr vector
Hnum   <- function(H) t(vapply(H, as.numeric, numeric(length(H))))   # mpfr row list -> double matrix
inf_m  <- function(M) max(rowSums(abs(M)))                           # inf-norm of a double matrix
inf_ml <- function(H) max(vapply(H, function(r) as.numeric(sum(abs(r))), 0)) # same, mpfr row list
ex_pt <- function(it, thd) {                       # exact quantities at the double point thd
  th <- mkm(thd, PREC); e <- item_eval(th, it$n, it$K, PREC); stopifnot(!is.null(e))
  d <- gsolve(e$H, e$g)
  list(th = th, g = e$g, H = e$H, d = d, dn = inf_v(d), beta = inf_ml(ginv(e$H, PREC)))
}

# ---- double-precision evaluator: STAND-IN for dwlsmv_cx_item_eval (NOT Mata) --
item_eval_d <- function(th, n, K) {
  N <- sum(n); g <- numeric(K); H <- matrix(0, K, K); ll <- 0; Ag <- 0
  for (xg in 0:1) for (c in 0:(K - 1)) {
    cnt <- n[xg * K + c + 1]; if (cnt == 0) next
    lofin <- c >= 1; upfin <- c <= K - 2
    al <- numeric(K); au <- numeric(K); al[K] <- -xg; au[K] <- -xg
    l <- 0; u <- 0; fl <- 0; fu <- 0; dl <- 0; du <- 0
    if (lofin) { l <- th[c] - th[K] * xg; al[c] <- 1; fl <- dnorm(l); dl <- -l * fl }
    if (upfin) { u <- th[c + 1] - th[K] * xg; au[c + 1] <- 1; fu <- dnorm(u); du <- -u * fu }
    if (lofin && l > 0) {
      hi <- pnorm(-l); lo <- if (upfin) pnorm(-u) else 0
    } else {
      hi <- if (upfin) pnorm(u) else 1; lo <- if (lofin) pnorm(l) else 0
    }
    P <- hi - lo
    if (!(P > 0)) return(NULL)
    q <- (hi + lo) / P                      # cancellation factor of the subtraction hi - lo
    gc <- (fu * au - fl * al) / P
    D  <- (du * tcrossprod(au) - dl * tcrossprod(al)) / P - tcrossprod(gc)
    w  <- cnt / N
    ll <- ll + cnt * log(P); g <- g + w * gc; H <- H - w * D
    Ag <- Ag + w * max(abs(gc)) * (1 + q)   # A_g: sum of |terms| with their cancellation factor
  }
  list(ll = ll, g = g, H = H, Ag = Ag)
}
chol_step <- function(H, g) {          # Cholesky solve H d = g; NULL if not PD
  R <- tryCatch(chol(H), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(R)) return(NULL)
  backsolve(R, backsolve(R, g, transpose = TRUE))
}

# ---- the items: six real, five constructed ----------------------------------
items <- list()
for (ds in names(DATA)) {
  raw <- read.csv(DATA[[ds]], colClasses = "character")
  stopifnot(identical(names(raw), c("y1", "y2", "y3", "x")), nrow(raw) == 1500L)
  dat <- as.data.frame(lapply(raw, as.integer))
  for (j in 1:3) {
    K <- KS[j]
    n <- as.numeric(table(factor(dat$x * K + dat[[j]] + 1, levels = 1:(2 * K))))
    items[[sprintf("%s_y%d", ds, j)]] <- list(name = sprintf("%s_y%d", ds, j), n = n, K = K, real = TRUE)
  }
}
# CONSTRUCTED AFTER MEASURING (to reach larger ||H^-1||): rare-category tables (N 1500 to 150000).
# Cell order x-major: n[x K + c + 1]. These are not data of the project.
SYN <- list(S_rare1 = list(n = c(745, 4, 700, 51), K = 2L),
            S_rare2 = list(n = c(748, 1, 745, 6),  K = 2L),
            S_rare3 = list(n = c(749, 1, 749, 1),  K = 2L),
            S_rare4 = list(n = c(7499, 1, 7499, 1), K = 2L),
            S_rare5 = list(n = c(74999, 1, 74999, 1), K = 2L),
            S_narrow = list(n = c(700, 1, 49, 600, 1, 149), K = 3L))
for (nm in names(SYN)) {
  stopifnot(all(SYN[[nm]]$n >= 1))
  items[[nm]] <- c(list(name = nm), SYN[[nm]], list(real = FALSE))
}
for (nm in names(items)) {
  it <- items[[nm]]; f <- item_fit(it$n, it$K, PREC)
  items[[nm]]$th <- f$th; items[[nm]]$thd <- as.numeric(f$th)
  Hi <- ginv(f$H, PREC)
  items[[nm]]$beta <- inf_ml(Hi); items[[nm]]$Hn <- Hnum(f$H)
  items[[nm]]$condH <- inf_m(Hnum(f$H)) * items[[nm]]$beta
  cat(sprintf("  item %-8s K %d  max|g| %.1e  ||H^-1||_inf %.4g  ||H||_inf %.4g  cond_inf %.4g\n",
              nm, it$K, inf_v(f$g), items[[nm]]$beta, inf_ml(f$H), items[[nm]]$condH))
}
nfail <- 0L; ncase <- 0L          # global tallies
tally <- function(ok, label) {
  ncase <<- ncase + 1L
  if (!isTRUE(ok)) { nfail <<- nfail + 1L; cat("  FAIL:", label, "\n") }
  invisible(ok)
}
```

### Result 1: the error in terms of the exact Newton step

**Statement.** Let $\theta_k\in\mathcal D$, $\beta=\|H(\theta_k)^{-1}\|$, $h=L\beta\|d_k\|$, with (L) holding on
the ball about $\theta_k$ of radius $r_+=(1+\sqrt{1-2h})/(L\beta)$ (the Kantorovich radius; it contains $\hat\theta$ and the segment to it).
If $h\le\tfrac12$:
$$\|\theta_k-\hat\theta\|\le\frac{2}{1+\sqrt{1-2h}}\,\|d_k\|,\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\frac{2}{1+\sqrt{1-2h}}\le1+h\ \text{ for }h\le0.4.$$
Conversely, with no condition on $h$, $\|d_k\|\le\big(1+\tfrac12L\beta\|e\|\big)\|e\|$. And one more Newton
step lands at $\|e+d_k\|\le\tfrac12L\beta\|e\|^2$ (Corollary 1).

*Proof.* **(a) Mean value.** $g(\hat\theta)=0$, and $\mathcal D$ is convex, so $g(\theta)=-\bar H e$ with
$\bar H=\int_0^1H(\hat\theta+te)\,dt$, positive definite as an average of positive definite matrices.
Hence $d=H^{-1}g=-H^{-1}\bar He$ at $\theta=\theta_k$, and
$$e+d=H^{-1}(H-\bar H)\,e,\qquad \|H-\bar H\|\le\int_0^1L(1-t)\|e\|\,dt=\tfrac12L\|e\|.$$
**(b) Both inequalities.** From (a), $\|e\|\le\|d\|+\tfrac12L\beta\|e\|^2$ and $\|d\|\le\|e\|+\tfrac12L\beta\|e\|^2$.
The second is the converse. Corollary 1 is $\|e+d\|\le\tfrac12L\beta\|e\|^2$. **(c) Removing the quadratic.**
The first inequality alone gives $\|e\|\le r_-$ or $\|e\|\ge r_+$, where $r_\pm=(1\pm\sqrt{1-2h})/(L\beta)$. The
second branch is excluded by the Newton-Kantorovich theorem (Kantorovich 1948; Ortega and Rheinboldt 1970, 12.6.2,
**cited, not proved here**): its hypotheses are those of the statement, and it gives a zero of $g$ in the closed
ball of radius $r_-$, unique in the open ball of radius $r_+$. By (C) that zero is $\hat\theta$. Finally
$r_-=\|d\|(1-\sqrt{1-2h})/h=2\|d\|/(1+\sqrt{1-2h})$. **(d)** $2/(1+\sqrt{1-2h})=(1-\sqrt{1-2h})/h=\sum_nC_n(h/2)^n$,
the Catalan series, with positive coefficients, so it is convex; it equals $1+h$ at $h=0$ and is below it at
$h=0.4$ ($1.382<1.4$), hence below it on $[0,0.4]$. ∎

**When the correction is negligible.** The factor exceeds 1 by $\eta\approx h/2$, $h=L\beta\|d_k\|\le L\beta\delta$
at a stop. With $L$ and $\beta$ as measured below, $h\le L\beta\delta\le2.3\times10^{-10}$ on the six real items at $\delta=10^{-12}$; the factor is 1 to
nine digits. A correction of $10^{-6}$ relative needs $L\beta\delta\approx2\times10^{-6}$, that is $L\beta\approx2\times10^{6}$
at $\delta=10^{-12}$. The constructed `S_narrow` item (a rare middle category, $\|H\|=63$,
$L\approx10^5$) has $L\beta\approx3\times10^6$ and $h\approx3\times10^{-6}$ at $10^{-12}$.

**Measured** (`cx-itemstop-lip`, `cx-itemstop-exact`). Twelve items: the six of `condx_A` and `condx_D` and six
constructed tables (not project data; **constructed after measuring** to reach larger $\|H^{-1}\|$ and larger $\|H\|$):
rare-category binary items with $N=1500$ to $150000$, $\|H^{-1}\|$ up to $2.3\times10^4$, and `S_narrow`.

| item | $\beta=\|H^{-1}\|$ | $\|H\|$ | $L$ at $\hat\theta$ | $L$ sampled sup, radius 0.25 | $L$ used (×1.25) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A_y1, A_y2, A_y3 | 9.39, 9.55, 9.34 | 1.17, 1.19, 0.88 | 2.4, 2.7, 0.05 | 13.5, 18.1, 0.14 | 16.8, 22.7, 0.17 |
| D_y1, D_y2, D_y3 | 9.33, 9.52, 9.55 | 1.03, 1.13, 0.86 | 1.8, 2.4, 0.23 | 7.3, 14.0, 0.31 | 9.1, 17.5, 0.39 |
| S_rare1 to S_rare5 | 98, 311, 416, 2975, 23070 | 0.29 to 0.0004 | 0.53 to 0.002 | 0.60 to 0.012 | 0.75 to 0.015 |
| S_narrow | 26.4 | 62.8 | $3.8\times10^4$ | $3.8\times10^4$ | $4.8\times10^4$ |

The Lipschitz premise itself was checked directly on 170 random pairs in the balls (none exceeds $L$ used). The
sampled sup is over 25 to 29 points per item (the ball's corners and random points whose thresholds stay ordered;
`S_narrow`'s ball is cut to a sliver by the ordering, its two thresholds being about 0.006 apart).

The bound was tested at 2120 double-precision points $\theta_k=\hat\theta+sv$, $s=10^{-1},\dots,10^{-13}$, in the
$2^K$ sign directions, six random directions and $\pm$ the softest eigenvector of $H$, with $e$ and $d$ exact
(200-bit MPFR; $\theta_k$ is a double, so $e$ is its exact distance). **Result.** 1788 of the 2120 points lie inside the premise $h\le\tfrac12$ (with $L$ used). At all
1788 the bound $\|e\|\le2/(1+\sqrt{1-2h})\|d\|$ held, and $\|e\|\le(1+h)\|d\|$ held at all of those with $h\le0.4$. The converse
$\|d\|\le(1+\tfrac12L\beta\|e\|)\|e\|$ held at all 2120. The other 332 points (the large perturbations, on the items with large
$L\beta$) are outside the theorem and are not tested against it. Inside the premise $\|e\|/\|d\|$ lies in
$[0.965,\,1.006]$, against the permitted factor up to 2: the largest $(r-1)/h$ is 0.044, so the realised correction
used 4% of $h$ (the small-$h$ limit is $\tfrac12$ with the *local* $L$; the sampled supremum over the ball is several
times the local value). At $s=10^{-10}$ the largest $\|e\|/\|d\|-1$ is $4.8\times10^{-8}$.

```{r cx-itemstop-lip}
# The Lipschitz constant L of H (inf-norm) near theta-hat. A PREMISE of Result 1, MEASURED here, not
# proved: L is the sup over a ball of ||H'(theta)[v]||_inf over ||v||_inf = 1. The map v -> ||H'[v]||_inf is
```
