```{r deltad-core}
  exp(-(a * a - 2 * r * a * b + b * b) / (2 * (1 - r * r))) / (2 * pi * sqrt(1 - r * r))
dd_N  <- function(a, b, r) if (r >= 0) (a - b)^2 + 2 * (1 - r) * a * b else (a + b)^2 - 2 * (1 + r) * a * b
dd_sN <- function(a, b, r) exp(-dd_N(a, b, r) / (2 * (1 - r * r))) / (2 * pi * sqrt(1 - r * r))
dd_s2 <- function(a, b, r) { s2 <- (1 - r) * (1 + r); exp(-dd_N(a, b, r) / (2 * s2)) / (2 * pi * sqrt(s2)) }
# The corrected per-corner model (relative) for production's expression: the numerator's
# error over 2(1 - rho rho), the denominator's 1 - rho rho, exp, and the rest.
dd_dDc <- function(a, b, r, z) { s2 <- 1 - r * r; mag <- a^2 + 2 * abs(r * a * b) + b^2
  dd_eps * (2 * mag / s2 + abs(z) * (1 + 1 / s2) + 1 / (2 * s2) + 7) }
dd_corners <- function(a, b, r) {
  g <- expand.grid(a = a, b = b)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(g)), function(k) {
    x <- g$a[k]; y <- g$b[k]; ref <- dd_mp(x, y, r)
    rel <- function(f) asNumeric(abs(f(x, y, r) - ref) / ref)
    z <- (x * x - 2 * r * x * y + y * y) / (2 * (1 - r * r))
    data.frame(rho = r, a = x, b = y, phi = asNumeric(ref), z = z,
               cancel = (x^2 + 2 * abs(r * x * y) + y^2) / abs(dd_N(x, y, r)),
               naive = rel(dd_naive), sN = rel(dd_sN), s2 = rel(dd_s2), dD = dd_eps * (abs(z) + 7),
               dDc = dd_dDc(x, y, r, z))
  }))
}
dd_D <- function(f) function(a, b, rho) {               # rectangle differences, as production
  A <- c(-Inf, a, Inf); B <- c(-Inf, b, Inf)
  G <- outer(A, B, Vectorize(function(p, q) if (!is.finite(p) || !is.finite(q)) 0 else f(p, q, rho)))
  G[-1, -1] - G[-nrow(G), -1] - G[-1, -ncol(G)] + G[-nrow(G), -ncol(G)]
}
dd_Dmp <- function(a, b, rho) {                          # reference D, differenced in 256 bits
  A <- c(-Inf, a, Inf); B <- c(-Inf, b, Inf); G <- matrix(list(), length(A), length(B))
  for (r in seq_along(A)) for (s in seq_along(B))
    G[[r, s]] <- if (is.finite(A[r]) && is.finite(B[s])) dd_mp(A[r], B[s], rho) else mpfr(0, dd_prec)
  outer(seq_len(length(A) - 1), seq_len(length(B) - 1), Vectorize(function(r, s)
    asNumeric(G[[r + 1, s + 1]] - G[[r, s + 1]] - G[[r + 1, s]] + G[[r, s]])))
}
dd_Dnaive <- dd_D(dd_naive); dd_Ds2 <- dd_D(dd_s2)
# The score's error from D alone (pi held fixed), against tau_S and against its delta_D part.
dd_gap <- function(n, a, b, x) {
  P <- cellP(a, b, x); O <- n > 0; w <- n[O] / sum(n); e <- rf_eval(n, a, b, x); Dm <- dd_Dmp(a, b, x)
  c(gap = abs(sum(w * (dd_Dnaive(a, b, x)[O] - Dm[O]) / P[O])),
    gap_s2 = abs(sum(w * (dd_Ds2(a, b, x)[O] - Dm[O]) / P[O])),
    tauS = e$tauS, tauS_D = sum(w * dd_eps * rf_absD(a, b, x)[O] / P[O]))
}

# (1)-(2) Every pair of the 20 replicates: corners, score gap, and the root-finder run
# with production's density and with the stable one (N_s and (1 - rho)(1 + rho)).
dd_pairs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(rf_pairs)), function(k) {
  p <- rf_pairs[k, ]; q <- rf_pair(p$cond, p$rep, p$i, p$j)
  r0 <- rf_root(q$n, q$a, q$b); r1 <- rf_root(q$n, q$a, q$b, dS = dd_Ds2)
  ct <- dd_corners(q$a, q$b, r0$rho); ct <- ct[ct$phi > 1e-290, ]   # drop underflowing corners
  data.frame(cond = p$cond, rep = p$rep, i = p$i, j = p$j, rho = r0$rho,
             case = r0$case, case_s2 = r1$case, evals = r0$evals, evals_s2 = r1$evals,
             drho = r1$rho - r0$rho, ulp = rf_ulp(r0$rho),
             cancel = max(ct$cancel), over_dD = max(ct$naive / ct$dD), over_dDc = max(ct$naive / ct$dDc), t(dd_gap(q$n, q$a, q$b, r0$rho)))
}))
# (2) A stress beyond the data: population tables (counts round(1e6 pi)) with equal
# thresholds, b = sign(rho) a, up to B and at -B; thresholds within [-2.5, 2.5].
dd_stress <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.99, 0.995, 0.998, 0.999, -0.999), function(r)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(list(0, 1, 2, 2.5, c(-1, 1), c(-2.5, 0, 2.5), qnorm(c(.15, .5, .8))), function(t) {
    a <- t; b <- sign(r) * t; n <- round(1e6 * pmax(cellP(a, b, r), 0)); g <- dd_gap(n, a, b, r)
    data.frame(rho = r, thr = paste(round(t, 2), collapse = " "),
               gap_tauS = g[["gap"]] / g[["tauS"]], gap_tauS_D = g[["gap"]] / g[["tauS_D"]]) }))))
# (3) Accuracy grid, no data: a in [0.1, 2.5], b = sign(rho) a (1 + d).
dd_grid <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.5, 0.9, 0.99, 0.998, 0.999, 0.9999, -0.99, -0.999), function(r)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5), function(a)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0, 1e-3, 1e-2, 0.1), function(d) dd_corners(a, sign(r) * a * (1 + d), r)))))))
dd_grid_max <- aggregate(cbind(naive, sN, s2, naive / dD, sN / dD, s2 / dD) ~ rho, dd_grid, max)
```

```{r deltad-assert}
I <- dd_pairs[dd_pairs$case == "root", ]
aggregate(cbind(cancel, over_dD, gap / tauS, gap / tauS_D, gap_s2 / tauS) ~ cond, dd_pairs, max)
table(dd_pairs$case, dd_pairs$case_s2)
c(max_drho_ulps = max(abs(I$drho) / I$ulp), max_devals = max(abs(I$evals_s2 - I$evals)),
  stress_gap_tauS = max(dd_stress$gap_tauS), stress_gap_tauS_D = max(dd_stress$gap_tauS_D))
dd_grid_max
stopifnot(nrow(I) == 116, sum(dd_pairs$case == "no sign change up to the bound") == 4,
          dd_pairs$case == dd_pairs$case_s2,              # same outcome with the stable density
          abs(I$drho) <= 4 * I$ulp,
          max(dd_pairs$over_dD) > 10,                     # the regime is reached: delta_D exceeded per corner
          max(dd_pairs$gap / dd_pairs$tauS) < 1e-2,       # ... yet tau_S bounds the score's D error
          max(dd_stress$gap_tauS) < 1e-2,
          max(dd_grid$s2 / dd_grid$dD) <= 1,              # the stable form is within delta_D's model
          max(dd_grid$sN / dd_grid$dD) > 10,              # N_s alone is not
          max(dd_pairs$over_dDc) <= 1,                    # the corrected model covers production
          max(dd_grid$naive / dd_grid$dDc) <= 1)
c(pairs_over_dDc = max(dd_pairs$over_dDc), grid_over_dDc = max(dd_grid$naive / dd_grid$dDc))
```

Results.

**1. Reachability: yes.** The 120 pairs are evaluated at their fitted $\hat\rho$.
Corners whose $\phi_2$ underflows below $10^{-290}$ are excluded: their relative error
is meaningless and they contribute nothing to $D$. The largest cancellation factor is
1999 in `mc_c_999` (equal thresholds, $\hat\rho=0.999$), 1106 in `mc_c_998`, 522 in
`mc_B_9975` and 234 in `mc_B_995`. The measured per-corner error of $\phi_2$ exceeds
$\delta_D$'s $\varepsilon(|z|+7)$ by up to 64× (`mc_c_998`), 37× (`mc_B_9975`) and 12×
(`mc_B_995`). These figures use $\varepsilon=2^{-52}$, as `rf_absD` does.
`@sec-condx-hess` used the unit roundoff $2^{-53}$ and other points, so its 349× is not
the same figure. **The score's error is still far inside $\tau_S$.** With $\pi$ held
fixed, $\bar S$ from production's $D$ differs from $\bar S$ from the 256-bit $D$ by at
most **0.0042 $\tau_S$** (`mc_c_998`). The gap is at most 0.78 of the $\delta_D$ share
of $\tau_S$ alone. Two reasons explain this. The $\delta_P$ term dominates $\tau_S$ in
this regime. And the corners with the largest relative error lie near the diagonal,
where $|\phi_2|$ is large, so $\delta_D$'s $|\phi_2|$ weighting is already generous
there. On population tables with equal thresholds up to $|\rho|=B$, including
$\rho=-B$ with $b=-a$, the gap is at most $2.3\times10^{-4}\,\tau_S$.

**2. Stopping behaviour: nothing changes.** `rf_root()` gives the same outcome on all
120 pairs with the stable density as with production's: 116 roots, and 4 "no sign
change up to the bound", the `mc_c_999` bound pairs. $\hat\rho$ moves by at most
4.4e-16, within 4 ulps, and the evaluation count by at most one. **Neither an
evaluation cap nor a wrong root occurs.** The earlier reading, an evaluation cap rather
than a wrong root, described a failure that does not happen at these magnitudes. The
density's error is more than two orders of magnitude below $\tau_S$, so it cannot move
$|\bar S|$ across the tolerance. Level R1 had already run these pairs with production's
density, and every interior pair converged. What it lacked was a reference for this
error: Level R1c replaced $\pi$ only, and this section replaces $D$. The measurement
uses R's `exp`, not Mata's. A Stata probe would change the conclusion only if Mata's
density erred about 100 times more than R's, so none was run. If one is wanted, it
would evaluate `dwlsmv_dcellprob_rho` on these pairs at their $\hat\rho$ and compare
against an exported 256-bit $D$ by the same gap/$\tau_S$ ratio.

**3. The proposed exponent alone does not cure it.** The largest relative error on the
grid, as a multiple of $\delta_D$'s model:

| ρ | production | $N_s$ only | $N_s$ and $(1-\rho)(1+\rho)$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.9 | 1.7× | 0.21 | 0.21 |
| 0.99 | 12× | 0.95 | 0.21 |
| 0.998 | 79× | 2.8× | 0.30 |
| 0.999 | 84× | 46× | 0.63 |
| 0.9999 | 1164× | 1080× | 0.50 |
| −0.999 | 84× | 46× | 0.63 |

At $|\rho|\ge0.999$ the remaining error comes from $1-\rho\cdot\rho$: rounding $\rho^2$
costs $\varepsilon/(1-\rho^2)$ relative. $\delta_D$'s model holds everywhere only with
both changes, and then the largest error is 0.63 of the model. The same
$1-\rho\cdot\rho$ appears in `sig`, the normalising $\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$, so a fix would
change both. On these 120 pairs it would change nothing observable: $\hat\rho$ stays
within 4 ulps and every status is the same. It would make $\delta_D$'s stated model
true, where today it holds only because the $\delta_P$ term's margin covers it.

Tolerances. Set before running: the same outcome on every pair, and
$|\Delta\hat\rho|\le4$ ulps. **Chosen after measuring:** the $10^{-2}$ ceiling on
gap/$\tau_S$ (measured 0.0042), and the "> 10" thresholds showing that the regime is
reached and that $N_s$ alone falls short (measured 64 and 1080).

**The corrected model (decided by the user, 2026-10-25: the stated model is corrected;
the production density and $\tau_S$'s code are unchanged).** For production's
expression, with $s^2=1-\rho\cdot\rho$ and $m=a^2+2|\rho ab|+b^2$, the relative error
of a computed $\phi_2$ corner is bounded by
$$\varepsilon\Bigl(\frac{2m}{s^2} + |z|\Bigl(1+\frac1{s^2}\Bigr) + \frac1{2s^2} + 7\Bigr).$$
The four terms are:

- **$2m/s^2$:** the numerator's rounding, about $\varepsilon m$ absolute, divided by
  $2s^2$. It is the exponent cancellation. Against $|z|$ it is the cancellation
  factor $m/N$ times larger.
- **$|z|(1+1/s^2)$:** the rounding of $\rho^2$ in $1-\rho\cdot\rho$, amplified by
  $1/s^2$, plus `exp`'s amplification of $z$'s own rounding. This is the term a stable
  exponent alone leaves (46× at $\rho=0.999$).
- **$1/(2s^2)$:** the same $s^2$ inside the normaliser $\sqrt{s^2}$.
- **7:** the remaining arithmetic and the three additions, as before.

The model is the same in form as `@sec-condx-hess`'s exponent model, with the constant
of $\delta_D$ kept. The production expression's measured error is within 0.24 of it on
every non-underflowing corner of the 120 pairs, and within 0.19 on the grid (asserted:
at most 1). $\delta_{D,rs}$ in this corrected form is $\varepsilon\sum_{\text{corners}}|\phi_2|$ times the
bracket. **v1 keeps computing the old $\delta_D$ in $\tau_S$.** That $\tau_S$ covers the
score's density error with a measured margin of more than 200×, from the $\delta_P$
term, but no derivation guarantees that margin. The stable density was not adopted. A
consumer that needs a per-corner bound, such as `@sec-condx-hess`'s $\tau_U$, uses the
corrected model.

## Conditional mode: the full fit against lavaan {#sec-condx-full}

**Executed 2026-10-25** in a side session (R 4.5.2, base R; lavaan 0.7.2 only through the
committed fixtures of `fixtures/generate/99i_lavaan_condx_fit.R`). This is item 4b of the
work order (E-006, 2026-10-24). The chunks below were run after
`cx-setup`, `cx-stage1`, `cx-model`, `cxn-psi` and `cxn-lavaan`, which they build on. **It
decides nothing.** The normaliser is decided (Hessian, 2026-10-25), and so is the sample-size
divisor, which this section only confirms for the mode.

The model is `@sec-condx`'s, on the committed `condx_A` data ($N=1500$): $y_1,y_2,y_3$ on
one factor, $f\sim x$, $\psi=1$. lavaan is fitted with WLSMV, delta, `conditional.x = TRUE`,
`std.lv = TRUE`, `zero.add = c(0.5, 0)` and `zero.keep.margins = TRUE`. Ours is DWLS with
$W_D=\operatorname{diag}(\hat\Gamma)^{-1}$, fitted once with each normaliser's $\hat\Gamma$
from the same $s$.

### Results

| Quantity | BHHH against lavaan | Hessian against lavaan | Tolerance (BHHH) |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\hat\theta$, max abs | 1.8e-8 | 2.0e-4 (loadings, γ); thresholds 0 | 1e-5 abs + 1e-4 rel |
| SE, max rel | 4.0e-8 | up to 3.4% ($\tau_{2,2}$); γ 0.055%; binary item's τ 0 | 1e-5 rel + 1e-8 abs |
| $T$, rel | 5.5e-7 | −0.27% | 1e-5 rel + 1e-6 abs |
| $a$, rel | 2.4e-9 | −0.31% | 1e-5 rel |
| $b$, abs | 8.4e-10 | −0.0030 (−15% rel; $b=0.019$) | 1e-6 abs |
| $T_3$, rel | 5.4e-7 | −0.78% | 1e-5 rel + 1e-6 abs |
| df | 2 = 2 | 2 | exact |

**C1. Point estimates.** Under BHHH they equal lavaan's to its optimiser tolerance, which
is the same 3e-8 at which $s$ agrees (`@sec-condx-norm`). The point estimate depends on the
normaliser **only through $W_D$**: $\hat\Gamma$'s diagonal differs between the two forms by
up to 6.5% here, and the model does not fit exactly ($F_M>0$, df = 2), so a different
weighting moves $\hat\lambda$ and $\hat\gamma$, by 2.0e-4 here. That is a weighting effect
of order (misfit) × (weight change), not an optimiser gap. The thresholds do not move:
$\hat\tau=s_\tau$ under any diagonal $W$, since τ enters no other row and the fit is
single-group with no invariance constraint (`@sec-marker-recovery` Result 5). The binary
item's own Γ̂ entries are identical under both forms (its univariate model is saturated;
`@sec-condx-norm`), and so is its threshold SE.

**C2. SEs.** BHHH matches lavaan; the Hessian form differs by up to 3.4% on one
threshold, and by under 1% on the loadings and γ. That is the expected $O(N^{-1/2})$
convention gap of `@sec-condx-norm` N1 ($\sqrt N\times$ 3.4% ≈ 1.3, the size of N1's rate
table). It is not an error in either. Production follows the decided Hessian form and so
**will not reproduce lavaan's SEs** in this mode; the gap shrinks with $N$ under a correct
Stage 1, and under a misspecified Stage 1 the Hessian form is the one that is right.

**C3. T and T₃.** $T$, $a$ and $b$ under BHHH match lavaan. Under the Hessian form $T$
moves only through $\hat\theta$ and $W_D$ (0.27%); $a$ and $b$ move through $U\Gamma$ as
well. $b$ is small in absolute terms here (0.019), so a 0.003 shift is 15% relative.

**C4. The divisor.** lavaan's $T$ is $(N-1)\,r'W_Dr$ and its SEs are
$\sqrt{\mathrm{ACOV}/(N-1)}$, with ACOV built from the $N$-divided Γ̂ that
`lavInspect(fit, "gamma")` reports. With $N$ in place of $N-1$, SE and $T$ would miss by
$1/(2N)$ and $1/N$ relative (3.3e-4 and 6.7e-4), outside their tiers. So v1's decided
convention (T = (N−1)F, e(V) = ACOV/(N−1); decisions 2026-09-23, E-038) **carries over to the mode
unchanged**. $a$ and $b$ are invariant to the divisor, since they are invariant to
rescaling Γ̂. Two incidental readings: lavaan's `fmin` is $T/(2N)$, not $r'W_Dr/2$; and its
`x ~~ x` (0.24120) divides by $N-1$. The latter enters nothing in this mode, because x is
conditioned on.

**C5. The estimand mapping.** lavaan's `f ~ x` is our γ and its `y|t` are our thresholds
at $x=0$, with no transformation: both fits agree on them to 1.8e-8. γ is the effect of x
on f in units of $\sqrt\psi=\mathrm{SD}(f\mid x)=1$ (`@sec-condx`). lavaan's `y ~~ y` is
derived, not free, and equals $1-\hat\lambda_j^2\psi$ (to 2.5e-8 against our
$\hat\lambda$, the size of the two fits' agreement), because the delta parameterization fixes $\operatorname{Var}(y^*\mid x)=1$.
lavaan prints no SE for it; ours derives none either (Θ is never free).

**C6. Admissibility is conditional on x.** In conditional mode $\operatorname{Var}(y_j^*\mid x)=1$, so
$\theta_{jj}=1-(\Lambda\Phi\Lambda')_{jj}$ with $\Phi=(I-B)^{-1}\Psi(I-B)^{-\top}$ the conditional (residual)
covariance of the factors given $x$, and the residual correlation matrix of the $\rho$ rows is
$\Lambda\Phi\Lambda'+\Theta$. Module 7's conditions (derived $\theta_{jj}\ge 0$, factor correlations in
$[-1,1]$, $\Phi$ and that matrix positive definite, $I-B$ nonsingular, thresholds increasing) are therefore
conditions on these conditional quantities. $\gamma$ and $\kappa$ enter only the slope rows
$b=\Lambda(I-B)^{-1}\gamma+\kappa$, which carry no scale constraint, so they do not enter any of them.

**Not covered.** One binary x, one group and a correct Stage 1. The Hessian–lavaan gap is
measured at one $N$; its rate is N1's. Several covariates, a continuous x and κ are not
compared to lavaan here.

Tolerances. Every BHHH comparison uses the spec §7.2 tiers (decisions 2026-09-24, E-032),
set before this run. The checks that the $N$ divisor would fail them are their negative
controls. The Hessian rows are reported, not equated. Their assertions (each gap larger
than the BHHH tier, and below 10% for SEs and T₃) were **chosen after measuring**: they
record the measured size, and are not a tolerance.

```{r cxfull-fit}
# Item 4b: the full DWLS fit on condx_A under both normalisers, against lavaan
# 0.7.2's WLSMV fit (fixtures of 99i_lavaan_condx_fit.R). theta = (tau,
# lambda, gamma), psi = 1; lavaan's labels are mapped onto that order.
# Divisor: T = (N - 1) r'Wr and e(V) = ACOV / (N - 1) (decisions 2026-09-23, E-038);
# the N-divided versions are kept as negative controls.
N_A <- nrow(datA)
lav_e <- rd("expected/lavaan_condx_fit_est.csv")
lav_e$est <- as.numeric(lav_e$est); lav_e$se <- as.numeric(lav_e$se)
lav_t <- rd("expected/lavaan_condx_fit_test.csv")
lav_t <- setNames(as.numeric(lav_t$value), lav_t$quantity)
lab <- paste0(lav_e$lhs, lav_e$op, lav_e$rhs)
th_lab <- c("y1|t1", "y1|t2", "y2|t1", "y2|t2", "y3|t1",
            "f=~y1", "f=~y2", "f=~y3", "f~x")
lav_th <- lav_e$est[match(th_lab, lab)]; lav_se <- lav_e$se[match(th_lab, lab)]
cxa_fit <- function(G, start) {
  W <- diag(1 / diag(G)); th <- start
  for (it in 1:200) {
    r <- fitA$s - cx_sig_th(th); D <- cx_delta(th)
    step <- drop(solve(t(D) %*% W %*% D, t(D) %*% W %*% r))
    th <- th + step
    if (max(abs(step)) < 1e-14) break
  }
  D <- cx_delta(th); B <- solve(t(D) %*% W %*% D)
  acov <- B %*% t(D) %*% W %*% G %*% W %*% D %*% B      # ACOV of sqrt(N)(theta-hat)
  r <- fitA$s - cx_sig_th(th)
  U <- W - W %*% D %*% B %*% t(D) %*% W
  UG <- U %*% G; df <- length(r) - length(th)
  a <- sqrt(df / sum(diag(UG %*% UG))); b <- df - a * sum(diag(UG))
  F <- drop(t(r) %*% W %*% r)
  list(th = th, se = sqrt(diag(acov) / (N_A - 1)), se_N = sqrt(diag(acov) / N_A),
       T = (N_A - 1) * F, T_N = N_A * F, a = a, b = b, T3 = a * (N_A - 1) * F + b,
       df = df, W = diag(W))
}
fb <- cxa_fit(GA_b, th0); fh <- cxa_fit(GA_h, th0)
# C1: point estimates, and W_D's diagonal (relative) between the normalisers
gap_th_b <- max(abs(fb$th - lav_th)); gap_th_h <- max(abs(fh$th - lav_th))
gap_tau_bh <- max(abs(fh$th[1:nt] - fb$th[1:nt]))
gap_W <- max(abs(fh$W / fb$W - 1))
# C2, C4: SEs, relative; the N divisor as negative control
rse_b <- abs(fb$se / lav_se - 1); rse_h <- fh$se / lav_se - 1
rse_b_N <- max(abs(fb$se_N / lav_se - 1))
# C3: T, a, b, T3; lavaan's scaling.factor is 1 / a, its shift.parameter is b
lav_tst <- c(T = lav_t[["chisq"]], a = 1 / lav_t[["scaling.factor"]],
             b = lav_t[["shift.parameter"]], T3 = lav_t[["chisq.scaled"]])
tst <- function(f) c(T = f$T, a = f$a, b = f$b, T3 = f$T3)
d_b <- tst(fb) - lav_tst; d_h <- tst(fh) - lav_tst
rT_N <- abs(fb$T_N / lav_tst[["T"]] - 1)
gap_fmin <- abs(lav_t[["chisq"]] - 2 * N_A * lav_t[["fmin"]]) / lav_t[["chisq"]]
# C5: lavaan's residual variances are 1 - lambda^2 psi (psi = 1), derived;
# its x variance divides by N - 1
lav_rv <- lav_e$est[match(c("y1~~y1", "y2~~y2", "y3~~y3"), lab)]
gap_rv <- max(abs(lav_rv - (1 - fb$th[nt + 1:cx_p]^2)))
vx <- mean(datA$x) * (1 - mean(datA$x))
gap_vx <- abs(lav_e$est[lab == "x~~x"] - vx * N_A / (N_A - 1))
```

```{r cxfull-assert}
tier <- function(d, ref, rel, abs = 0) all(abs(d) <= rel * abs(ref) + abs)
stopifnot(
  lav_t[["N"]] == N_A, lav_t[["df"]] == fb$df, lav_t[["df.scaled"]] == fb$df,
  # BHHH against lavaan, spec 7.2 tiers (set before running)
  tier(fb$th - lav_th, lav_th, 1e-4, 1e-5),
  tier(fb$se - lav_se, lav_se, 1e-5, 1e-8),
  tier(d_b["T"], lav_tst["T"], 1e-5, 1e-6), tier(d_b["T3"], lav_tst["T3"], 1e-5, 1e-6),
  tier(d_b["a"], lav_tst["a"], 1e-5), abs(d_b["b"]) <= 1e-6,
  # negative controls: the N divisor fails the same tiers
  rse_b_N > 1e-5, rT_N > 1e-5,
  # thresholds equal s_tau under either W_D
  gap_tau_bh < 1e-12,
  # C5 and incidental readings (rounding-level; 1e-7 chosen after measuring 2.5e-8)
  gap_rv < 1e-7, gap_fmin < 1e-12, gap_vx < 1e-12,
  # Hessian form: a real gap, beyond the BHHH tier, and below 10% (both
  # chosen after measuring; a record of size, not a tolerance)
  gap_th_h > 1e-5, max(abs(rse_h)) > 1e-3, max(abs(rse_h)) < 0.1,
  abs(d_h["T3"] / lav_tst["T3"]) > 1e-3, abs(d_h["T3"] / lav_tst["T3"]) < 0.1)
```

**Factor reflection with a covariate (added 2026-11-13; prose only, not re-rendered).** Let $D$ be a
diagonal matrix of $pm1$. Replacing $ambda	oambda d$, $b	o dbd$, $psi	o dpsi d$ and
$gamma_x	o dgamma_x$ leaves $ambda(i-b)^{-1}gamma_x$ unchanged, because
$(i-dbd)^{-1}=d(i-b)^{-1}d$ and $d^2=i$; $k$ does not involve the factors and is unchanged, and the
correlations are unchanged as without a covariate. so $sigma(	heta)$ is invariant exactly when the γ of a
reversed factor changes sign with its loadings. a γ fixed at a nonzero value cannot change sign, so such a
factor is not reflectable. the sign canonicalization after the fit follows this (`dwlsmv_signcanon()`).

## Conditional mode: the unit-variance to marker transform {#sec-condx-recovery}

This section extends `@sec-marker-recovery` (Results 1 to 5) to the model of `@sec-condx`: one
binary $x$, one group, with the effects of $x$ on the factors ($\gamma$, ptype 8) and on the
items ($\kappa$, ptype 9). The owner decided on 2026-11-15 to build recovery in conditional mode,
with E4 below, no retry on the first marker fit, and a trigger of non-convergence or an admissibility flag (whether the bread-rank row joins it is open, as is a cutoff for $c_f$).

### Setting

The model is `@sec-condx` Item 4, with $M=(I-B)^{-1}$:
$$y^*=\Lambda\eta+\kappa x+\varepsilon,\qquad \eta=\Gamma x+B\eta+\zeta,\qquad
\operatorname{Var}\zeta=\Psi,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(y^*\mid x)=1,$$
$$\sigma(\theta)=(\tau,\;b,\;\rho),\qquad
b=\Lambda M\Gamma+\kappa,\qquad \rho=\operatorname{offdiag}(\Lambda\Phi\Lambda'),\quad
\Phi=M\Psi M^\top,\qquad \Theta_{jj}=1-(\Lambda\Phi\Lambda')_{jj}.$$
$\Gamma$ is the vector of $\gamma_f$ (ptype 8, row $=$ factor, column $=$ covariate) and $\kappa$ the
vector of $\kappa_j$ (ptype 9, row $=$ indicator, column $=$ covariate). Both are per unit of $x$.
$\Phi$ here is the **conditional** covariance of the factors given $x$; the total covariance
of the factors is $\Phi+q(1-q)\,M\Gamma\Gamma^\top M^\top$ for $P(x=1)=q$, and nothing in
$\sigma$ depends on it.

As in `@sec-marker-recovery`, $\mathcal M$ is the requested marker model (each factor $f$ has a
marker $m(f)$, $\lambda_{m(f)f}=1$ fixed, $\psi_{ff}$ free) and $\mathcal U(\mathcal M)$ the same
model with $\lambda_{m(f)f}$ free and $\psi_{ff}=1$ fixed. The rows $\gamma_{fk}$ and $\kappa_{jk}$
are the same rows in both tables, free or fixed alike. The free sets differ by exactly one
swap per factor, as before, so $J$ below is square (19 against 19 in the verification model).

**What unit variance fixes when $x$ predicts the factor.** A factor with any $\gamma$ (free or
fixed nonzero) or any path from $x$ is endogenous. `unitvariance` fixes $\psi_{ff}$, the
disturbance variance, which is $\operatorname{Var}(\eta_f\mid x, \text{other predictors})$. It
does not fix the total variance, which is $\psi_{ff}+q(1-q)\gamma_f^2+\dots$ and depends on the
treatment proportion $q$. This is spec §4.8's rule applied without change; the verification
model shows it numerically (UV total $\operatorname{Var}(F_1)=1.0194=1+\gamma_1^2q(1-q)$ at
$q=0.4$, a value that is not 1).

### Result C1: the map, and $\sigma$ is exactly unchanged

For any unit-variance point $\theta_U$ with $c_f:=\lambda^U_{m(f)f}\neq0$ (either sign), let
$D=\operatorname{diag}(c_f)$ and $\eta^M=D\eta^U$. Then
$$\Lambda^M=\Lambda^UD^{-1},\quad B^M=DB^UD^{-1},\quad \Psi^M=D\Psi^UD,\quad
\boxed{\Gamma^M=D\,\Gamma^U},\quad \boxed{\kappa^M=\kappa^U},\quad \tau^M=\tau^U,$$
because $y^*=\Lambda^UD^{-1}(D\eta^U)+\kappa x+\varepsilon$ and
$D\eta=(DBD^{-1})D\eta+D\Gamma x+D\zeta$. Elementwise (row $f$, column $g$ for $\beta$ and $\psi$):
$$\lambda_{jf}\mapsto\lambda_{jf}/c_f,\quad \beta_{fg}\mapsto\beta_{fg}c_f/c_g,\quad
\gamma_{fk}\mapsto c_f\,\gamma_{fk},\quad \kappa_{jk}\mapsto\kappa_{jk},\quad
\psi_{fg}\mapsto\psi_{fg}c_fc_g,\quad \tau\mapsto\tau,$$
with $\psi^M_{ff}=c_f^2$ because $\psi^U_{ff}=1$, and $\lambda^M_{m(f)f}=1$.

*Proof that $\sigma$ is unchanged.* $(I-B^M)^{-1}=DMD^{-1}$, so
$$\Lambda^M(I-B^M)^{-1}\Gamma^M=\Lambda^UD^{-1}\,D M D^{-1}\,D\Gamma^U=\Lambda^UM\Gamma^U,$$
hence $b^M=b^U$ ($\kappa$ is added unchanged). $\Phi^M=D\Phi^UD$ and
$\Lambda^M\Phi^M\Lambda^{M\prime}=\Lambda^U\Phi^U\Lambda^{U\prime}$ exactly as in Result 1, so $\rho$
and $\Theta$ are unchanged. $\tau$ is untouched. $\square$

So $\sigma_M(h(\theta_U))=\sigma_U(\theta_U)$ identically: the same fit, $F$, $T_{\text{raw}}$,
admissibility ($\Theta_{jj}\ge0$ and $\Phi$ positive semidefinite are congruence-invariant) and
the same $b$, including $b_{\text{marker}}=\gamma+\kappa_{\text{marker}}$ in the marker's
$y^*$ units. The inverse, given the signs of $c_f$, is
$c_f=\pm\sqrt{\psi^M_{ff}}$, $\lambda^U=\lambda^Mc_f$, $\beta^U_{fg}=\beta^M_{fg}c_g/c_f$,
$\gamma^U_{fk}=\gamma^M_{fk}/c_f$, $\psi^U_{fg}=\psi^M_{fg}/(c_fc_g)$.

*Why $\gamma$ moves and $\kappa$ does not.* $\kappa$ is a direct effect on $y^*$, and $y^*$ is
not rescaled (delta parameterization: $\operatorname{Var}(y^*\mid x)=1$ in both metrics, only the
factor is rescaled). $\gamma$ is an effect on $\eta$, in the units of $\eta$ (spec §4.8,
*Meaning*): disturbance SDs under `unitvariance`, marker-$y^*$ units under `marker`. Moving
from one to the other multiplies it by the conversion factor $c_f$, which is also the factor
that turns $\psi^U_{ff}=1$ into $\psi^M_{ff}=c_f^2$. (The marker, not the disturbance variance,
carries the scale: $c_f$ is the marker's loading at the UV optimum, one real number per factor.)

*Executed (R, chunk `cxr-verify` §§0, 1).* 500 random unit-variance points (382 with a negative
$c_f$, minimum $\Theta_{jj}$ 0.052): $\max|\sigma_M(h(\theta_U))-\sigma_U(\theta_U)|=2.2\times10^{-16}$
(elementwise rule) and $3.3\times10^{-16}$ (matrix rule); every fixed row of the marker table
(including the fixed $\kappa$ and $\psi_{12}=0$) is met to $0$; round trips both ways
$1.1\times10^{-16}$. $\sigma$ itself is checked against an independent joint-covariance
computation of $(x,\eta,y^*)$ ($b=\operatorname{Cov}(y^*,x)/\operatorname{Var}x$ to $0$, conditional
correlation to $5.6\times10^{-17}$, conditional variance 1), at the UV point and at its image.
Tolerance $10^{-12}$ is the section's tier for floating-point identities.

**Negative controls**, each killed on $\sigma$ (gap $>10^{-4}$, the section's kill threshold):
$\gamma$ left untransformed (1.9), $\gamma/c_f$ instead of $c_f\gamma$ (2.0), $\kappa$ scaled by
$c$ (0.66), $\psi^M_{ff}$ set to $c_f^2\Phi^U_{ff}$ (0.11), $\psi^M_{ff}$ set to $c_f^2$ times the
**total** variance including $q(1-q)\gamma^2$ (0.15).

### Result C2: reflections, with $\gamma$

The symmetry $\eta_f\to-\eta_f$ of $\mathcal U$ now also flips $\gamma_{f\cdot}$ (with
$\lambda_{\cdot f}$, $\beta_{f\cdot}$, $\beta_{\cdot f}$, $\psi_{f\cdot}$, $\psi_{\cdot f}$). It leaves $\sigma$ unchanged
($b$ contains $\lambda_{jf}\gamma_f$, a product of two flipped quantities), and it flips $c_f$.
Then $c_f\gamma_f$ is unchanged, so **$h$ is again constant on reflection orbits**: the marker point
does not depend on which of the $2^F$ equivalent UV solutions was found, and nothing here needs
`dwlsmv_signcanon()`. (A *fixed nonzero* $\gamma$ breaks the symmetry in $\mathcal U$; that is
the case Result C3 excludes.) Executed: 0 gap for each single-factor reflection, in both $\sigma$
and $h$.

### Result C3: eligibility (Result 2 extended)

**Claim.** $h(\theta_U)$ satisfies every fixed entry of $\mathcal M$ for every $\theta_U$ with all
$c_f\neq0$ iff $\mathcal M$ meets E1 to E3 of Result 2 **and**

* (E4) every fixed $\gamma$ is exactly $0$.

A fixed $\kappa$ may take any value: it is a parameter of both tables, with the same meaning.

*Proof.* A fixed value $v$ at $\gamma_{fk}$ maps to $c_fv$, equal to $v$ for every $c_f$ iff
$v=0$. If $\mathcal U$ keeps $\gamma_{fk}$ fixed at $v$, then $h$ leaves $\mathcal M$'s parameter
space; if $\mathcal U$ frees it, $\mathcal U$ has one more free parameter than $\mathcal M$ and a
different degrees of freedom. A fixed $\gamma=v\neq0$ in $\mathcal M$ means
"$v$ marker-$y^*$ units"; at the UV optimum that is $v/c_f$ disturbance SDs, and $c_f$ is not
known before the UV fit, so no UV table can state it. $\kappa$: $\kappa^M=\kappa^U$. $\square$

A fixed $\gamma=0$ is equivalent to an absent $\gamma$ for $\sigma$ and passes. Executed:
eight variants (base, $\gamma_1$ fixed 0, $\gamma_1$ fixed 0.5, $\kappa_5$ fixed 0.2, $\kappa_5$ fixed 0,
$\beta$ fixed 0.4, $\beta$ fixed 0, $\psi_{12}$ fixed 0.3), 30 draws each: "all fixed rows
survive $h$" coincides with "E1 to E4 hold" in all eight. Fixed $\gamma_1=0.5$ at UV maps to a
marker value 0.318 at $c_1=0.635$; forcing the marker table's 0.5 changes $\sigma$ by 0.18. Without
E4 that variant would pass E1 to E3 (checked) and be reported as a recovery of a different model.

**What changes in D11** (adopted 2026-11-15): one new
reason in the eligibility check (a fixed nonzero $\gamma$), one new branch in the transform
($\gamma\mapsto c_f\gamma$ and its inverse, keyed on ptype 8 with row $=$ factor), and
$\kappa$ passed through. The existing `else` branch in the transform treats every other ptype as
$\psi$ and would index $c$ by the covariate's column (`recover.md` §3).

### Result C4: thresholds, and the final fit's start (Result 5 extended)

Thresholds are the same parameters in both metrics, $\tau^M=\tau^U$ (they are the thresholds at
$x=0$; the single-group model has no intercepts, so there is nothing for $c_f$ to rescale). In
this model $\sigma_\tau=\tau$, and $\sigma_b$ and $\sigma_\rho$ do not involve $\tau$, so $\Delta$ has an
identity threshold block and zero off-blocks (`@sec-condx` (d)). With a diagonal $W$
($W_D=\operatorname{diag}(\Gamma)^{-1}$ or $I$) $F$ separates exactly as in Result 5:
$\hat\tau=s_\tau$ for every stationary point, whatever $(\lambda,\beta,\gamma,\kappa,\psi)$ are,
and a start at $s_\tau$ has a zero threshold gradient. **This corrects one sentence of Result
5**, which lists "covariates" among the cases where the argument fails. That sentence is true of
a design in which $x$ shifts the thresholds or the slopes are not rows of $\sigma$; it is not true
of the conditional single-group model, where the slopes are in $s$ and $\tau$ stays alone. It
remains true at $G>1$ with invariance constraints. Executed: the $\tau\times\tau$ block of both $\Delta_M$ and
$\Delta_U$ is $I$ to $10^{-14}$ with zero off-blocks, and the $\tau$ gradient is $0$ at $s_\tau$ with
the other parameters arbitrary (and $0.15$ away from it, as a control).

### Result C5: Jacobian, stationarity, decrement, rank

Let $h:\theta_U\mapsto\theta_M$ on $\{c_f\neq0\}$, $J=\partial h/\partial\theta_U$ (square). Because
$\sigma_U=\sigma_M\circ h$ identically (C1), the argument of Result 4 uses $\sigma$ only through that
identity, so it is unchanged: $\Delta_U=\Delta_MJ$, $g_U=J^\top g_M$, $H_U=J^\top H_MJ$, stationarity
and the Newton decrement transfer, $\operatorname{rank}\Delta_M=\operatorname{rank}\Delta_U$. $J$ is
nonsingular where all $c_f\ne0$ (the inverse is smooth where $\psi^M_{ff}>0$). The $\gamma$ rows add
$\partial\gamma^M_f/\partial\gamma^U_f=c_f$ and $\partial\gamma^M_f/\partial\lambda^U_{m(f)f}=\gamma^U_f$;
$\kappa$ rows are the identity. Executed (30 points): $J$ by complex step against central
differences $1.5\times10^{-10}$; $\Delta_U=\Delta_MJ$ to $6.7\times10^{-16}$; smallest
$|\det J|=4.8$; the analytic entries above to $4.4\times10^{-16}$. A stationary point **with**
nonzero residual is built without an optimizer, as in Result 4 ($\|r\|\ge0.108$): gradient in the UV
chart $8\times10^{-16}$ (relative), in the marker chart at $h(\theta_U)$ $2.7\times10^{-15}$; $F$
equal to $5.6\times10^{-17}$ and the decrement to $1.3\times10^{-15}$ (relative) at non-stationary points.

**The anchor condition is metric-free.** With $C=(\Lambda M)[A,F_\gamma]$ of `@sec-condx-anchor`,
$\Lambda^M(I-B^M)^{-1}=\Lambda^UD^{-1}DMD^{-1}=\Lambda^UMD^{-1}$: the columns are rescaled by
nonzero constants, so $C^M=C^UD_\gamma^{-1}$ has the same rank at the mapped point, and the set
$A$ (indicators with no free $\kappa$) is the same in both tables. "Present loading" holds for a
marker (fixed at 1) and for its free UV counterpart alike. Executed: $\Lambda M$ in the
marker metric against $\Lambda^UMD^{-1}$ to $2.2\times10^{-16}$; the base model has rank 19 of 19
in both; a model with a free $\kappa$ on every item has rank 22 of 24 in both. **Not shown:** that
Module 3's rank check passes at the *starting values* of each table (it is a statement at one
point; the mapped start is generic, the table's start values are not).

### Result C6: end to end, population level

A misfit $s=\sigma(\theta_0)+e$, $r\ne0$ at the optimum, diagonal $W$, UV fit by a damped
Gauss–Newton written for this check (not Mata's optimizer): the mapped point has the same $F$ to
$1.4\times10^{-17}$, a decrement of $1.7\times10^{-19}$ (zero iterations needed), and agrees with a
separately converged marker fit to $1.7\times10^{-10}$ (that fit started at $\lambda=0.7$, which
on this design lands at the same optimum); $\hat\tau=s_\tau$ in both; ACOV by the sandwich satisfies
$\operatorname{ACOV}_M=J\operatorname{ACOV}_UJ^\top$ to $3.4\times10^{-15}$ (relative). The last
holds at the shared stationary point and says the standard errors may be read from the marker
refit's own inference without discrepancy; D11 does refit rather than transform
(`recover.md` §1.5), so this is a consistency check, not a method.
*Diagnostic, not a check, and optimizer-specific:* on 40 designs whose generating point has a
reversed factor (a negative $c_f$), the toy Gauss–Newton from the table's starting values
($\lambda=0.7$, everything else 0, $\tau=s_\tau$, 100 iterations) missed the best $F$ in 17 with
the marker table and in 1 with the UV table; the marker fit started from the mapped UV optimum
missed in the same 1 (it inherits a UV miss; it cannot repair one). This shows that the
orientation sensitivity of E-016 exists in the conditional model for **this** optimizer, with a
chosen design family and no preregistered rate. It says nothing about Stata's ULS+DWLS path, about
the retry, or about the rate in real data.

### What is not established

1. The empirical premise of D11 in conditional mode (that a marker fit fails where the UV fit does not,
   at what rate, and that the UV fit is admissible there). Nothing above measures it.
2. Stata behavior: `dwls_identify` on the transformed text, the optimizer's iteration count, the
   anchor screen and rank check at the transformed start, `dwlsmv_breaddiag` on the conditional
   $\Delta$ and $\hat\Gamma$ (not established per the spec). The R check uses an exact
   complex-step $\Delta$ and a stand-in $\Gamma$.
3. More than one covariate, a continuous $x$, $G>1$. The algebra of C1 is column-by-column in
   $\Gamma$ and holds for any number of covariates, and it never uses the distribution of $x$;
   but the check ran one covariate, and the spec specifies those cases only when their
   derivations land (E-006).
4. The cutoff for $|c_f|$ near 0 (open, as in `@sec-marker-recovery`): $\gamma^M=c_f\gamma^U\to0$ and
   $\lambda^M\to\infty$ as $c_f\to0$, $\psi^M_{ff}\to0$.
5. A genuine Heywood case (a negative $\Theta_{jj}$ or an indefinite $\Phi$ at the UV optimum) is
   mapped as it is; recovery does not cure it. Only $\psi^M_{ff}<0$ is a marker-chart artifact, and
   $\psi^M_{ff}=c_f^2>0$ always.

*Executed:* the chunk below is the verification behind every "Executed" figure in this section (base R; 43 checks, 0 failures on R 4.6.0, 2026-11-15, main session). It is wrapped in `local()` and restores the random-number state, so it changes nothing for later chunks.

```{r cxr-verify}
local({
  .old_seed <- if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())) get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) else NULL
  on.exit(if (is.null(.old_seed)) { if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())) rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) } else assign(".Random.seed", .old_seed, envir = globalenv()))
# recovery_verify.R -- D11 marker <-> unit-variance map in conditional-covariate mode
# (one binary 0/1 covariate x, one group). Base R only. Read-only agent draft,
# 2026-11-15; run in scratch: Rscript recovery_verify.R > recovery_verify.log
#
# Parameter table: ptype in tau, lambda, beta, gamma(8), kappa(9), psi, in theta order
# (spec 4.8: tau, lambda, beta, gamma, kappa, psi). row/col as in the spec:
#   lambda (indicator, factor), beta (factor, factor), gamma (factor, covariate),
#   kappa (indicator, covariate), psi (factor, factor).
# sigma(theta) = (tau, b, rho), b = Lambda (I-B)^-1 Gamma + kappa,
#   rho = lower-triangle offdiag of Lambda Phi Lambda', Phi = (I-B)^-1 Psi (I-B)^-T.

set.seed(20261115)
nchk <- 0L; nfail <- 0L
chk <- function(name, ok, detail = "") {
  nchk <<- nchk + 1L
  if (!isTRUE(ok)) nfail <<- nfail + 1L
  cat(sprintf("%-4s %-62s %s\n", if (isTRUE(ok)) "PASS" else "FAIL", name, detail))
}
fmt <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 2)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the model
Kc <- c(2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 2)           # categories per item
p  <- length(Kc); m <- 2L; ntau <- sum(Kc - 1)
pairs_lt <- which(lower.tri(diag(p)), arr.ind = TRUE)   # column-major lower triangle

build_table <- function(gamma_rows = NULL, kappa_rows = NULL, beta_rows = NULL,
                        psi12 = NULL) {
  tau <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(p), function(j)
    data.frame(ptype = "tau", row = j, col = seq_len(Kc[j] - 1), free = TRUE, value = NA_real_)))
  lam <- data.frame(ptype = "lambda",
                    row  = c(1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6),
                    col  = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2),
                    free = c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE),
                    value = c(1, NA, NA, NA, 1, NA, NA))
  bet <- if (is.null(beta_rows)) data.frame(ptype = "beta", row = 2, col = 1, free = TRUE, value = NA_real_) else beta_rows
  gam <- if (is.null(gamma_rows)) data.frame(ptype = "gamma", row = c(1, 2), col = 1, free = TRUE, value = NA_real_) else gamma_rows
  kap <- if (is.null(kappa_rows)) data.frame(ptype = "kappa", row = c(2, 5), col = 1,
                                             free = c(FALSE, TRUE), value = c(0.15, NA)) else kappa_rows
  psi <- data.frame(ptype = "psi", row = c(1, 2, 2), col = c(1, 2, 1),
                    free = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE), value = c(NA, NA, 0))
  if (!is.null(psi12)) psi[3, c("free", "value")] <- psi12
  par <- rbind(tau, lam, bet, gam, kap, psi)
  rownames(par) <- NULL
  par
}
MARKER_ITEM <- c(1L, 4L)   # marker indicator of factor 1, 2 (same in every table below)
marker_rows <- function(par) sapply(1:m, function(f)
  which(par$ptype == "lambda" & par$col == f & par$row == MARKER_ITEM[f]))
psi_ff_rows <- function(par) sapply(1:m, function(f)
  which(par$ptype == "psi" & par$row == f & par$col == f))

# unit-variance table of the same model (derivation Setup)
uv_table <- function(par) {
  u <- par
  for (f in 1:m) {
    i <- marker_rows(par)[f]; u$free[i] <- TRUE;  u$value[i] <- NA_real_
    j <- psi_ff_rows(par)[f]; u$free[j] <- FALSE; u$value[j] <- 1
  }
  u
}

vals_of <- function(par, theta) {
  v <- as.numeric(par$value)
  if (is.complex(theta)) v <- as.complex(v)
  v[par$free] <- theta
  v
}
mats_of <- function(par, v) {
  z <- if (is.complex(v)) 0i else 0
  L <- matrix(z, p, m); B <- matrix(z, m, m); G <- rep(z, m); Kp <- rep(z, p)
  Ps <- matrix(z, m, m); tau <- rep(z, ntau)
  tt <- 0L
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(par))) {
    r <- par$row[i]; cc <- par$col[i]; val <- v[i]
    switch(par$ptype[i],
      tau    = { tt <- tt + 1L; tau[tt] <- val },
      lambda = L[r, cc] <- val,
      beta   = B[r, cc] <- val,
      gamma  = G[r] <- val,
      kappa  = Kp[r] <- val,
      psi    = { Ps[r, cc] <- val; Ps[cc, r] <- val })
  }
  list(tau = tau, L = L, B = B, G = G, K = Kp, Ps = Ps)
}
sigma_mats <- function(mt) {
  IB <- solve(diag(m) - mt$B)
  b   <- as.vector(mt$L %*% IB %*% mt$G) + mt$K
  Phi <- IB %*% mt$Ps %*% t(IB)
  R   <- mt$L %*% Phi %*% t(mt$L)
  c(mt$tau, b, R[pairs_lt])
}
sigma_of <- function(par, theta) sigma_mats(mats_of(par, vals_of(par, theta)))

# --------------------------------------------------- the map (elementwise, boxed)
h_elem <- function(par, v) {              # unit-variance full values -> marker full values
  cc <- v[marker_rows(par)]               # c_f = marker loading at the UV point
  out <- v
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(par))) {
    r <- par$row[i]; k <- par$col[i]
    out[i] <- switch(par$ptype[i],
      tau = v[i], lambda = v[i] / cc[k], beta = v[i] * cc[r] / cc[k],
      gamma = v[i] * cc[r],               # gamma: x -> eta, row = factor
      kappa = v[i],                       # kappa: x -> y*, metric-free
      psi = v[i] * cc[r] * cc[k])
  }
  out
}
h_inv_elem <- function(par, v, sgn) {      # marker full values -> UV full values
  cc <- sgn * sqrt(v[psi_ff_rows(par)])
  out <- v
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(par))) {
    r <- par$row[i]; k <- par$col[i]
    out[i] <- switch(par$ptype[i],
      tau = v[i], lambda = v[i] * cc[k], beta = v[i] * cc[k] / cc[r],
      gamma = v[i] / cc[r], kappa = v[i], psi = v[i] / (cc[r] * cc[k]))
  }
  out
}
h_mat <- function(par, v) {                 # the same map in matrix form: D = diag(c)
  mt <- mats_of(par, v); cc <- v[marker_rows(par)]; D <- diag(cc, m)
  mt$L <- mt$L %*% solve(D); mt$B <- D %*% mt$B %*% solve(D)
  mt$G <- as.vector(D %*% mt$G); mt$Ps <- D %*% mt$Ps %*% D
  mt
}
# wrong maps used as negative controls
h_wrong <- function(par, v, which) {
  cc <- v[marker_rows(par)]; out <- h_elem(par, v)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(par))) {
    r <- par$row[i]; k <- par$col[i]; pt <- par$ptype[i]
    if (which == "gamma_untransformed" && pt == "gamma") out[i] <- v[i]
    if (which == "gamma_over_c"        && pt == "gamma") out[i] <- v[i] / cc[r]
    if (which == "kappa_times_c"       && pt == "kappa") out[i] <- v[i] * cc[1]
    if (which == "psi_total_incl_x"    && pt == "psi" && r == k) out[i] <- cc[r]^2 * joint_check(par, v)$Vfac[r, r]   # total Var(eta_f) incl. gamma^2 q(1-q)
    if (which == "psi_total_variance"  && pt == "psi" && r == k) {
      # Phi_ff (conditional total of the disturbance chain), not the disturbance
      Phi <- { mt <- mats_of(par, v); IB <- solve(diag(m) - mt$B); IB %*% mt$Ps %*% t(IB) }
      out[i] <- cc[r]^2 * Phi[r, r]
    }
  }
  out
}

free_of_full <- function(par, v) v[par$free]

# --------------------------------------------------------- random UV points
draw_uv <- function(parU, minTheta = 0.05, pos = FALSE) {
  repeat {
    v <- as.numeric(parU$value)
    mk <- marker_rows(parU)
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(parU))) if (parU$free[i]) {
      v[i] <- switch(parU$ptype[i],
        tau = NA,
        lambda = { s <- if (pos) 1 else sample(c(-1, 1), 1); if (i %in% mk) s * runif(1, .45, .85) else s * runif(1, .15, .7) },
        beta = runif(1, -.5, .5), gamma = runif(1, -.8, .8), kappa = runif(1, -.4, .4),
        psi = runif(1, -.2, .2))
    }
    # thresholds item-major, increasing
    ti <- which(parU$ptype == "tau")
    for (j in seq_len(p)) {
      idx <- ti[parU$row[ti] == j]
      v[idx] <- sort(runif(length(idx), -1.5, 1.5))
    }
    th <- v[parU$free]
    mt <- mats_of(parU, v); IB <- solve(diag(m) - mt$B)
    Phi <- IB %*% mt$Ps %*% t(IB); Th <- 1 - diag(mt$L %*% Phi %*% t(mt$L))
    if (min(Th) > minTheta) return(list(theta = th, v = v, minTheta = min(Th)))
  }
}

# complex-step Jacobian of a function of the free vector
cs_jac <- function(f, theta, h = 1e-30) {
  f0 <- Re(f(theta + 0i)); J <- matrix(0, length(f0), length(theta))
  for (k in seq_along(theta)) {
    e <- rep(0i, length(theta)); e[k] <- 1i * h
    J[, k] <- Im(f(theta + e)) / h
  }
  J
}
fd_jac <- function(f, theta, h = 1e-6) {
  f0 <- f(theta); J <- matrix(0, length(f0), length(theta))
  for (k in seq_along(theta)) {
    e <- rep(0, length(theta)); e[k] <- h
    J[, k] <- (f(theta + e) - f(theta - e)) / (2 * h)
  }
  J
}
numrank <- function(M, tol = 1e-10) { s <- svd(M)$d; sum(s / s[1] > tol) }

# =============================================================== TABLES
parM <- build_table()
parU <- uv_table(parM)
nU <- sum(parU$free); nM <- sum(parM$free)
cat("== Tables ==\n")
cat(sprintf("free parameters: marker %d, unit variance %d; items %d, factors %d, thresholds %d\n",
            nM, nU, p, m, ntau))
cat("free by ptype (marker):",  paste(names(table(parM$ptype[parM$free])), table(parM$ptype[parM$free]), collapse = "  "), "\n")
cat("free by ptype (UV):    ",  paste(names(table(parU$ptype[parU$free])), table(parU$ptype[parU$free]), collapse = "  "), "\n")
chk("equal number of free parameters (square J)", nU == nM)
chk("same keys and order in both tables", identical(parM[, 1:3], parU[, 1:3]))
nonmetric <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(parM)), c(marker_rows(parM), psi_ff_rows(parM)))
chk("tables differ on exactly 2*nfac rows",
    identical(parM$free[nonmetric], parU$free[nonmetric]) && 2 * m == length(c(marker_rows(parM), psi_ff_rows(parM))))

# ====================================== 0. sigma(theta) against a joint path model
cat("\n== 0. sigma(theta) against an independent joint-covariance computation ==\n")
joint_check <- function(par, v, q = 0.4) {
  mt <- mats_of(par, v); IB <- solve(diag(m) - mt$B)
  Phi <- IB %*% mt$Ps %*% t(IB); Th <- 1 - diag(mt$L %*% Phi %*% t(mt$L))
  # u = (x, zeta(m), eps(p));  v = A u, v = (x, eta, y*)
  nu <- 1 + m + p
  A <- matrix(0, 1 + m + p, nu)
  A[1, 1] <- 1
  A[2:(1 + m), 1] <- IB %*% mt$G; A[2:(1 + m), 2:(1 + m)] <- IB
  A[(2 + m):(1 + m + p), ] <- cbind(mt$L %*% IB %*% mt$G + mt$K, mt$L %*% IB, diag(p))
  Cu <- matrix(0, nu, nu); Cu[1, 1] <- q * (1 - q); Cu[2:(1 + m), 2:(1 + m)] <- mt$Ps
  diag(Cu)[(2 + m):nu] <- Th
  Cv <- A %*% Cu %*% t(A)
  iy <- (2 + m):(1 + m + p)
  bb <- Cv[iy, 1] / Cv[1, 1]
  Rc <- Cv[iy, iy] - outer(bb, bb) * Cv[1, 1]
  list(b = bb, Rc = Rc, Vfac = Cv[2:(1 + m), 2:(1 + m)])
}
pt <- draw_uv(parU)
js <- joint_check(parU, pt$v)
sg <- sigma_of(parU, pt$theta)
chk("b = Cov(y*,x)/Var(x) from joint model (UV)", max(abs(js$b - sg[ntau + 1:p])) < 1e-12,
    fmt(max(abs(js$b - sg[ntau + 1:p]))))
chk("conditional corr = rho, conditional variance = 1 (UV)",
    max(abs(js$Rc[pairs_lt] - sg[ntau + p + seq_len(nrow(pairs_lt))])) < 1e-12 &&
      max(abs(diag(js$Rc) - 1)) < 1e-12,
    fmt(max(abs(js$Rc[pairs_lt] - sg[ntau + p + seq_len(nrow(pairs_lt))]))))
vM <- h_elem(parU, pt$v); jsM <- joint_check(parM, vM)
chk("joint model at the mapped marker point: same b and conditional R",
    max(abs(jsM$b - js$b)) < 1e-12 && max(abs(jsM$Rc - js$Rc)) < 1e-12,
    paste(fmt(max(abs(jsM$b - js$b))), fmt(max(abs(jsM$Rc - js$Rc)))))
cc <- pt$v[marker_rows(parU)]
chk("total factor variance scales as D V D (c_f^2 on the diagonal)",
    max(abs(jsM$Vfac - diag(cc, m) %*% js$Vfac %*% diag(cc, m))) < 1e-12)
cat(sprintf("   c_f = (%.4f, %.4f); UV Var(F1)=%.4f = 1 + gamma1^2 q(1-q) = %.4f (total variance is NOT 1)\n",
            cc[1], cc[2], js$Vfac[1, 1], 1 + pt$v[which(parU$ptype == "gamma")[1]]^2 * .4 * .6))

# ===================================== 1. sigma unchanged, many random points
cat("\n== 1. sigma_M(h(theta_U)) = sigma_U(theta_U), random points incl. negative c_f ==\n")
R1 <- 500; g_sig <- g_mat <- g_fix <- g_rt1 <- g_rt2 <- g_marker <- 0; neg <- 0L; minTh <- 1
for (r in seq_len(R1)) {
  pt <- draw_uv(parU); vU <- pt$v; vM <- h_elem(parU, vU)
  thM <- free_of_full(parM, vM)
  g_sig <- max(g_sig, max(abs(sigma_of(parM, thM) - sigma_of(parU, pt$theta))))
  vm2 <- sigma_mats(h_mat(parU, vU)); g_mat <- max(g_mat, max(abs(vm2 - sigma_of(parU, pt$theta))))
  fx <- !parM$free
  g_fix <- max(g_fix, max(abs(vM[fx] - parM$value[fx])))
  g_marker <- max(g_marker, max(abs(vM[marker_rows(parM)] - 1)))
  sgn <- sign(vU[marker_rows(parU)])
  g_rt1 <- max(g_rt1, max(abs(h_inv_elem(parM, vM, sgn) - vU)))
  g_rt2 <- max(g_rt2, max(abs(h_elem(parU, h_inv_elem(parM, vM, sgn)) - vM)))
  neg <- neg + any(sgn < 0); minTh <- min(minTh, pt$minTheta)
}
cat(sprintf("   %d draws, %d with a negative c_f, min Theta_jj over draws %.3f\n", R1, neg, minTh))
chk("sigma unchanged, elementwise map (max abs gap)", g_sig < 1e-12, fmt(g_sig))
chk("sigma unchanged, matrix form D-map", g_mat < 1e-12, fmt(g_mat))
chk("every fixed row of the marker table is satisfied (lambda=1, psi12=0, kappa)", g_fix < 1e-12, fmt(g_fix))
chk("marker loadings equal 1", g_marker < 1e-12, fmt(g_marker))
chk("round trip  h^-1(h(theta_U)) = theta_U", g_rt1 < 1e-12, fmt(g_rt1))
chk("round trip  h(h^-1(theta_M)) = theta_M", g_rt2 < 1e-12, fmt(g_rt2))

# ============================================ 2. reflection: eta_f -> -eta_f
cat("\n== 2. reflection invariance (Result 3 with gamma) ==\n")
pt <- draw_uv(parU); vU <- pt$v; gref <- 0
for (f in 1:m) {
  s <- rep(1, m); s[f] <- -1; Sg <- diag(s, m)
  mt <- mats_of(parU, vU)
  mt$L <- mt$L %*% Sg; mt$B <- Sg %*% mt$B %*% Sg; mt$G <- as.vector(Sg %*% mt$G); mt$Ps <- Sg %*% mt$Ps %*% Sg
  # write back into a value vector
  vR <- vU
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(parU))) vR[i] <- switch(parU$ptype[i],
    tau = vU[i], lambda = mt$L[parU$row[i], parU$col[i]], beta = mt$B[parU$row[i], parU$col[i]],
    gamma = mt$G[parU$row[i]], kappa = vU[i], psi = mt$Ps[parU$row[i], parU$col[i]])
  gref <- max(gref, max(abs(sigma_of(parU, free_of_full(parU, vR)) - sigma_of(parU, pt$theta))),
              max(abs(h_elem(parU, vR) - h_elem(parU, vU))))
}
chk("reflecting one factor: sigma_U and h(theta_U) both unchanged (incl. gamma)", gref < 1e-12, fmt(gref))

# ============================================== 3. Jacobian, Delta_U = Delta_M J
cat("\n== 3. Jacobian J of h and Delta_U = Delta_M J ==\n")
hfree <- function(th) free_of_full(parM, h_elem(parU, vals_of(parU, th)))
g_J <- g_JFD <- g_D <- g_Dfd <- 0; detmin <- Inf; g_ana <- 0
for (r in 1:30) {
  pt <- draw_uv(parU); th <- pt$theta
  J  <- cs_jac(hfree, th); Jfd <- fd_jac(function(t) Re(hfree(t)), th)
  DU <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(parU, t), th)
  thM <- Re(hfree(th))
  DM <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(parM, t), thM)
  g_J  <- max(g_J, max(abs(J - Jfd)))
  g_D  <- max(g_D, max(abs(DU - DM %*% J)))
  detmin <- min(detmin, abs(det(J)))
  # analytic spot checks: d gamma^M / d gamma^U = c_f ; d gamma^M_f / d lambda_marker^U = gamma^U_f
  # d psi^M_ff / d lambda_marker^U = 2 c_f ; d lambda_jf^M / d lambda_jf^U = 1/c_f
  iU <- which(parU$free); keyU <- paste(parU$ptype, parU$row, parU$col)[iU]
  keyM <- paste(parM$ptype, parM$row, parM$col)[which(parM$free)]
  vU <- pt$v; c1 <- vU[marker_rows(parU)[1]]
  a1 <- J[match("gamma 1 1", keyM), match("gamma 1 1", keyU)] - c1
  gU1 <- vU[parU$ptype == "gamma" & parU$row == 1]
  a2 <- J[match("gamma 1 1", keyM), match("lambda 1 1", keyU)] - gU1
  a3 <- J[match("psi 1 1", keyM), match("lambda 1 1", keyU)] - 2 * c1
  a4 <- J[match("lambda 2 1", keyM), match("lambda 2 1", keyU)] - 1 / c1
  a5 <- J[match("kappa 5 1", keyM), match("kappa 5 1", keyU)] - 1
  g_ana <- max(g_ana, abs(a1), abs(a2), abs(a3), abs(a4), abs(a5))
}
chk("J complex-step vs central FD (30 points, h=1e-6)", g_J < 1e-7, fmt(g_J))
chk("Delta_U = Delta_M J (complex step, 30 points)", g_D < 1e-12, fmt(g_D))
chk("J nonsingular: smallest |det J| over points", detmin > 1e-10, fmt(detmin))
chk("analytic J entries (gamma, psi_ff, lambda, kappa)", g_ana < 1e-12, fmt(g_ana))

# ============================================ 4. thresholds: identity block, tau-hat = s_tau
cat("\n== 4. thresholds: Delta block is the identity; tau-hat = s_tau for diagonal W ==\n")
pt <- draw_uv(parU); thM <- Re(hfree(pt$theta))
tauM <- which(parM$ptype[parM$free] == "tau"); nth <- length(thM)
DM <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(parM, t), thM); DU <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(parU, t), pt$theta)
for (nm in c("M", "U")) {
  D <- if (nm == "M") DM else DU
  th <- which((if (nm == "M") parM else parU)$ptype[(if (nm == "M") parM else parU)$free] == "tau")
  blk  <- D[seq_len(ntau), th]; offr <- D[seq_len(ntau), -th]; offc <- D[-seq_len(ntau), th]
  chk(sprintf("Delta_%s: tau rows x tau columns = I, other blocks 0", nm),
      max(abs(blk - diag(ntau))) < 1e-14 && max(abs(offr)) < 1e-14 && max(abs(offc)) < 1e-14)
}
# F separates: for any diagonal W>0 and any other parameters, tau-gradient zero iff tau = s_tau
sstat <- sigma_of(parM, thM) + rnorm(length(sigma_of(parM, thM)), 0, .03)  # misfitting s
w <- runif(length(sstat), .5, 3)
gradF <- function(par, th) { r <- sstat - sigma_of(par, th); D <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(par, t), th); -2 * as.vector(t(D) %*% (w * r)) }
th2 <- thM; th2[tauM] <- sstat[seq_len(ntau)]               # tau at s_tau, rest arbitrary
chk("tau-gradient exactly 0 at tau = s_tau, other parameters arbitrary (marker)", max(abs(gradF(parM, th2)[tauM])) < 1e-14,
    fmt(max(abs(gradF(parM, th2)[tauM]))))
chk("tau-gradient nonzero away from s_tau (control)", max(abs(gradF(parM, thM)[tauM])) > 1e-3,
    fmt(max(abs(gradF(parM, thM)[tauM]))))

# ============================================ 5. stationarity and decrement invariance
cat("\n== 5. stationarity at the mapped point, non-vacuous (Result 4 with gamma, kappa) ==\n")
gs <- gsd <- gdec <- 0; rmin <- Inf; relgU <- relgM <- 0
for (r in 1:30) {
  pt <- draw_uv(parU); th <- pt$theta; thM <- Re(hfree(th))
  D <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(parU, t), th); n <- length(sigma_of(parU, th))
  w <- runif(n, .5, 3); e <- rnorm(n, 0, .05)
  P <- D %*% solve(t(D) %*% (w * D), t(D) %*% diag(w))     # W-projection onto col(Delta_U)
  s <- sigma_of(parU, th) + as.vector((diag(n) - P) %*% e)
  rU <- s - sigma_of(parU, th); gU <- -2 * as.vector(t(D) %*% (w * rU))
  DMm <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(parM, t), thM)
  rM <- s - sigma_of(parM, thM); gM <- -2 * as.vector(t(DMm) %*% (w * rM))
  rmin <- min(rmin, sqrt(sum(rU^2)))
  relgU <- max(relgU, max(abs(gU)) / sum(abs(rU) * 1)); relgM <- max(relgM, max(abs(gM)) / sum(abs(rU) * 1))
  # decrement invariance at a NON-stationary point: random s
  s2 <- sigma_of(parU, th) + rnorm(n, 0, .05)
  gU2 <- -2 * as.vector(t(D) %*% (w * (s2 - sigma_of(parU, th))))
  gM2 <- -2 * as.vector(t(DMm) %*% (w * (s2 - sigma_of(parM, thM))))
  HU <- 2 * t(D) %*% (w * D); HM <- 2 * t(DMm) %*% (w * DMm)
  dU <- as.numeric(t(gU2) %*% solve(HU, gU2)); dM <- as.numeric(t(gM2) %*% solve(HM, gM2))
  gdec <- max(gdec, abs(dU - dM) / dU)
  FU <- sum(w * (s2 - sigma_of(parU, th))^2); FM <- sum(w * (s2 - sigma_of(parM, thM))^2)
  gsd <- max(gsd, abs(FU - FM))
}
chk("constructed stationary point has nonzero residual (non-vacuous)", rmin > 1e-4, paste("min ||r|| =", fmt(rmin)))
chk("gradient in UV chart is 0 (rel.)", relgU < 1e-12, fmt(relgU))
chk("gradient in marker chart at h(theta_U) is 0 (rel.)", relgM < 1e-12, fmt(relgM))
chk("objective F equal at non-stationary points", gsd < 1e-12, fmt(gsd))
chk("Newton decrement equal at non-stationary points (relative)", gdec < 1e-10, fmt(gdec))

# ============================================ 6. rank transfers, anchor screen
cat("\n== 6. rank of Delta and the anchor condition in the two metrics ==\n")
rk <- function(parU_, parM_) {
  out <- NULL
  for (r in 1:20) {
    pt <- draw_uv(parU_); th <- pt$theta; thM <- Re(free_of_full(parM_, h_elem(parU_, vals_of(parU_, th))))
    DU <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(parU_, t), th); DM <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(parM_, t), thM)
    mt <- mats_of(parU_, pt$v); IB <- solve(diag(m) - mt$B); LM_U <- mt$L %*% IB
    vM <- h_elem(parU_, pt$v); mM <- mats_of(parM_, vM); LM_M <- mM$L %*% solve(diag(m) - mM$B)
    cc <- pt$v[marker_rows(parU_)]
    out <- rbind(out, c(numrank(DU), numrank(DM), ncol(DU),
                        max(abs(LM_M - LM_U %*% diag(1 / cc, m)))))
  }
  out
}
r1 <- rk(parU, parM)
chk("base model (anchors exist): rank Delta_U = rank Delta_M = npar",
    all(r1[, 1] == r1[, 2]) && all(r1[, 1] == r1[, 3]), paste("rank", r1[1, 1], "of", r1[1, 3]))
chk("Lambda(I-B)^-1 in marker metric = Lambda(I-B)^-1 in UV times D^-1 (columns scaled)",
    max(r1[, 4]) < 1e-12, fmt(max(r1[, 4])))
# every item with a free kappa: anchor fails, both metrics should fail identically
kall <- data.frame(ptype = "kappa", row = 1:p, col = 1, free = TRUE, value = NA_real_)
parM2 <- build_table(kappa_rows = kall); parU2 <- uv_table(parM2)
r2 <- rk(parU2, parM2)
chk("no anchor (free kappa on every item): same deficiency in both metrics",
    all(r2[, 1] == r2[, 2]) && all(r2[, 1] < r2[, 3]), paste("rank", r2[1, 1], "of", r2[1, 3], "in both"))

# ============================================ 7. eligibility, and what fixed gamma does
cat("\n== 7. eligibility: which fixed rows survive the map (Result 2 extended) ==\n")
elig <- function(par, e4 = TRUE) {                # E1-E3 as in mr_eligibility + E4 (draft)
  reasons <- character()
  fixed <- par[!par$free, ]
  for (f in 1:m) {
    fl <- fixed[fixed$ptype == "lambda" & fixed$col == f & fixed$value != 0, ]
    if (nrow(fl) != 1L || fl$value != 1) reasons <- c(reasons, sprintf("E1 factor %d", f))
    pf <- par[par$ptype == "psi" & par$row == f & par$col == f, ]
    if (nrow(pf) != 1L || !pf$free) reasons <- c(reasons, sprintf("E2 factor %d", f))
  }
  oth <- fixed[(fixed$ptype %in% c("beta", "lambda") & fixed$value != 0) |
                 (fixed$ptype == "psi" & fixed$row != fixed$col & fixed$value != 0), ]
  oth <- oth[!(oth$ptype == "lambda" & oth$value == 1 & paste(oth$row, oth$col) %in% paste(par$row[marker_rows(par)], par$col[marker_rows(par)])), ]
  if (nrow(oth)) reasons <- c(reasons, sprintf("E3 fixed nonzero %s[%d,%d]", oth$ptype, oth$row, oth$col))
  if (e4) {
    g <- fixed[fixed$ptype == "gamma" & fixed$value != 0, ]
    if (nrow(g)) reasons <- c(reasons, sprintf("E4 fixed nonzero gamma[%d,%d]=%g", g$row, g$col, g$value))
  }
  reasons
}
variants <- list(
  base                      = build_table(),
  `gamma1 fixed 0`          = build_table(gamma_rows = data.frame(ptype = "gamma", row = 1:2, col = 1, free = c(FALSE, TRUE), value = c(0, NA))),
  `gamma1 fixed 0.5`        = build_table(gamma_rows = data.frame(ptype = "gamma", row = 1:2, col = 1, free = c(FALSE, TRUE), value = c(0.5, NA))),
  `kappa5 fixed 0.2`        = build_table(kappa_rows = data.frame(ptype = "kappa", row = c(2, 5), col = 1, free = FALSE, value = c(0.15, 0.2))),
  `kappa5 fixed 0`          = build_table(kappa_rows = data.frame(ptype = "kappa", row = c(2, 5), col = 1, free = FALSE, value = c(0.15, 0))),
  `beta fixed 0.4`          = build_table(beta_rows = data.frame(ptype = "beta", row = 2, col = 1, free = FALSE, value = 0.4)),
  `beta fixed 0`            = build_table(beta_rows = data.frame(ptype = "beta", row = 2, col = 1, free = FALSE, value = 0)),
  `psi12 fixed 0.3`         = build_table(psi12 = list(FALSE, 0.3)))
cat(sprintf("%-20s %-10s %-34s %s\n", "variant", "eligible", "reasons", "fixed rows survive h (max change)"))
allagree <- TRUE; e3only <- TRUE
for (nm in names(variants)) {
  pm <- variants[[nm]]; pu <- uv_table(pm)
  ch <- 0
  for (r in 1:30) {
    pt <- draw_uv(pu); vM <- h_elem(pu, pt$v); fx <- !pm$free
    ch <- max(ch, max(abs(vM[fx] - pm$value[fx])))
  }
  rs <- elig(pm); surv <- ch < 1e-12
  allagree <- allagree && (surv == (length(rs) == 0L))
  e3only <- e3only && (length(elig(pm, e4 = FALSE)) == 0L) == (surv || nm %in% c("gamma1 fixed 0.5"))
  cat(sprintf("%-20s %-10s %-34s %s  %s\n", nm, length(rs) == 0L, if (length(rs)) paste(rs, collapse = "; ") else "-", fmt(ch),
              if (surv) "survive" else "VIOLATED"))
}
chk("eligible  <=>  every fixed row of the marker table survives h (8 variants, 30 draws each)", allagree)
chk("without E4, fixed nonzero gamma would pass E1-E3 yet is violated by h", e3only)

# a fixed gamma at UV is a different model at marker: sigma gap
pm <- variants[["gamma1 fixed 0.5"]]; pu <- uv_table(pm)
pt <- draw_uv(pu); vU <- pt$v; vM <- h_elem(pu, vU)
cat(sprintf("   fixed gamma1: UV value %.3f maps to marker value %.4f (c_1=%.4f); marker table says 0.5\n",
            vU[pu$ptype == "gamma" & pu$row == 1], vM[pu$ptype == "gamma" & pu$row == 1], vU[marker_rows(pu)[1]]))
vBad <- vM; vBad[pu$ptype == "gamma" & pu$row == 1] <- 0.5      # force the marker table's fixed value
gapfix <- max(abs(sigma_of(pm, free_of_full(pm, vBad)) - sigma_of(pu, pt$theta)))
chk("forcing the marker's fixed 0.5 changes sigma (different model, not a reparameterization)", gapfix > 1e-4, fmt(gapfix))

# ============================================ 8. negative controls
cat("\n== 8. negative controls: wrong maps are killed ==\n")
for (wn in c("gamma_untransformed", "gamma_over_c", "kappa_times_c", "psi_total_variance", "psi_total_incl_x")) {
  mx <- 0
  for (r in 1:50) {
    pt <- draw_uv(parU); vM <- h_wrong(parU, pt$v, wn)
    mx <- max(mx, max(abs(sigma_of(parM, free_of_full(parM, vM)) - sigma_of(parU, pt$theta))))
  }
  chk(sprintf("control %-22s sigma gap > 1e-4", wn), mx > 1e-4, fmt(mx))
}

# ============================================ 9. end-to-end: fit UV, map, marker refit
cat("\n== 9. end-to-end (population-level DWLS with misfit): UV fit, map, marker refit ==\n")
dwls_fit <- function(par, s, w, th0, maxit = 200, tolrel = 1e-18) {
  th <- th0; F <- function(t) sum(w * (s - sigma_of(par, t))^2); it <- 0L; dec <- NA
  repeat {
    r <- s - sigma_of(par, th); D <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(par, t), th)
    g <- -2 * as.vector(t(D) %*% (w * r)); H <- 2 * t(D) %*% (w * D)
    sv <- function(H, g) tryCatch(solve(H, g), error = function(e) solve(H + 1e-6 * mean(diag(H)) * diag(nrow(H)), g))
    dec <- as.numeric(t(g) %*% sv(H, g))
    if (dec < tolrel || it >= maxit) break
    step <- -sv(H, g); a <- 1
    while (F(th + a * step) > F(th) && a > 1e-8) a <- a / 2
    th <- th + a * step; it <- it + 1L
  }
  list(theta = th, iter = it, dec = dec, F = F(th))
}
pt0 <- draw_uv(parU, pos = TRUE)   # a generating point (UV draw, mapped)
vgen <- h_elem(parU, pt0$v); thgen <- free_of_full(parM, vgen)
sgen <- sigma_of(parM, thgen)
sstat <- sgen; sstat[-seq_len(ntau)] <- sstat[-seq_len(ntau)] + rnorm(length(sstat) - ntau, 0, .02)  # misfit
wst <- 1 / (0.01 + runif(length(sstat), .5, 2) * 0.05)
# UV cold start like the table starts (lambda .7, beta 0, gamma 0, kappa 0), tau at s_tau
start_for_s <- function(par, sstat) {
  th <- numeric(sum(par$free)); pf <- par[par$free, ]
  th[pf$ptype == "tau"] <- sstat[seq_len(ntau)]
  th[pf$ptype == "lambda"] <- 0.7; th[pf$ptype == "beta"] <- 0; th[pf$ptype == "gamma"] <- 0
  th[pf$ptype == "kappa"] <- 0; th[pf$ptype == "psi"] <- 1
  th
}
start_for <- function(par) start_for_s(par, sstat)
fU <- dwls_fit(parU, sstat, wst, start_for(parU))
thU <- fU$theta; vUhat <- vals_of(parU, thU); cU <- vUhat[marker_rows(parU)]
cat(sprintf("   UV fit: %d iterations, F=%.6e, decrement %.2e, c_f=(%.4f,%.4f)\n", fU$iter, fU$F, fU$dec, cU[1], cU[2]))
vMmap <- h_elem(parU, vUhat); thMmap <- free_of_full(parM, vMmap)
Fm <- sum(wst * (sstat - sigma_of(parM, thMmap))^2)
chk("F at mapped marker start equals F at UV optimum", abs(Fm - fU$F) < 1e-14, fmt(abs(Fm - fU$F)))
fM <- dwls_fit(parM, sstat, wst, thMmap)
chk("marker refit from the mapped start: 0 iterations (decrement already below 1e-18)", fM$iter == 0L,
    paste("iter", fM$iter, "decrement", fmt(fM$dec)))
cold <- dwls_fit(parM, sstat, wst, start_for(parM))
cat(sprintf("   marker cold start: %d iterations, F=%.6e (mapped-start F=%.6e)\n", cold$iter, cold$F, fM$F))
chk("marker cold-start optimum = mapped point (same stationary point)", max(abs(cold$theta - thMmap)) < 1e-7,
    fmt(max(abs(cold$theta - thMmap))))
tauhat <- thMmap[parM$ptype[parM$free] == "tau"]
chk("tau-hat = s_tau in both fits", max(abs(tauhat - sstat[seq_len(ntau)])) < 1e-12 &&
      max(abs(thU[parU$ptype[parU$free] == "tau"] - sstat[seq_len(ntau)])) < 1e-12)
# SE equivariance: ACOV transforms by J (delta method) -- the sandwich is chart-covariant at a stationary point
Dm <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(parM, t), thMmap); Du <- cs_jac(function(t) sigma_of(parU, t), thU)
gam <- 1 / wst                       # stand-in Gamma diagonal; W = diag(1/Gamma)
bread <- function(D) solve(t(D) %*% (wst * D))
meat  <- function(D) t(D) %*% ((wst^2 * gam) * D)
acovU <- bread(Du) %*% meat(Du) %*% bread(Du); acovM <- bread(Dm) %*% meat(Dm) %*% bread(Dm)
Jh <- cs_jac(hfree, thU)
chk("ACOV(marker) = J ACOV(UV) J' at the mapped point (sandwich is chart-covariant)",
    max(abs(acovM - Jh %*% acovU %*% t(Jh))) / max(abs(acovM)) < 1e-9,
    fmt(max(abs(acovM - Jh %*% acovU %*% t(Jh))) / max(abs(acovM))))

# diagnostic (not a check): 40 designs with at least one REVERSED factor (negative c_f at the
# generating point), toy Gauss-Newton optimizer, cold starts at the table's starting values.
{
  nd <- 40L; badU <- badM <- badMap <- 0L; itmap <- integer(0)
  for (d in seq_len(nd)) {
    ptn <- draw_uv(parU)
    while (!any(ptn$v[marker_rows(parU)] < 0)) ptn <- draw_uv(parU)
    vg <- h_elem(parU, ptn$v); sg2 <- sigma_of(parM, free_of_full(parM, vg))
    ss <- sg2; ss[-seq_len(ntau)] <- ss[-seq_len(ntau)] + rnorm(length(ss) - ntau, 0, .02)
    fU2 <- dwls_fit(parU, ss, wst, start_for_s(parU, ss), maxit = 100)
    fM2 <- dwls_fit(parM, ss, wst, start_for_s(parM, ss), maxit = 100)
    thMap2 <- free_of_full(parM, h_elem(parU, vals_of(parU, fU2$theta)))
    fMm <- dwls_fit(parM, ss, wst, thMap2, maxit = 100)
    Fbest <- min(fU2$F, fM2$F, fMm$F)
    badU <- badU + (fU2$F > Fbest + 1e-9); badM <- badM + (fM2$F > Fbest + 1e-9)
    badMap <- badMap + (fMm$F > Fbest + 1e-9); itmap <- c(itmap, fMm$iter)
  }
  cat(sprintf("   DIAGNOSTIC %d reversed-factor designs, toy optimizer (100 it): cold UV missed best F in %d, cold marker in %d, marker from mapped start in %d (iterations from mapped start: max %d)\n",
              nd, badU, badM, badMap, max(itmap)))
}

cat(sprintf("\n== summary: %d checks, %d failed ==\n", nchk, nfail))
cat("sessionInfo:", R.version.string, "\n")
stopifnot(nfail == 0)
})
```

## Conditional mode: what Module 10's diagnostics become {#sec-condx-m10}

*Executed* by the main session on 2026-11-15 (R 4.6.0, base R): chunk `m10-verify` at the end of this section, 20 of 20 checks, standalone run; the full render is batched. Drafted by a read-only agent; the main session reran it and changed only the wrapper (the chunk runs in `local()`, restores the RNG state and the reused `cx_K`, `cx_true`, and ends in `stopifnot`). R doubles stand in for Mata and certify no Mata routine; the two Mata measurements quoted in M3(d) and M5 come from E-097. The owner's decisions are recorded at the end.

This section does for Module 10 what `@sec-condx` (b) did for the pattern lemma and `@sec-condx-policy` did for
aliasing: it states which diagnostics keep their derivation, which change, and which fail. One binary $x\in\{0,1\}$,
one group, ordinal items. Reuses the chunks `cx-setup`, `cx-stage1`, `cx-psi` and `cx-model` of `@sec-condx`.
$D=T+p+P$, the slopes being the new $p$ statistics.

### M1. Patterns are $(y,x)$ (Row 3, and the cut $r^*$ of Rows 6 and 7)

*Lemma 1 carries over with the covariate in the pattern.* $\hat\psi_i$ is a function of $(y_i,x_i)$ alone, by `@sec-condx`'s
Item 1 and Item 2 formulas: the item score looks up $(y_{ij},x_i)$, the pair score looks up $(y_{ij},y_{ik},x_i)$,
and every normaliser is a sample constant. Hence $\hat\Gamma=G'\operatorname{diag}(n_m/N)G$ over the $n_{\rm pat}$ distinct
rows of $(Y,x)$, and, when every score equation is solved, Theorem 1 of `@sec-gamma-rank` gives
$\operatorname{rank}\hat\Gamma\le\min(D,\,n_{\rm pat}-1)$ with $n_{\rm pat}$ counted on $(y,x)$.

*Consequences for the row.* (i) $n_{\rm pat}\ge n_{\rm pat}^{(y)}$, the count on $y$ alone, so v1's count can flag a deficiency that is not
there: a design whose every $y$-pattern occurs in both groups has $n_{\rm pat}=2n^{(y)}_{\rm pat}$. (ii) The bound is an
inequality and is **not a detector of a cause**; it says what rank is possible.

*Check.* Seven random designs of 8 to 36 patterns on `cx_true`'s items ($D=11$): rank $=\min(D,n_{\rm pat}-1)$ on all seven
(measured, not proved to be tight), and two designs where the $y$-only rule flags ($n^{(y)}_{\rm pat}-1<D$) while $\hat\Gamma$ has full rank 11.

*Verification:* chunk `m10-verify`, section V1.

### M2. Centring: the item rows are bounded by the step rule, the pair rows gain a term (Row 5)

In v1, $\bar\psi_\tau=0$ to rounding because $\hat\tau$ solves its score exactly (`@sec-gamma-rank`, Lemma 2). Here
$\psi_{\theta_j}=H_j^{-1}g_j$ and $\hat\theta_j$ is an iterative ML fit, so
$$\bar\psi_{\theta_j}=H_j^{-1}\bar g_j=d(\hat\theta_j),$$
the Newton step at the returned point, **exactly** (same $H_j$). The item fit stops when $\|d\|_\infty\le\delta_1$
(`@sec-condx-itemstop`, $\delta_1=10^{-12}$), and returns $\theta_k$, so $\|\bar\psi_{\theta_j}\|_\infty\le\delta_1$ and
$$z_k\le\delta_1/\sqrt{\hat\Gamma_{kk}}\qquad(k\ \text{an item row}).$$
For a pair, averaging $\psi_\rho=-U_\rho^{-1}(u+U_\theta\psi_{\theta})$ over the sample (Lemma 2's step, without the vanishing
propagation sum) gives
$$\bar\psi_{\rho_{ij}}=-U_\rho^{-1}\big(\bar S_{ij}(\hat\rho)+U_\theta\,(\bar\psi_{\theta_i}',\bar\psi_{\theta_j}')'\big).$$
The first term is v1's. The second is new, of order $\|U_\rho^{-1}U_\theta\|\,\delta_1$.

*What is established.* The identity above (R, gap $7\times10^{-17}$ at a deliberately perturbed first stage), and the
step-rule bound (gap to $d_k$ $1.4\times10^{-16}$; $\max|\bar\psi_\theta|=1.5\times10^{-13}$; $z$ at most $8\times10^{-14}$,
against the flag $10^{-6}$). Theorem 1(2) on the scale-free matrix survives with item rows in $z$: at a perturbed first stage,
$\lambda_{r^*+1}(R\hat\Gamma R)=1.5\times10^{-6}\le\sum_k z_k^2=2.4\times10^{-5}$.

*What is not.* The pair bound $z_\rho\le2\tau_S/\sqrt J$ of `@sec-gamma-budgets` $(\ast)$ is derived for v1's pair score. Whether it
holds for the **pooled** score (`@sec-condx-rootfind`) with its own $\tau_S$ is not derived here. The row stays at $10^{-6}$
only on the argument that $10^{-12}$ is the finest precision at which $\hat\Gamma$ is validated, which is unchanged.
The O6 exclusion is void (no repair in this mode). The $\rho$ entries sit at positions $T+p+k$.

*Verification:* chunk `m10-verify`, section V2.

### M3. Aliasing: v1's cause test does not transfer, and one cause survives with a different count (Row 4, $d_{\rm alias}$)

`@sec-condx-policy` (P3) showed that a collapse $y_3=\mathbb 1\{y_1\ge1\}$ costs one rank in the population and is not exact
in samples, and that exact duplication is exact. Three additions.

**M3(a). Duplication loses $K_j$, not $K_j-1$.** If $y_2=y_1$ (or $K-1-y_1$) on every row, item 2's $\hat\theta_2$ is a fixed function of
item 1's in every sample, so $\hat\Gamma_{\theta\theta}$ loses the $K_2-1$ thresholds **and the slope**: $K_2$ ranks. v1's
`dwlsmv_dalias` counts $K_2-1$ for the identical threshold columns by components. With binary items: 2 lost
(smallest two ratios $\le1.2\times10^{-16}$ in the population and at $N=2000$, same and reversed; kept ratio 0.052), v1 would count 1.
It also loses the corresponding $\rho$ entries (the pairs $(1,k)$ and $(2,k)$ have identical $\psi_\rho$), which this section does not count.

**M3(b). Identical or complementary threshold columns with a non-binary partner give no exact deficiency at all.** Take $K=(3,3,3)$ and let
$\mathbb 1\{y_1<1\}=\mathbb 1\{y_3<1\}$ on the support, by deleting the patterns where they disagree. v1's test fires (identical
columns). Item 3 is not saturated under the parallel shift (three parameters against the four dimensions of functions of
$(\mathbb 1\{y_3<1\},x)$ centred within groups), so item 1's surviving combination need not lie in item 3's span, and does not. The smallest singular
ratio of $\hat\Gamma_{\theta\theta}$ is $1.5\times10^{-5}$ **in the population**, and between $2\times10^{-7}$ and $10^{-4}$ in samples
of 500 to 32000 (three draws each). The complementary version gives $3.6\times10^{-5}$ and $8\times10^{-6}$ to $2\times10^{-5}$. $\rho_{13}=0.85$
is interior, so Stage 1 does not stop it. **v1's cause test would certify an exact deficiency of one that the population itself does not have.**

**M3(c). The exact population null needs a saturated (binary) aliased item,** and then $y_3$ is a function of $y_1$:
perfect association in both groups, and `@sec-condx-policy` P2 says $\hat\rho\to1$ with no finite estimate. **Measured in Mata (StataMP 18,
`probe_cx_delta.do`):** Stage 1 refuses the pair with status 2 at $B=0.999$, rc 3498, so a same-orientation duplication never reaches $\hat\Gamma$.

**M3(d). Mixed orientation is admitted, and its loss is exact.** Let item $k$ equal item $i$ when $x=0$ and its reverse when $x=1$. Within each group the
association is perfect, but pooled over $x$ it is not, so the pair is interior and Stage 1 accepts it. $\hat\theta_k$ is still a fixed function of $\hat\theta_i$
in every sample, so $\hat\Gamma$ loses rank exactly: 2 columns for a binary item, 3 for a ternary one (R, E-097). $\Delta$
keeps full rank. Production agrees: the Mata probe gives $\hat\Gamma$ three singular values near $10^{-15}$. This case is not embedded in `m10-verify`
because its script patches `cx_pair_fit`; its log is the record.

*Not established.* Any other cause (partial duplication, duplication across items with different $K$, relations among three or more
columns, relations involving $x$ itself). The statement is: one cause exact in samples (duplication, loss $K_j$), identical and complementary columns not.

*Verification:* chunk `m10-verify`, section V3 (M3(a) to M3(c) in R); M3(d) as cited above.

### M4. Counts are per $(\text{category},x)$ cell (the small-count family)

For a binary item the conditional estimates are $\hat\tau=\Phi^{-1}(\hat p_0)$ and $\hat b=\Phi^{-1}(\hat p_0)-\Phi^{-1}(\hat p_1)$ with
$\hat p_g$ the proportion in category 0 within group $g$. Then, with $\pi_g=n_g/N$ and $\tau_1=\tau-b$,
$$\hat\Gamma_{\tau\tau}=\frac{p_0(1-p_0)}{\phi(\tau)^2\pi_0},\quad \hat\Gamma_{\tau b}=\hat\Gamma_{\tau\tau},\quad
\hat\Gamma_{bb}=\hat\Gamma_{\tau\tau}+\frac{p_1(1-p_1)}{\phi(\tau_1)^2\pi_1},$$
two independent binomials, each on its own group's $n_g$. The exact small-count reference of `@sec-gamma-smallcount` therefore applies to **each group's
boundary cell** with $(N,m)$ replaced by $(n_g,m_g)$, up to the factor $N/(N-1)$ against $n_g/(n_g-1)$ in the standard error: the mean-SE to SD ratio
for $(m,n_0,N)=(1,2500,5000)$ is 1.903 against v1's 1.903 at $N=2500$, and 1.892, 1.113, 0.963 against 1.893, 1.114, 0.963 at $n_0=500$.

The **pooled** boundary count cannot see this. Two tables of $N=2000$ with $n_0=1800$, $n_1=200$ and pooled $y=0$ counts of 701 and 800 give
$\widehat{SE}(\hat b)=0.35$ and $0.09$: the first has one observation in the $(y=0,x=1)$ cell, the second 100. The slope's precision is set by the group cell.

*Not established.* $K_j>2$: the parallel shift is not saturated, so $(\hat\tau,\hat b)$ are not functions of group proportions and no exact reference
exists (same position as v1's interior-category mode). Pair cells: nothing derived. A threshold for any row: none, as in v1.

*Verification:* chunk `m10-verify`, section V4.

### M5. The bread's numerical-rank criterion on $W_D^{1/2}\Delta$ with slope rows

`@sec-bread-rank` bounds the noise by rounding alone because every correlation is at most quadratic in each single parameter,
and the weights cancel from $\nu\le\sqrt P\,\eta$. The slope rows are $b_j=\lambda_j\gamma+\kappa_j$ (single factor, $\psi$ fixed), bilinear: the same argument applies,
$\eta\lesssim\sqrt{n_s}\,\varepsilon\,|\sigma_k|/(h\|\Delta_k\|)$ with $|\sigma_k|/\|\Delta_k\|\le\min(|\lambda_j|,|\gamma|)$ for a row with no free $\kappa$.
The threshold block stays a literal identity (`@sec-condx`, `tau_block_identity`, also with $\kappa$ free).

*Check, on a population design (a model of production's arithmetic, not its bits).* Central differences, $h=10^{-5}\max(1,|\theta|)$: noise
$\nu=3.5\times10^{-11}$; genuine ratio 0.376 at $q=0.4$ and 0.174 at $q=0.05$ (row-weight spreads 7.7 and 39); an exact null
(disturbance variance free, scale $(\lambda,\gamma,\psi)\to(c\lambda,\gamma/c,\psi/c^2)$) reads $2.9\times10^{-13}$ and $1.4\times10^{-13}$.
An all-$\kappa$ model has npar $12>D=11$: row 1 flags it before any ratio is read. The two-decade margins on each side hold on these designs.

**Production, measured (StataMP 18, `probe_cx_delta.do`, Mata).** The bread ratio of production's conditional $\Delta$ is 0.15 (`condx_A`) and 0.12 (`condx_D`)
for a healthy fit, and $4.0\times10^{-13}$ and $1.2\times10^{-13}$ for an exact scale twin. The $10^{-8}$ criterion separates them by about five orders on each side.

*Not established.* Designs with a boundary threshold or a near-1 residual correlation (large weight spread) were not run with a covariate. Models with $B$
and several factors were not run, and Stata 16.1 was not measured.

*Verification:* chunk `m10-verify`, section V5; production by the probe above.

### Decisions taken (owner, 2026-11-15)

All recorded in the development record (E-107), with their evidence.

- **Row 3 (patterns)** counts patterns on $(y,x)$; `dwlsmv_npatterns` and `dwlsmv_gammadiag` take the covariate (M1). The cut is $r^*=\min(D,n_{\rm pat}-1)$.
- **Row 4 (aliasing)** is not evaluated in conditional mode (M3): v1's cause test would certify deficiencies the population lacks (M3(b)) and misses
  the loss of the slope (M3(a)). The mixed-orientation limitation of M3(d) is stated to the user. An exact detector is later work, derivation first.
- **Counts (M4):** the per-(item, category, $x$-group) counts are reported, and the pooled counts kept.
- **Posted values:** `e(gamma_ratio)`, `e(gamma_ratio_raw)`, `e(gamma_rank)` and `e(bread_ratio)`.
- **Bread (M5):** the bread rank enters the conditional D11 trigger, as in v1 ("Yes, both").
- **Notes' wording for slope rows** follows the session's recommendation (a mechanical choice).

```{r m10-verify}
local({
  .old_seed <- if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())) get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) else NULL
  on.exit({ if (exists("cx_K_orig", inherits = FALSE)) { cx_K <<- cx_K_orig; cx_true <<- cx_true_orig } }, add = TRUE)
  on.exit(if (is.null(.old_seed)) { if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())) rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) } else assign(".Random.seed", .old_seed, envir = globalenv()), add = TRUE)
# m10_verify.R -- base-R verification for the Module 10 / conditional-mode draft (m10_deriv_draft.qmd).
# DRAFT by a read-only agent. Reads the derivation file only to reuse its chunks cx-setup, cx-stage1,
# cx-psi, cx-model (base R, no package). Writes nothing in the repository.
# R doubles, NOT Mata. Nothing here certifies a Stata/Mata routine.
cat("m10_verify.R   R", as.character(getRversion()), "\n")
cat("Reused chunks: cx-setup cx-stage1 cx-psi cx-model (R doubles, NOT Mata)\n\n")
nt <- sum(cx_K - 1)
fails <- character()
chk <- function(name, ok) { cat(sprintf("  [%s] %s\n", if (isTRUE(ok)) "ok " else "FAIL", name)); if (!isTRUE(ok)) fails <<- c(fails, name) }
rank_of <- function(G, tol = 1e-10) { s <- svd(G)$d; sum(s / s[1] > tol) }
```
