```{r m10-verify}
npat_y  <- function(d) nrow(unique(d$Y))
sep_ok  <- function(d) all(vapply(seq_len(ncol(d$Y)), function(j) {
  a <- d$Y[d$x == 0, j]; b <- d$Y[d$x == 1, j]
  length(a) > 0 && length(b) > 0 && max(a) > min(b) && max(b) > min(a) &&
    all(0:(cx_K[j] - 1) %in% d$Y[, j])
}, TRUE))
sub_design <- function(pop, idx, cnt) {
  w <- numeric(length(pop$w)); w[idx] <- cnt; w <- w / sum(w); k <- w > 0
  list(Y = pop$Y[k, , drop = FALSE], x = pop$x[k], w = w[k])
}

# ======================================================================================
cat("V1  Row 3, patterns are (y, x): rank(Gamma_hat) <= min(D, n_pat - 1), n_pat counted on (y,x)\n")
set.seed(20261115)
pop <- cx_population(cx_true)
D <- nt + cx_p + nrow(cx_pairs)
cat(sprintf("    design K = (%s); D = T + p + P = %d + %d + %d = %d; 36 population patterns, 18 y-patterns\n",
            paste(cx_K, collapse = ","), nt, cx_p, nrow(cx_pairs), D))
try_design <- function(make) {
  for (a in 1:200) {
    d <- make()
    if (!sep_ok(d)) next
    r <- try({ f <- cx_stage1(d); if (any(abs(f$rho) > 0.98)) stop("boundary"); list(f = f, psi = cx_psi(d, f)) }, silent = TRUE)
    if (!inherits(r, "try-error")) return(c(list(d = d), r))
  }
  NULL
}
res1 <- list()
for (m in c(8, 9, 10, 12, 16, 24, 36)) {
  mk <- if (m == 16) function() {                      # 8 y-patterns, each in BOTH x groups
    yi <- sample.int(18, 8); sub_design(pop, c(yi, yi + 18), sample(2:6, 16, TRUE)) }
        else if (m == 36) function() sub_design(pop, 1:36, sample(2:6, 36, TRUE))
        else function() { idx <- sample.int(36, m); sub_design(pop, idx, sample(2:6, m, TRUE)) }
  r <- try_design(mk)
  if (is.null(r)) { cat("    n_pat", m, ": no admissible random design found\n"); next }
  G <- crossprod(r$psi * sqrt(r$d$w)); npx <- nrow(r$d$Y)
  res1[[length(res1) + 1]] <- c(n_pat = npx, n_pat_y = npat_y(r$d), rank = rank_of(G), bound = min(D, npx - 1),
                                v1_rule_flags = (npat_y(r$d) - 1 < D), xrule_flags = (npx - 1 < D))
}
R1 <- do.call(rbind, res1); print(R1)
chk("rank <= min(D, n_pat-1) on every design", all(R1[, "rank"] <= R1[, "bound"]))
chk("rank == min(D, n_pat-1) on every design (measured; the theorem gives <= only)", all(R1[, "rank"] == R1[, "bound"]))
paired <- R1[R1[, "v1_rule_flags"] == 1 & R1[, "xrule_flags"] == 0, , drop = FALSE]
cat(sprintf("    designs where the y-only count flags but the (y,x) count does not: %d\n", nrow(paired)))
chk("the paired design: v1's y-only count flags 'too few patterns', the (y,x) count and the rank say no deficiency",
    nrow(paired) >= 1 && all(paired[, "v1_rule_flags"] == 1) && all(paired[, "rank"] == D))

# ======================================================================================
cat("\nV2  Centring: psibar_theta = d_k (the last Newton step); psibar_rho = -U_rho^-1 (Sbar + U_theta psibar_theta)\n")
nine <- local({ keep <- c(1, 3, 8, 13, 15, 22, 23, 29, 36); sub_design(pop, keep, c(3, 2, 3, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2)) })
fit_step <- function(d, d1 = 1e-12) {                     # production-like rule: stop on the Newton step
  th <- lapply(seq_len(cx_p), function(j) {
    K <- cx_K[j]; yj <- d$Y[, j]
    pm <- cumsum(tapply(d$w, factor(yj, 0:(K - 1)), sum))[-K]; t <- c(qnorm(pm / sum(d$w)), 0)
    for (it in 1:60) {
      g <- colSums(d$w * cx_uni_score(yj, d$x, t))
      H <- -cx_jac(function(u) colSums(d$w * cx_uni_score(yj, d$x, u)), t)
      dd <- solve(H, g)
      if (max(abs(dd)) <= d1) return(list(th = t, d = dd))
      t <- t + dd
    }
    stop("no step stop") })
  list(th = lapply(th, `[[`, "th"), dstep = lapply(th, `[[`, "d"))
}
fs <- fit_step(nine)
fitN <- cx_stage1(nine); fitN$th <- fs$th            # items by the step rule, pairs by the stage-1 root
fitN$rho <- apply(cx_pairs, 1, function(ij) cx_pair_fit(cx_pair_cells(nine$Y[, ij[1]], nine$Y[, ij[2]], nine$x, nine$w), fs$th[[ij[1]]], fs$th[[ij[2]]]))
psiN <- cx_psi(nine, fitN); pbN <- colSums(nine$w * psiN)
dstep_all <- c(unlist(lapply(fs$dstep, function(v) v[-length(v)])), vapply(fs$dstep, function(v) v[length(v)], 0))
pbth <- pbN[seq_len(nt + cx_p)]
chk(sprintf("psibar_theta equals the last Newton step (max gap %.1e)", max(abs(pbth - dstep_all))),
    max(abs(pbth - dstep_all)) < 1e-12)
chk(sprintf("|psibar_theta| <= delta1 = 1e-12 (max %.1e)", max(abs(pbth))), max(abs(pbth)) <= 1e-12)
GN <- crossprod(psiN * sqrt(nine$w)); zN <- abs(pbN) / sqrt(diag(GN))
cat(sprintf("    z = max|psibar_k|/sqrt(Gamma_kk): theta rows %.2e, rho rows %.2e (flag at 1e-6)\n",
            max(zN[seq_len(nt + cx_p)]), max(zN[-seq_len(nt + cx_p)])))
chk("z (all rows) below the 1e-6 flag at the step rule's delta1", max(zN) < 1e-6)
# the identity for rho, at a deliberately sloppy first stage
sl <- fitN
sl$th <- lapply(seq_len(cx_p), function(j) sl$th[[j]] + c(rep(3e-3, cx_K[j] - 1), -2e-3))
sl$rho <- sl$rho + 2e-3
psiS <- cx_psi(nine, sl); pbS <- colSums(nine$w * psiS)
th_bar <- pbS[seq_len(nt + cx_p)]
form <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(cx_pairs)), function(m) {
  i <- cx_pairs[m, 1]; j <- cx_pairs[m, 2]; thi <- sl$th[[i]]; thj <- sl$th[[j]]; rho <- sl$rho[m]
  cells <- cx_pair_cells(nine$Y[, i], nine$Y[, j], nine$x, nine$w)
  ubar <- function(ti, tj, r) sum(cells$w * cx_pair_u(cells, ti, tj, r))
  h <- 1e-6; Ur <- (ubar(thi, thj, rho + h) - ubar(thi, thj, rho - h)) / (2 * h)
  ni <- length(thi); U1 <- cx_jac(function(t) ubar(t[1:ni], t[-(1:ni)], rho), c(thi, thj))
  bar_item <- function(jj) { ii <- c(seq_len(cx_K[jj] - 1) + sum(cx_K[seq_len(jj - 1)] - 1), nt + jj); th_bar[ii] }
  tb <- c(bar_item(i), bar_item(j))
  -(ubar(thi, thj, rho) + sum(U1 * tb)) / Ur }, 0)
gapf <- max(abs(form - pbS[-seq_len(nt + cx_p)]))
chk(sprintf("psibar_rho = -(Sbar + U_theta psibar_theta)/U_rho at a perturbed first stage (max gap %.1e)", gapf), gapf < 1e-9)
# Theorem 1(2) on the scale-free matrix: lambda_{r+1}(R G R) <= sum z_k^2
GS <- crossprod(psiS * sqrt(nine$w)); s <- sqrt(diag(GS)); Rg <- GS / (s %o% s)
ev <- sort(eigen(Rg, symmetric = TRUE)$values, decreasing = TRUE); zS <- abs(pbS) / s
cat(sprintf("    sloppy first stage: lambda_9 of the scale-free Gamma = %.2e, sum z^2 = %.2e (r* = 8)\n", ev[9], sum(zS^2)))
chk("lambda_{r*+1} <= sum z_k^2, and the extra eigenvalue is visible", ev[9] <= sum(zS^2) * (1 + 1e-6) && ev[9] > 1e-12)

cat("\nV3  Aliasing: which causes are exact in samples under x?\n")
cx_K_orig <- cx_K; cx_true_orig <- cx_true
cx_merge <- function(d) { key <- do.call(paste, c(as.data.frame(d$Y), list(d$x)))
  w <- tapply(d$w, key, sum); first <- match(names(w), key)
  list(Y = d$Y[first, , drop = FALSE], x = d$x[first], w = as.numeric(w)) }
uni_psi <- function(dd) do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(cx_p), function(j) {
  th <- cx_uni_fit(dd$Y[, j], dd$x, dd$w, cx_K[j]); G <- cx_uni_score(dd$Y[, j], dd$x, th)
  H <- -cx_jac(function(t) colSums(dd$w * cx_uni_score(dd$Y[, j], dd$x, t)), th); G %*% t(solve(H)) }))
svr <- function(dd) { d <- svd(crossprod(uni_psi(dd) * sqrt(dd$w)))$d; d / d[1] }
resample <- function(pp, NN) { cnt <- tabulate(sample.int(length(pp$w), NN, TRUE, pp$w), length(pp$w))
  w <- cnt / NN; k <- w > 0; list(Y = pp$Y[k, , drop = FALSE], x = pp$x[k], w = w[k]) }
# (a) exact duplication, binary pair (K = 2,2,3): loss is K_j = 2 (tau and the slope), not K_j - 1 = 1
cx_K <<- c(2L, 2L, 3L)
cx_true <<- list(tau = list(-0.3, 0.2, c(-0.2, 0.8)), lambda = c(0.8, 0.7, 0.6), gamma = 0.5, q = 0.4)
p2 <- cx_population(cx_true)
dupb <- p2; dupb$Y[, 2] <- p2$Y[, 1]; dupb <- cx_merge(dupb)
revb <- p2; revb$Y[, 2] <- 1L - p2$Y[, 1]; revb <- cx_merge(revb)
set.seed(11)
dup_out <- t(sapply(list(dup = dupb, rev = revb), function(pp) {
  rp <- svr(pp); sm <- svr(resample(pp, 2000)); c(pop_lost2 = max(tail(rp, 2)), samp_lost2 = max(tail(sm, 2)),
                                                 kept = rp[length(rp) - 2]) }))
print(signif(dup_out, 3))
chk("exact duplication (binary, same and reversed): K_j = 2 ranks lost, exactly, in population and sample (<= 1e-14); v1 counts 1",
    all(dup_out[, "pop_lost2"] < 1e-14) && all(dup_out[, "samp_lost2"] < 1e-14) && all(dup_out[, "kept"] > 1e-3))
# (b) block aliasing: Z_{1,1} == Z_{3,1} on the support, item 3 ternary, so rho_13 is not forced to the boundary
cx_K <<- c(3L, 3L, 3L)
cx_true <<- list(tau = list(c(-0.5, 0.6), c(-0.2, 0.9), c(-0.3, 0.5)), lambda = c(0.8, 0.7, 0.6), gamma = 0.5, q = 0.4)
p3 <- cx_population(cx_true)
blk <- p3; blk$w <- blk$w * ((blk$Y[, 1] == 0) == (blk$Y[, 3] == 0)); blk$w <- blk$w / sum(blk$w)
k <- blk$w > 0; blk <- list(Y = blk$Y[k, , drop = FALSE], x = blk$x[k], w = blk$w[k])
chk("block design: 1{y1<1} == 1{y3<1} on every supported pattern (v1's cause test would fire: identical columns)",
    all((blk$Y[, 1] < 1) == (blk$Y[, 3] < 1)))
fb <- try(cx_stage1(blk), silent = TRUE)
if (inherits(fb, "try-error")) { cat("    cx_stage1 on the block design failed:", conditionMessage(attr(fb, "condition")), "\n"); rho13 <- NA
} else { rho13 <- fb$rho[2]; cat(sprintf("    block design: rho_12 = %.4f, rho_13 = %.4f, rho_23 = %.4f\n", fb$rho[1], fb$rho[2], fb$rho[3])) }
chk("rho_13 is interior in the block design (|rho_13| < 0.99), so Stage 1 does not refuse it", isTRUE(abs(rho13) < 0.99))
rp <- svr(blk)
cat(sprintf("    block population: three smallest singular ratios of Gamma_thetatheta: %s\n", paste(signif(tail(rp, 3), 3), collapse = " ")))
chk("block population (item 3 ternary): NO exact null direction even in the population (smallest ratio in (1e-9, 1e-2)), only a near one",
    tail(rp, 1) > 1e-9 && tail(rp, 1) < 1e-2)
set.seed(7)
bs <- t(sapply(c(500, 2000, 8000, 32000), function(NN) {
  r <- replicate(3, tail(svr(resample(blk, NN)), 1)); c(N = NN, min_ratio = min(r), max_ratio = max(r)) }))
print(signif(bs, 3))
chk("block aliasing is NOT exact in samples either: smallest ratio > 1e-9 at every N", all(bs[, "min_ratio"] > 1e-9))
# the contrast: with item 3 BINARY the same identity forces y3 = 1{y1 >= 1}, a null direction in the population (qmd, cxp-alias2)
# and perfect association in both x groups (rho -> 1; P2), so Stage 1's boundary rule acts first
# (c) complementary columns: Z_{3,1} = 1 - Z_{1,1} on the support (the other diagonal)
cmp <- p3; cmp$w <- cmp$w * ((cmp$Y[, 1] == 0) != (cmp$Y[, 3] == 0)); cmp$w <- cmp$w / sum(cmp$w)
k <- cmp$w > 0; cmp <- list(Y = cmp$Y[k, , drop = FALSE], x = cmp$x[k], w = cmp$w[k])
rc <- svr(cmp)
set.seed(8); cs <- t(sapply(c(500, 8000), function(NN) { r <- replicate(3, tail(svr(resample(cmp, NN)), 1)); c(N = NN, min_ratio = min(r)) }))
cat(sprintf("    complementary block: population smallest ratio %.2e; sample min ratio at N = 500, 8000: %s\n",
            tail(rc, 1), paste(signif(cs[, 2], 3), collapse = ", ")))
chk("complementary block: no exact null direction in the population or in samples (ratios > 1e-9)", tail(rc, 1) > 1e-9 && all(cs[, 2] > 1e-9))
cx_K <<- cx_K_orig; cx_true <<- cx_true_orig

# ======================================================================================
cat("\nV4  Counts: for a binary item the exact reference is binomial in the (category, x-group) cell\n")
tab <- matrix(c(700, 1100, 1, 199), 2, 2, dimnames = list(y = 0:1, x = 0:1))  # rows y, cols x; N = 2000
cnts <- as.vector(tab)
dd <- list(Y = cbind(rep(0:1, 2)), x = rep(0:1, each = 2)); dd$w <- cnts / sum(cnts); N <- sum(cnts)
th <- cx_uni_fit(dd$Y[, 1], dd$x, dd$w, 2)
Hh <- -cx_jac(function(t) colSums(dd$w * cx_uni_score(dd$Y[, 1], dd$x, t)), th)
Ps <- cx_uni_score(dd$Y[, 1], dd$x, th) %*% t(solve(Hh)); Gm <- crossprod(Ps * sqrt(dd$w))
n0 <- sum(tab[, 1]); n1 <- sum(tab[, 2]); p0 <- tab[1, 1] / n0; p1 <- tab[1, 2] / n1
tau <- qnorm(p0); b <- qnorm(p0) - qnorm(p1)
g_tt <- p0 * (1 - p0) / (dnorm(tau)^2 * (n0 / N)); g_bb <- g_tt + p1 * (1 - p1) / (dnorm(tau - b)^2 * (n1 / N))
cat(sprintf("    sample: tau-hat %.4f (closed form %.4f), b-hat %.4f (closed form %.4f)\n", th[1], tau, th[2], b))
chk("Gamma_tt, Gamma_tb, Gamma_bb equal the two-binomial closed forms", max(abs(c(Gm[1, 1] - g_tt, Gm[1, 2] - g_tt, Gm[2, 2] - g_bb)) / c(g_tt, g_tt, g_bb)) < 1e-6)
se_b <- sqrt(Gm[2, 2] / (N - 1))
cat(sprintf("    this table: pooled count of y = 0 is %d, the (y = 0, x = 1) cell is %d; SE(b-hat) = %.2f\n", sum(tab[1, ]), tab[1, 2], se_b))
tab2 <- tab; tab2[1, 2] <- 100; tab2[2, 2] <- 100; d2 <- dd; d2$w <- as.vector(tab2) / sum(tab2); N2 <- sum(tab2)
th2 <- cx_uni_fit(d2$Y[, 1], d2$x, d2$w, 2); H2 <- -cx_jac(function(t) colSums(d2$w * cx_uni_score(d2$Y[, 1], d2$x, t)), th2)
P2 <- cx_uni_score(d2$Y[, 1], d2$x, th2) %*% t(solve(H2)); G2 <- crossprod(P2 * sqrt(d2$w))
se_b2 <- sqrt(G2[2, 2] / (N2 - 1))
cat(sprintf("    a table with 100 in the (y = 0, x = 1) cell instead: pooled count %d, SE(b-hat) = %.2f\n", sum(tab2[1, ]), se_b2))
chk("pooled count 701 vs 800 look alike, the group cell (1 vs 100) does not: SE(b) is > 3x larger", se_b > 3 * se_b2)
pg_small <- function(m, N = 5000) { k <- 1:(N - 1); w <- dbinom(k, N, m / N); w <- w / sum(w); q <- k / N; th <- qnorm(q)
  se <- sqrt(q * (1 - q) / (N - 1)) / dnorm(th); mu <- sum(w * th); v <- sum(w * (th - mu)^2); sum(w * se) / sqrt(v) }
cond_small <- function(m, n0, NN) { k <- 1:(n0 - 1); w <- dbinom(k, n0, m / n0); w <- w / sum(w); q <- k / n0; th <- qnorm(q)
  se <- sqrt(q * (1 - q) / dnorm(th)^2 / n0 * NN / (NN - 1)); mu <- sum(w * th); v <- sum(w * (th - mu)^2); sum(w * se) / sqrt(v) }
tb <- t(sapply(list(c(1, 2500, 5000), c(1, 500, 1000), c(3, 500, 1000), c(10, 500, 1000)),
               function(a) c(m = a[1], n0 = a[2], N = a[3], cond = cond_small(a[1], a[2], a[3]), v1_at_n0 = pg_small(a[1], a[2]))))
print(signif(tb, 4))
chk("E[SE]/SD of a boundary threshold in group 0 = the v1 table with N replaced by n0 (|diff| < 0.01)", all(abs(tb[, "cond"] - tb[, "v1_at_n0"]) < 0.01))

# ======================================================================================
cat("\nV5  Bread: the 1e-8 criterion on W^1/2 Delta for a conditional model (slope rows; bilinear b = lambda*gamma + kappa)\n")
cd_jac <- function(f, th) sapply(seq_along(th), function(k) { h <- 1e-5 * max(1, abs(th[k])); e <- replace(numeric(length(th)), k, h)
  (f(th + e) - f(th - e)) / (2 * h) })          # production's recipe for the structural columns (@sec-bread-rank)
bread <- function(popX, kap = integer(), label = "") {
  fitX <- cx_stage1(popX); Gx <- crossprod(cx_psi(popX, fitX) * sqrt(popX$w)); Wd <- 1 / diag(Gx)
  th <- c(th0, rep(0.2, length(kap)))
  sigf <- function(t) cx_sig_th(t, kap)
  Dn <- cd_jac(sigf, th)
  Da <- cx_jac(sigf, th)                 # reference: central difference at h = 1e-6, the model is bilinear so no truncation
  Dn[1:nt, 1:nt] <- diag(nt)             # the threshold block is a literal identity
  E <- Dn - Da; E[1:nt, ] <- 0; E[, 1:nt] <- 0
  M <- sqrt(Wd) * Dn; sM <- svd(M)$d; nu <- norm(sqrt(Wd) * E, "2") / sM[1]
  eta <- max(sqrt(rowSums(E^2)) / pmax(sqrt(rowSums(Da^2)), 1e-300))
  cat(sprintf("    %-34s npar %2d  ratio(W^1/2 Delta) %.3e  noise nu %.1e  eta %.1e  weight spread %.1e\n",
              label, ncol(Dn), min(sM) / sM[1], nu, eta, max(Wd) / min(Wd)))
  c(ratio = min(sM) / sM[1], nu = nu, eta = eta)
}
# a model with the disturbance variance free: rho_ij = lambda_i lambda_j psi, b_j = lambda_j gamma; the scale
# (lambda, gamma, psi) -> (c lambda, gamma / c, psi / c^2) leaves sigma unchanged: an EXACT null direction of Delta
sig_psi <- function(t) { lam <- t[nt + 1:3]; gam <- t[nt + 4]; ps <- t[nt + 5]
  c(t[1:nt], lam * gam, apply(cx_pairs, 1, function(ij) lam[ij[1]] * lam[ij[2]] * ps)) }
bread_gen <- function(popX, sigf, th, label) {
  fitX <- cx_stage1(popX); Gx <- crossprod(cx_psi(popX, fitX) * sqrt(popX$w)); Wd <- 1 / diag(Gx)
  Dn <- cd_jac(sigf, th); Da <- cx_jac(sigf, th); Dn[1:nt, 1:nt] <- diag(nt)
  E <- Dn - Da; E[1:nt, ] <- 0; E[, 1:nt] <- 0
  M <- sqrt(Wd) * Dn; sM <- svd(M)$d; nu <- norm(sqrt(Wd) * E, "2") / sM[1]
  cat(sprintf("    %-38s npar %2d  D %d  ratio(W^1/2 Delta) %.3e  noise nu %.1e  weight spread %.1e\n",
              label, ncol(Dn), nrow(Dn), min(sM) / sM[1], nu, max(Wd) / min(Wd)))
  c(ratio = min(sM) / sM[1], nu = nu)
}
popq <- cx_population(modifyList(cx_true, list(q = 0.05)))
th_p <- c(th0, 1)
b_h  <- bread_gen(pop,  function(t) cx_sig_th(t), th0, "healthy (q = 0.4)")
b_hq <- bread_gen(popq, function(t) cx_sig_th(t), th0, "healthy, rare x (q = 0.05)")
b_t  <- bread_gen(pop,  sig_psi, th_p, "psi free: scale twin (deficient)")
b_tq <- bread_gen(popq, sig_psi, th_p, "psi free: scale twin, rare x")
chk("healthy: noise nu at least 100x below 1e-8, genuine ratio at least 100x above it",
    b_h["nu"] < 1e-10 && b_h["ratio"] > 1e-6 && b_hq["nu"] < 1e-10 && b_hq["ratio"] > 1e-6)
chk("the scale twin (exact null) reads below 1e-8 at both x prevalences: the criterion catches it",
    b_t["ratio"] < 1e-8 && b_tq["ratio"] < 1e-8)
chk("an all-kappa model has npar > D (12 > 11): row 1 of breaddiag flags it before any ratio",
    { kt <- c(th0, rep(0.2, 3)); ncol(cd_jac(function(t) cx_sig_th(t, 1:3), kt)) > D })

cat("\n")
if (length(fails)) { cat("FAILED CHECKS:\n"); print(fails) } else cat("m10-verify: all checks passed\n")
stopifnot(length(fails) == 0)
})
```

## A tail-accurate cell probability: the conditional rectangle integral {#sec-tphi}

**Status (2026-10-29): a candidate under derivation, not a production method.** The Φ₂ tail
study (E-063) found that Stata's `binormal()` returns 0 below about
$10^{-13}$, so four-corner cell probabilities lose all relative accuracy in the tail. The user
accepted this section's architecture (E-067, 2026-10-29): integrate the rectangle
directly (D1), in log space with $\ln P$ returned beside $P$ (D2), derivatives later (D4), over
v1's domain and conditional mode's ($|{\rm bound}|\le4$, $|\rho|\le0.999$; D6). The fixed
quadrature rule (D3) is **conditional**: it is adopted only once this section gives a
quantitative quadrature bound, a certified truncation bound and an acceptable node count over
the whole domain. Verification against references (D5) is conditional on a §3a independence
audit; M4 is **not** independent of this method (same integrand and rule family). Production
adoption is gated on the measured envelope (step 2) and a production accuracy study (step 5).

Notation: a cell $R=[a_1,a_2]\times[b_1,b_2]$, $-\infty\le a_1<a_2\le\infty$ and likewise $b$;
$\rho\in(-1,1)$, $s=\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$; $\beta_j(x)=(b_j-\rho x)/s$; $\Phi(\pm\infty)=1,0$.

### Result T1: the rectangle is a one-dimensional integral (proved)

$$P(R)=\int_{a_1}^{a_2} f(x)\,dx,\qquad f(x)=\varphi(x)\,D(x),\qquad D(x)=\Phi(\beta_2(x))-\Phi(\beta_1(x)).$$

*Proof.* $Y\mid X=x\sim N(\rho x,s^2)$, so $\Pr(b_1\le Y\le b_2\mid x)=D(x)$; integrate against
$\varphi$. ∎ The roles of the two axes may be swapped ($\rho$ unchanged), a cost choice only.
**What it buys:** $f\ge0$, so a rule with positive weights adds positive terms; there is no
cancellation between corners, and the relative error of the sum is controlled by the relative
error of each term (T5).

### Result T2: $f$ is log-concave (proved)

The bivariate normal density is log-concave in $(x,y)$, and so is its product with the indicator
of the convex strip $b_1\le y\le b_2$. By Prékopa's theorem a marginal of a log-concave function
over a convex set is log-concave, so $x\mapsto\int_{b_1}^{b_2}\varphi_2(x,y;\rho)\,dy=f(x)$ is
log-concave. ∎ Consequences: $f$ is unimodal on $\mathbb R$; and $\ell(x)=\ln f(x)$ has a
non-increasing derivative
$$\ell'(x)=-x+\frac{D'(x)}{D(x)},\qquad D'(x)=-\frac{\rho}{s}\bigl(\varphi(\beta_2)-\varphi(\beta_1)\bigr),$$
both computable in log space.

### Result T3: a bound on $f$ off the real axis (proved)

For $z=u+iv$,
$$|f(u+iv)|\le f(u)\,\exp\!\Bigl(\frac{v^2}{2s^2}\Bigr).$$

*Proof.* $|\varphi(z)|=\varphi(u)e^{v^2/2}$. $D(z)=\int_{b_1}^{b_2}\varphi((y-\rho z)/s)\,dy/s$, and
${\rm Re}\,(y-\rho z)^2=(y-\rho u)^2-\rho^2v^2$, so by the triangle inequality
$|D(z)|\le e^{\rho^2v^2/(2s^2)}D(u)$. Multiply: $v^2/2+\rho^2v^2/(2s^2)=v^2/(2s^2)$. ∎
**What it buys:** the analyticity constant of a Gauss–Legendre error bound on a panel reduces to
real values of $f$ and one explicit factor. On a panel of half-length $h$ mapped to $[-1,1]$, the
Bernstein ellipse $E_r$ has semi-minor axis $h(r-r^{-1})/2$, so the factor is
$\exp\{h^2(r-r^{-1})^2/(8s^2)\}$; panels of half-length of order $s$ keep it near $e^{1/2}$.

### Result T4: a certified truncation of an infinite end (proved)

If $a_1=-\infty$ and $L$ has $\lambda=\ell'(L)>0$, then
$$\int_{-\infty}^{L} f(x)\,dx\le\frac{f(L)}{\lambda}.$$

*Proof.* By T2, $\ell(x)\le\ell(L)+\lambda(x-L)$ for all $x$ (a concave function lies below its
tangent); integrate $e^{\ell}$ over $(-\infty,L]$. ∎ Symmetrically for $a_2=+\infty$ with
$\ell'(L)<0$, bound $f(L)/|\ell'(L)|$. With a certified lower bound $\underline P$ on the
retained part (the computed sum less its rule bound), choosing $L$ with
$f(L)/\lambda\le\eta\,\underline P$ certifies a relative truncation error $\le\eta$. The test uses
only $\ln f(L)$, $\ell'(L)$ and $\ln\underline P$, so it never underflows.

### Result T5: positive sums in log space (proved; standard)

With weights $w_i>0$ and computed $\hat G_i=\ln w_i+\ell(x_i)$ with absolute errors
$|\hat G_i-G_i|\le e_i$, the log-sum-exp $\ln\hat Q=\hat G^*+\ln\sum_i e^{\hat G_i-\hat G^*}$ has
relative error in $Q$ at most $\max_i e_i$ plus the summation's $\gamma_n$, to first order.
**The cost of the log scale:** an absolute error $\varepsilon\,|G_i|$ in a logarithm is a
relative error $\varepsilon\,|G_i|$ in the term, and on the domain $|G_i|$ reaches about $1.6\times10^4$
($\beta\approx-179$ at $b=-4$, $x=4$, $\rho=0.999$), i.e. about $3.6\times10^{-12}$. This matches
the problem's own conditioning: $d\ln P/d\ln b$ is of order $\beta^2$ there, so rounding the inputs
alone moves $P$ by the same relative amount. The achievable target is therefore
$O\bigl((1+|\ln P|)\,\varepsilon\bigr)$ relative, not $O(\varepsilon)$; Arm D's $10^{-8}$ lies above it
everywhere on the domain.

### Evaluating $D$: four regimes (error model stated, constants not yet derived)

With $w=\beta_2-\beta_1=(b_2-b_1)/s$:
- **N (narrow):** $w\,(1+\max_j|\beta_j|)\le c_N$: $D=\int_{\beta_1}^{\beta_2}\varphi$ by a short
  Gauss–Legendre rule in log space; $\varphi$ is entire, so its rule bound is elementary. Relative
  accuracy $O(\varepsilon)$, with no narrow-interval cancellation.
- **T (both lower, $\beta_2\le0$):** $\ln D=\ln\Phi(\beta_2)+\ln(1-e^{-\Delta})$,
  $\Delta=\ln\Phi(\beta_2)-\ln\Phi(\beta_1)$, the second term by `log1mexp` (Mächler, 2012). Outside N,
  $\Delta\ge w\max(0.798,|\beta_2|)$ (the Mills ratio $\varphi/\Phi$ is decreasing and $\ge|\beta|$ on
  $\beta\le0$), which bounds the amplification of the error in $\Delta$.
- **U (both upper, $\beta_1\ge0$):** T mirrored, with $\Phi(-\beta)$.
- **M (straddling 0):** $D=1-\Phi(\beta_1)-\Phi(-\beta_2)$, both terms $<\tfrac12$; outside N, $D$ is
  bounded below, so linear-scale rounding is relative $O(\varepsilon)$.

**Assumption, not established:** T and U need `lnnormal()` with absolute error
$O(\varepsilon\,|\ln\Phi(\beta)|)$ for $\beta$ down to about $-180$. Stata documents no accuracy for it;
it is a separate component to certify (the tail study's univariate add-on measured `normal()`,
not `lnnormal()`).

### The panel rule (DRAFT, not frozen; revised 2026-10-29 at the user's request)

The user retained the principles of the first draft (fixed deterministic placement,
concavity-based enclosures, explicit failure statuses, a preregistered cost gate) and asked for
four revisions before freezing. Each is below; the rule is not frozen and no node count has been
measured.

**R-a. The quadrature theorem, verified at source.** Trefethen (2008, *SIAM Review* 50:67–87),
Theorem 4.5, eq. (4.14): for $I_n$ the **$(n+1)$-point** Gauss rule on $[-1,1]$ and $f$ analytic
with $|f|\le M$ in the region bounded by the Bernstein ellipse $E_r$ (foci $\pm1$, semiaxes
summing to $r>1$), $|I-I_n|\le 64M/\{15(1-r^{-2})r^{2n+2}\}$. For an $m$-point rule ($n=m-1$)
this is
$$|I-I_m^{\rm GL}|\le\frac{64}{15}\,\frac{M\,r^{-2(m-1)}}{r^2-1}.$$
The first draft wrote $r^{-2m}$ (citing *ATAP* without checking its indexing): too optimistic by
$r^2$. Read from the 2008 paper itself; the constant 64/15 is proved in its §5. On a panel
$[c-h,c+h]$ the integral is $h\int_{-1}^1 f(c+ht)\,dt$, so the bound gains a factor $h$, and $M$ is
taken over the image ellipse, semiaxes $h(r\pm r^{-1})/2$. Chunk `tphi-gl` checks the indexing
numerically on $\cos(kx)$, where $M=\cosh\{k(r-r^{-1})/2\}$ is exact.

**R-b. The panel bound from two end evaluations (from T2, T3).** For a panel $[c-h,c+h]$ let
$T_L,T_R$ be the tangents of $\ell$ at $c-h$ and $c+h$. By concavity $\ell\le\min(T_L,T_R)$ on
all of $\mathbb R$ and $\ell\ge$ the chord on the panel. With $H=h(r+r^{-1})/2$ and
$v_r=h(r-r^{-1})/2$:
$$\underline I=\int_{c-h}^{c+h}e^{\rm chord},\qquad
\overline M=\exp\Bigl\{\max_{[c-H,c+H]}\min(T_L,T_R)\Bigr\}\,e^{v_r^2/(2s^2)},\qquad
E\le\frac{64}{15}\,h\,\frac{\overline M\,r^{-2(m-1)}}{r^2-1},$$
all in closed form from $\ell(c\pm h)$, $\ell'(c\pm h)$. A panel passes if $E\le\eta_Q\,\underline I$.

**R-c. Placement, fixed.** $m=20$ nodes; $r\in\{1.5,2,3,5\}$, taking the smallest $E$; half-widths
on the ladder $h_k=h_{\max}2^{-k}$, $h_{\max}=\min(1,s)$, $k=0,\dots,40$; each segment is filled left
to right, each panel taking the largest $h_k$ that passes (the last clipped to the segment end, and
tested as clipped). No $h_k$ passing gives status **panel failure**. Nothing depends on a computed
estimate of the integral's error. The constants 20, the $r$ set, $h_{\max}$ and 40 are proposals,
fixed before any measurement.

**R-d. Every switch, enumerated.** For a fixed cell and axis, the evaluation formulas change at:
1. $\beta_j(x)=0$, i.e. $x_j^*=b_j/\rho$, finite $b_j$, $\rho\ne0$: the boundaries between T
   ($\beta_2\le0$), M and U ($\beta_1\ge0$). At most two points.
2. The boundary of N: with $\mu=c_N/w-1$, N holds where $|\beta_1|\le\mu$ and $|\beta_2|\le\mu$, an
   interval whose ends are among $x=(b_j\mp s\mu)/\rho$, $j=1,2$. At most four candidate points;
   none if $\mu<0$, $w=\infty$ (an infinite $b_j$) or $\rho=0$.
3. Inside T or U, the two branches of `log1mexp` at $\Delta=\ln2$ (Mächler, 2012).
4. An infinite $b_j$: $\beta_j\equiv\mp\infty$, so $\Phi(\beta_j)$ is exactly 0 or 1 and only the other
   bound's switch (item 1) remains. $\rho=0$: no switch in $x$.
5. Outside $x$, two discrete choices per cell: the axis (P4: the narrower finite interval, the
   first axis on a tie), and, for each infinite end, the truncation point (R-f).

**Role of the switches.** $f$ is entire whatever formula evaluates it, so R-a and R-b do not depend
on them. The arithmetic bound (R-g) is applied **per node**, with the constant of the formula used
at that node, so a panel may straddle a switch of items 2–3 without a breakpoint. Only item 1's
points are fixed breakpoints, with $a_1,a_2$ where finite, because $D$ changes from near 0 to near
1 over a width of about $s/|\rho|$ there; that is for cost, not validity.

**R-e. The budget, with both tails counted.** Let $t\in\{0,1,2\}$ be the number of infinite ends of
the chosen axis ($t=2$ only when its interval is all of $\mathbb R$, which an ordinal item with at
least two categories never gives, but the rule covers it). Each truncated end gets $\eta_T/t$. The
method's relative error is at most
$$\eta_Q+\eta_T+\eta_A,$$
with $\eta_A$ from R-g. The first draft gave $\eta_T$ to each end, so a two-tailed cell could
spend $2\eta_T$. The panel and truncation tests use certified lower bounds of what is retained,
so a test made before the other tail is laid is only more conservative.

**R-f. Truncation, fixed.** From the outermost finite breakpoint, step $L$ outward by $h_{\max}$,
laying panels by R-c; stop at the first $L$ with $f(L)/|\ell'(L)|\le(\eta_T/t)\,\underline P$, where
$\underline P$ is the sum of $\underline I$ over every panel laid so far. At most 200 steps; beyond
that, status **truncation failure**. By T2, $\ell'\to\pm\infty$ in the tails, so the sign condition of
T4 is met after finitely many steps.

**R-g. Floating-point margins (derived to first order in $u=2^{-53}$; rests on assumption A-L).**
The enclosures of R-b and R-f are computed in double precision without directed rounding, so each
computed quantity is widened by a bound on its own error, as follows.
- **A-L (assumed, to be certified):** `lnnormal(β)` has absolute error at most
  $c_L u\,(1+|\ln\Phi(\beta)|)$, and `normal()` relative error $c_\Phi u$, over $|\beta|\le200$.
- **$\ell$:** $|\hat\ell(x)-\ell(x)|\le e_\ell(x)=u\,\{c_\varphi(1+x^2/2)+e_D(x)\}$, where $e_D$ is the
  regime's bound: T/U $c_L(1+|\ln\Phi(\beta_2)|+|\ln\Phi(\beta_1)|)\,\kappa_\Delta+c_{\rm lm}$ with
  $\kappa_\Delta=e^{-\Delta}/(1-e^{-\Delta})$ bounded outside N by R-d's $\Delta\ge w\max(0.798,|\beta_2|)$;
  M $c_\Phi/D$; N the short rule's bound plus $c_\varphi(1+\max_j\beta_j^2/2)$.
- **$\ell'$:** formed as $-x-(\rho/s)\{e^{\ln\varphi(\beta_2)-\ln D}-e^{\ln\varphi(\beta_1)-\ln D}\}$; each
  exponential has relative error at most $e_\ell$-type terms, so
  $e_{\ell'}(x)\le u|x|+(|\rho|/s)\,(\varphi(\beta_1)+\varphi(\beta_2))/D\cdot(e_D+c_\varphi(1+\max_j\beta_j^2/2))$. The
  two exponentials can cancel; the bound is absolute and does not assume they do not.
- **Widening:** a tangent from $x_0$ evaluated anywhere on $[c-H,c+H]$ is raised by
  $e_\ell(x_0)+e_{\ell'}(x_0)\cdot2H$; the chord is lowered by $\max(e_\ell(c-h),e_\ell(c+h))$; the closed
  forms of $\underline I$, $\overline M$, $E$ add a fixed flop count's $\gamma_k$; the truncation test uses
  $e_\ell(L)+e_{\ell'}(L)/|\ell'(L)|$.
- **$\eta_A$:** T5 over the cell's nodes, $\eta_A\le\max_i e_\ell(x_i)+\gamma_{N_{\rm nodes}}$.
- **Not yet derived:** the constants $c_\varphi,c_{\rm lm}$ and the N rule's bound in closed form,
  and $c_L,c_\Phi$ (A-L, which needs its own certification). Until A-L is certified, every bound in
  R-b to R-f is conditional on it.

**R-h. Where regime M needs `normal()` (proved; added 2026-10-29, raised after measuring).** In
regime M, $\beta_1<0<\beta_2$ and $D=1-x-y$ with $x=\Phi(\beta_1)<\tfrac12$ and
$y=\Phi(-\beta_2)<\tfrac12$. Let $\beta_h$ be the largest double with $\Phi(\beta_h)\le2^{-55}$:
$\beta_h=-8.3743889230674569$ (MPFR, 256 bits). The candidate uses `normal()` only for arguments
in $(\beta_h,0]$ and sets a term to 0 when its argument is at or below $\beta_h$, i.e. omits it
only when its value is at most $2^{-55}$. The relative effect on $D$ of the omissions, exactly:
- **One term omitted**, say $x\le2^{-55}$, $y$ kept: the computed $D$ is $1-y$, so the relative
  change is $x/(1-x-y)\le x/(\tfrac12-x)\le2^{-55}/(\tfrac12-2^{-55})=2^{-54}/(1-2^{-54})$, using
  $y<\tfrac12$. (This is slightly **above** $2^{-54}$; an earlier draft wrote "$<2^{-54}$", which
  was wrong, user 2026-10-29.)
- **Both omitted**, $x,y\le2^{-55}$: the computed $D$ is 1, and the relative change is
  $(x+y)/(1-x-y)\le2^{-54}/(1-2^{-54})$.

So in every case the flush changes $D$ by a relative amount at most
$$\varepsilon_F=\frac{2^{-54}}{1-2^{-54}}=2^{-54}+\frac{2^{-108}}{1-2^{-54}}<2^{-53}.$$
**The budget.** The candidate adds the **flush term** $\eta_F=2^{-53}$ to $\eta_A$, which covers
$\varepsilon_F$ with margin about $2^{-54}$. The computed $D$ carries the flush and the rounding of
the kept terms as factors $(1+\delta_F)(1+\delta_R)$, $|\delta_F|\le\varepsilon_F$, so the total is
$|\delta_F|+|\delta_R|+|\delta_F\delta_R|$, and $\eta_F$ is charged for $|\delta_F|+|\delta_F\delta_R|$.
The cross term is at most $\varepsilon_F|\delta_R|$. For $|\delta_R|\le\tfrac12$ (far above any
first-order rounding bound in R-g) it is at most $\varepsilon_F/2<2^{-55}(1+2^{-53})$. That is
less than the margin $2^{-53}-\varepsilon_F=2^{-54}-2^{-108}/(1-2^{-54})$, so
$|\delta_F|+|\delta_F\delta_R|<2^{-53}=\eta_F$ exactly, not only to first order. This derivation does not depend on where `normal()` fails. It was
raised because the frozen A-L run found `normal()` returning 0 within 0.006 of
$\beta_{\min}\approx-37.519$ (E-068), and it is labelled as
**raised after measuring** for that reason. It replaces the earlier handoff at $\beta_{\min}$.

**Before freezing:** the constants of R-g; the cost gate's preregistration (from
`docs/prereg-template.md`, with its failure floors) giving the node-count criterion over v1's and
conditional mode's domains; and the user's choice of $\eta_Q,\eta_T$ (proposed $2^{-53}$ each).

### What is left before D3 can be adopted

1. **The panel rule** above: R-g's constants, then freezing.
2. **The node count over the domain.** Each cell's panels and nodes follow from that bound,
   deterministically, with no error estimate. Whether the worst case over v1's and conditional
   mode's domains is acceptable is the user's condition and is **not yet measured**. Near
   $\ell'\approx4000$ (the extreme corner of T5), panels must be about $1/4000$ wide near the mode,
   but by T2 the mass lies within a few such widths of it.
3. **`lnnormal()`'s accuracy** (the assumption above).
4. **The §3a audit** for D5: the arcsin-form references M1/M2 are independent of this method but
   have only absolute tolerances; a relative-tolerance MPFR rerun, or a far-tail asymptotic
   expansion, is needed to compare where it matters.

The chunk below checks T1–T4 numerically on moderate cells, where double precision and R's
`integrate()` suffice. It is a check of the algebra, **not certification**: `integrate()` and the
checked formulas share the integrand of T1. The assertion tolerances were set before running;
the check's own harness was corrected after its first runs, as its comments record (a
cancelling $D$, `integrate()`'s default absolute tolerance, and Miwa replaced by TVPACK as the
comparator). **Executed 2026-10-29** by the main session (chunk alone, R 4.6.0, mvtnorm 1.4.2):
T1 against TVPACK $2.2\times10^{-16}$ absolute over 180 cells, against the $\rho=0$ closed form
$7.4\times10^{-16}$ relative; T2 maximum second difference of $\ell$ $-1.0$ (the $\ln\varphi$ part
alone gives $-1$); T3 maximum ratio $1.000000$ over 180 complex points; T4 maximum tail-to-bound
ratio $0.9988$ over 180 (cell, $L$). The whole file has not been rerun.

```{r tphi-checks}
tp_s <- function(rho) sqrt(1 - rho^2)
tp_D <- function(x, b1, b2, rho) {               # regimes T/U/M on the linear scale
  s <- tp_s(rho); B1 <- (b1 - rho * x) / s; B2 <- (b2 - rho * x) / s
  # both upper: difference the upper tails, or Phi(B2) - Phi(B1) cancels to 0
  # (corrected after the first run, where it did; 2026-10-29)
  ifelse(B1 >= 0, pnorm(-B1) - pnorm(-B2), pnorm(B2) - pnorm(B1))
}
tp_f <- function(x, b1, b2, rho) dnorm(x) * tp_D(x, b1, b2, rho)
tp_lf <- function(x, b1, b2, rho) dnorm(x, log = TRUE) + log(tp_D(x, b1, b2, rho))
tp_dl <- function(x, b1, b2, rho) {               # l'(x) of T2
  s <- tp_s(rho)
  dD <- -(rho / s) * (dnorm((b2 - rho * x) / s) - dnorm((b1 - rho * x) / s))
  -x + dD / tp_D(x, b1, b2, rho)
}
tp_cells <- expand.grid(a1 = c(-Inf, -1.5, 0.2), w = c(0.3, 1.2), b1 = c(-Inf, -0.8, 1),
                        bw = c(0.25, 2), rho = c(-0.95, -0.5, 0, 0.6, 0.99))
tp_cells$a2 <- ifelse(is.finite(tp_cells$a1), tp_cells$a1 + tp_cells$w, 0.4)
tp_cells$b2 <- ifelse(is.finite(tp_cells$b1), tp_cells$b1 + tp_cells$bw, -0.3)

# integrate()'s abs.tol defaults to rel.tol, which is loose for tiny integrals: every call
# here sets abs.tol = 0 (the first run's T3/T4 ratios of 1.0014/1.0004 were that; 2026-10-29)
tp_int <- function(f, lo, hi, ..., at = 0) integrate(f, lo, hi, ..., rel.tol = 1e-12, abs.tol = at,
                                             subdivisions = 5000)$value
# T1: against TVPACK corners (Owen's T / Drezner-type, a different method; absolute
# accuracy about 1e-16, so compared in absolute terms), and the rho = 0 closed form
# (relative). Miwa was the first comparator; its own error was 7.3e-10 (it maps
# +-Inf to +-1000), shown against TVPACK; replaced after the first run, 2026-10-29.
tp_F <- function(h, k, r) {
  if (h == -Inf || k == -Inf) return(0)
  mvtnorm::pmvnorm(upper = c(h, k), corr = matrix(c(1, r, r, 1), 2),
                   algorithm = mvtnorm::TVPACK(abseps = 1e-16))[1]
}
t1 <- t(apply(tp_cells, 1, function(c) {
  r <- c[["rho"]]
  i1 <- tp_int(tp_f, c[["a1"]], c[["a2"]], b1 = c[["b1"]], b2 = c[["b2"]], rho = r)
  g <- tp_F(c[["a2"]], c[["b2"]], r) - tp_F(c[["a1"]], c[["b2"]], r) -
       tp_F(c[["a2"]], c[["b1"]], r) + tp_F(c[["a1"]], c[["b1"]], r)
  cf <- if (r == 0) (pnorm(c[["a2"]]) - pnorm(c[["a1"]])) * (pnorm(c[["b2"]]) - pnorm(c[["b1"]])) else NA
  c(P = i1, abs_tv = abs(i1 - g), rel_cf = abs(i1 - cf) / cf)
}))

# T2: second differences of l on a grid inside each finite x-range (h = 1e-3)
t2 <- apply(tp_cells, 1, function(c) {
  lo <- if (is.finite(c[["a1"]])) c[["a1"]] else -4
  x <- seq(lo, c[["a2"]], length.out = 201); hh <- 1e-3
  l <- function(x) tp_lf(x, c[["b1"]], c[["b2"]], c[["rho"]])
  max((l(x + hh) - 2 * l(x) + l(x - hh)) / hh^2)
})

# T3: |f(u + iv)| <= f(u) exp(v^2 / (2 s^2)), D(z) by integrating Re and Im over y
tp_fz <- function(u, v, b1, b2, rho) {
  s <- tp_s(rho); z <- complex(real = u, imaginary = v)
  g <- function(y, part) {
    w <- exp(-((y - rho * z) / s)^2 / 2) / (s * sqrt(2 * pi))
    if (part == 1) Re(w) else Im(w)
  }
  lo <- if (is.finite(b1)) b1 else rho * u - 40 * s
  hi <- if (is.finite(b2)) b2 else rho * u + 40 * s
  # Re/Im can be near 0 (relative tolerance unreachable): absolute tolerance 1e-13 of the
  # integral of |w|, in closed form. Set after the first runs: abs.tol 0 and then 1e-15
  # stopped on roundoff (2026-10-29)
  at <- 1e-13 * exp(rho^2 * v^2 / (2 * s^2)) * tp_D(u, b1, b2, rho)
  Dz <- complex(real = tp_int(g, lo, hi, part = 1, at = at),
                imaginary = tp_int(g, lo, hi, part = 2, at = at))
  Mod(exp(-z^2 / 2) / sqrt(2 * pi) * Dz)
}
set.seed(20261029)
t3 <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(tp_cells)), function(q) {
  c <- tp_cells[q, ]; u <- runif(1, -2, 2); v <- runif(1, 0, 0.5) * tp_s(c$rho)
  tp_fz(u, v, c$b1, c$b2, c$rho) / (tp_f(u, c$b1, c$b2, c$rho) * exp(v^2 / (2 * tp_s(c$rho)^2)))
})

# T4: the tangent bound against the true lower tail, at points with l'(L) > 0
inf_cells <- tp_cells[!is.finite(tp_cells$a1), ]
t4 <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(inf_cells)), function(q) {
  c <- inf_cells[q, ]
  sapply(c(-3, -2.5, -2), function(L) {
    lam <- tp_dl(L, c$b1, c$b2, c$rho)
    if (!(lam > 0)) return(NA)
    tail <- tp_int(tp_f, -Inf, L, b1 = c$b1, b2 = c$b2, rho = c$rho)
    tail / (tp_f(L, c$b1, c$b2, c$rho) / lam)
  })
}))

cat(sprintf("T1: %d cells, max abs vs TVPACK %.2e, max rel vs rho=0 closed form %.2e\n",
            nrow(t1), max(t1[, "abs_tv"]), max(t1[, "rel_cf"], na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("T2: max second difference of l %.3e (log-concave: <= 0 up to rounding)\n", max(t2)))
cat(sprintf("T3: max |f(z)| / bound %.6f over %d points\n", max(t3), length(t3)))
cat(sprintf("T4: %d (cell, L) with l'(L) > 0, max tail / bound %.6f, min %.3e\n",
            sum(!is.na(t4)), max(t4, na.rm = TRUE), min(t4, na.rm = TRUE)))
stopifnot(
  # absolute against TVPACK, as its accuracy is absolute; the first run's relative test
  # against Miwa was ill-posed (2026-10-29). 1e-14 set before the rerun
  max(t1[, "abs_tv"]) < 1e-14, max(t1[, "rel_cf"], na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-12,
  max(t2) < 1e-5,                     # rounding of a second difference at h = 1e-3
  max(t3) <= 1 + 1e-9,
  sum(!is.na(t4)) > 0, max(t4, na.rm = TRUE) <= 1 + 1e-9)
```

Chunk `tphi-gl` checks R-a's indexing: $m$-point Gauss–Legendre (Golub–Welsch) on $\cos(kx)$
over $[-1,1]$, exact integral $2\sin k/k$, against the $m$-point bound with
$M=\max_{E_r}|\cos kz|=\cosh\{k(r-r^{-1})/2\}$. It asserts the corrected bound wherever the bound
exceeds rounding ($>10^{-13}$), and reports, as a diagnostic, how often the first draft's $r^{-2m}$
would have been violated. Tolerances set before running. **Executed 2026-10-29** (main session,
chunk alone, R 4.6.0): 446 cases with bound $>10^{-13}$, max error/bound 0.25; the draft's
$r^{-2m}$ is violated in 21 of them, so its indexing error was real, not only optimistic.

```{r tphi-gl}
gl_rule <- function(m) {                          # Golub-Welsch
  b <- seq_len(m - 1) / sqrt(4 * seq_len(m - 1)^2 - 1)
  J <- matrix(0, m, m); J[cbind(1:(m - 1), 2:m)] <- b; J[cbind(2:m, 1:(m - 1))] <- b
  e <- eigen(J, symmetric = TRUE)
  list(x = e$values, w = 2 * e$vectors[1, ]^2)
}
gl_grid <- expand.grid(m = 2:20, k = c(1, 5, 10, 20, 40), r = c(1.2, 1.5, 2, 3, 5))
gl_res <- t(apply(gl_grid, 1, function(g) {
  q <- gl_rule(g[["m"]]); k <- g[["k"]]; r <- g[["r"]]
  err <- abs(sum(q$w * cos(k * q$x)) - 2 * sin(k) / k)
  M <- cosh(k * (r - 1 / r) / 2)
  c(err = err, b_new = 64 / 15 * M * r^(-2 * (g[["m"]] - 1)) / (r^2 - 1),
    b_old = 64 / 15 * M * r^(-2 * g[["m"]]) / (r^2 - 1))
}))
use <- gl_res[, "b_new"] > 1e-13
cat(sprintf("GL: %d (m, k, r) with bound > 1e-13; max err / bound %.4f; draft r^-2m violated %d times\n",
            sum(use), max(gl_res[use, "err"] / gl_res[use, "b_new"]),
            sum(gl_res[use, "err"] > gl_res[use, "b_old"])))
stopifnot(sum(use) > 100, all(gl_res[use, "err"] <= gl_res[use, "b_new"] * (1 + 1e-9)))
```

## Stage 1's reachability envelope for binormal() {#sec-phi2-reach}

**Status (2026-11-04):** what $(Y,K)$ and the solver imply for where `binormal()` is evaluated.
It settles no budget and certifies no accuracy. The simulation of what it leaves open is
preregistered in E-101. Notation there: $D$ is
$|\rho|\le0.999$, $h,k\in[-2.5,2.5]$; $F$ the points in $D$ where `binormal()` returns exactly 0;
$c=10^{-15}$, $e=2.5\cdot2^{-52}$, phase 2's **empirical envelope** on $D$, certified nowhere else.
Results R3 and R5 inherit that status; they are proofs given the envelope.

**Call graph (read from `src/`).** `binormal()` is called only in `dwlsmv_cellprob_raw()`, whose
callers are `dwlsmv_rf_evalp()`, `dwlsmv_rf_usable()` and `dwlsmv_pairinfo()`; `dwls_sample_stats()`
reaches them through `dwls_polychoric()` and, for the one-empty-cell repair, directly. Inputs are
thresholds and trial $\rho$. Conditional mode has no cell code in `src/`.

**R0.** Every evaluation has $|\rho|\le B=0.999$. Leaving $D$ is through thresholds alone.

**R1.** Stage 1 refuses an empty category, so cumulative counts lie in $[1,N-1]$ and
$|\tau|\le T(N)=-\Phi^{-1}(1/N)$, per group. A threshold leaves $D$ iff its cumulative proportion is
below $\Phi(-2.5)$ or above its complement.

**R2.** With such a threshold every evaluation of each pair using it, $\hat\rho$ and pairinfo
included, has a corner outside $D$.

**R3.** `dwlsmv_rf_check()` evaluates $\pm B$ on every status 1 path. As $X+Y\sim N(0,2(1+\rho))$,
for $h+k<0$
$$\Phi_2(h,k;\rho)\le\Phi\!\left(\frac{h+k}{\sqrt{2(1+\rho)}}\right).$$
Given the envelope, a corner in $D$ with $P<c-e$ flushes, so $h+k\le-\sqrt{2(1+\rho)}\,z^*$ with
$z^*=-\Phi^{-1}(c-e)$ is sufficient: $h+k\le-0.360$ at $\rho=-B$.

**R4.** For $\rho\ge0$, Slepian gives $\Phi_2\ge\Phi(h)\Phi(k)\ge N^{-2}$, above $c+e$ for
$N<2.54\cdot10^7$.

**R5.** Given the envelope, in $D$, at a usable evaluation a flushed corner $(r,s)$ has
$\sum_{r'\le r,s'\le s}n_{r's'}=0$. A cell in that quadrant has corners of true value at most
$P(r,s)\le c+e$, so outputs at most $c+2e$, and computed $\pi$ at most the sum of its two added
corners, $2(c+2e)<\delta_P$. An observed cell there makes the point unusable. ∎ By Fréchet, this
needs $m_1+m_2\le N$. **Binary pairs in $D$ do not flush at an accepted $\hat\rho$:** one corner;
observed, R5 applies; empty, the repair refits an all-positive table or Stage 1 refuses.

**R6.** $\Phi_2$ rises in $h,k,\rho$, so a flush at $h=k=-t$ needs $\rho\le\rho^*(t)$, where
$\Phi_2(-t,-t;\rho^*)=c+e$. Beyond $t=2.5$ this extends the envelope outside $D$, uncertified.

```{r phi2-reach-checks}
# Double precision by T1 in log space: a check of these statements, not a certified value.
reach_lp <- function(h, k, r) {
  s <- sqrt(1 - r^2)
  lf <- function(x) dnorm(x, log = TRUE) + pnorm((k - r * x) / s, log.p = TRUE)
  x0 <- optimize(lf, c(h - 40, h), maximum = TRUE, tol = 1e-8)$maximum
  m <- lf(x0); g <- function(x) exp(lf(x) - m)
  w <- 0.5 * s
  v <- integrate(g, max(x0 - w, h - 40), min(x0 + w, h), rel.tol = 1e-10, subdivisions = 2000L)$value +
    (if (x0 - w > h - 40) integrate(g, x0 - 10, x0 - w, rel.tol = 1e-10, subdivisions = 2000L,
                                    stop.on.error = FALSE)$value else 0) +
    (if (x0 + w < h) integrate(g, x0 + w, h, rel.tol = 1e-10, subdivisions = 2000L,
                               stop.on.error = FALSE)$value else 0)
  m + log(v)
}
c0 <- 1e-15; e0 <- 2.5 * 2^-52; dP <- 4 * 9.3908313968469e-16 + 3 * 2^-52
# R1
stopifnot(floor(1 / pnorm(-2.5)) + 1 == 162, floor(2 / pnorm(-2.5)) + 1 == 323,
          floor(5 / pnorm(-2.5)) + 1 == 806, floor(1 / pnorm(-4)) + 1 == 31575)
# R3: the bound on a grid, and the constant
zs <- -qnorm(c0 - e0)
stopifnot(abs(-sqrt(2 * (1 - 0.999)) * zs - -0.35961) < 1e-4)
g <- expand.grid(h = c(-3, -1, -.2), k = c(-2, -.5, .1), r = c(-.999, -.9, -.5, 0, .5))
g <- g[g$h + g$k < 0, ]
lb <- pnorm((g$h + g$k) / sqrt(2 * (1 + g$r)), log.p = TRUE)
lp <- mapply(reach_lp, g$h, g$k, g$r)
stopifnot(all(lp <= lb + 1e-8))
# R3 against StataMP 18's recorded outputs (docs/notes/phi2-reach/probe_stage1_stata18_20261104.log)
stopifnot(exp(reach_lp(-.2, -.2, -.999)) < c0 - e0, exp(reach_lp(-1, .5, -.999)) < c0 - e0,
          abs(exp(reach_lp(-.15, -.15, -.999)) / 2.52e-14 - 1) < 0.01,
          abs(exp(reach_lp(-1, .8, -.999)) / 9.46e-09 - 1) < 0.01,
          abs(exp(reach_lp(-2.5, -2.5, -.7)) / 2.68e-12 - 1) < 0.01)
# R4
stopifnot(all(mapply(reach_lp, g$h, g$k, abs(g$r) * 0 + .3) >= pnorm(g$h, log.p = TRUE) + pnorm(g$k, log.p = TRUE)),
          1 / sqrt(c0 + e0) > 2.5e7)
# R5
stopifnot(2 * (c0 + 2 * e0) < dP)
# R6, with phase 1's observed reach of F (rho = -0.78) at t = 2.5
rs <- function(t) uniroot(function(r) reach_lp(-t, -t, r) - log(c0 + e0), c(-.9995, -.001), tol = 1e-7)$root
stopifnot(abs(rs(2.5) - -0.7755) < 5e-4, abs(rs(4) - -0.4364) < 5e-4)
cat("phi2-reach checks pass\n")
```

### Accepted-level flushes in $D$: what they reach {#sec-phi2-flush}

**Status (2026-11-04):** Investigation A only. This subsection gives the size of the effect of a
flushed corner in $D$ at an accepted $\hat\rho$. It sets no budget and does not say what is
negligible. P1–P5 are proofs **given phase 2's empirical envelope**, which is certified on $D$ only, at
its enumerated points, for StataMP 18 and 16.1. The bound is no stronger than that. The constructed tables
show the arithmetic; they are not evidence of how often a case occurs.

**Notation.** $\kappa=c+e=1.5551\cdot10^{-15}$. Corner $(i,j)$ is $(a_i,b_j)$, with true value $P_{ij}$.
$\pi^\circ$ is the cell probability with each flushed corner replaced by its true value and every other
corner unchanged, and $\Delta=\hat\pi-\pi^\circ$. So this measures the flush alone, not $\pi^\circ$'s
remaining error. $r_{rs}=|\Delta_{rs}|/\pi^\circ_{rs}$, $\bar r=\max_O r$ over observed cells $O$,
$w=n/N$, $u=D/\pi$, $J=-S'(\rho)=\sum_O w(u^2-D'/\pi)$, with $D'$ the rectangle difference of
$\partial_\rho\phi_2$.

**What uses the flushed corner (read from `src/`).** Only `dwlsmv_cellprob_raw()` calls `binormal()`.
`dwlsmv_dcellprob_rho()` uses `exp()`, `dwlsmv_wmat()` uses `normal()` and `normalden()`, and
`dwlsmv_psi_tau_table()` uses $q$ alone. So $D$, the $w_{c,s}$ and $\psi_\tau$ hold no corner: at fixed
$\rho$ the flush enters only through $\pi$, and otherwise only through the $\hat\rho$ it moves.
`dwlsmv_pairinfo()` zeroes $u$ where $W=0$ and $\hat\pi\le0$. Its sums carry the factor $W$, and
`dwlsmv_psi_matrix()` looks $\psi_\rho$ up at each observation's own cell, so **no empty cell reaches
$\hat I$, $\psi_i$ or $\hat\Gamma$**.

**P1 (cells).** Corner $(i,j)$ enters only cells $(i,j)$ and $(i{+}1,j{+}1)$, lowering them by $P_{ij}$,
and $(i{+}1,j)$ and $(i,j{+}1)$, raising them by $P_{ij}$. If none of the four is observed, every observed
$\hat\pi$, and so everything at that evaluation below, is unchanged. By R5, $(i,j)$ is always empty and an
observed cell's upper-right corner is never flushed. So for an observed cell, with the other three corners
ll, ul, lr,
$$\Delta=-P_{\rm ll}\mathbf 1_{\rm ll}+P_{\rm ul}\mathbf 1_{\rm ul}+P_{\rm lr}\mathbf 1_{\rm lr}.$$
As $P_{\rm ll}\le\min(P_{\rm ul},P_{\rm lr})$, $|\Delta|\le\kappa$ unless ul and lr are both flushed, and
then $|\Delta|\le2\kappa$ with $\Delta>0$. ∎ Therefore
$$r_{rs}\le\frac{m\kappa}{\pi^\circ_{rs}},\qquad m\in\{1,2\}.$$
Usability alone does not make this small: $\hat\pi>\delta_P$ gives only $|\Delta|/\hat\pi<2\kappa/\delta_P=0.704$.
Both ul and lr flushed on an observed cell occurs in a constructed table (D1 below).

**P2 (fixed $\rho$, exact, for $\bar r<1$).** Sum over $A$, the observed cells with $\Delta\ne0$:
$$|\Delta S|\le\frac{1}{1-\bar r}\sum_A w|u|r,\qquad
\frac{|\Delta I_{\rho\rho}|}{I_{\rho\rho}}\le\frac{\sum_A wu^2\,[(1-r)^{-2}-1]}{I_{\rho\rho}}\le(1-\bar r)^{-2}-1,$$
$$|\Delta I_{\rho a_c}|\le\sum_{A\cap\{{\rm rows}\ c,c+1\}}w_{c,s}\,\frac{w|u|}{\pi}\,[(1-r)^{-2}-1],$$
and likewise for $I_{\rho b}$, and $\|\Delta u\|_w\le\sqrt{I_{\rho\rho}}\,\bar r/(1-\bar r)$ with $\|x\|_w^2=\sum_O wx^2$.
$I_{\rho\rho}$ carries a relative bound because it is a weighted mean. $I_{\rho a}$ does not: its terms can
cancel, so its bound is absolute. ∎

**P3 ($\hat\rho$).** Let $S^\circ$ have a root $\rho^\circ$, with $S^{\circ\prime}\le-J_m<0$ on an interval
containing it and the computed $\hat\rho$, and $|\hat S-S^\circ|\le\eta_S$ there. If $|\hat S(\hat\rho)|\le\tau$
then $|\hat\rho-\rho^\circ|\le(\tau+\eta_S)/J_m$. This holds across a flush frontier, where $\hat S$ jumps, as
it uses no continuity of $\hat S$. For the exact root ($\tau=0$), Cauchy–Schwarz on P2 gives
$$|\delta|\le\frac{\sqrt{I_{\rho\rho}}\sqrt{\sum_A wr^2}}{J_m(1-\bar r)},\qquad
\frac{|\delta|}{(NI_{\rho\rho})^{-1/2}}\le\frac{I_{\rho\rho}}{J_m}\,\frac{\sqrt{\sum_A n\,r^2}}{1-\bar r}.$$
So on the scale $(NI_{\rho\rho})^{-1/2}$ the shift depends only on observed cells' $\pi$ and counts, and on
$I_{\rho\rho}/J_m$. **That ratio is not bounded here:** $J$ can fall below $I_{\rho\rho}$ under misfit and is
measured, 1.00 to 1.98 on these tables. This scale is not $\hat\rho$'s standard error, which is $\psi_\rho$'s. ∎

**P4 ($\psi_\rho$).** With $\hat\psi_\rho=(\hat u-\psi_a\hat I_{\rho a}-\psi_b\hat I_{\rho b})/\hat I_{\rho\rho}$ and
$\psi_a,\psi_b$ free of corners,
$$\hat\psi_\rho-\psi_\rho=\frac{\Delta u-\psi_a\Delta I_{\rho a}-\psi_b\Delta I_{\rho b}-\psi_\rho\,\Delta I_{\rho\rho}}{\hat I_{\rho\rho}}$$
exactly, each $\Delta$ being the total change, fixed-$\rho$ part (P2) plus the shift through $\delta$. The triangle
inequality then bounds $\gamma=\|\Delta\psi_\rho\|_w/\|\psi_\rho\|_w$. No constant multiple of $\bar r$ follows, as
$\|\psi_\rho\|_w$ can be small where $u$ and the propagation cancel; $\gamma/\bar r$ is measured. ∎

**P5 ($\hat\Gamma$).** With $\hat\Gamma=N^{-1}\sum\psi_i\psi_i'$, for entries $p,q$,
$$\frac{|\Delta\hat\Gamma_{pq}|}{\sqrt{\hat\Gamma_{pp}\hat\Gamma_{qq}}}\le\gamma_p+\gamma_q+\gamma_p\gamma_q,$$
where $\gamma=0$ for a threshold entry and for a pair with no flushed corner touching an observed cell. So the
threshold block is untouched, a $\rho$–$\tau$ entry moves by at most $\gamma_p$, and $\rho\rho$ by at most
$\gamma(2+\gamma)$. ∎

**First-order form.** At fixed $\rho$, with signed $s=\Delta/\pi^\circ$: $\Delta u\approx-us$,
$\Delta S\approx-\sum_A wus$, $\Delta I_{\rho\rho}\approx-2\sum_A wu^2s$; then $\delta\approx\Delta S/J$, and each
total change adds $\delta\,\partial_\rho(\cdot)$. Two conditions are needed. **(a)** $\bar r\le0.01$, under which P2's
exact factors exceed their first-order forms by at most 1.1% ($k=1$) and 1.6% ($k=2$). By P1, $\pi\ge3.11\cdot10^{-13}$
guarantees this at $m=2$, and $1.56\cdot10^{-13}$ at $m=1$. **(b)** $\max_O|u\,\delta|\ll1$, since $\delta$ moves
$\pi$ by the relative amount $u\delta$. It has no threshold in $\pi$, and is checked per table ($4.4\cdot10^{-3}$ at
$\bar r=0.01$ on A1). The value 0.01 is a descriptive choice for the remainder, chosen after measuring, not
a tolerance. Measured on A1 by perturbing its smallest cell, first order misstates the change by:

| $\bar r$ | $\delta$ | $\Delta I_{\rho\rho}$ | $\gamma$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.001 | 0.10% | 0.15% | 0.07% |
| 0.01 | 0.97% | 1.5% | 0.72% |
| 0.05 | 4.7% | 6.9% | 3.5% |
| 0.2 | 16% | 23% | 13% |
| 0.7 | 41% | 53% | 35% |

**Against the rough estimate $\kappa/\pi$.** At $\pi=1.28\cdot10^{-8}$, $\kappa/\pi=1.2\cdot10^{-7}$ is the right
size for $r$ at $m=1$, but the ceiling is $2.4\cdot10^{-7}$ at $m=2$, and it is the cell, not the output. It also
overstates the typical case, as a flushed corner's true value is usually below $\kappa$, often far below (D1's
lower-left is $8\cdot10^{-27}$). Downstream the changes stayed within a small multiple of $\bar r$ on these tables,
up to 3.2 for the largest relative change in $I_{\rho a},I_{\rho b}$; that ratio has no proved ceiling, because of cancellation.

**Measured.** Exact root of the score with true corners against the root with the flushed set, base R, in the
chunk below. Top: the true flushed values. Below: the envelope's worst case, $+2\kappa$ on the smallest observed
cell, whether or not a table's flush pattern allows it. Tables A are $3\times3$, $N=2\cdot10^4$, $n=1$ in the small
cell, one flushed corner. D have $N=10^8$ and $10^{10}$, $n=1$, with ul and lr both flushed. These $N$ are constructed
to reach the case, not claimed to occur. Max rel. $I$ is over $I_{\rho a},I_{\rho b}$.

| Table | $\min_O\pi$ | $\bar r$ | $\delta$ | $\Delta I_{\rho\rho}/I_{\rho\rho}$ | max rel. $I$ | $\gamma$ | $\Delta\Gamma_{\rho\rho}/\Gamma_{\rho\rho}$ | max $\rho\tau$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A0 | $1.22\cdot10^{-8}$ | $5.8\cdot10^{-8}$ | $-2.9\cdot10^{-11}$ | $-3.0\cdot10^{-8}$ | $9.6\cdot10^{-8}$ | $3.3\cdot10^{-8}$ | $3.1\cdot10^{-8}$ | $8.5\cdot10^{-9}$ |
| A1 | $6.72\cdot10^{-9}$ | $1.0\cdot10^{-7}$ | $-5.2\cdot10^{-11}$ | $-5.5\cdot10^{-8}$ | $1.7\cdot10^{-7}$ | $5.9\cdot10^{-8}$ | $5.7\cdot10^{-8}$ | $1.6\cdot10^{-8}$ |
| A2 | $8.68\cdot10^{-11}$ | $9.6\cdot10^{-6}$ | $-5.7\cdot10^{-9}$ | $-6.9\cdot10^{-6}$ | $1.4\cdot10^{-5}$ | $6.3\cdot10^{-6}$ | $6.7\cdot10^{-6}$ | $1.6\cdot10^{-6}$ |
| A3 | $1.63\cdot10^{-12}$ | $3.3\cdot10^{-4}$ | $-2.6\cdot10^{-7}$ | $-3.0\cdot10^{-4}$ | $1.1\cdot10^{-3}$ | $2.3\cdot10^{-4}$ | $2.6\cdot10^{-4}$ | $4.5\cdot10^{-5}$ |
| D1 | $1.00\cdot10^{-8}$ | $5.6\cdot10^{-8}$ | $-7.5\cdot10^{-11}$ | $-9.6\cdot10^{-8}$ | $1.1\cdot10^{-7}$ | $4.8\cdot10^{-8}$ | $9.6\cdot10^{-8}$ | $1.5\cdot10^{-11}$ |
| D2 | $1.00\cdot10^{-10}$ | $8.5\cdot10^{-6}$ | $-6.3\cdot10^{-9}$ | $-1.5\cdot10^{-5}$ | $1.7\cdot10^{-5}$ | $7.5\cdot10^{-6}$ | $1.5\cdot10^{-5}$ | $2.3\cdot10^{-10}$ |
| A0, $+2\kappa$ | $1.22\cdot10^{-8}$ | $2.6\cdot10^{-7}$ | $-1.3\cdot10^{-10}$ | $-1.3\cdot10^{-7}$ | $4.2\cdot10^{-7}$ | $1.5\cdot10^{-7}$ | $1.4\cdot10^{-7}$ | $3.8\cdot10^{-8}$ |
| A2, $+2\kappa$ | $8.68\cdot10^{-11}$ | $3.6\cdot10^{-5}$ | $-2.1\cdot10^{-8}$ | $-2.6\cdot10^{-5}$ | $5.4\cdot10^{-5}$ | $2.3\cdot10^{-5}$ | $2.5\cdot10^{-5}$ | $5.9\cdot10^{-6}$ |
| A3, $+2\kappa$ | $1.63\cdot10^{-12}$ | $1.9\cdot10^{-3}$ | $-1.5\cdot10^{-6}$ | $-1.7\cdot10^{-3}$ | $6.1\cdot10^{-3}$ | $1.3\cdot10^{-3}$ | $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ | $2.6\cdot10^{-4}$ |
| D1, $+2\kappa$ | $1.00\cdot10^{-8}$ | $3.1\cdot10^{-7}$ | $-4.1\cdot10^{-10}$ | $-5.3\cdot10^{-7}$ | $5.9\cdot10^{-7}$ | $2.7\cdot10^{-7}$ | $5.3\cdot10^{-7}$ | $8.1\cdot10^{-11}$ |

**Production arithmetic (StataMP 18, executed 2026-11-04; 16.1 not run).**
E-102: `stage1_run` runs production `dwlsmv_rootfind()` and `dwlsmv_pairinfo()` on each table and
reports the flushed corners. `stage2gen.R` computes those corners by the 256-bit M4 reference (agreeing with the
chunk's double-precision T1 to $1.2\cdot10^{-13}$ relative or better). `stage2_run` then replaces only flushed corners
and reruns at production's own $\hat\rho$. Fixed-$\rho$ changes agree with the R chunk: A1 $\Delta I_{\rho\rho}/I_{\rho\rho}=-6.605\cdot10^{-8}$
against $-6.6055\cdot10^{-8}$, $\gamma=6.250\cdot10^{-8}$ against $6.2496\cdot10^{-8}$, $\Delta S=-4.413\cdot10^{-9}$ against
$-4.4125\cdot10^{-9}$. Table Z1 has corner $(1,1)$, touching no observed cell, and three more below $10^{-47}$ touching
observed cells: every observed quantity is **exactly** unchanged. The root was not rerun in production arithmetic
with corners patched at each trial $\rho$, so $\delta$ is R's only. At production's $\hat\rho$, $|\Delta S|/\tau_S$ was
between 0.12 and 0.19 on A0–A3, D1 and D2, so on these tables $\delta$ lies within the solver's own
stopping tolerance. This is a measurement about these tables, and it says nothing about solver decisions.

**What this does not reach.**

- **Stored `f.u` at empty cells.** Not bounded: on these tables it moved by up to $2.3\cdot10^{4}$, zeroed by
  `dwlsmv_pairinfo()` on one side and a ratio of tiny numbers on the other. `dwlsmv_psi_rho_table()` copies it into
  $\psi_\rho$'s empty cells, which nothing reads.
- **Expected-information uses.** `dwlsmv_rf_evalp()`'s $c$, and any $W=\pi$ call of `dwlsmv_pairinfo()`, weight empty
  cells, where $r$ is not small. $c$ only scales Fisher steps and $\tau_\rho$. Neither is bounded here.
- **Other corner errors.** $\Delta$ is the flush alone. With the two other corners at $e$ and rounding, the envelope gives
  $|\hat\pi-\pi|\le2\kappa+2e+3\cdot2^{-52}=4.89\cdot10^{-15}$, above v1's $\delta_P=4.42\cdot10^{-15}$. This assumes `normal()` at
  the table's edges is within $e$, which phase 2 did not test. It is the open v1 budget question and is not settled here.
- **Outside $D$, and small $\pi$ with no flush on the cell.** These are Investigations C and B; P1–P5 give them nothing.
- **Solver decisions, walks, status.** Investigation D. P3 assumes a sign-certified bracket. On an exploratory table with
  $\pi\approx10^{-14}$, production returned status 6 at the walk point $-0.984375$ (executed, not in the kept logs), so
  a returned point can be far from the root where $\bar r$ is large.
- **Steps after $\hat\Gamma$.** $\hat\rho$ and $\hat\Gamma$ feed $W_D$, $\hat\theta$, SEs and T3; none is traced here.
- **Rates.** Whether $\pi$ at a real flushed corner takes these values is the reachability study's question. No
  tier in the spec states what size is negligible here; that is for the user.

```{r phi2-flush-propagation}
# phi2 flush propagation: core functions (same text goes into the qmd chunk)
pf_kappa <- 1e-15 + 2.5 * 2^-52
pf_dP <- 4 * 9.3908313968469e-16 + 3 * 2^-52
# log Phi2(h,k;r), tail-accurate
pf_lp <- function(h, k, r) {
  s <- sqrt(1 - r^2)
  lf <- function(x) dnorm(x, log = TRUE) + pnorm((k - r * x) / s, log.p = TRUE)
  x0 <- optimize(lf, c(h - 40, h), maximum = TRUE, tol = 1e-8)$maximum
  m <- lf(x0); g <- function(x) exp(lf(x) - m); w <- 0.5 * s
  v <- integrate(g, max(x0 - w, h - 40), min(x0 + w, h), rel.tol = 1e-11, abs.tol = 0, subdivisions = 2000L)$value +
    (if (x0 - w > h - 40) integrate(g, x0 - 10, x0 - w, rel.tol = 1e-10, abs.tol = 0, subdivisions = 2000L, stop.on.error = FALSE)$value else 0) +
    (if (x0 + w < h) integrate(g, x0 + w, h, rel.tol = 1e-10, abs.tol = 0, subdivisions = 2000L, stop.on.error = FALSE)$value else 0)
  m + log(v)
}
pf_P <- function(h, k, r) exp(pf_lp(h, k, r))
# One cell by the conditional rectangle integral, relative accuracy in both tails.
pf_cell1 <- function(lo1, hi1, lo2, hi2, r) {
  s <- sqrt(1 - r^2)
  f <- function(x) {
    u <- (hi2 - r * x) / s; l <- (lo2 - r * x) / s
    v <- ifelse(l > 0, pnorm(l, lower.tail = FALSE) - pnorm(u, lower.tail = FALSE), pnorm(u) - pnorm(l))
    dnorm(x) * v
  }
  lo <- max(lo1, -9); hi <- min(hi1, 9)
  if (lo >= hi) return(0)
  # the mass concentrates where the conditional band meets [lo, hi]: split there
  brk <- sort(unique(c(lo, hi, pmin(pmax(c(lo2, hi2)[is.finite(c(lo2, hi2))] * r, lo), hi),
                       pmin(pmax(c(lo2, hi2)[is.finite(c(lo2, hi2))] / r, lo), hi))))
  v <- 0
  for (i in seq_len(length(brk) - 1)) {
    v <- v + integrate(f, brk[i], brk[i + 1], rel.tol = 1e-12, abs.tol = 0, subdivisions = 2000L,
                       stop.on.error = FALSE)$value
  }
  v
}
pf_cells <- function(a, b, r) {
  A <- c(-Inf, a, Inf); B <- c(-Inf, b, Inf)
  outer(seq_len(length(a) + 1), seq_len(length(b) + 1), Vectorize(function(i, j)
    pf_cell1(A[i], A[i + 1], B[j], B[j + 1], r)))
}
pf_d2 <- function(x, y, r) {
  s2 <- 1 - r^2; z <- ifelse(is.finite(x) & is.finite(y), (x^2 - 2 * r * x * y + y^2) / (2 * s2), Inf)
  ifelse(is.finite(z), exp(-z) / (2 * pi * sqrt(s2)), 0)
}
pf_rect <- function(G) {
  K1 <- nrow(G) - 1; K2 <- ncol(G) - 1
  G[-1, -1, drop = FALSE] - G[-(K1 + 1), -1, drop = FALSE] - G[-1, -(K2 + 1), drop = FALSE] +
    G[-(K1 + 1), -(K2 + 1), drop = FALSE]
}
pf_D <- function(a, b, r) pf_rect(outer(c(-Inf, a, Inf), c(-Inf, b, Inf), pf_d2, r = r))
# d phi2 / d rho = phi2 [ (x - r y)(y - r x) / s2^2 + r / s2 ]
pf_D1 <- function(a, b, r) {
  f <- function(x, y) {
    p <- pf_d2(x, y, r)
    ifelse(p > 0, p * ((x - r * y) * (y - r * x) / (1 - r^2)^2 + r / (1 - r^2)), 0)
  }
  pf_rect(outer(c(-Inf, a, Inf), c(-Inf, b, Inf), f))
}
pf_wm <- function(a, b, r) {
  s <- sqrt(1 - r^2); B <- c(-Inf, b, Inf)
  t(sapply(a, function(x) dnorm(x) * diff(pnorm((B - r * x) / s))))
}
# Delta[pi] for a flushed set: pi_hat - pi = - sum over flushed corners of sign * P
# corner (i, j) is (a[i], b[j]); it adds +P to cells (i,j), (i+1,j+1), -P to (i+1,j), (i,j+1).
pf_incid <- function(a, b, r, fl) {
  d <- matrix(0, length(a) + 1, length(b) + 1)
  if (nrow(fl)) for (q in seq_len(nrow(fl))) {
    i <- fl[q, 1]; j <- fl[q, 2]; p <- pf_P(a[i], b[j], r)
    d[i, j] <- d[i, j] - p; d[i + 1, j + 1] <- d[i + 1, j + 1] - p
    d[i + 1, j] <- d[i + 1, j] + p; d[i, j + 1] <- d[i, j + 1] + p
  }
  d
}
# All outputs at (r, cells pi), production formulas, W = n/N
pf_out <- function(n, a, b, r, P, psa, psb) {
  w <- n / sum(n); O <- n > 0; D <- pf_D(a, b, r)
  u <- ifelse(O, D / P, 0)
  Irr <- sum(w * u^2); S <- sum(w * u)
  Wa <- pf_wm(a, b, r); Wb <- pf_wm(b, a, r)
  K1 <- nrow(n); K2 <- ncol(n)
  g <- ifelse(O, w * u / P, 0)
  Ira <- sapply(seq_along(a), function(c) sum(Wa[c, ] * (g[c, ] - g[c + 1, ])))
  Irb <- sapply(seq_along(b), function(d) sum(Wb[d, ] * (g[, d] - g[, d + 1])))
  psi <- (u - matrix(psa %*% Ira, K1, K2) - t(matrix(psb %*% Irb, K2, K1))) / Irr
  list(S = S, u = u, Irr = Irr, Ira = Ira, Irb = Irb, psi = psi)
}
# staircase: psi_tau[r, c] = (1{r <= c} - q_c) / phi(tau_c), q = cum prop, centred table
pf_psitau <- function(mar) {
  q <- cumsum(mar)[-length(mar)] / sum(mar)
  t(sapply(seq_along(mar), function(r) ((r <= seq_along(q)) - q) / dnorm(qnorm(q))))
}
pf_mk <- function(N, a, b, r, ones) {
  n <- round(N * pf_cells(a, b, r)); for (o in ones) n[o[1], o[2]] <- o[3]; n
}
pf_tabs <- list(
  A0 = pf_mk(2e4, c(-.65, .5), c(-.65, -.19), -.985, list(c(1, 2, 1))),
  A1 = pf_mk(2e4, c(-.65, .5), c(-.65, -.21), -.985, list(c(1, 2, 1))),
  A2 = pf_mk(2e4, c(-.65, .5), c(-.65, -.35), -.985, list(c(1, 2, 1))),
  A3 = pf_mk(2e4, c(-.66, .5), c(-.66, -.46), -.985, list(c(1, 2, 1))),
  D1 = pf_mk(1e8, c(-.95, -.45), c(-.95, -.45), -.985, list(c(2, 2, 1))),
  D2 = pf_mk(1e10, c(-.74, -.45), c(-.74, -.45), -.985, list(c(2, 2, 1))),
  Z1 = pf_mk(2e4, c(-1.5, -1, 1), c(-1.5, -1, 1), -.99, list())
)
# ---- propagation of a flushed set: exact comparison against every corner true
pf_sc <- function(n, a, b, r, P) { O <- n > 0; sum((n / sum(n) * pf_D(a, b, r) / P)[O]) }
pf_prop <- function(n, dfun, hint = NULL) {
  N <- sum(n); w <- n / N; O <- n > 0
  a <- qnorm(cumsum(rowSums(n))[-nrow(n)] / N); b <- qnorm(cumsum(colSums(n))[-ncol(n)] / N)
  psa <- pf_psitau(rowSums(n)); psb <- pf_psitau(colSums(n))
  S0 <- function(r) pf_sc(n, a, b, r, pf_cells(a, b, r))
  gr <- seq(-.9989, .9, length = 40); sv <- sapply(gr, S0); i <- which(sv[-1] < 0 & sv[-40] > 0)
  stopifnot(length(i) == 1)
  rs <- uniroot(S0, gr[c(i, i + 1)], tol = 1e-15, maxiter = 200)$root
  P <- pf_cells(a, b, rs); De <- dfun(a, b, rs)
  ou <- pf_out(n, a, b, rs, P, psa, psb)
  sr <- ifelse(O, De / P, 0)                    # signed r = Delta / pi on observed cells
  rb <- max(abs(sr)); D1 <- pf_D1(a, b, rs)
  J <- sum(w[O] * (ou$u[O]^2 - D1[O] / P[O]))
  # fixed rho, exact
  fx <- pf_out(n, a, b, rs, P + De, psa, psb)
  # the root of the perturbed score, exact (not first order)
  dS1 <- -sum(w * ou$u * sr); dlt1 <- dS1 / J
  Sf <- function(r) pf_sc(n, a, b, r, pf_cells(a, b, r) + dfun(a, b, r))
  if (rb > 0) {
    wd <- max(16 * abs(dlt1), 1e-9); rh <- uniroot(Sf, rs + c(-wd, wd), tol = 1e-16, maxiter = 200)$root
  } else rh <- rs
  Pf <- pf_cells(a, b, rh); tot <- pf_out(n, a, b, rh, Pf + dfun(a, b, rh), psa, psb)
  # d/drho at true cells, central differences for the shift term
  h <- 1e-5 * (1 - abs(rs)); up <- pf_out(n, a, b, rs + h, pf_cells(a, b, rs + h), psa, psb)
  dn <- pf_out(n, a, b, rs - h, pf_cells(a, b, rs - h), psa, psb)
  dq <- function(x) (up[[x]] - dn[[x]]) / (2 * h)
  gg <- ifelse(O, w * ou$u / P, 0)
  Wa <- pf_wm(a, b, rs); Wb <- pf_wm(b, a, rs); gs <- gg * sr
  fIrr <- -2 * sum(w * ou$u^2 * sr)
  fIra <- -2 * sapply(seq_along(a), function(c) sum(Wa[c, ] * (gs[c, ] - gs[c + 1, ])))
  fIrb <- -2 * sapply(seq_along(b), function(d) sum(Wb[d, ] * (gs[, d] - gs[, d + 1])))
  fu <- -ou$u * sr
  lin <- list(u = fu + dlt1 * dq("u"), Irr = fIrr + dlt1 * dq("Irr"), Ira = fIra + dlt1 * dq("Ira"),
              Irb = fIrb + dlt1 * dq("Irb"))
  K1 <- nrow(n); K2 <- ncol(n)
  lpsi <- (lin$u - matrix(psa %*% lin$Ira, K1, K2) - t(matrix(psb %*% lin$Irb, K2, K1)) - ou$psi * lin$Irr) / ou$Irr
  nrm <- function(x) sqrt(sum(w * x^2))
  dpsi <- ifelse(O, tot$psi - ou$psi, 0)
  dpsi_f <- ifelse(O, fx$psi - ou$psi, 0)
  gam <- nrm(dpsi) / nrm(ou$psi)
  G <- sum(w * ou$psi^2); Gf <- sum(w * tot$psi^2)
  # Gamma_{rho,tau} by threshold of each variable; correlation-scale change
  gtau <- function(q, by) {
    qq <- q[if (by == 1) row(n) else col(n), , drop = FALSE]
    sapply(seq_len(ncol(q)), function(c) {
      m <- matrix(qq[, c], K1, K2)
      sum(w * (tot$psi - ou$psi) * m) / sqrt(G * sum(w * m^2))
    })
  }
  etaS <- sum(w * abs(ou$u) * abs(sr)) / (1 - rb)
  dbcs <- sqrt(ou$Irr) * sqrt(sum(w * sr^2)) / (abs(J) * (1 - rb))
  list(rs = rs, rh = rh, rb = rb, J = J, Irr = ou$Irr, minO = min(P[O]), etaS = etaS, dS1 = dS1, dlt1 = dlt1,
       dlt = rh - rs, dbcs = dbcs, snorm = sqrt(sum(n * sr^2)) * ou$Irr / abs(J) / (1 - rb),
       dIrr_fx = fx$Irr / ou$Irr - 1, dIrr = tot$Irr / ou$Irr - 1, dIrr_f = lin$Irr / ou$Irr,
       fxb = sum(w * ou$u^2 * ((1 + sr)^-2 - 1)) / ou$Irr,
       dIra = tot$Ira - ou$Ira, dIra_f = lin$Ira, dIrb = tot$Irb - ou$Irb, dIrb_f = lin$Irb, Ira = ou$Ira, Irb = ou$Irb,
       du = max(abs((tot$u - ou$u)[O])), du_f = max(abs(lin$u[O])), gam = gam, gam_f = nrm(ifelse(O, lpsi, 0)) / nrm(ou$psi),
       gam_fx = nrm(dpsi_f) / nrm(ou$psi),
       dGrr = Gf / G - 1, gtau = c(gtau(psa, 1), gtau(psb, 2)), G = G, ubar = max(abs(ou$u[O] * dlt1)))
}
# ---- the flushed sets, as StataMP 18 returned them at its own rho-hat (docs/notes/phi2-flush/)
pf_fl <- list(A0 = rbind(c(1, 1)), A1 = rbind(c(1, 1)), A2 = rbind(c(1, 1)), A3 = rbind(c(1, 1)),
              D1 = rbind(c(1, 1), c(1, 2), c(2, 1)), D2 = rbind(c(1, 1), c(1, 2), c(2, 1)),
              Z1 = rbind(c(1, 1), c(1, 2), c(2, 1), c(2, 2)))
pf_show <- function(tag, x) cat(sprintf(
  "%-9s minpi %8.2e rb %8.2e | dS %9.2e etaS %8.2e | drho %9.2e fo %9.2e cs %8.2e nscale %8.2e | I/J %6.3f | dIrr %9.2e fo %9.2e | maxrel Ia,b %8.2e | gam %8.2e fo %8.2e | dGrr %9.2e maxGrt %8.2e\n",
  tag, x$minO, x$rb, x$dS1, x$etaS, x$dlt, x$dlt1, x$dbcs, x$snorm, x$Irr / x$J, x$dIrr, x$dIrr_f,
  max(abs(c(x$dIra / x$Ira, x$dIrb / x$Irb))), x$gam, x$gam_f, x$dGrr, max(abs(x$gtau))))
# (1) the true flushed values: replace flush with truth
R1 <- lapply(names(pf_tabs), function(nm) {
  x <- pf_prop(pf_tabs[[nm]], function(a, b, r) pf_incid(a, b, r, pf_fl[[nm]])); pf_show(nm, x); x })
names(R1) <- names(pf_tabs)
# a flushed corner below the frontier obeys the envelope; every cell that moved touches a flushed corner
for (nm in setdiff(names(pf_tabs), "Z1")) {
  x <- R1[[nm]]; n <- pf_tabs[[nm]]
  a <- qnorm(cumsum(rowSums(n))[-nrow(n)] / sum(n)); b <- qnorm(cumsum(colSums(n))[-ncol(n)] / sum(n))
  stopifnot(all(mapply(function(i, j) pf_P(a[i], b[j], x$rs) < pf_kappa, pf_fl[[nm]][, 1], pf_fl[[nm]][, 2])),
            abs(x$dlt) <= x$dbcs * (1 + 1e-3),           # Cauchy-Schwarz bound on the exact shift
            abs(x$dIrr_fx - x$fxb) <= 1e-6 * abs(x$fxb),
            abs(x$dIrr_fx) <= 2 * x$rb / (1 - x$rb)^2,   # Result P3, fixed rho
            abs(x$dGrr) <= x$gam * (2 + x$gam) * (1 + 1e-6),  # Result P5
            all(abs(x$gtau) <= x$gam * (1 + 1e-6)))
}
# Z1: corner (1,1) touches no observed cell (Result P1, exact zero). The other three touch observed
# cells but are below 1e-47, far under an ulp of pi; StataMP 18 returned exactly no change.
Z0 <- pf_prop(pf_tabs$Z1, function(a, b, r) pf_incid(a, b, r, rbind(c(1, 1))))
stopifnot(Z0$rb == 0, Z0$dlt == 0, Z0$dIrr == 0, Z0$gam == 0, R1$Z1$rb < 1e-45, abs(R1$Z1$dlt) < 1e-14)
# first order against exact, r <= 3.3e-4. Tolerance 2e-3 CHOSEN AFTER MEASURING; it describes the
# remainder of this comparison and says nothing about what is negligible.
for (nm in c("A0", "A1", "A2", "A3", "D1", "D2")) {
  x <- R1[[nm]]
  stopifnot(abs(x$dlt / x$dlt1 - 1) < 2e-3, abs(x$dIrr / x$dIrr_f - 1) < 2e-3, abs(x$gam / x$gam_f - 1) < 2e-3)
}
# (2) worst case allowed by the envelope, 2 kappa on the smallest observed cell, fixed in rho
pf_stress <- function(n, mk) { O <- n > 0
  function(a, b, r) { P <- pf_cells(a, b, r); m <- which(O & P == min(P[O]), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
    d <- matrix(0, nrow(n), ncol(n)); d[m[1], m[2]] <- mk(P[m[1], m[2]]); d } }
for (nm in c("A0", "A2", "A3", "D1", "D2"))
  pf_show(paste0(nm, "+2k"), pf_prop(pf_tabs[[nm]], pf_stress(pf_tabs[[nm]], function(p) 2 * pf_kappa)))
# (3) where the first-order form holds: a relative perturbation r of the smallest cell on A1
for (r0 in c(1e-3, .01, .05, .2, .7)) {
  x <- pf_prop(pf_tabs$A1, pf_stress(pf_tabs$A1, function(p) r0 * p))
  cat(sprintf("r=%5.3f  drho/fo-1 %9.2e  dIrr/fo-1 %9.2e  gam/fo-1 %9.2e  max|u*drho| %8.2e\n", r0,
              x$dlt / x$dlt1 - 1, x$dIrr / x$dIrr_f - 1, x$gam / x$gam_f - 1, x$ubar))
  if (r0 == .01) stopifnot(abs(x$dlt / x$dlt1 - 1) < .05, abs(x$dIrr / x$dIrr_f - 1) < .05, abs(x$gam / x$gam_f - 1) < .05)
}
stopifnot(((1 - .01)^-2 - 1) / .02 < 1.016, ((1 - .01)^-1 - 1) / .01 < 1.011,
          2 * pf_kappa / pf_dP < .71, abs(2 * pf_kappa / .01 - 3.11e-13) < 1e-15,
          abs(pf_kappa / 1.28e-8 - 1.215e-7) < 1e-9, abs(2 * pf_kappa / 1.28e-8 - 2.43e-7) < 1e-9)
# D1 = rectangle derivative matches FD (the shift's only new ingredient)
tA <- c(-.65, .5); tB <- c(-.65, -.21)
stopifnot(max(abs(pf_D1(tA, tB, -.9) - (pf_D(tA, tB, -.9 + 1e-6) - pf_D(tA, tB, -.9 - 1e-6)) / 2e-6)) < 1e-6)
cat("phi2-flush propagation checks pass\n")
```

## EFA: oblique geomin rotation (point estimates) {#sec-geomin}

*Added 2026-10-29, derivation first, for the 0.3.0 scope decided 2026-10-26 (user; spec §5
Module 12 release plan).* Nothing in `src/` or `tests/` depends on this section yet. It derives
the oblique geomin criterion and its gradient, oblique gradient projection (GPA) with step halving,
the rotated loadings and factor correlations, and why the rotation leaves $\sigma(\hat\theta)$ and
therefore $F$, $T_3$ and df unchanged. It does **not** derive rotated-loading standard errors (out
of scope for 0.3.0), and it settles none of the open conventions (ε, normalization, starts, sign and
column order, surface). Their consequences are listed at the end for the user's decision. lavaan
0.7.2's own defaults, read from its installed source, are in E-069.
New chunk names start with `gm-` and every new R name with `gm_`. The chunks are base R, plus
lavaan in `gm-lavaan`, which follows `fi-lavaan`'s precedent: it calls lavaan directly on Case E
and on simulated data, and reads or writes no fixture.

### Setting

An unrotated $m$-factor EFA is the echelon CFA of `test_efa_unrotated.do`: a $p\times m$ loading
matrix $A$ with $m(m-1)/2$ anchor zeros, $\Phi=I$, and $\Theta=I-\operatorname{diag}(AA')$ under
the delta parameterization. It fits through v1 unchanged (E-006, 2026-10-24). Every
$\Lambda$ with $\Lambda\Phi\Lambda'=AA'$ gives the same model, and a rotation picks one.

### Result GM1: the oblique family leaves σ unchanged

Let $T$ be a nonsingular $m\times m$ matrix with unit-length columns, $\operatorname{diag}(T'T)=1$.
Put
$$\Lambda = A\,(T')^{-1}, \qquad \Phi = T'T .$$
Then $\Phi$ is a correlation matrix, and
$$\Lambda\Phi\Lambda' = A(T')^{-1}\,T'T\,T^{-1}A' = AA'.$$
So the model-implied correlations, $\Theta$, the thresholds, and with them $F$, $T_3$, df and the
scaled fit indices are identical before and after rotation. The rotation is a pure
post-processing of $\hat\theta$; $\hat\Gamma$, $W_D$ and $\Delta$ never see it. (lavaan's `std_ov`
step divides $A$'s rows by $\sqrt{\operatorname{diag}(AA'+\Theta)}$ before rotating and
multiplies back afterwards. Under the delta parameterization that diagonal is 1, so the step is the
identity here; `gm-lavaan` checks it.)

### Result GM2: the geomin criterion and its gradients

With $\varepsilon>0$,
$$Q(\Lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^{p}\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^{m}(\lambda_{ij}^2+\varepsilon)\Bigr)^{1/m}.$$
Write $r_i$ for the $i$-th summand. Since $\partial r_i/\partial\lambda_{ij} =
r_i\cdot\frac1m\cdot\frac{2\lambda_{ij}}{\lambda_{ij}^2+\varepsilon}$,
$$\frac{\partial Q}{\partial\lambda_{ij}} = \frac{2}{m}\,
  \frac{\lambda_{ij}}{\lambda_{ij}^2+\varepsilon}\, r_i \;=:\; (G_Q)_{ij}.$$
The criterion is evaluated as $\exp\bigl(m^{-1}\sum_j\log(\lambda_{ij}^2+\varepsilon)\bigr)$,
which avoids underflow of the product. As a function of $T$, $f(T)=Q\bigl(A(T')^{-1}\bigr)$, and
from $d(T')^{-1} = -(T')^{-1}\,dT'\,(T')^{-1}$,
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial T} = -\bigl(\Lambda' G_Q\, T^{-1}\bigr)' =: G .$$

### Result GM3: oblique GPA

The feasible set $\{T:\operatorname{diag}(T'T)=1\}$ is a product of unit spheres, one per column.
The projection of $G$ onto its tangent space at $T$ removes, column by column, the component
along $t_j$:
$$G_p = G - T\,\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\mathbf 1'(T\circ G)\bigr).$$
At a stationary point $G_p=0$. One iteration (Bernaards & Jennrich 2005): double the step size
$\alpha$, then halve it until
$$f\bigl(\mathcal N(T-\alpha G_p)\bigr) < f(T) - \tfrac12\,\alpha\,\|G_p\|_F^2 ,$$
where $\mathcal N$ rescales each column to unit length, and accept that point. lavaan 0.7.2
implements exactly this, with $\|G_p\|_F<10^{-5}$ as its convergence test (facts note, item 4–5).

**The stall floor (measured).** The halving test compares two values of $f$ whose difference must
exceed $\tfrac12\alpha\|G_p\|^2$. Once that is below the rounding error of $f$ (relative
$\approx 10^{-16}$, $f=O(1)$), no step passes, and further halving only burns time. Measured
2026-10-29 on random $9\times m$ loadings ($m=2,3$, several starts): GPA stalls at $\|G_p\|_F$
between $6\times10^{-8}$ and $3\times10^{-7}$, at $\varepsilon=0.001$ and at $0.01$ alike. A
convergence tolerance must sit above that floor; lavaan's $10^{-5}$ does, and a first prototype
that asked for $10^{-10}$ never terminated. `gm_gpa()` therefore stops when the halving fails,
and reports $\|G_p\|_F$ at that point.

### Result GM4: the start grid (pinned, user 2026-10-29)

Start 0 is $I_m$. For $k=1,\dots,n-1$, with the $m(m-1)/2$ index pairs $(i_q,j_q)$,
$q=1,\dots,m(m-1)/2$, in `combn(m, 2)` order, $c=(\sqrt5-1)/2$, and $\{x\}$ the fractional part,
$$T_k^{(0)}=\prod_{q} R_{i_qj_q}(a_{kq}),\qquad a_{kq}=\pi\,\{k(q+1)c\},$$
where $R_{ij}(a)$ is the identity with $\cos a$ at $(i,i),(j,j)$, $-\sin a$ at $(i,j)$ and
$\sin a$ at $(j,i)$, and the product runs left to right in $q$. Each $T_k^{(0)}$ is orthogonal, so
its columns have unit length and it is a feasible start. Two properties follow from the definition:
no random-number state is read or changed, so `set seed` has no effect; and $T_k^{(0)}$ depends
only on $k$, so the grid for $n$ starts contains the grid for any $n'<n$, and raising the count can
only find an equal or lower minimum. On data with several minima the grid is part of the result,
so changing it is a change of estimator default. Random starts are a recorded contingent
extension (spec §5 Module 12), not part of this result.

### Verification

```{r gm-impl}
# Oblique geomin by gradient projection (Bernaards & Jennrich 2005), written
# from the formulas in this section; lavaan supplies only the unrotated input
# and the comparison target.
gm_Q <- function(L, eps) {
  sum(exp(rowSums(log(L^2 + eps)) / ncol(L)))
}
gm_dQ <- function(L, eps) {                 # dQ/dLambda, elementwise
  l2 <- L^2 + eps
  r  <- exp(rowSums(log(l2)) / ncol(L))
  (2 / ncol(L)) * L / l2 * r
}
gm_rot <- function(A, T) t(solve(T, t(A)))  # Lambda = A (T')^-1
gm_G <- function(A, T, eps) {               # d Q(A (T')^-1) / dT
  L <- gm_rot(A, T)
  -t(t(L) %*% gm_dQ(L, eps) %*% solve(T))
}
gm_proj <- function(T, G) G - T %*% diag(colSums(T * G), ncol(T))
gm_unit <- function(X) sweep(X, 2, sqrt(colSums(X^2)), "/")

gm_gpa <- function(A, T, eps, maxit = 10000, nhalf = 60) {
  # Stops when no halving passes Armijo: below ||Gp|| ~ 1e-7 the required
  # decrease 0.5 al ||Gp||^2 is lost in the rounding of Q (the stall floor).
  al <- 1
  f  <- gm_Q(gm_rot(A, T), eps)
  G  <- gm_G(A, T, eps)
  for (it in 0:maxit) {
    Gp <- gm_proj(T, G)
    s  <- sqrt(sum(Gp^2))
    al <- 2 * al
    ok <- FALSE
    for (h in 1:nhalf) {                    # Armijo step halving
      Tn <- gm_unit(T - al * Gp)
      fn <- gm_Q(gm_rot(A, Tn), eps)
      if (fn < f - 0.5 * s^2 * al) { ok <- TRUE; break }
      al <- al / 2
    }
    if (!ok) break
    T <- Tn; f <- fn; G <- gm_G(A, T, eps)
  }
  list(T = T, f = f, s = s, it = it, stalled = !ok)
}

# Deterministic starts, the pinned grid of Result GM4 (user, 2026-10-29): no
# RNG state enters, and start k depends only on k, so the grids are nested.
gm_starts <- function(m, n = 30) {
  out <- list(diag(m))
  pr  <- combn(m, 2)
  for (k in seq_len(n - 1)) {
    S <- diag(m)
    for (q in seq_len(ncol(pr))) {
      a <- pi * ((k * (q + 1) * (sqrt(5) - 1) / 2) %% 1)
      R <- diag(m); i <- pr[1, q]; j <- pr[2, q]
      R[i, i] <- cos(a); R[j, j] <- cos(a); R[i, j] <- -sin(a); R[j, i] <- sin(a)
      S <- S %*% R
    }
    out[[k + 1]] <- S
  }
  out
}

gm_geomin <- function(A, eps = 0.001, nstart = 30) {
  fits <- lapply(gm_starts(ncol(A), nstart), function(T0) gm_gpa(A, T0, eps))
  best <- fits[[which.min(sapply(fits, `[[`, "f"))]]
  L <- gm_rot(A, best$T)
  list(L = L, Phi = crossprod(best$T), T = best$T, f = best$f, s = best$s,
       stalled = best$stalled, fall = sapply(fits, `[[`, "f"))
}

# Up to column sign and permutation: match Y's columns to X's, then reflect.
gm_align <- function(X, Y, PX = NULL, PY = NULL) {
  m <- ncol(X); perms <- gm_perms(m); best <- Inf
  for (p in perms) {
    sg <- sign(colSums(X * Y[, p, drop = FALSE])); sg[sg == 0] <- 1
    Yp <- sweep(Y[, p, drop = FALSE], 2, sg, "*")
    d  <- max(abs(X - Yp))
    if (d < best) { best <- d; bp <- p; bs <- sg }
  }
  out <- list(dL = best, p = bp, sg = bs)
  if (!is.null(PY)) {
    Pp <- PY[bp, bp] * outer(bs, bs)
    out$dPhi <- max(abs(PX - Pp))
  }
  out
}
gm_perms <- function(m) {
  if (m == 1) return(list(1))
  out <- list()
  for (p in gm_perms(m - 1)) for (k in 0:(m - 1))
    out[[length(out) + 1]] <- append(p, m, after = k)
  out
}
```

**Gradients.** Both gradients of Result GM2 against the complex step, which has no subtractive
cancellation. Tolerance $10^{-12}$ relative, fixed before running.

