```{r gm-grad}
# (1) dQ/dLambda and dQ/dT against the complex step, which has no
# subtractive cancellation: tolerance 1e-12 relative, fixed before running.
gm_cs <- function(f, X, h = 1e-30) {
  D <- X * 0
  for (k in seq_along(X)) {
    Z <- X + 0i; Z[k] <- Z[k] + 1i * h
    D[k] <- Im(f(Z)) / h
  }
  D
}
gm_Qc <- function(L, eps) sum(exp(rowSums(log(L^2 + eps)) / ncol(L)))
set.seed(20261028)
gm_gr <- sapply(2:3, function(m) {
  A <- matrix(runif(9 * m, -0.9, 0.9), 9, m)
  T <- gm_unit(matrix(rnorm(m * m), m, m))
  e1 <- max(abs(gm_cs(function(Z) gm_Qc(Z, 0.001), A) - gm_dQ(A, 0.001))) /
        max(abs(gm_dQ(A, 0.001)))
  e2 <- max(abs(gm_cs(function(Z) gm_Qc(t(solve(Z, t(A))), 0.001), T) -
                gm_G(A, T, 0.001))) / max(abs(gm_G(A, T, 0.001)))
  c(dQdL = e1, dQdT = e2)
})
colnames(gm_gr) <- c("m=2", "m=3")
print(signif(gm_gr, 2))
stopifnot(all(gm_gr < 1e-12))
```

**Against lavaan.** For Case E at $m=2$, and a simulated 9-item, 4-category, $m=3$ data set, the
unrotated fit (`rotation = "none"`) supplies $A$. `gm_geomin()` rotates it from 30 deterministic
starts at $\varepsilon=0.001$. The result is compared, up to column sign and permutation, with
lavaan's `rotation = "geomin"` at the same ε, 30 random starts, `std_ov`, and `gpa_tol` $10^{-6}$.
Tolerances: σ invariance $10^{-12}$, fixed before the first run. Λ and Φ $10^{-5}$, **chosen after
measuring** the stall floor above: the first run's $10^{-6}$ assumed both sides could converge to
$10^{-10}$. $\|G_p\|_F$ at our stall is asserted only below lavaan's default $10^{-5}$.

```{r gm-lavaan}
library(lavaan)
gm_fit <- function(dat, m, rot, ...) {
  yn <- names(dat)
  rhs <- paste(yn, collapse = " + ")
  lhs <- paste(sprintf('efa("b")*f%d', 1:m), collapse = " + ")
  lavaan::sem(paste(lhs, "=~", rhs), data = dat, ordered = yn,
              estimator = "WLSMV", parameterization = "delta",
              test = "scaled.shifted", zero.add = c(0.5, 0.0),
              zero.keep.margins = TRUE, rotation = rot, ...)
}
gm_case <- function(dat, m) {
  f0 <- gm_fit(dat, m, "none")
  f1 <- gm_fit(dat, m, "geomin",
               rotation.args = list(geomin_epsilon = 0.001, rstarts = 30,
                                    gpa_tol = 1e-6, std_ov = TRUE))
  stopifnot(lavInspect(f0, "converged"), lavInspect(f1, "converged"))
  ra <- lavInspect(f1, "options")$rotation.args      # the options took
  stopifnot(ra$geomin_epsilon == 0.001, ra$gpa_tol == 1e-6, ra$rstarts == 30)
  e0 <- lavInspect(f0, "est"); e1 <- lavInspect(f1, "est")
  A  <- e0$lambda
  # std_ov is the identity here: delta parameterization, var(y*) = 1.
  ov <- diag(A %*% e0$psi %*% t(A) + e0$theta)
  g  <- gm_geomin(A)
  al <- gm_align(g$L, e1$lambda, g$Phi, e1$psi)
  S  <- A %*% e0$psi %*% t(A)
  Sr <- g$L %*% g$Phi %*% t(g$L)
  c(m = m, std_ov_dev = max(abs(ov - 1)),
    sigma_inv = max(abs(S - Sr)), gp_norm = g$s,
    dLambda = al$dL, dPhi = al$dPhi,
    Q_ours = g$f, Q_lav = gm_Q(e1$lambda, 0.001),
    n_optima = length(unique(round(g$fall, 8))),
    T_rel = abs(f1@test$standard$stat / f0@test$standard$stat - 1))
}

gm_root <- file.path("..", "..")
datE <- read.csv(file.path(gm_root, "fixtures", "data", "case_E.csv"))
datE[] <- lapply(datE, ordered)

set.seed(26102803)                          # simulated m = 3, 9 items, 4 categories
gm_L3 <- cbind(c(.7, .7, .6, 0, 0, .3, 0, 0, 0),
               c(0, 0, 0, .7, .6, .5, 0, .3, 0),
               c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, .7, .6, .7))
gm_P3 <- matrix(.3, 3, 3); diag(gm_P3) <- 1
gm_eta <- matrix(rnorm(800 * 3), 800, 3) %*% chol(gm_P3)
gm_ys  <- gm_eta %*% t(gm_L3) +
          sweep(matrix(rnorm(800 * 9), 800, 9), 2, sqrt(1 - diag(gm_L3 %*% gm_P3 %*% t(gm_L3))), "*")
dat3 <- as.data.frame(apply(gm_ys, 2, cut, breaks = c(-Inf, -1, 0, 1, Inf), labels = FALSE))
names(dat3) <- paste0("y", 1:9)
dat3[] <- lapply(dat3, ordered)

gm_res <- rbind(caseE_m2 = gm_case(datE, 2), sim9_m3 = gm_case(dat3, 3))
print(signif(gm_res, 3))
# Tolerances. sigma 1e-12, fixed before the first run (no convergence
# enters). Lambda and Phi against lavaan 1e-5, CHOSEN AFTER MEASURING
# (2026-10-29): Armijo GPA stalls near ||Gp|| = 1e-7 (measured 6e-8 to
# 3e-7 at eps 0.001 and 0.01), so the first run's 1e-10 was unreachable;
# lavaan runs at gpa_tol 1e-6, above that floor. Our ||Gp|| at the stall
# is reported and asserted only below lavaan's own 1e-5 default.
stopifnot(gm_res[, "sigma_inv"] < 1e-12, gm_res[, "gp_norm"] < 1e-5,
          gm_res[, "dLambda"] < 1e-5, gm_res[, "dPhi"] < 1e-5)
```

Measured 2026-10-29 with the pinned GM4 grid (lavaan 0.7.2): gradients ≤ 3.7e-16; σ invariance
≤ 2.2e-16 on both cases; $\|G_p\|_F$ at the stall 1.3e-8 (Case E) and 1.0e-8 (m = 3); Λ / Φ
against lavaan 2.4e-9 / 5.1e-9 (Case E) and 2.2e-7 / 3.5e-7 (m = 3); the minimized criterion agrees (0.141, 0.148); all 30 starts
reach one optimum (to 8 digits) in each case; the test statistic is identical between the rotated and unrotated
lavaan fits.

### What this leaves for the conventions (Unit 3; none settled here)

- **ε.** The criterion and the result change with ε; lavaan uses 0.001 for every $m$. Mplus's
  default is not established from installed sources.
- **Row normalization.** lavaan's geomin uses none. Kaiser weights would rescale rows before
  rotating; GM1 holds either way.
- **Starts.** Here all 30 starts reached one optimum, but geomin has local optima in general.
  lavaan's starts are random and unseeded; `gm_starts()` is deterministic. *Settled 2026-10-29
  (user): the GM4 grid, 30 starts, and the reporting in spec §5 Module 12.*
- **Convergence.** Any $\|G_p\|_F$ tolerance must sit above the stall floor of about $10^{-7}$;
  whether to stop at a fixed tolerance (lavaan's $10^{-5}$) or at the stall is a choice.
- **Sign and column order.** Q is invariant to column sign and order; the result is defined only
  up to both. lavaan reflects columns with negative sums and orders by the row position of the large
  loadings (`"index"`); E-070 sketches sum-positive plus sum-of-squares order.

## EFA: standard errors of the rotated solution {#sec-rot-se}

*Added 2026-11-17, roadmap unit A2 (E-108 §4.1, hypotheses RS1 to RS7), derivation
first.* Nothing in `src/` or `tests/` depends on this section. It derives the covariance of the
geomin-rotated estimate of @sec-geomin: the rotated estimator as a constrained minimum (RS1), its
bordered sandwich covariance (RS2), the equivalence with the delta method through the rotation map
and what that equivalence does and does not test (RS3), the constraint Jacobian in closed form
(RS4), invariants (RS5), where the covariance exists and what it approximates (RS6), and the routes
by which the code can obtain it (RS7). It settles no convention: what is posted, the inferential
scope near zero loadings, several minima, a bad unrotated fit and tolerances are unit A3's owner
gate. New chunk names start with `rs-` and every new R name with `rs_`; the chunks reuse `gm_`
functions of @sec-geomin and call lavaan only as `gm-lavaan` does (unrotated input, and one
comparison target in `rs-2`).

### Setting and notation

The unrotated fit is the echelon CFA of @sec-geomin: $\theta_u=(\tau,a)$, $a$ the free entries of
the $p\times m$ matrix $A$ ($A_{ij}=0$ for $i<j$), $\Phi=I$, $n_u$ free parameters, with
$\Delta_u=\partial\sigma/\partial\theta_u'$ of full column rank and
$\operatorname{ACOV}_u=(\Delta_u'W\Delta_u)^{-1}\Delta_u'W\Gamma W\Delta_u(\Delta_u'W\Delta_u)^{-1}$
(@sec-acov). The rotated parameter vector is
$$\theta^*=(\tau,\ \operatorname{vec}\Lambda,\ \phi),\qquad \phi=\text{the strict lower triangle of }\Phi,$$
with $n^*=n_u+m(m-1)$ entries (every loading free, $m(m-1)/2$ correlations, against
$m(m-1)/2$ anchors). $\sigma(\theta^*)=(\tau,\ \text{off-diagonal of }\Lambda\Phi\Lambda')$ under
the delta parameterization, and $\Delta^*=\partial\sigma/\partial\theta^{*\prime}$. The rotation of
GM1 is the map
$$g(\theta_u,T)=\bigl(\tau,\ A(T')^{-1},\ T'T\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{diag}(T'T)=1,$$
and $\sigma(g(\theta_u,T))=\sigma(\theta_u)$ for every $T$ (GM1). Tangent vectors at $T$ are
written $dT=(T')^{-1}Y$ with $\operatorname{diag}(Y)=0$: since $Y=T'dT$, the condition
$\operatorname{diag}(T'dT)=0$ is $\operatorname{diag}(Y)=0$, so the $m(m-1)$ off-diagonal
entries of $Y$ are coordinates of the tangent space. In them,
$$d\Lambda=-\Lambda Y'\Phi^{-1},\qquad d\Phi=Y+Y',$$
from $d\Lambda=-\Lambda\,dT'(T')^{-1}$ and $d\Phi=dT'T+T'dT$. Write $G_u=\partial g/\partial\theta_u'$
at fixed $T$ ($d\Lambda=dA\,(T')^{-1}$) and $G_T=\partial g/\partial Y$, an $n^*\times m(m-1)$
matrix, and $G=[G_u,\ G_T]$, which is square.

### Result RS1: the estimator

With $M=\Lambda'G_Q$ ($G_Q$ of GM2) define the $m\times m$ matrix and the stationarity function
$$E=M-\operatorname{diag}(M)\,\Phi,\qquad r(\theta^*)=\bigl(E_{jk}\bigr)_{j\neq k}\in\mathbb R^{m(m-1)},$$
ordered column by column. Its diagonal is zero by construction since $\operatorname{diag}\Phi=1$.

**Lemma RS1.1.** For every feasible $T$, with $\Lambda=A(T')^{-1}$, $\Phi=T'T$ and $G_p$ of GM3,
$$E=-G_p'\,T .$$
*Proof.* GM2 gives $G'=-\Lambda'G_QT^{-1}$, so $M=-G'T$. Put $D=\operatorname{diag}(T'G)$; GM3
reads $G=G_p+TD$, so $M=-G_p'T-D\Phi$. Since $G_p$ is tangent, $\operatorname{diag}(G_p'T)=0$, so
$\operatorname{diag}(M)=-D$ and $E=M+D\Phi=-G_p'T$. $\square$

Since $T$ is nonsingular, $r=0$ exactly when $G_p=0$: **$r=0$ is the first-order condition of the
geomin criterion on the oblique manifold** (GM2, GM3), with $m(m-1)$ conditions, and at a GPA
stall $\lvert r\rvert\le\lVert G_p\rVert_F\lVert T\rVert_2$.

**Lemma RS1.2 (the fiber is the orbit).** If $A$ has full column rank, every $\theta^*$ with
$\Lambda\Phi\Lambda'=AA'$ and $\Phi$ a positive definite correlation matrix is $g(\theta_u,T)$ for
some feasible $T$. *Proof.* With $C$ the Cholesky factor of $\Phi=CC'$, $(\Lambda C)(\Lambda C)'=AA'$,
so $\Lambda C=AO$ for an orthogonal $O$; put $T'=CO'$. Then $T'T=CC'=\Phi$ and
$A(T')^{-1}=AOC^{-1}=\Lambda$. $\square$

So the DWLS objective $F(\theta^*)$ is minimized on the whole orbit of $\hat\theta_u$, and
$\hat\theta^*$ minimizes $F$ subject to $r(\theta^*)=0$. That does not determine it: $r=0$ holds at
every stationary point of the criterion on the orbit, minima of any depth, saddles and maxima.
**The estimator is the stationary point the existing procedure selects**: the GM4 start grid, the
best converged start by $Q$, then the sign and order rule (spec Module 12). Everything below is a
local statement at that point. That the selection is stable under sampling needs the population's
selected minimum to be strictly lower than every other (no tie in $Q$) and nondegenerate (RS6).
What is reported when the starts reach several distinct minima is unit A3's item, not settled here.

### Result RS2: the bordered covariance

**Lemma RS2.1 (rank of $\Delta^*$).** Let $A$ have full column rank. (a) $\Delta^*G_u=\Delta_u$ and
$\Delta^*G_T=0$. (b) $G_T$ has full column rank $m(m-1)$, so
$\operatorname{rank}\Delta^*\le n_u$. (c) If $\Delta_u$ has full column rank then $G$ is
nonsingular, $\operatorname{rank}\Delta^*=n_u$, and $\operatorname{null}\Delta^*=\operatorname{range}G_T$:
the null space of $\Delta^*$ is exactly the $m(m-1)$ directions along which a rotation moves
$\theta^*$.

*Proof.* (a) differentiates $\sigma(g(\theta_u,T))=\sigma(\theta_u)$. (b) If $G_Ty=0$ then
$\Lambda Y'\Phi^{-1}=0$, so $Y=0$ as $\Lambda$ has full column rank. (c) Suppose $Gv=0$,
$v=(v_u,y)$. Then $G_uv_u=-G_Ty$: the echelon direction $v_u$, carried to the rotated point,
coincides with a rotation of the solution, and by (a) $\Delta_uv_u=\Delta^*G_uv_u=0$, so
$v_u=0$, then $y=0$ by (b). With $G$ nonsingular, $[\Delta_u,0]=\Delta^*G$ gives
$\operatorname{rank}\Delta^*=\operatorname{rank}\Delta_u=n_u$ and
$\operatorname{null}\Delta^*=G\,\operatorname{null}[\Delta_u,0]=\operatorname{range}G_T$. $\square$

Let $R=\partial r/\partial\theta^{*\prime}$ ($m(m-1)\times n^*$, RS4) and $Z$ a basis of
$\operatorname{null}R$.

**Result RS2.** If $R$ has full row rank and $Z'\Delta^{*\prime}W\Delta^*Z$ is nonsingular, then
$$\boxed{\;\operatorname{ACOV}(\hat\theta^*)=V\,\Delta^{*\prime}W\Gamma W\Delta^*\,V,\qquad
V=Z\,(Z'\Delta^{*\prime}W\Delta^*Z)^{-1}Z'\;}$$
with $\Delta^*$ at $\hat\theta^*$ and the divisor of @sec-acov, $e(V)=\operatorname{ACOV}/(N-1)$.
$V$ does not depend on the choice of $Z$, nor on any row scaling of $R$ (only
$\operatorname{null}R$ enters), and equals the leading $n^*\times n^*$ block of
$\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}\Delta^{*\prime}W\Delta^*&R'\\R&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]^{-1}$ whenever
that matrix is nonsingular, which is the same condition.

*Derivation.* By the implicit function theorem $\{r=0\}$ is near $\hat\theta^*$ a manifold
$\theta^*=\theta^*_0+Zu+O(\lVert u\rVert^2)$. On it the problem is an unconstrained minimum
distance problem in $u$ with Jacobian $\Delta^*Z$, and @sec-acov's linearization applies with
$\Delta$ replaced by $\Delta^*Z$; mapping back by $Z$ gives the box. Its conditions are those of
@sec-acov (correct specification, expected information as bread) plus the two in the statement,
which RS6 characterizes. RS3 reaches the same matrix by a second argument.

### Result RS3: the delta method, and what agreement tests

**(ii) The derivative of the rotation map.** Let $R\,G_T$ be nonsingular. Then
$\Psi(\theta_u,Y)=r(g(\theta_u,T))$ has a nonsingular derivative in $Y$, so by the implicit
function theorem the selected stationary point continues smoothly: there is a $C^1$ map
$\rho$ with $r(\rho(\theta_u))=0$ near $\hat\theta_u$, and
$$J=\frac{\partial\rho}{\partial\theta_u'}=\bigl(I-G_T(RG_T)^{-1}R\bigr)G_u .$$
Differentiating $r(\rho)=0$ gives $RJ=0$, and by RS2.1(a) $\Delta^*J=\Delta^*G_u=\Delta_u$. Every
$\tilde J$ with $\Delta^*\tilde J=\Delta_u$ and $R\tilde J=0$ equals $J$, because the columns of
$J-\tilde J$ lie in $\operatorname{null}\Delta^*\cap\operatorname{null}R=\{0\}$ (RS6). So $J$ is
also the unique solution of the stacked system $[\Delta^*;R]\,J=[\Delta_u;0]$. Both statements need
$R$ to be the true derivative of $r$: with any other $\tilde R$ the stacked solution $\tilde J$ still
satisfies $\Delta^*\tilde J=\Delta_u$, but it is not $\partial\rho/\partial\theta_u'$.

**(i) An algebraic identity.** Let $\Delta_u$ have full column rank and let $\tilde R$ be *any*
$m(m-1)\times n^*$ matrix of full row rank with $\operatorname{null}\tilde R\cap\operatorname{null}\Delta^*=\{0\}$,
$\tilde Z$ a basis of its null space, $\tilde V$ as in RS2, and $\tilde J$ any matrix with
$\Delta^*\tilde J=\Delta_u$ and $\tilde R\tilde J=0$. Then
$$\tilde J\operatorname{ACOV}_u\tilde J'=\tilde V\,\Delta^{*\prime}W\Gamma W\Delta^*\,\tilde V .$$
*Proof.* $\tilde J=\tilde ZB$ for an $n_u\times n_u$ matrix $B$ ($\dim\operatorname{null}\tilde R=n_u$),
and $\Delta^*\tilde ZB=\Delta_u$ forces $B$ nonsingular. Then
$\tilde J(\Delta_u'W\Delta_u)^{-1}\Delta_u'W=\tilde ZB(B'\tilde Z'\Delta^{*\prime}W\Delta^*\tilde ZB)^{-1}B'\tilde Z'\Delta^{*\prime}W
=\tilde V\Delta^{*\prime}W$, and both sides are this matrix times $\Gamma$ times its transpose. $\square$

The identity holds exactly for the sample quantities, not only in the limit, and it holds for a
wrong $\tilde R$. **Agreement of the bordered and delta-method covariances therefore does not
validate $R$** (E-109, prototype; the negative control below). What ties
the covariance to the rotation is (ii) with the true $R$, verified below against a re-rotation
that does not use $R$.

**The statistical statement.** If the population's selected stationary point is a strict, unique
lowest minimum of $Q$ on its orbit and nondegenerate, then for $N$ large the selected sample
solution is $\rho(\hat\theta_u)$ with probability tending to one, and the delta method gives
$\sqrt N(\hat\theta^*-\theta_0^*)\to N(0,J\operatorname{ACOV}_uJ')$, the matrix of RS2. Neither
condition is checkable from one sample; unit A3 decides what is said when the starts find several
minima.

### Result RS4: the constraint Jacobian in closed form

With $\ell_{ij}=\lambda_{ij}^2+\varepsilon$, $h_{ij}=\lambda_{ij}/\ell_{ij}$,
$h'_{ij}=(\varepsilon-\lambda_{ij}^2)/\ell_{ij}^2$, $Q_i$ the $i$-th summand of GM2 and
$(G_Q)_{ij}=\tfrac2m h_{ij}Q_i$, the Hessian of $Q_i$ in row $i$ is
$$H_i[k,l]=\frac{\partial (G_Q)_{ik}}{\partial\lambda_{il}}=\frac2m\,Q_i\Bigl(\delta_{kl}h'_{ik}+\frac2m\,h_{ik}h_{il}\Bigr).$$
From $M_{jk}=\sum_i\lambda_{ij}(G_Q)_{ik}$, for the row of $r$ at $(j,k)$, $j\ne k$:
$$\frac{\partial r_{jk}}{\partial\lambda_{il}}=\delta_{lj}(G_Q)_{ik}+\lambda_{ij}H_i[k,l]
-\Phi_{jk}\bigl(\delta_{lj}(G_Q)_{ij}+\lambda_{ij}H_i[j,l]\bigr),\qquad
\frac{\partial r_{jk}}{\partial\phi_{\{jk\}}}=-M_{jj},$$
zero for every other correlation and for every threshold. Each loading enters $R$ through
$h'_{ij}$, which is $1/\varepsilon$ at $\lambda_{ij}=0$ and changes sign at
$\lvert\lambda_{ij}\rvert=\sqrt\varepsilon$; RS6 returns to this. Production uses the closed form; a
numerical Jacobian is an oracle only.

### Result RS5: invariants

(a) *Threshold block.* $\rho$ leaves $\tau$ unchanged, so $J$'s threshold rows are $[I,0]$ and the
rotated threshold block equals $\operatorname{ACOV}_{u,\tau\tau}$, which is $\Gamma_{\tau\tau}$
(@sec-acov).

(b) *Rotation-invariant functions.* If $h(\theta^*)$ is constant on orbits, $\nabla h\,G_T=0$ and
$\nabla h\,G_u=\nabla h_u$, so $\nabla h\,J=\nabla h_u$ and
$\nabla h\operatorname{ACOV}^*\nabla h'=\nabla h_u\operatorname{ACOV}_u\nabla h_u'$. In particular
$\Delta^*\operatorname{ACOV}^*\Delta^{*\prime}=\Delta_u\operatorname{ACOV}_u\Delta_u'$. This needs no
property of $R$ beyond RS3's conditions.

(c) *Signed column permutation.* For a signed permutation $P$, $\pi(\theta^*)=(\tau,\Lambda P,P'\Phi P)$
is linear with matrix $\Pi$. $G_Q(\Lambda P)=G_Q(\Lambda)P$ ($h$ is odd, $Q_i$ invariant), so
$M\mapsto P'MP$ and $r(\pi\theta^*)=S\,r(\theta^*)$ for a signed permutation $S$ of the rows. Hence
$\Delta^*(\pi\theta^*)\Pi=\Delta^*(\theta^*)$, $R(\pi\theta^*)\Pi=SR(\theta^*)$, the null basis
maps to $\Pi Z$, and the covariance recomputed at $\pi\hat\theta^*$ is
$\Pi\operatorname{ACOV}^*\Pi'$. The sign and order rule can be applied before or after the
covariance is formed.

### Result RS6: where it exists, and what it approximates

Three questions are kept apart: whether the bordered system is nonsingular, how well conditioned it
is, and whether the SEs are calibrated. Only the first is answered by a theorem.

**(i) Nonsingularity.** Let $A$ have full column rank. Then
$$Z'\Delta^{*\prime}W\Delta^*Z\ \text{nonsingular}\iff
\operatorname{rank}\Delta^*=n_u\ \text{and}\ RG_T\ \text{nonsingular},$$
and when $G$ is nonsingular, $\operatorname{rank}\Delta^*=n_u$ is the same as $\Delta_u$ having full
column rank (the unrotated bread nonsingular). *Proof.* $W$ is positive definite, so the left side
is $\operatorname{rank}(\Delta^*Z)=$ number of columns of $Z$. (Numerically the rank is taken of
$W^{1/2}\Delta^*Z$, not of its cross-product, whose squared singular values would move spec §4.8's
$10^{-8}$ cut.) If it holds,
$\dim\operatorname{null}R\ge n^*-m(m-1)=n_u$ forces $\operatorname{rank}\Delta^*\ge n_u$, hence
$=n_u$ (RS2.1b), $R$ has full row rank, and $\operatorname{null}R\cap\operatorname{range}G_T=\{0\}$,
i.e. $RG_T$ is nonsingular. Conversely, $RG_T$ nonsingular gives $R$ full row rank and, with
$\operatorname{null}\Delta^*=\operatorname{range}G_T$ (which holds when $\operatorname{rank}\Delta^*=n_u$,
by RS2.1b), $\Delta^*Z$ injective. The last clause is $[\Delta_u,0]=\Delta^*G$. $\square$

$G$ is singular exactly when an echelon direction coincides with a rotation (proof of RS2.1c), that
is when the echelon chart itself is degenerate, as with $a_{11}=0$ at $m=2$; then $\Delta_u$ is
rank deficient while the rotated system can be regular (`rs-6`, matrix S2). A singular unrotated
bread is expected to stop the unrotated fit before any rotation; that has not been run on such a
case, and what is said there is A3's item. $m=1$ is the
case without constraints: $R$ has no rows, $Z=I$, $J=G_u$ is the sign of the single column, and the
rotated covariance is the unrotated one.

*What $RG_T$ is.* At a stationary point, differentiating Lemma RS1.1 along $dT$ gives
$dE=-(dG_p)'T$, because the term $G_p'dT$ vanishes; and $dG_p$ is tangent there (differentiate
$\operatorname{diag}(G_p'T)=0$). $dG_p$ is then the Riemannian Hessian of $f(T)=Q(A(T')^{-1})$
applied to $dT$. So $RG_T$ is that Hessian seen through $T'$, and **$RG_T$ is nonsingular exactly
when the selected solution is a nondegenerate critical point of the criterion**: it holds at a
minimum with positive definite Hessian, and fails where two minima merge or a direction is flat.
Large condition numbers of the bordered system at poorer local minima
(E-109, regularity) are consistent with near-degenerate critical points;
that reading is not established for those cases.

**(ii) What the covariance approximates.** RS3 makes the covariance the first-order (delta-method)
covariance of $\rho(\hat\theta_u)$. It describes the sampling distribution of $\hat\theta^*$ when
$\rho$ is close to linear over the region where $\hat\theta_u$ falls. The criterion fixes the scale
on which $\rho$ is close to linear in a loading near zero. Each loading enters $R$, and so $J$,
through $h'(\lambda)=(\varepsilon-\lambda^2)/(\lambda^2+\varepsilon)^2$, and
$$\frac{h'(\lambda_0+\delta)}{h'(\lambda_0)}\Big|_{\lambda_0=0}=\frac{1-u}{(1+u)^2},\qquad u=\delta^2/\varepsilon:$$
the weight the criterion puts on a loading at zero falls by half at $\lvert\delta\rvert\approx0.4\sqrt\varepsilon$
and changes sign at $\lvert\delta\rvert=\sqrt\varepsilon$. So $J$ is roughly constant over the
sampling range of a loading only if that range is small against $\sqrt\varepsilon$, and the
relative error of the first-order term is of order $s/\sqrt\varepsilon$, with $s$ the sampling
spread of the loading. Three consequences follow from the derivation, and they are statements about
the approximation, not results about coverage:

- For fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and a nondegenerate selected minimum the covariance is asymptotically
  correct, since $s\propto N^{-1/2}$. The sample size at which the approximation becomes accurate
  near a zero loading grows like $1/\varepsilon$: dividing $\varepsilon$ by 100 multiplies it by 100.
  Improvement between $N=500$ and $N=2000$ need not be visible at $\varepsilon=10^{-4}$.
- A loading whose population value is within a few $\sqrt\varepsilon$ of zero and whose spread is
  comparable to $\sqrt\varepsilon$ is where $J$ changes most over the sampling range. The reported
  SE, evaluated at the estimate, then moves with the estimate.
- A loading held near zero with spread much smaller than $\sqrt\varepsilon$ sits where
  $h'\approx1/\varepsilon$ is nearly constant, and one far from zero ($\lvert\lambda\rvert\gg\sqrt\varepsilon$,
  spread $\ll\lvert\lambda\rvert$) where $h'\approx-1/\lambda^2$ varies slowly. That is a statement
  about each loading's own weight only. $R$ couples every parameter of the block through the
  rotation, and its rows are dominated by the near-zero loadings (`regularity/finding.md`), so a
  loading far from zero can still inherit nonlinearity from small loadings in the same solution:
  `rs-6-ill` shows it on Case E.

These are consistent with the descriptive findings (E-109, calibration map),
which were not used to derive them. They do not predict a coverage figure, locate a boundary, or
justify a threshold, a change of $\varepsilon$, a floor on SEs or another interval.
**Status: the scale of the approximation is derived; its quantitative link to coverage is not
established.** Not explained by this derivation, and left open: the two-sided misses at loadings
generated as zero at $m=3$, $\varepsilon=10^{-3}$, $N=2000$ (mean SE close to the empirical SD,
so not the one-sided mechanism above; whether several minima are involved is not established), and
the undercoverage of clearly nonzero cross-loadings and a factor correlation at $N=500$ in one
population, which goes away with $N$ and is not near zero, so not this mechanism.

**(iii) Computable quantities.** The derivation yields one family of quantities that measure the
mechanism in (ii) on the observed sample: how much $\rho$ departs from linear, and how much the
SE changes, when $\hat\theta_u$ is moved by one SE in the direction that moves a given loading
(the chunk `rs-6-ill`), together with $\lvert\hat\lambda\rvert/\sqrt\varepsilon$ and
$\mathrm{SE}/\sqrt\varepsilon$. They are computable without simulation. **Whether any of them
separates calibrated from miscalibrated intervals, and at what value, is not established**; that
needs a study preregistered under `docs/prereg-template.md` §3a before it touches data, and the
calibration map's records are not to be searched for it. The condition number of the bordered
system is not among them: (i) shows it measures closeness to a degenerate critical point or a
singular unrotated bread, which is a different question.

### Result RS7: how the code can obtain the covariance

Three routes, equal by RS2 and RS3:

| Route | Computes | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Bordered, $\Delta^*$ from Δ | $\Delta^*$ by `dwlsmv_delta_cols()` at $\hat\theta^*$ on the echelon table with every block loading and factor covariance selected (fixed rows included), then RS2 | $\hat\theta^*$, the parameter table, $R$, $W$, $\Gamma$ |
| 2. Bordered, $\Delta^*$ by the chain rule | $\Delta^*=[\Delta_u,\ 0]\,G^{-1}$ (RS2.1), then RS2 | fitted $\Delta_u$, $A$, $\hat\Lambda,\hat\Phi$, $(T')^{-1}$, $R$, $W$, $\Gamma$ |
| 3. Delta method | $J=(I-G_T(RG_T)^{-1}R)G_u$, then $J\operatorname{ACOV}_uJ'$ | $\operatorname{ACOV}_u$, $A$, $\hat\Lambda,\hat\Phi$, $(T')^{-1}$, $R$; no $\Delta$, $W$ or $\Gamma$ |

Since $\hat\Lambda=A(T')^{-1}$ and $A$ has full column rank, $(T')^{-1}=(A'A)^{-1}A'\hat\Lambda$,
so the rotation matrix need not be returned by `dwlsmv_geomin()`. Route 1 is the one a source reading
supports (E-109, architecture); it has never been exercised with fixed
rows, and unit A2b probes it in Stata. None of the three calls `dwls_identify()`,
`dwls_inference()` or `dwlsmv_acov()` on rotated quantities, and none touches a locked signature.
Which route production computes, and therefore what the A3 snapshot holds, is A3's item. A test
oracle should differ from production in route; by RS3(i) the oracle for $R$ itself is the complex
step, and for $J$ the re-rotation.

### Verification

**§3a form** (`docs/prereg-template.md`; the roadmap's §4.3 reading, for the owner to confirm at
A3). The layers are certified separately: a pass at one is not evidence for another.

| Layer | Deciding criterion (fixed before running) | Comparator and its independence | Shares |
|---|---|---|---|
| $R$ (RS4) | closed form against complex step, $10^{-12}$ relative | different representation (derivative formula against differentiated $r$) and algorithm | $r$, i.e. GM2's gradient |
| $J$ (RS3 ii) | closed form against the complex step of a re-rotation, $10^{-10}$ relative | different representation (implicit root of $r=0$ against a linear formula), no use of $R$ | $r$, $g$ |
| Bordered covariance (RS2) | lavaan's own pieces reproduce its `vcov`, $10^{-12}$; own pieces at lavaan's point within spec §7.2's SE row | lavaan: independent in code, shares the method | the method, W, Γ, the unrotated fit |
| Identity (RS3 i) | $100\,u\,\kappa$ | none: it is algebra, and passes with a wrong $R$ | everything |

Domain: Cases E ($m=2$, $\varepsilon=10^{-4}$), F ($m=3$, $10^{-3}$), G (binary, $m=2$, $10^{-4}$),
lavaan 0.7.2, each at its selected solution, plus $m=1$ on Case E and two constructed loading
matrices for RS6(i). **Not certified:** calibration of the SEs (A3, A6); other data, $m\ge4$,
several minima, near ties in the ordering statistic, empty binary cells; the Stata code route
(A2b); tolerances against lavaan and Mplus for production (A3); the GPA stall point as against the
Newton-polished point beyond the diagnostic printed in `rs-7`.

**Provenance.** The main session wrote `rs-impl` to `rs-4` and the three `rs-3` chunks from the
formulas above. A read-only drafting agent (Sonnet-class) wrote `rs-5`, `rs-6`, `rs-6-ill` and
`rs-7` from a specification the main session gave it; the main session read them against this
section and reran them (a reproduction of the agent's code, with identical output, not an
independent implementation). The R prototype (E-109) was used only to
check the algebra; no number here is taken from it.

**Implementation and inputs.** lavaan supplies the unrotated fit only. The rotation is
`gm_geomin()` (GM4 grid, 30 starts) followed by Newton on $r=0$ from the selected start, then the
sign and order rule. Newton is used so that the checks below are not limited by the GPA stall;
`rs-7` reports how far the stall point is from the polished one.

```{r rs-impl}
# Rotated covariance (@sec-rot-se), written from the formulas of this section.
# theta* = (tau, vec(Lambda) column-major, phi = strict lower triangle of Phi column-major).
# theta_u = (tau, a), a = the free echelon loadings A[row >= col], column-major.
# r = off-diagonal entries of E = M - diag(M) Phi, M = Lambda' G_Q, column-major.
rs_off   <- function(m) which(row(diag(m)) != col(diag(m)), arr.ind = TRUE)
rs_low   <- function(p) which(lower.tri(diag(p)), arr.ind = TRUE)
rs_phidx <- function(a, b, m) {                 # position of phi_ab in phi
  lw <- rs_low(m); which(lw[, 1] == max(a, b) & lw[, 2] == min(a, b))
}
rs_Phi <- function(phi, m) {                    # complex-safe, no conjugation
  P <- matrix(0 * phi[1], m, m); if (m > 1) P[lower.tri(P)] <- phi
  P <- P + t(P); diag(P) <- 1; P
}
rs_unpack <- function(x, p, m, nth) {
  list(L = matrix(x[nth + seq_len(p * m)], p, m),
       Phi = rs_Phi(x[nth + p * m + seq_len(m * (m - 1) / 2)], m))
}
rs_pack <- function(tau, L, Phi) c(tau, as.vector(L), Phi[lower.tri(Phi)])
rs_sig  <- function(L, Phi) { S <- L %*% Phi %*% t(L); S[rs_low(nrow(L))] }
rs_Emat <- function(L, Phi, eps) {
  M <- t(L) %*% gm_dQ(L, eps); M - diag(diag(M), ncol(L)) %*% Phi
}
rs_r <- function(L, Phi, eps) { E <- rs_Emat(L, Phi, eps); E[rs_off(ncol(L))] }

# Result RS4: the closed-form Jacobian R = dr/dtheta*'.
rs_R <- function(L, Phi, eps, nth) {
  p <- nrow(L); m <- ncol(L); off <- rs_off(m)
  l2 <- L^2 + eps; Qi <- exp(rowSums(log(l2)) / m)
  Gq <- (2 / m) * L / l2 * Qi; h <- L / l2; hp <- (eps - L^2) / l2^2
  M <- t(L) %*% Gq
  H <- function(k, l) (2 / m) * Qi * ((k == l) * hp[, k] + (2 / m) * h[, k] * h[, l])
  R <- matrix(0, nrow(off), nth + p * m + m * (m - 1) / 2)
  for (q in seq_len(nrow(off))) {
    j <- off[q, 1]; k <- off[q, 2]
    for (l in 1:m) {
      dMjk <- (l == j) * Gq[, k] + L[, j] * H(k, l)
      dMjj <- (l == j) * Gq[, j] + L[, j] * H(j, l)
      R[q, nth + (l - 1) * p + 1:p] <- dMjk - Phi[j, k] * dMjj
    }
    R[q, nth + p * m + rs_phidx(j, k, m)] <- -M[j, j]
  }
  R
}

# Delta* (all of Lambda and phi) and Delta_u (echelon free loadings, Phi = I).
rs_Dstar <- function(L, Phi, nth) {
  p <- nrow(L); m <- ncol(L); lw <- rs_low(p); LP <- L %*% Phi
  D <- matrix(0, nth + nrow(lw), nth + p * m + m * (m - 1) / 2)
  D[cbind(seq_len(nth), seq_len(nth))] <- 1
  for (s in seq_len(nrow(lw))) {
    a <- lw[s, 1]; b <- lw[s, 2]
    for (j in 1:m) {
      D[nth + s, nth + (j - 1) * p + a] <- LP[b, j]
      D[nth + s, nth + (j - 1) * p + b] <- LP[a, j]
    }
    if (m > 1) for (q in seq_len(m * (m - 1) / 2)) {
      j <- rs_low(m)[q, 1]; k <- rs_low(m)[q, 2]
      D[nth + s, nth + p * m + q] <- L[a, j] * L[b, k] + L[a, k] * L[b, j]
    }
  }
  D
}
rs_free <- function(p, m) as.vector(row(matrix(0, p, m)) >= col(matrix(0, p, m)))
rs_ucols <- function(p, m, nth) c(seq_len(nth), nth + which(rs_free(p, m)))
rs_Du <- function(A, nth) rs_Dstar(A, diag(ncol(A)), nth)[, rs_ucols(nrow(A), ncol(A), nth)]

# G = [G_u, G_T]: derivatives of g(theta_u, T) = (tau, A T'^-1, T'T) at the rotated point.
# G_u at fixed T: dLambda = dA T'^-1. G_T in the coordinates Y = T' dT, diag(Y) = 0:
# dLambda = -Lambda Y' Phi^-1, dPhi = Y + Y'; one column per off-diagonal (a, b), as r.
rs_Gu <- function(L, Minv, nth) {               # Minv = T'^-1
  p <- nrow(L); m <- ncol(L); fr <- which(rs_free(p, m))
  G <- matrix(0, nth + p * m + m * (m - 1) / 2, nth + length(fr))
  G[cbind(seq_len(nth), seq_len(nth))] <- 1
  for (c in seq_along(fr)) {
    i <- (fr[c] - 1) %% p + 1; j <- (fr[c] - 1) %/% p + 1
    dL <- matrix(0, p, m); dL[i, ] <- Minv[j, ]
    G[nth + seq_len(p * m), nth + c] <- as.vector(dL)
  }
  G
}
rs_GT <- function(L, Phi, nth) {
  p <- nrow(L); m <- ncol(L); off <- rs_off(m); Pi <- solve(Phi)
  G <- matrix(0, nth + p * m + m * (m - 1) / 2, nrow(off))
  for (q in seq_len(nrow(off))) {
    Y <- matrix(0, m, m); Y[off[q, 1], off[q, 2]] <- 1
    G[nth + seq_len(p * m), q] <- as.vector(-L %*% t(Y) %*% Pi)
    G[nth + p * m + rs_phidx(off[q, 1], off[q, 2], m), q] <- 1
  }
  G
}

# The three covariances (ACOV scale; e(V) = ACOV / (N - 1), @sec-acov).
rs_acov_u <- function(Du, W, Gam) {
  Bi <- solve(crossprod(Du * sqrt(W))); X <- W * Du
  Bi %*% crossprod(X, Gam %*% X) %*% Bi
}
rs_nullbasis <- function(R, n) {                # orthonormal basis of null(R)
  if (nrow(R) == 0) return(diag(n))
  s <- svd(t(R), nu = n); s$u[, (nrow(R) + 1):n, drop = FALSE]
}
rs_bordered <- function(Ds, R, W, Gam) {        # Result RS2
  Z <- rs_nullbasis(R, ncol(Ds)); X <- W * Ds
  V <- Z %*% solve(crossprod(Ds %*% Z * sqrt(W)), t(Z))
  list(acov = V %*% crossprod(X, Gam %*% X) %*% V, V = V, Z = Z)
}
rs_J <- function(R, Gu, GT) {                   # Result RS3: dρ/dθ_u, no Delta, W or Gamma
  if (ncol(GT) == 0) return(Gu)
  Gu - GT %*% solve(R %*% GT, R %*% Gu)
}

# Newton on r over the oblique manifold, Y-coordinates, retraction = column scaling.
rs_polish <- function(A, T, eps, maxit = 50, tol = 1e-14) {
  m <- ncol(A); off <- rs_off(m); it <- 0
  if (m > 1) for (it in 1:maxit) {
    Minv <- solve(t(T)); L <- A %*% Minv; Phi <- crossprod(T)
    rv <- rs_r(L, Phi, eps)
    if (max(abs(rv)) <= tol * max(1, max(abs(gm_dQ(L, eps))))) break
    K <- rs_R(L, Phi, eps, 0) %*% rs_GT(L, Phi, 0)
    Y <- matrix(0, m, m); Y[off] <- -solve(K, rv)
    T <- gm_unit(T + solve(t(T), Y))
  }
  Minv <- solve(t(T))
  list(T = T, L = A %*% Minv, Phi = crossprod(T), Minv = Minv, it = it,
       res = max(0, abs(rs_r(A %*% Minv, crossprod(T), eps))))
}

# The project's sign and order rule (spec Module 12): reflect negative-sum columns,
# then order by the mean row index of the loadings with |lambda| >= 0.8 max |lambda|.
rs_canon <- function(L, Phi, T) {
  s <- ifelse(colSums(L) < 0, -1, 1); S <- diag(s, ncol(L))
  L <- L %*% S; T <- T %*% S; Phi <- S %*% Phi %*% S
  ix <- sapply(seq_len(ncol(L)), function(j) {
    a <- abs(L[, j]); mean(which(a >= 0.8 * max(a)))
  })
  o <- order(ix)
  list(L = L[, o, drop = FALSE], Phi = Phi[o, o, drop = FALSE], T = T[, o, drop = FALSE])
}

# Complex-step Jacobian of a vector function (no subtractive cancellation).
rs_csjac <- function(f, x, h = 1e-30) {
  sapply(seq_along(x), function(k) {
    z <- x + 0i; z[k] <- z[k] + 1i * h; Im(f(z)) / h
  })
}
rs_relmax <- function(X, Y) max(abs(X - Y)) / max(abs(Y))
rs_cond   <- function(X) { d <- svd(X)$d; max(d) / min(d) }
rs_nrank  <- function(X) { d <- svd(X)$d; sum(d > 1e-8 * max(d)) }   # spec §4.8's criterion
```

```{r rs-setup}
# Cases E (m = 2), F (m = 3) and G (binary, m = 2) at the spec's epsilon rule.
# lavaan supplies only the unrotated echelon fit: A, tau, W (WLS.VD), Gamma (NACOV), N.
library(lavaan)
rs_root  <- file.path("..", "..")
rs_read  <- function(cs) {
  d <- read.csv(file.path(rs_root, "fixtures", "data", paste0("case_", cs, ".csv")))
  d[] <- lapply(d, ordered); d
}
rs_eps   <- c(E = 1e-4, F = 1e-3, G = 1e-4)
rs_m     <- c(E = 2, F = 3, G = 2)
rs_prep  <- function(cs, m = rs_m[[cs]], eps = rs_eps[[cs]]) {
  dat <- rs_read(cs)
  f0  <- gm_fit(dat, m, "none")
  stopifnot(lavInspect(f0, "converged"))
  A   <- unname(lavInspect(f0, "est")$lambda)
  stopifnot(all(A[!rs_free(nrow(A), m)] == 0))           # echelon anchors
  tau <- as.numeric(f0@implied$th[[1]]); nth <- length(tau)
  W   <- as.numeric(f0@SampleStats@WLS.VD[[1]]); Gam <- f0@SampleStats@NACOV[[1]]
  N   <- f0@SampleStats@ntotal
  Du  <- rs_Du(A, nth)
  g   <- if (m > 1) gm_geomin(A, eps = eps, nstart = 30) else list(T = diag(1), s = 0)
  pz  <- rs_polish(A, g$T, eps)                          # Newton from the selected start
  cn  <- rs_canon(pz$L, pz$Phi, pz$T)
  Minv <- solve(t(cn$T)); L <- A %*% Minv; Phi <- crossprod(cn$T)
  Ds  <- rs_Dstar(L, Phi, nth); R <- rs_R(L, Phi, eps, nth)
  Gu  <- rs_Gu(L, Minv, nth); GT <- rs_GT(L, Phi, nth)
  list(cs = cs, m = m, eps = eps, dat = dat, A = A, tau = tau, nth = nth, W = W,
       Gam = Gam, N = N, p = nrow(A), g = g, pz = pz, T = cn$T, L = L, Phi = Phi,
       Minv = Minv, Ds = Ds, Du = Du, R = R, Gu = Gu, GT = GT,
       acov_u = rs_acov_u(Du, W, Gam))
}
rs_cases <- lapply(c(E = "E", F = "F", G = "G"), rs_prep)
print(t(sapply(rs_cases, function(x) c(m = x$m, eps = x$eps, N = x$N,
  n_star = ncol(x$Ds), n_u = ncol(x$Du), constraints = nrow(x$R),
  newton_its = x$pz$it, gpa_Gp = x$g$s))))
```

**RS1.** The identity of Lemma RS1.1 at feasible $T$ far from stationarity, where $E$ and $G_p$ are
$O(1)$; at the GPA stall, the bound on $\lvert r\rvert$; after Newton, $r$ at rounding. *The first
run tested the identity at the stall, normalized by $\max\lvert G_p\rvert\approx10^{-8}$: it failed
at $10^{-10}$ because $E$ there is a difference of $O(1)$ terms whose rounding is $10^{-16}$ of
those terms, not of $G_p$. The normalizer was wrong, not the identity; the check was moved to
non-stationary $T$ with the normalizer $\max\lvert E\rvert$ after that run (2026-11-17), the
tolerance unchanged.*

```{r rs-1}
# RS1: E = -G_p' T holds for every feasible T, so r = 0 exactly when G_p = 0.
# (a) The identity at feasible T far from stationarity (20 random T per case), where
#     E and G_p are O(1): 1e-12 relative to max|E|, fixed before running.
# (b) At the GPA stall the bound |r| <= ||G_p||_F ||T||_2, and after Newton |r| < 1e-13.
set.seed(20261117)
rs1 <- t(sapply(rs_cases, function(x) {
  id <- max(sapply(1:20, function(k) {
    T0 <- gm_unit(matrix(rnorm(x$m^2), x$m, x$m))
    E  <- rs_Emat(gm_rot(x$A, T0), crossprod(T0), x$eps)
    Gp <- gm_proj(T0, gm_G(x$A, T0, x$eps))
    max(abs(E + t(Gp) %*% T0)) / max(abs(E))
  }))
  T0 <- x$g$T; rS <- max(abs(rs_r(gm_rot(x$A, T0), crossprod(T0), x$eps)))
  Gp <- gm_proj(T0, gm_G(x$A, T0, x$eps))
  c(identity = id, Gp_stall = sqrt(sum(Gp^2)), r_stall = rS,
    bound_ok = rS <= sqrt(sum(Gp^2)) * norm(T0, "2"), r_polished = x$pz$res)
}))
print(signif(rs1, 3))
stopifnot(rs1[, "identity"] < 1e-12, rs1[, "bound_ok"] == 1, rs1[, "r_polished"] < 1e-13)
```

**RS4.** Closed-form $R$ and $\Delta^*$ against the complex step.

```{r rs-4}
# RS4: closed-form R against the complex step of r; Delta* against the complex step
# of sigma. Tolerance 1e-12 relative to the largest entry, fixed before running (as GM2).
rs4 <- t(sapply(rs_cases, function(x) {
  th <- rs_pack(x$tau, x$L, x$Phi); p <- x$p; m <- x$m; nth <- x$nth
  rf <- function(z) { u <- rs_unpack(z, p, m, nth); rs_r(u$L, u$Phi, x$eps) }
  sf <- function(z) { u <- rs_unpack(z, p, m, nth); c(z[seq_len(nth)], rs_sig(u$L, u$Phi)) }
  c(R_vs_cs = rs_relmax(x$R, rs_csjac(rf, th)),
    Dstar_vs_cs = rs_relmax(x$Ds, rs_csjac(sf, th)),
    rank_R = rs_nrank(x$R), rows_R = nrow(x$R))
}))
print(signif(rs4, 3))
stopifnot(rs4[, "R_vs_cs"] < 1e-12, rs4[, "Dstar_vs_cs"] < 1e-12,
          rs4[, "rank_R"] == rs4[, "rows_R"])
```

**RS2.** Against lavaan with `std_ov = FALSE`. (a) is the statement that lavaan computes RS2's
formula; (b) puts the own $\Delta^*$ and closed-form $R$ in lavaan's place at lavaan's estimate.
Expected: (a) near $10^{-16}$; (b) near $10^{-10}$, limited by lavaan's Richardson Jacobian. The
diagnostics compare the own polished solution with lavaan's, whose rotation stops at
`gpa_tol` $10^{-6}$ (its $r$ is printed), so they measure lavaan's stopping point and decide nothing.

```{r rs-2}
# RS2 against lavaan 0.7.2 (std_ov = FALSE, the comparator setting of A1).
# (a) lavaan's own Delta, W, Gamma and constraint Jacobian through RS2's formula
#     reproduce vcov(fit): 1e-12 relative to the largest entry, fixed before running.
# (b) Own Delta* and own closed-form R at lavaan's rotated estimate, lavaan's W and
#     Gamma: SEs against vcov(fit) within spec §7.2's SE row, 1e-8 + 1e-5 |b|.
# Diagnostic only: own rotated point and SEs against lavaan's.
rs2_one <- function(x) {
  set.seed(20261117)                            # lavaan's random rotation starts
  fr <- gm_fit(x$dat, x$m, "geomin",
               rotation.args = list(geomin_epsilon = x$eps, rstarts = 30,
                                    gpa_tol = 1e-6, std_ov = FALSE))
  stopifnot(lavInspect(fr, "converged"))
  ra <- lavInspect(fr, "options")$rotation.args
  stopifnot(identical(ra$std_ov, FALSE), ra$geomin_epsilon == x$eps)
  Vl <- unclass(lavInspect(fr, "vcov")); N <- fr@SampleStats@ntotal
  Dl <- lavTech(fr, "delta")[[1]]; Wl <- as.numeric(fr@SampleStats@WLS.VD[[1]])
  Gl <- fr@SampleStats@NACOV[[1]]; Jl <- fr@Model@ceq.efa.JAC
  a  <- rs_relmax(rs_bordered(Dl, Jl, Wl, Gl)$acov / (N - 1), Vl)
  # own pieces at lavaan's point, mapped to lavaan's free-parameter order
  est <- lavInspect(fr, "est"); Ll <- unname(est$lambda); Pl <- unname(est$psi)
  pt <- parTable(fr); lv <- lavNames(fr, "lv"); ov <- lavNames(fr, "ov")
  thr <- pt$id[pt$op == "|"]                     # thresholds in statistic order
  ix <- sapply(order(pt$free)[pt$free[order(pt$free)] > 0], function(k) {
    o <- pt$op[k]
    if (o == "=~") return(x$nth + (match(pt$lhs[k], lv) - 1) * x$p + match(pt$rhs[k], ov))
    if (o == "|") return(match(pt$id[k], thr))
    if (o == "~~" && pt$lhs[k] != pt$rhs[k])
      return(x$nth + x$p * x$m + rs_phidx(match(pt$lhs[k], lv), match(pt$rhs[k], lv), x$m))
    NA
  })
  stopifnot(!anyNA(ix), !anyDuplicated(ix), length(ix) == ncol(x$Ds))
  own <- rs_bordered(rs_Dstar(Ll, Pl, x$nth), rs_R(Ll, Pl, x$eps, x$nth), Wl, Gl)$acov /
         (N - 1)
  own <- own[ix, ix]; se_o <- sqrt(diag(own)); se_l <- sqrt(diag(Vl))
  b_ok <- all(abs(se_o - se_l) <= 1e-8 + 1e-5 * se_l)
  # diagnostic: own selected and polished point, own SEs
  own2 <- rs_bordered(x$Ds, x$R, x$W, x$Gam)$acov[ix, ix] / (x$N - 1)
  c(lav_pieces = a, own_at_lav_se = max(abs(se_o - se_l) / se_l), b_ok = b_ok,
    own_at_lav_cov = rs_relmax(own, Vl), lav_r = max(abs(rs_r(Ll, Pl, x$eps))),
    diag_dL = max(abs(x$L - Ll)), diag_se = max(abs(sqrt(diag(own2)) - se_l) / se_l))
}
rs2 <- t(sapply(rs_cases, rs2_one))
print(signif(rs2, 3))
stopifnot(rs2[, "lav_pieces"] < 1e-12, rs2[, "b_ok"] == 1)
```

**RS3 (i).** Expected from the condition numbers (the prototype's rule): $100\,u\,\kappa$, about
$10^{-12}$ on E and G and $5\times10^{-10}$ on F, whose unrotated bread has condition number about
$2\times10^4$.

```{r rs-3}
# RS3 (i): the bordered and delta-method covariances are one matrix, given only
# Delta* J = Delta_u and R J = 0. Tolerance 100 u kappa, kappa the largest condition
# number among Z'Delta*'W Delta* Z, the unrotated bread and R G_T: rule fixed before running.
rs3 <- t(sapply(rs_cases, function(x) {
  B  <- rs_bordered(x$Ds, x$R, x$W, x$Gam)
  J  <- rs_J(x$R, x$Gu, x$GT)
  Js <- qr.solve(rbind(x$Ds, x$R), rbind(x$Du, matrix(0, nrow(x$R), ncol(x$Du))),
                 tol = 1e-12)
  kap <- max(rs_cond(crossprod(x$Ds %*% B$Z * sqrt(x$W))),
             rs_cond(crossprod(x$Du * sqrt(x$W))), rs_cond(x$R %*% x$GT))
  c(kappa = kap, tol = 100 * .Machine$double.eps * kap,
    DJ_minus_Du = rs_relmax(x$Ds %*% J, x$Du),
    RJ = max(abs(x$R %*% J)) / (max(abs(x$R)) * max(abs(J))),
    J_closed_vs_stacked = rs_relmax(J, Js),
    bordered_vs_delta = rs_relmax(B$acov, J %*% x$acov_u %*% t(J)))
}))
print(signif(rs3, 3))
stopifnot(rs3[, 3:6] < rs3[, "tol"])
```

**RS3 (ii).** Expected: $\lesssim10^{-13}$ relative ($R G_T$ is well conditioned). The real
re-rotation diagnostic should show the first-order error falling about 100-fold per decade of the
step.

```{r rs-3-rerot}
# RS3 (ii): J is the derivative of the rotation map. Comparator: the complex step of an
# actual re-rotation. The perturbed loadings are a + i h e_c; Newton on r = 0 in
# coordinates of the oblique manifold, with an iteration matrix from forward differences
# of the real map (R is not used). Tolerance 1e-10 relative to max|J|, fixed before running.
rs_rerot_cs <- function(x, h = 1e-20) {
  m <- x$m; T0 <- x$T; nc <- m * (m - 1)
  Bs <- lapply(1:m, function(j) qr.Q(qr(cbind(T0[, j], diag(m))))[, -1, drop = FALSE])
  Tof <- function(cv) {
    X <- T0 + 0 * cv[1]
    for (j in 1:m) X[, j] <- T0[, j] + Bs[[j]] %*% cv[(j - 1) * (m - 1) + seq_len(m - 1)]
    gm_unit(X)
  }
  Ff <- function(cv, A) { T <- Tof(cv); rs_r(A %*% solve(t(T)), crossprod(T), x$eps) }
  K <- sapply(1:nc, function(k) {
    e <- numeric(nc); e[k] <- 1e-7; (Ff(e, x$A) - Ff(numeric(nc), x$A)) / 1e-7
  })
  sapply(which(rs_free(x$p, m)), function(c) {
    A <- x$A + 0i; A[c] <- A[c] + 1i * h; cv <- complex(nc)
    for (it in 1:12) cv <- cv - solve(K, Ff(cv, A))
    T <- Tof(cv); L <- A %*% solve(t(T)); P <- crossprod(T)
    Im(c(as.vector(L), P[lower.tri(P)])) / h
  })
}
for (cs in names(rs_cases)) {
  x <- rs_cases[[cs]]
  rs_cases[[cs]]$J   <- rs_J(x$R, x$Gu, x$GT)
  rs_cases[[cs]]$Jcs <- rs_rerot_cs(x)
}
rs_Jrot <- function(x, J) J[-seq_len(x$nth), -seq_len(x$nth), drop = FALSE]
rs3b <- sapply(rs_cases, function(x) rs_relmax(rs_Jrot(x, x$J), x$Jcs))
print(signif(rs3b, 3))
stopifnot(rs3b < 1e-10)
# Diagnostic: a real re-rotation at t and t/10 along one direction; the first-order
# error should fall about 100-fold (quadratic remainder).
set.seed(20261119)
rs3c <- t(sapply(rs_cases, function(x) {
  e <- rnorm(sum(rs_free(x$p, x$m))); e <- e / sqrt(sum(e^2))
  th0 <- c(as.vector(x$L), x$Phi[lower.tri(x$Phi)])
  err <- sapply(c(1e-3, 1e-4), function(t) {
    A <- x$A; A[rs_free(x$p, x$m)] <- A[rs_free(x$p, x$m)] + t * e
    z <- rs_polish(A, x$T, x$eps)
    max(abs(c(as.vector(z$L), z$Phi[lower.tri(z$Phi)]) - th0 - t * x$Jcs %*% e))
  })
  c(err_1e3 = err[1], err_1e4 = err[2], ratio = err[1] / err[2])
}))
print(signif(rs3c, 3))
```

**The negative control.** A wrong $R$ passes (i) and fails (ii); RS4's complex-step check fails it
too (`R_vs_R` is its distance from the true $R$). The SEs it produces differ from the true ones by
factors up to `se_ratio_max`.

```{r rs-3-wrong}
# Negative control: R replaced by R plus noise of 0.3 max|R| (threshold columns kept 0).
# Expected: the identity of (i) still holds to its tolerance; the re-rotation check of (ii)
# and the complex-step check of RS4 both fail by orders of magnitude.
set.seed(20261118)
rs3w <- t(sapply(rs_cases, function(x) {
  Rw <- x$R; cl <- -seq_len(x$nth)
  Rw[, cl] <- Rw[, cl] + 0.3 * max(abs(x$R)) * rnorm(length(Rw[, cl]))
  Bw <- rs_bordered(x$Ds, Rw, x$W, x$Gam)
  Jw <- rs_J(Rw, x$Gu, x$GT)
  kap <- max(rs_cond(crossprod(x$Ds %*% Bw$Z * sqrt(x$W))),
             rs_cond(crossprod(x$Du * sqrt(x$W))), rs_cond(Rw %*% x$GT))
  se <- sqrt(diag(rs_bordered(x$Ds, x$R, x$W, x$Gam)$acov)); sw <- sqrt(diag(Bw$acov))
  c(identity = rs_relmax(Bw$acov, Jw %*% x$acov_u %*% t(Jw)),
    tol = 100 * .Machine$double.eps * kap,
    rerot = rs_relmax(rs_Jrot(x, Jw), x$Jcs), R_vs_R = rs_relmax(Rw, x$R),
    se_ratio_max = max(sw / se), se_ratio_min = min(sw / se))
}))
print(signif(rs3w, 3))
stopifnot(rs3w[, "identity"] < rs3w[, "tol"], rs3w[, "rerot"] > 1e-3)
```

**RS5.**

```{r rs-5}
# RS5 (invariants of the bordered covariance Bc = rs_bordered(Ds, R, W, Gamma)):
# (a) Bc[tau, tau] = acov_u[tau, tau];  (b) Ds Bc Ds' = Du acov_u Du';
# (c) equivariance under a signed column permutation P: with L2 = L P, Phi2 = P' Phi P,
#     B2 = Pi Bc Pi' (Pi the linear map on theta*), and max|r| at (L2, Phi2) at rounding.
# Expected: all differences at rounding times kappa. Tolerance 100 u kappa (kappa as in rs3,
# at the original point), relative to the largest entry; max|r| < 1e-13: fixed before running.
rs_P <- function(m) {
  o <- if (m == 2) c(2, 1) else c(2, 3, 1); s <- if (m == 2) c(-1, 1) else c(-1, 1, -1)
  P <- matrix(0, m, m); P[cbind(o, seq_len(m))] <- s; P
}
rs_Pi <- function(P, p, m, nth) {               # linear map on theta* (off-diagonal phi only)
  n <- nth + p * m + m * (m - 1) / 2
  sapply(seq_len(n), function(k) {
    e <- numeric(n); e[k] <- 1
    P0 <- matrix(0, m, m); P0[lower.tri(P0)] <- e[nth + p * m + seq_len(m * (m - 1) / 2)]
    P0 <- P0 + t(P0)
    Lm <- matrix(e[nth + seq_len(p * m)], p, m)
    c(e[seq_len(nth)], as.vector(Lm %*% P), (t(P) %*% P0 %*% P)[lower.tri(P0)])
  })
}
rs5 <- t(sapply(rs_cases, function(x) {
  B  <- rs_bordered(x$Ds, x$R, x$W, x$Gam); Bc <- B$acov; tt <- seq_len(x$nth)
  kap <- max(rs_cond(crossprod(x$Ds %*% B$Z * sqrt(x$W))),
             rs_cond(crossprod(x$Du * sqrt(x$W))), rs_cond(x$R %*% x$GT))
  P <- rs_P(x$m); L2 <- x$L %*% P; Phi2 <- t(P) %*% x$Phi %*% P
  Ds2 <- rs_Dstar(L2, Phi2, x$nth); R2 <- rs_R(L2, Phi2, x$eps, x$nth)
  B2 <- rs_bordered(Ds2, R2, x$W, x$Gam)$acov
  Pi <- rs_Pi(P, x$p, x$m, x$nth)
  c(kappa = kap, tol = 100 * .Machine$double.eps * kap,
    a_tau_block = rs_relmax(Bc[tt, tt], x$acov_u[tt, tt]),
    b_DsBDs = rs_relmax(x$Ds %*% Bc %*% t(x$Ds), x$Du %*% x$acov_u %*% t(x$Du)),
    c_perm = rs_relmax(B2, Pi %*% Bc %*% t(Pi)),
    c_sigma = rs_relmax(Ds2 %*% Pi, x$Ds),
    c_maxr = max(abs(rs_r(L2, Phi2, x$eps))))
}))
print(signif(rs5, 3))
stopifnot(rs5[, 3:6] < rs5[, "tol"], rs5[, "c_maxr"] < 1e-13)
```

**RS6 (i).** $m=1$; then the theorem's equivalence on E, F, G and two constructed loading matrices
(population level, $W=I$, no thresholds). S1: the second factor has two indicators, so the
unrotated bread is singular by one with $G$ nonsingular; predicted: the bordered system singular.
S2: $a_{11}=0$, so the echelon chart is degenerate ($G$ singular); the theorem predicts nothing about
$\Delta_u$ there, and the rotated system turns out regular. Last, $RG_T$ against the Riemannian
Hessian of the criterion, by the complex step.

```{r rs-6}
# RS6(i): nonsingularity. With A of full column rank:
#   Z'Ds'W Ds Z nonsingular  <=>  rank(Ds) = n_u  AND  R G_T nonsingular;
#   and G = [G_u, G_T] nonsingular  =>  rank(Ds) = rank(Du).
# "Nonsingular" is numerical rank (singular value > 1e-8 max, spec 4.8's criterion), applied
# to Ds Z sqrt(W) (the square root of Z'Ds'W Ds Z, so the squared ratio is not what is cut).
# Tolerances are exact rank equalities; fixed before running.
# (a) m = 1 on Case E: no constraints, bordered = delta method with the sign map, 1e-12.
x1 <- rs_prep("E", m = 1, eps = 1e-4)
s1 <- x1$T[1, 1]; Pi1 <- diag(c(rep(1, x1$nth), rep(s1, x1$p)))
rs6a <- c(rows_R = nrow(x1$R), sign = s1,
          bordered_vs_Pi_acov_u = rs_relmax(rs_bordered(x1$Ds, x1$R, x1$W, x1$Gam)$acov,
                                            Pi1 %*% x1$acov_u %*% t(Pi1)))
print(signif(rs6a, 3))
stopifnot(rs6a["rows_R"] == 0, rs6a["bordered_vs_Pi_acov_u"] < 1e-12)

# (b) the three cases and two constructed ones (population, W = 1, nth = 0).
rs_mkcase <- function(A, eps, nth = 0) {
  p <- nrow(A); m <- ncol(A)
  g <- gm_geomin(A, eps = eps, nstart = 30)
  pz <- tryCatch(rs_polish(A, g$T, eps), error = function(e) NULL)
  T0 <- if (is.null(pz)) g$T else pz$T
  L0 <- A %*% solve(t(T0)); cn <- rs_canon(L0, crossprod(T0), T0)
  Minv <- solve(t(cn$T)); L <- A %*% Minv; Phi <- crossprod(cn$T)
  Ds <- rs_Dstar(L, Phi, nth)
  list(A = A, p = p, m = m, nth = nth, eps = eps, T = cn$T, L = L, Phi = Phi,
       Ds = Ds, Du = rs_Du(A, nth), R = rs_R(L, Phi, eps, nth), W = rep(1, nrow(Ds)),
       Gu = rs_Gu(L, Minv, nth), GT = rs_GT(L, Phi, nth),
       polished = !is.null(pz), maxr = max(abs(rs_r(L, Phi, eps))))
}
rs_S1 <- rs_mkcase(cbind(c(.7, .6, .7, .6, .5, .6), c(0, 0, 0, 0, .6, .5)), 1e-4)
rs_S2 <- rs_mkcase(cbind(c(0, .6, .7, .6, .5, .6), c(0, .5, .4, 0, .3, .5)), 1e-4)
rs6_info <- function(x) {
  nst <- ncol(x$Ds); nu <- ncol(x$Du); nr <- nrow(x$R); mm <- x$m * (x$m - 1)
  Z <- rs_nullbasis(x$R, nst); DZ <- x$Ds %*% Z * sqrt(x$W)
  Bm <- crossprod(DZ); RG <- x$R %*% x$GT; G <- cbind(x$Gu, x$GT)
  KKT <- rbind(cbind(crossprod(x$Ds * sqrt(x$W)), t(x$R)), cbind(x$R, matrix(0, nr, nr)))
  sr <- function(X) { d <- svd(X)$d; min(d) / max(d) }
  c(n_star = nst, n_u = nu, rank_Du = rs_nrank(x$Du), rank_Ds = rs_nrank(x$Ds),
    rank_R = rs_nrank(x$R), m_m1 = mm, rank_RGT = rs_nrank(RG),
    rank_G = rs_nrank(G), rank_DsZ = rs_nrank(DZ), rank_Bm = rs_nrank(Bm),
    rank_KKT = rs_nrank(KKT), KKT_dim = nrow(KKT),
    sv_Du = sr(x$Du), sv_Ds = sr(x$Ds), sv_RGT = sr(RG), sv_G = sr(G), sv_DsZ = sr(DZ),
    sv_KKT = sr(KKT), maxr = max(abs(rs_r(x$L, x$Phi, x$eps))))
}
rs6b_cases <- c(rs_cases, list(S1 = rs_S1, S2 = rs_S2))
rs6b <- t(sapply(rs6b_cases, rs6_info))
print(signif(rs6b, 3))
rs6b_chk <- t(apply(rs6b, 1, function(v) {
  v <- unname(v) |> setNames(colnames(rs6b)); lhs <- unname(v["rank_DsZ"] == v["n_u"])
  rhs <- unname(v["rank_Ds"] == v["n_u"] && v["rank_RGT"] == v["m_m1"])
  Gnon <- unname(v["rank_G"] == v["n_star"])
  c(lhs = lhs, rhs = rhs, equiv = lhs == rhs, G_nonsing = Gnon,
    G_implies_rank = unname(!Gnon || v["rank_Ds"] == v["rank_Du"]))
}))
print(rs6b_chk)
stopifnot(rs6b_chk[, "equiv"] == 1, rs6b_chk[, "G_implies_rank"] == 1,
          rs6b_chk[c("E", "F", "G"), "lhs"] == 1,
          rs6b["S1", "rank_Bm"] < rs6b["S1", "n_u"], rs6b_chk["S1", "G_nonsing"] == 1)

# (c) R G_T[, q] = vecoff(-(dGp_q)' T): the Riemannian Hessian seen through T'.
# Complex step along xi_q = T'^-1 Y_q. Stationary point: x$T of each case. 1e-10 relative to
# max|R G_T|, fixed before running.
rs6c <- sapply(c(rs_cases, list(S1 = rs_S1)), function(x) {
  off <- rs_off(x$m); T <- x$T; h <- 1e-30
  RG <- x$R %*% x$GT
  H <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(off)), function(q) {
    Y <- matrix(0, x$m, x$m); Y[off[q, 1], off[q, 2]] <- 1
    Tz <- T + 1i * h * solve(t(T), Y)
    dGp <- Im(gm_proj(Tz, gm_G(x$A, Tz, x$eps))) / h
    (-t(dGp) %*% T)[off]
  })
  rs_relmax(RG, H)
})
print(signif(rs6c, 3))
stopifnot(rs6c < 1e-10)
```

**RS6 (ii) and (iii): an illustration, not a criterion.** For each rotated loading of Case E,
$\hat\theta_u$ is moved by the direction that moves that loading by one SE to first order, in both
senses, and the solution re-rotated. `ratio_plus`, `ratio_minus` are the actual moves in units of
the SE (1 if $\rho$ were linear); `se_plus`, `se_minus` the SE recomputed there over the SE at the
estimate. Expected before running: at $\varepsilon=10^{-4}$ departures of order one for loadings
within a few $\sqrt\varepsilon$ of zero with SE comparable to $\sqrt\varepsilon$, and small ones at
$\varepsilon=10^{-2}$. Nothing is asserted, and no value here is a threshold.

```{r rs-6-ill}
# Illustration only (no assertions): how far the first-order SE is from the true local
# behaviour of the re-rotated loading. delta moves each rotated loading by one SE to first
# order (delta = Vu g' / SE, g = row of J, Vu = ACOV_u / (N - 1) of the free loadings).
rs_ill <- function(x) {
  p <- x$p; m <- x$m; nth <- x$nth; fr <- which(rs_free(p, m)); a <- nth + seq_along(fr)
  Vu <- x$acov_u[a, a] / (x$N - 1); J <- rs_J(x$R, x$Gu, x$GT)
  se_at <- function(z, c, g0 = NULL) {
    J2 <- rs_J(rs_R(z$L, z$Phi, x$eps, nth), rs_Gu(z$L, z$Minv, nth), rs_GT(z$L, z$Phi, nth))
    g <- J2[nth + c, a]; sqrt(drop(g %*% Vu %*% g))
  }
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(p * m), function(c) {
    g <- J[nth + c, a]; se <- sqrt(drop(g %*% Vu %*% g)); d <- drop(Vu %*% g) / se
    mv <- function(sg) { A2 <- x$A; A2[fr] <- A2[fr] + sg * d; rs_polish(A2, x$T, x$eps) }
    zp <- mv(1); zm <- mv(-1)
    data.frame(row = (c - 1) %% p + 1, fac = (c - 1) %/% p + 1,
               lam_sqeps = x$L[c] / sqrt(x$eps), se_sqeps = se / sqrt(x$eps),
               ratio_plus = (zp$L[c] - x$L[c]) / se, ratio_minus = (x$L[c] - zm$L[c]) / se,
               se_plus = se_at(zp, c) / se, se_minus = se_at(zm, c) / se,
               res = max(zp$res, zm$res))
  }))
}
for (e in c(1e-4, 1e-2)) {
  xi <- if (e == rs_cases$E$eps) rs_cases$E else rs_prep("E", eps = e)
  cat("\nCase E, eps =", e, "\n"); print(signif(rs_ill(xi), 3))
}
```

**RS7.** The chain-rule $\Delta^*$ against the analytic one; route 3 against the bordered form built
on the chain-rule $\Delta^*$; and, as a diagnostic, the SEs at the GPA stall point (which is what
production would rotate to) against the Newton-polished point.

```{r rs-7}
# RS7: routes to Delta*. (1) analytic Ds; (2) chain rule Ds = [Du, 0] G^-1, G = [Gu, GT];
# (3) J (no Delta, W or Gamma) vs the bordered covariance with the chain-rule Ds.
# Tolerances: (2) 100 u cond(G), relative; (3) 100 u kappa as in rs3 (cond(G) not included):
# fixed before running. Diagnostic (no assertion): SEs by route 3 at the unpolished GPA stall
# point (production's estimate) against the polished point.
rs7 <- t(sapply(rs_cases, function(x) {
  G <- cbind(x$Gu, x$GT); Dch <- cbind(x$Du, matrix(0, nrow(x$Du), ncol(x$GT))) %*% solve(G)
  B <- rs_bordered(x$Ds, x$R, x$W, x$Gam)
  kap <- max(rs_cond(crossprod(x$Ds %*% B$Z * sqrt(x$W))),
             rs_cond(crossprod(x$Du * sqrt(x$W))), rs_cond(x$R %*% x$GT))
  J <- rs_J(x$R, x$Gu, x$GT)
  Bch <- rs_bordered(Dch, x$R, x$W, x$Gam)$acov
  # diagnostic: stall point
  Ts <- x$g$T; cn <- rs_canon(x$A %*% solve(t(Ts)), crossprod(Ts), Ts)
  Mi <- solve(t(cn$T)); Ls <- x$A %*% Mi; Ps <- crossprod(cn$T)
  Js <- rs_J(rs_R(Ls, Ps, x$eps, x$nth), rs_Gu(Ls, Mi, x$nth), rs_GT(Ls, Ps, x$nth))
  se1 <- sqrt(diag(J %*% x$acov_u %*% t(J)) / (x$N - 1))
  se2 <- sqrt(diag(Js %*% x$acov_u %*% t(Js)) / (x$N - 1))
  c(condG = rs_cond(G), tol2 = 100 * .Machine$double.eps * rs_cond(G),
    chain_vs_Ds = rs_relmax(Dch, x$Ds),
    kappa = kap, tol3 = 100 * .Machine$double.eps * kap,
    J_vs_chainbordered = rs_relmax(J %*% x$acov_u %*% t(J), Bch),
    diag_stall_L = max(abs(Ls - x$L)), diag_stall_se_maxrel = max(abs(se2 - se1) / se1))
}))
print(signif(rs7, 3))
stopifnot(rs7[, "chain_vs_Ds"] < rs7[, "tol2"], rs7[, "J_vs_chainbordered"] < rs7[, "tol3"])
```

Measured 2026-11-17 (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2): see the printed output above; in brief, RS1's identity
$\le4\times10^{-15}$, $\lvert r\rvert$ after Newton $\le7\times10^{-15}$; RS4 $\le3.2\times10^{-16}$;
RS2 (a) $\le8.2\times10^{-15}$, (b) SEs within $1.2\times10^{-10}$ relative; RS3 (i) within its
tolerance on all three cases (F $8.1\times10^{-12}$ against $5.1\times10^{-10}$), (ii)
$\le5.5\times10^{-15}$, the wrong-$R$ control passing (i) and failing (ii) by 0.87 to 3.7; RS5
$\le6.7\times10^{-12}$; RS6 (i) as predicted on all five matrices; RS7 chain rule
$\le5.3\times10^{-15}$; SEs at the stall point within $1.1\times10^{-7}$ relative of the polished
point. In `rs-6-ill` at $\varepsilon=10^{-4}$ the near-zero loadings move by 0.64 to 2.19 SEs and
their SEs by factors 0.27 to 3.8, and the large loadings' SEs by up to 17%; at $\varepsilon=10^{-2}$

## Second-order factors: moments, identification, metrics, recovery, standardization, admissibility {#sec-second-order}

*Added 2026-11-19, roadmap unit B2 (E-108 §5.1, items SO1 to SO6), derivation first.*
Nothing in `src/` or `tests/` depends on this section. It derives, for a model with one or two
higher-order factors $G$ over first-order factors $F_1,\dots,F_K$ of ordinal items: that $\sigma(\theta)$
and $\Delta$ need no new term (SO1); local identification, the rank check's two points and what it
reports, and the relation to the correlated-first-order model, kept apart from each other (SO2); the
maps between four metrics and where each breaks down (SO3); the unit-variance to marker transform for a
latent anchor (SO4); standardization for a factor without indicators (SO5); sign and admissibility,
including what a numerical error in a $\hat\psi$ consists of (SO6). It decides nothing. The spelling of
the latent marker, the metric offered, whether recovery is eligible, the anchor of $G$'s sign, the
boundary policy of the disturbance-variance check and the release scope are unit B3's; the questions
that bear on them are collected in the last subsection. New chunk names start with `so-` and every new R
name with `so_`; the only thing taken from the rest of the file is the `setup` chunk, and lavaan is
called only as a comparison target (`so-lavaan-setup` onward). Production facts are cited as file:line,
read 2026-11-19 at commit `97f296f`; "production coordinates" means the parameter order, the starts and the
second point of the Module 3 source, evaluated here in R (the run in Stata is B5's first step, since
Module 3 rejects these models until then). Effort level, decided before the work (a project rule,
proportionate effort): the standard checks (closed forms, complex-step and central differences, lavaan
0.7-2 as tier 2); the boundary behaviour as $\psi_k\to0$ or a path $\to0$ is described by rates, not
certified, since nothing here is a numerical component whose error reaches an SE or a test statistic.
Drafted by a read-only agent; reviewed, corrected and run by the main session.

### Setting, notation, the four metrics {#sec-so-setting}

One group, ordinal items, delta parameterization, $\sigma(\theta)=(\tau,\ \operatorname{vech}_{\rm off}
(\Lambda\Phi\Lambda^\top))$ with $\Phi=(I-B)^{-1}\Psi(I-B)^{-\top}$ and $\Theta$ derived (@sec-delta). A
second-order model has $G$ (or $G_1,G_2$) exogenous and the $F_k$ endogenous: $B$ has the entries
$\beta_{F_kG}=:b_k$ and nothing else, so $B^2=0$ and $(I-B)^{-1}=I+B$; $\Psi$ is diagonal (plus
$\psi_{G_2G_1}$ with two $G$'s). **$\psi_{kk}$ is the disturbance variance of $F_k$, never its total
variance** $\phi_{kk}=b_k^2\psi_G+\psi_{kk}$ (a project rule; spec §4.8). The production factor order is
`e(lxvars)` then `e(lyvars)` (`dwlsmv_translate.mata:79`), so $G$ comes first and $F_1,\dots,F_K$ follow;
$\theta$ is ordered thresholds, then $\lambda$ by (item, factor), $\beta$ by (to, from), $\psi$ lower
triangle by (row, col) (`dwls_identify.mata:243-385`), and `fidx`, hence the second point's index $k$,
counts the thresholds (`dwlsmv_id_rank.mata:90-96`). Starts are $\lambda=0.7$, $\beta=0$, $\psi_{gg}=1$,
$\psi_{gh}=0$ (`dwlsmv_id_parse.mata:298,314,326`); a *fixed* row keeps its fixed value at the start.

The four metrics, a scale for each $F_k$ crossed with a scale for $G$ (the names are used throughout):

| | $F_k$ by an item marker ($\lambda_{m(k)k}=1$, $\psi_k$ free) | $F_k$ by its disturbance ($\psi_k=1$, loadings free) |
|---|---|---|
| **$G$ by a latent marker** ($b_1=1$, $\psi_G$ free) | **M**, `sem`'s default | **W** |
| **$G$ by its variance** ($\psi_G=1$, paths free) | **V**, `sem`'s `var(G@1)`; already has a canonical spelling (`metric marker F_k y`, `metric unitvariance G`; B1 finding 1.1, D2c) | **U**, lavaan `std.lv`, dwlsmv `unitvariance` |

$b_1$ is on the *first* child; $a_k$ is the marker item's loading in a metric where it is free, and
$c=a_1b_1$ (SO3). With an item loading on $G$ (B0's MD) "marker" for $G$ means that item's loading fixed
at 1 (what `sem` does, B1 probe P10) and no path is fixed. Models are named as in B0: M2, M3, M4, M5 ($G$
over 2 to 5 factors of three items), M2c (both second-order loadings fixed at 1), MT2 and MT1 (the last
factor with two items, one item), MD, M22 and M33 (two correlated $G$'s over $2+2$ and $3+3$), M22u (the
same with $\psi_{G_2G_1}=0$). The builder `so_build()` writes the parameter table of each in each metric;
`so_rankcheck()` is Module 3's check (`dwlsmv_id_rank.mata`, `dwlsmv_numrank.mata`) with the structural
block of $\Delta$ taken as production takes it, a central difference at $h=10^{-5}\max(1,|v|)$
(`dwlsmv_delta_cols.mata:122`), padded with the identity of the threshold block.

Every verification below ends in `so_check()`, which counts; the last chunk prints `so-verify: N of N` and
stops if any failed. Tolerances: algebraic identities $10^{-10}$ relative (most hold to $10^{-15}$);
closed-form $\Delta$ against production's central difference $10^{-8}$, two decades above the $10^{-10}$
rounding floor that @sec-delta records for the same $h$; every other tolerance is stated where it is used,
and the ones chosen after seeing a measurement say so.

```{r so-core}
so_checks <- new.env(); so_checks$n <- 0; so_checks$ok <- 0; so_checks$bad <- character()
so_check <- function(label, so_cond) {
  so_cond <- isTRUE(all(so_cond)) && length(so_cond) > 0
  so_checks$n <- so_checks$n + 1
  if (so_cond) so_checks$ok <- so_checks$ok + 1 else so_checks$bad <- c(so_checks$bad, label)
  invisible(so_cond)
}
so_rel <- function(so_a, so_b) max(abs(so_a - so_b)) / max(abs(so_b), 1e-300)   # relative to the largest reference entry

# (I - B)^-1 for a nilpotent (recursive) B, as a finite sum: exact, and valid for complex entries
so_A <- function(B) {
  m <- nrow(B); A <- diag(m) + 0 * B; Bk <- diag(m) + 0 * B
  for (k in seq_len(m - 1)) { Bk <- Bk %*% B; A <- A + Bk }
  stopifnot(max(Mod(Bk %*% B)) == 0)
  A
}
so_Phi   <- function(B, Psi) { A <- so_A(B); A %*% Psi %*% t(A) }          # t(), never conjugate
so_Sig   <- function(L, B, Psi) { so_Ph <- so_Phi(B, Psi); L %*% so_Ph %*% t(L) }
so_sigma <- function(L, B, Psi) { S <- so_Sig(L, B, Psi); S[lower.tri(S)] } # correlation block of sigma (delta)

# A model = production's parameter table for one group: NA = no row (fixed 0), *f = free flag.
# Theta order is dwls_identify()'s: thresholds, then lambda by (item, factor), beta by (to, from),
# psi lower triangle by (row, col); fidx counts thresholds. Factor order is Module 11's:
# e(lxvars) then e(lyvars), so G's come first.
so_model <- function(Lv, Lf, Bv, Bf, Pv, so_Pf, nthr = 2, label = "") {
  rowmajor <- function(so_V, F, lower = FALSE, ty) {
    so_d <- NULL
    for (so_r in seq_len(nrow(so_V))) for (c in seq_len(ncol(so_V))) {
      if (lower && c > so_r) next
      if (!is.na(so_V[so_r, c])) so_d <- rbind(so_d, data.frame(type = ty, r = so_r, c = c, free = F[so_r, c], val = so_V[so_r, c]))
    }
    so_d
  }
  tab <- rbind(rowmajor(Lv, Lf, FALSE, "l"), rowmajor(Bv, Bf, FALSE, "b"), rowmajor(Pv, so_Pf, TRUE, "p"))
  fr <- tab[tab$free, ]
  L0 <- Lv; L0[is.na(L0)] <- 0; B0 <- Bv; B0[is.na(B0)] <- 0
  P0 <- Pv; P0[is.na(P0)] <- 0; P0[upper.tri(P0)] <- t(P0)[upper.tri(P0)]
  list(label = label, p = nrow(Lv), m = ncol(Lv), nthr = nthr, tab = tab, fr = fr, npar_s = nrow(fr),
       T = nthr * nrow(Lv), L0 = L0, B0 = B0, P0 = P0, start = fr$val)
}
so_mats <- function(so_md, so_th) {
  so_z <- so_th[1] * 0; L <- so_md$L0 + so_z; B <- so_md$B0 + so_z; P <- so_md$P0 + so_z; fr <- so_md$fr
  for (so_j in seq_len(nrow(fr))) {
    so_r <- fr$r[so_j]; c <- fr$c[so_j]
    if (fr$type[so_j] == "l") L[so_r, c] <- so_th[so_j]
    else if (fr$type[so_j] == "b") B[so_r, c] <- so_th[so_j]
    else { P[so_r, c] <- so_th[so_j]; P[c, so_r] <- so_th[so_j] }
  }
  list(L = L, B = B, P = P)
}
so_msigma <- function(so_md, so_th) { so_x <- so_mats(so_md, so_th); so_sigma(so_x$L, so_x$B, so_x$P) }

# production's Delta, structural block: central difference, h = 1e-5 max(1, |v|) (dwlsmv_delta_cols)
so_delta_fd <- function(so_md, so_th) {
  so_D <- matrix(0, length(so_msigma(so_md, so_th)), length(so_th))
  for (so_j in seq_along(so_th)) {
    so_h <- 1e-5 * max(1, abs(so_th[so_j])); tp <- so_th; tm <- so_th; tp[so_j] <- so_th[so_j] + so_h; tm[so_j] <- so_th[so_j] - so_h
    so_D[, so_j] <- (so_msigma(so_md, tp) - so_msigma(so_md, tm)) / (2 * so_h)
  }
  so_D
}
# closed form of @sec-delta's table
so_delta_cf <- function(so_md, so_th) {
  so_x <- so_mats(so_md, so_th); A <- so_A(so_x$B); so_Ph <- A %*% so_x$P %*% t(A)
  Lm <- so_x$L %*% A; Gm <- so_x$L %*% so_Ph; lt <- lower.tri(diag(so_md$p)); fr <- so_md$fr
  so_D <- matrix(0, sum(lt), nrow(fr))
  for (so_j in seq_len(nrow(fr))) {
    so_r <- fr$r[so_j]; c <- fr$c[so_j]; dS <- matrix(0, so_md$p, so_md$p)
    if (fr$type[so_j] == "l") { e <- rep(0, so_md$p); e[so_r] <- 1; dS <- e %o% Gm[, c] + Gm[, c] %o% e }
    else if (fr$type[so_j] == "b") dS <- Lm[, so_r] %o% Gm[, c] + Gm[, c] %o% Lm[, so_r]
    else if (so_r != c) dS <- Lm[, so_r] %o% Lm[, c] + Lm[, c] %o% Lm[, so_r]
    else dS <- Lm[, so_r] %o% Lm[, so_r]
    so_D[, so_j] <- dS[lt]
  }
  so_D
}
so_delta_cs <- function(so_md, so_th, so_h = 1e-20) {
  so_D <- matrix(0, length(so_msigma(so_md, so_th)), length(so_th))
  for (so_j in seq_along(so_th)) { tz <- as.complex(so_th); tz[so_j] <- tz[so_j] + 1i * so_h; so_D[, so_j] <- Im(so_msigma(so_md, tz)) / so_h }
  so_D
}

# the rank check of dwls_identify(): theta0 (starts), then theta2 (dwlsmv_id_rank) if theta0 is deficient
so_phi <- (sqrt(5) - 1) / 2
so_numrank <- function(Ds, T) {                       # Delta = blockdiag(I_T, Ds): singular values of both
  so_sv <- sort(c(svd(Ds)$d, rep(1, T)), decreasing = TRUE)
  list(rank = sum(so_sv > 1e-8 * so_sv[1]), n = length(so_sv), ratio = so_sv[length(so_sv)] / so_sv[1], sv = so_sv)
}
so_rankcheck <- function(so_md, delta = so_delta_fd) {
  so_th0 <- so_md$start; k <- so_md$T + seq_along(so_th0)
  th2 <- so_th0 + 0.1 * (((k * so_phi) %% 1) - 0.5)
  so_r0 <- so_numrank(delta(so_md, so_th0), so_md$T); r2 <- so_numrank(delta(so_md, th2), so_md$T)
  s <- svd(delta(so_md, so_th0)); nv <- s$v[, ncol(s$v)]
  list(npar = so_md$npar_s + so_md$T, rank0 = so_r0$rank, ratio0 = so_r0$ratio, rank2 = r2$rank, ratio2 = r2$ratio,
       th0 = so_th0, th2 = th2, pass0 = so_r0$rank == so_r0$n, pass2 = r2$rank == r2$n, nullv = nv)
}

# the builder. nk: items per first-order factor. gm: G by "marker" (b of the first child fixed 1; with md,
# the item on G fixed 1) or "var" (psi_G = 1). fm: each F_k by "item" (first item fixed 1, psi_k free) or
# "dist" (psi_k = 1 fixed, loadings free). M = (marker, item), U = (var, dist), V = (var, item), W = (marker, dist).
so_build <- function(nk = c(3, 3, 3), gm = "marker", fm = "item", so_ng = 1, gsplit = length(nk),
                     gcov = TRUE, fixb = integer(), mdi = FALSE, nthr = 2, glast = FALSE, label = "") {
  so_K <- length(nk); p <- sum(nk) + mdi; m <- so_ng + so_K; i0 <- cumsum(c(0, nk))
  Lv <- matrix(NA_real_, p, m); Lf <- matrix(FALSE, p, m)
  Bv <- matrix(NA_real_, m, m); Bf <- matrix(FALSE, m, m)
  Pv <- matrix(NA_real_, m, m); so_Pf <- matrix(FALSE, m, m)
  for (k in seq_len(so_K)) for (so_i in seq_len(nk[k])) {
    so_r <- i0[k] + so_i; Lv[so_r, so_ng + k] <- if (fm == "item" && so_i == 1) 1 else 0.7; Lf[so_r, so_ng + k] <- !(fm == "item" && so_i == 1)
  }
  kids <- split(seq_len(so_K), rep(seq_len(so_ng), gsplit))
  for (so_g in seq_len(so_ng)) for (k in kids[[so_g]]) {
    Bv[so_ng + k, so_g] <- 0; Bf[so_ng + k, so_g] <- TRUE
    if (gm == "marker" && !mdi && k == kids[[so_g]][1]) { Bv[so_ng + k, so_g] <- 1; Bf[so_ng + k, so_g] <- FALSE }
    if (k %in% fixb) { Bv[so_ng + k, so_g] <- 1; Bf[so_ng + k, so_g] <- FALSE }
  }
  if (mdi) { Lv[p, 1] <- if (gm == "marker") 1 else 0.7; Lf[p, 1] <- gm != "marker" }
  for (so_g in seq_len(so_ng)) { Pv[so_g, so_g] <- 1; so_Pf[so_g, so_g] <- gm != "var" }
  for (k in seq_len(so_K)) { Pv[so_ng + k, so_ng + k] <- 1; so_Pf[so_ng + k, so_ng + k] <- fm != "dist" }
  if (so_ng == 2 && gcov) { Pv[2, 1] <- 0; so_Pf[2, 1] <- TRUE }
  if (glast) {                                   # alternative factor order: the F's first, then the G's
    o <- c(so_ng + seq_len(so_K), seq_len(so_ng))
    Lv <- Lv[, o]; Lf <- Lf[, o]; Bv <- Bv[o, o]; Bf <- Bf[o, o]; Pv <- Pv[o, o]; so_Pf <- so_Pf[o, o]
  }
  so_md <- so_model(Lv, Lf, Bv, Bf, Pv, so_Pf, nthr, label)
  so_md$facn <- c(paste0("G", seq_len(so_ng)), paste0("F", seq_len(so_K))); if (glast) so_md$facn <- so_md$facn[o]
  so_md$itemn <- paste0("y", seq_len(p)); so_md$K <- so_K; so_md$ng <- so_ng; so_md$nk <- nk; so_md$gm <- gm; so_md$fm <- fm; so_md$mdi <- mdi
  so_md
}
```

The second group of helpers rescales latent variables, standardizes, and reads off the metric's fixed rows
(used from SO3 on).

```{r so-maps}
# rescale every latent variable by d (Result 1 of @sec-marker-recovery, any invertible diagonal D)
so_rescale <- function(so_x, so_d) {
  Di <- diag(1 / so_d, length(so_d)); Dd <- diag(so_d, length(so_d))
  list(L = so_x$L %*% Di, B = Dd %*% so_x$B %*% Di, P = Dd %*% so_x$P %*% Dd)
}
# the d that takes x into the metric of md, read off md's fixed rows: a fixed loading fixes d_f by lambda/d_f = v,
# a fixed psi_ff by d_f^2 psi_ff = v, a fixed beta (the latent marker) by (b d_child)/d_f = v AFTER the children are
# rescaled -- the order the roadmap asks about. Positive root for the psi rule.
so_d_for <- function(so_x, so_md) {
  m <- so_md$m; so_d <- rep(NA_real_, m); done <- rep(FALSE, m); tb <- so_md$tab
  for (so_f in seq_len(m)) {
    l <- tb[tb$type == "l" & tb$c == so_f & !tb$free & tb$val != 0, ]
    p <- tb[tb$type == "p" & tb$r == so_f & tb$c == so_f & !tb$free, ]
    if (nrow(l) >= 1) { so_d[so_f] <- so_x$L[l$r[1], so_f] / l$val[1]; done[so_f] <- TRUE }
    else if (nrow(p) == 1) { so_d[so_f] <- sqrt(p$val / so_x$P[so_f, so_f]); done[so_f] <- TRUE }
  }
  for (so_f in which(!done)) {
    so_b <- tb[tb$type == "b" & tb$c == so_f & !tb$free & tb$val != 0, ]
    stopifnot(nrow(so_b) == 1)             # a NaN child (psi <= 0 under a disturbance rule) propagates: not representable
    so_d[so_f] <- so_x$B[so_b$r, so_f] * so_d[so_b$r] / so_b$val
  }
  so_d
}
so_to_metric <- function(so_x, so_md) so_rescale(so_x, so_d_for(so_x, so_md))
so_theta_of <- function(so_md, so_x) {
  fr <- so_md$fr; so_th <- numeric(nrow(fr))
  for (so_j in seq_len(nrow(fr))) so_th[so_j] <- switch(fr$type[so_j], l = so_x$L[fr$r[so_j], fr$c[so_j]], b = so_x$B[fr$r[so_j], fr$c[so_j]], p = so_x$P[fr$r[so_j], fr$c[so_j]])
  so_th
}
# fixed rows of md must hold at the rescaled point
so_fixed_ok <- function(so_x, so_md, tol = 1e-10) {
  tb <- so_md$tab[!so_md$tab$free, ]; ok <- TRUE
  for (so_j in seq_len(nrow(tb))) {
    so_v <- switch(tb$type[so_j], l = so_x$L[tb$r[so_j], tb$c[so_j]], b = so_x$B[tb$r[so_j], tb$c[so_j]], p = so_x$P[tb$r[so_j], tb$c[so_j]])
    ok <- ok && abs(so_v - tb$val[so_j]) <= tol * max(1, abs(tb$val[so_j]))
  }
  ok
}
# a point in standardized form (unit total variance for every F_k): b*_k, item loadings lam*
so_std_point <- function(md0, bstar, lamstar = 0.7) {
  m <- md0$m; so_K <- length(bstar); so_ng <- m - so_K
  L <- md0$L0; L[L != 0] <- lamstar; B <- matrix(0, m, m); P <- diag(m)
  B[cbind(so_ng + seq_len(so_K), 1)] <- bstar; P[cbind(so_ng + seq_len(so_K), so_ng + seq_len(so_K))] <- 1 - bstar^2
  list(L = L, B = B, P = P)
}
# standardized solution (std.all under delta): lambda s_f, beta s_f / s_t, psi / (s s), Theta = 1 - diag(L Phi L')
so_std_mats <- function(so_x) {
  so_Ph <- so_Phi(so_x$B, so_x$P); s <- sqrt(diag(so_Ph)); Ds <- diag(s, length(s)); Di <- diag(1 / s, length(s))
  list(L = so_x$L %*% Ds, B = Di %*% so_x$B %*% Ds, P = Di %*% so_x$P %*% Di, Th = 1 - diag(so_x$L %*% so_Ph %*% t(so_x$L)), s = s, Phi = so_Ph)
}
```

### Result SO1: moments and $\Delta$ need no new term {#sec-so-moments}

**SO1.1.** $\sigma(\theta)$ is the existing function of $(\Lambda,B,\Psi)$ with the first-order factors
endogenous; nothing in @sec-theta-delta or @sec-delta assumed that an endogenous factor has no
descendants *in the data* or that a factor has items.

**SO1.2 (the direct form).** With $\gamma=(b_k)$ the vector of second-order loadings, for one $G$
$$\Phi_{GG}=\psi_G,\qquad \Phi_{FG}=\psi_G\gamma,\qquad
\Phi_{FF}=\psi_G\gamma\gamma^\top+\Psi_F,$$
and with two $G$'s $\Phi_{FF}=\Gamma\Psi_{GG}\Gamma^\top+\Psi_F$ ($\Gamma$ the $K\times2$ matrix of paths).
*Proof.* $B^2=0$ gives $(I-B)^{-1}=I+B$, and $\Phi=(I+B)\Psi(I+B)^\top$ has these blocks. $\square$

**SO1.3 ($\Delta$).** The table of @sec-delta applies to every column unchanged. Its derivation used
only $A=(I-B)^{-1}$, $L=\Lambda A$ and $G=\Lambda\Phi$ and the quadratic lemma. For a path $\beta_{F_kG}$
($g=F_k$, $h=G$) the column is $L_{jg}G_{kh}+G_{jh}L_{kg}$ with $L_{\cdot g}=\Lambda_{\cdot F_k}$ and
$G_{\cdot h}=\psi_G(\Lambda_{\cdot G}+\sum_k b_k\Lambda_{\cdot F_k})$; for $\psi_{F_kF_k}$ it is
$\Lambda_{jF_k}\Lambda_{kF_k}$, and for $\psi_G$ it is $L_{jG}L_{kG}$ with
$L_{\cdot G}=\Lambda_{\cdot G}+\sum_kb_k\Lambda_{\cdot F_k}$, so $\psi_G$ moves the correlation of every
pair of items whose factors have a nonzero path from $G$, within a first-order factor ($b_k^2\lambda_{jk}\lambda_{ik}$)
as well as across two.

**SO1.4 (no truncation error).** The lemma of @sec-delta holds for every path: the condition is that $B$
has no directed path $g\rightsquigarrow h$, i.e. none from $F_k$ to $G$, and there is none. So a central
difference has rounding error only, at any step.

*Verification (`so-1`).* For M3, M4, MD and M22 in each of the four metrics, at a seeded generic point:
(a) $\Phi_{FF}$ and $\sigma$ from SO1.2 equal those of the $(I-B)^{-1}$ form (MD excepted, where $G$ also
carries items; the direct form is the one-$G$ statement), $10^{-12}$; (b) the closed-form $\Delta$ equals the
complex-step derivative ($10^{-10}$) and production's central difference ($10^{-8}$); (c) every path column
is reproduced by a central difference at $H=1/8$ to $10^{-12}$, which a quadratic function allows and a
cubic one does not.

```{r so-1}
so_mets <- list(M = c("marker", "item"), U = c("var", "dist"), V = c("var", "item"), W = c("marker", "dist"))
so_rand_theta <- function(so_md, so_seed) {                 # a generic point: free entries only, fixed rows keep their values
  set.seed(so_seed); fr <- so_md$fr; so_n <- nrow(fr)
  so_v <- ifelse(fr$type == "l", runif(so_n, .4, .9), ifelse(fr$type == "b", runif(so_n, .3, .9), runif(so_n, .5, 1.5)))
  so_v[fr$type == "p" & fr$r != fr$c] <- 0.2; so_v
}
so_1_models <- list(
  M3 = list(nk = rep(3, 3)), M4 = list(nk = rep(3, 4)), MD = list(nk = rep(3, 3), mdi = TRUE),
  M22 = list(nk = rep(3, 4), so_ng = 2, gsplit = c(2, 2)))
so_1 <- list(); so_seed <- 100
for (so_nm in names(so_1_models)) for (so_mn in names(so_mets)) {
  so_seed <- so_seed + 1
  so_md <- do.call(so_build, c(so_1_models[[so_nm]], list(gm = so_mets[[so_mn]][1], fm = so_mets[[so_mn]][2])))
  so_th <- so_rand_theta(so_md, so_seed); so_x <- so_mats(so_md, so_th); so_K <- so_md$K; so_ng <- so_md$ng; so_Fi <- so_ng + seq_len(so_K)
  # (a) the direct second-order form of the first-order block: Phi_FF = G' diag(psi_G) G + Psi_F  (one G: gamma gamma' psi_G)
  so_Ph <- so_Phi(so_x$B, so_x$P); so_Gam <- so_x$B[so_Fi, seq_len(so_ng), drop = FALSE]
  so_PhFF <- so_Gam %*% so_x$P[seq_len(so_ng), seq_len(so_ng), drop = FALSE] %*% t(so_Gam) + diag(diag(so_x$P)[so_Fi], so_K)
  so_Sdir <- so_x$L[, so_Fi, drop = FALSE] %*% so_PhFF %*% t(so_x$L[, so_Fi, drop = FALSE])
  if (!so_md$mdi) so_check(paste("SO1a direct form", so_nm, so_mn), so_rel(so_Ph[so_Fi, so_Fi], so_PhFF) < 1e-12 && so_rel(so_Sdir[lower.tri(so_Sdir)], so_msigma(so_md, so_th)) < 1e-12)
  # (b) closed-form Delta against production's central difference and against the complex step
  so_Dcf <- so_delta_cf(so_md, so_th); so_Dfd <- so_delta_fd(so_md, so_th); so_Dcs <- so_delta_cs(so_md, so_th)
  so_1[[length(so_1) + 1]] <- data.frame(model = so_nm, metric = so_mn, npar = so_md$npar_s,
    cf_vs_cs = so_rel(so_Dcf, so_Dcs), cf_vs_fd = so_rel(so_Dcf, so_Dfd))
  so_check(paste("SO1b closed form = complex step", so_nm, so_mn), so_rel(so_Dcf, so_Dcs) < 1e-10)
  so_check(paste("SO1b closed form = production difference", so_nm, so_mn), so_rel(so_Dcf, so_Dfd) < 1e-8)
  # (c) the quadratic lemma on the beta columns: a central difference at H = 1/8 has no truncation error
  so_H <- 1/8; so_jb <- which(so_md$fr$type == "b")
  so_gap <- sapply(so_jb, function(so_j) {
    tp <- so_th; tm <- so_th; tp[so_j] <- tp[so_j] + so_H; tm[so_j] <- tm[so_j] - so_H
    max(abs((so_msigma(so_md, tp) - so_msigma(so_md, tm)) / (2 * so_H) - so_Dcf[, so_j]))
  })
  so_check(paste("SO1c beta columns exact at H=1/8", so_nm, so_mn), max(so_gap) < 1e-12)
}
```
